Prose rewritten. Full function read, plus tbnet_connect_failed (632-638).

name: tun_attach
prose: Static function tun_attach(tun, file, skip_filter, napi, napi_frags, publish_tun) attaches the tun_file tfile = file->private_data to tun; it uses rtnl_dereference, so it relies on the caller holding the rtnl lock. Checks in order, each returning a negative errno through the out label: the result of security_tun_dev_attach if negative; -EINVAL if tfile->tun is already set and tfile is not detached; -EBUSY if tun lacks IFF_MULTI_QUEUE and tun->numqueues == 1; -E2BIG if tfile is not detached and tun->numqueues + tun->numdisabled == MAX_TAP_QUEUES. Then err = 0. If skip_filter is false and tun->filter_attached is true it calls sk_attach_filter(&tun->fprog) on the socket under lock_sock; if that succeeds (err == 0) the function goes to out and returns 0 immediately, without setting tfile->queue_index, tfile->tun, tun->tfiles or tun->numqueues; if it fails, err keeps that error and the function continues. For a non-detached tfile it resizes the tx ptr_ring to dev->tx_queue_len; on failure it returns -ENOMEM. It then sets tfile->queue_index = tun->numqueues and clears RCV_SHUTDOWN in sk_shutdown. For a detached tfile it only updates xdp_rxq.queue_index (with a WARN if the xdp_rxq is unregistered); otherwise it registers xdp_rxq_info (an error is returned) and the page-shared memory model (an error unregisters the xdp_rxq and is returned), then sets err = 0. For a detached tfile it calls tun_enable_queue and tun_napi_enable; otherwise sock_hold(&tfile->sk) and tun_napi_init. If tun has an xdp_prog it sets SOCK_XDP on tfile->sk. If publish_tun is true it publishes tfile->tun with rcu_assign_pointer; it then publishes tfile in tun->tfiles[tun->numqueues], increments tun->numqueues, calls tun_set_real_num_queues and returns err. For a detached tfile whose earlier sk_attach_filter call failed, err is not reset, so the function completes the attach and then returns that filter error.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is tun_attach (tun.c:690-783). Reviewer original right (a successful filter attach jumps to out and returns 0 before the queue is set up, tun.c:716-723); r15 right that the -EINVAL path needs tfile->tun already set. Added the detached-with-failed-filter case where err is not cleared (the err = 0 at tun.c:765 is only on the non-detached branch). Source read in full.

name: kaweth_probe
prose: Static function kaweth_probe(intf, id) is the USB probe for Kawasaki LSI adapters. Return paths: (1) if usb_check_bulk_endpoints (endpoints 1 IN, 2 OUT) or usb_check_int_endpoints (endpoint 3 IN) fails it logs and returns -ENODEV. (2) alloc_etherdev failure returns -ENOMEM. After that it sets up kaweth, initialises the lock and wait queue, and calls kaweth_reset (result ignored). (3) If the high byte of bcdDevice is zero, it allocates a firmware page (failure: rv = -ENOMEM, goto err_free_netdev), downloads four firmware blobs and triggers the firmware; whether any step fails (the error is only logged) or all succeed, it then reaches err_fw, which frees the page and the netdev and returns -EIO (the device is expected to re-enumerate). (4) Otherwise it reads the configuration; a negative result, a hw_addr equal to the broadcast address FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF, a failed kaweth_set_urb_size, kaweth_set_sofs_wait or kaweth_set_receive_filter, or a failed allocation of the tx URB, rx URB, irq URB, interrupt coherent buffer or rx coherent buffer, each goes to a cleanup label that frees what was allocated so far (URBs, coherent buffers) and the netdev, and returns rv, which is -EIO at that point (so URB and buffer allocation failures also give -EIO, not -ENOMEM). (5) Otherwise it copies the broadcast address and the configured MAC to the netdev, sets netdev_ops, watchdog timeout, mtu from the configuration segment_size and ethtool_ops, initialises the lowmem work, stores kaweth with usb_set_intfdata and calls register_netdev; if that returns nonzero it goes to err_intfdata, which clears the interface data, frees both coherent buffers and the three URBs and the netdev and returns -EIO. (6) On success it logs and returns 0 with the netdev registered and kaweth stored as the interface data. Apart from the -ENODEV and the two -ENOMEM cases, every failure returns -EIO; raw USB errors from the firmware or configuration helpers are only logged.
note: slice cut the head: the real function is kaweth_probe (kaweth.c:874-1070). Reviewer r15 wrong on both points: the broadcast check is real (kaweth.c:1005-1010, hw_addr == bcast_addr jumps to err_free_netdev) and the firmware and configuration errors are only logged, rv stays -EIO (kaweth.c:906,960-1000). The old prose was right except that it omitted that the firmware-download branch returns -EIO even when every download step succeeds (kaweth.c:975-981 falls into err_fw). Source read in full.

name: lan78xx_resume
prose: Resume callback of the lan78xx USB driver: takes dev->dev_mutex, and every return path releases it (single exit label out). If EVENT_DEV_OPEN is set it first calls lan78xx_flush_tx_fifo (an error jumps to out and returns that errno; EVENT_DEV_ASLEEP is then still set), resubmits dev->urb_intr when non-NULL (a failure there is only warned about, with netif_device_detach on -ENODEV, and is not returned), and under txq.lock, if the netdev is present, submits the deferred TX URBs via lan78xx_submit_deferred_urbs (which releases the buffers of URBs when the device is absent, the carrier is off or a pipe halt was already seen, and which stops the queue on -EPIPE and detaches the netdev on -ENODEV); a reported pipe halt defers EVENT_TX_HALT. It then clears EVENT_DEV_ASLEEP, starts the netdev queue only if there was no pipe halt, the device is present and the pending TX data is below the URB space, calls lan78xx_start_tx_path (an error returns that errno), schedules NAPI and, if stat_monitor is not pending, sets dev->delta = 1 and arms the timer. If EVENT_DEV_OPEN is clear it only clears EVENT_DEV_ASLEEP. In both cases it then writes the wake-up registers in order WUCSR2=0, WUCSR=0, WK_SRC=0xFFF1FF1F, WUCSR2=(NS_RCD|ARP_RCD|IPV6_TCPSYN_RCD|IPV4_TCPSYN_RCD), WUCSR=(EEE_TX_WAKE|EEE_RX_WAKE|PFDA_FR|RFE_WAKE_FR|WUFR|MPR|BCST_FR); the first write that returns a negative value ends the function with that value, otherwise the return value is 0.
note: [rev:mixed] r1/r15 right that register writes (5337-5362) run also when EVENT_DEV_OPEN clear and that old prose mis-scoped them; r2 claim (stop queue/EVENT_TX_HALT only on -EPIPE) right for lan78xx_submit_deferred_urbs 5260-5262; r15 'device-absent deferred URBs are not released' wrong: 5245-5249 releases them when !netif_device_present/!carrier_ok/pipe_halted (but the call is only made if netif_device_present at 5305, so in resume the absent case never reaches the release)

name: rtl8152_check_firmware
prose: Validates a loaded Realtek r8152 firmware image (rtl_fw->fw) and returns a long: 0 on success, otherwise -EFAULT (the checksum helper also returns -EFAULT on mismatch). It fails if the file is smaller than struct fw_header (r8152.c:4655), if the SHA-256 of fw_hdr->version over size-32 bytes differs from fw_hdr->checksum (rtl8152_fw_verify_checksum, 4660), or if a block header would extend past the end of the file (4670). It then walks the blocks from sizeof(*fw_hdr), advancing by ALIGN(block->length, 8). RTL_FW_END must have length == sizeof(struct fw_block) and ends the walk; reaching the end of the file without an END block is not itself an error. PLA and USB blocks must each appear at most once and pass rtl8152_is_fw_mac_ok. PHY_START is rejected if START, any NC/UNION_NC/NC1/NC2/UC2/UC or STOP was already seen, and must have length == sizeof(struct fw_phy_patch_key); PHY_STOP requires START seen and no earlier STOP, with length == sizeof(struct fw_block); PHY_NC and the PHY_UNION_NC/NC1/NC2/UC2/UC blocks require START seen and STOP not seen, are each allowed once, and obey ordering constraints against the later-numbered union kinds, and each passes its rtl8152_is_fw_phy_nc_ok / rtl8152_is_fw_phy_union_ok check; PHY_UNION_MISC only has to pass the union check and may repeat; PHY_FIXUP must pass rtl8152_is_fw_phy_fixup_ok and may repeat; PHY_SPEED_UP is allowed once and must pass rtl8152_is_fw_phy_speed_up_ok; PHY_VER is allowed once, only before any START/NC/UNION/STOP block, and must pass rtl8152_is_fw_phy_ver_ok. Unknown block types only produce a warning and are skipped. After the walk (or at an END block) it fails with -EFAULT if PHY_START was seen but PHY_STOP was not; it does not require PLA, USB or any PHY block to be present. It only reads the firmware and logs; it takes no locks and allocates nothing.
note: [rev:mixed] r1 (success requires PLA and USB) wrong: no such check, flags only used for duplicates (4679-4706, 4920-4926); r15 (PHY_STOP unconditional) wrong: 4921 requires STOP only if START set; the 'slice cut head' - real function body at 4647-4929. Old prose also omitted that an unknown-type block with length 0 would not advance i (not asserted)

name: usbnet_probe
prose: Generic probe for usbnet-based USB network drivers. First, if the bound usb_driver does not yet support autosuspend it sets supports_autosuspend and calls pm_runtime_enable on the interface (usbnet.c:1720-1723). If prod->driver_info is NULL it returns -ENODEV (no allocation done). It allocates an etherdev (alloc_etherdev failure returns -ENOMEM straight through the out label), initialises the usbnet structure, queues, work items, timer and mutexes, and then either calls info->bind (a negative result goes to out1 without calling unbind), or, when info->in/out are not both set, calls usbnet_get_endpoints, or otherwise sets the in/out pipes from info, calls usb_set_interface unless FLAG_NO_SETINT, and checks the bulk endpoints (-EINVAL on failure). If status is still non-negative and dev->status is set it calls init_status. A negative status at that point goes to out3. It then defaults rx_urb_size, computes maxpacket (zero gives -ENODEV via out4), assigns a random MAC if the address is invalid, sets device types, updates the max queue lengths, and, when can_dma_sg is set without FLAG_SEND_ZLP/FLAG_MULTI_PACKET, allocates a 1-byte padding_pkt (failure: -ENOMEM via out4). register_netdev failure goes to out5. On success it stores dev as interface data, calls netif_device_attach, calls usbnet_link_change(dev,0,0) when FLAG_LINK_INTR is set, and returns 0. Error unwinding falls through: out5 kfree(padding_pkt), out4 usb_free_urb(dev->interrupt), out3 info->unbind if non-NULL, out1 usbnet_mark_going_away, cancel_work_sync(kevent), timer_delete_sync(delay), free_netdev, then out returns status. A failed bind therefore only runs the out1 steps, while any later failure also runs the steps below its label.
note: [rev:mixed] r1 (out2 label does not exist) right/obsolete (labels out,out1,out3,out4,out5); r2 (omitted usbnet_get_endpoints error) right for the old prose; r15 (alloc_etherdev failure goes direct not via out) wrong: usbnet.c:1737-1739 goto out; slice cut head, real body 1704-1906

name: virtnet_set_hashflow
prose: ethtool set_rxfh_fields handler of virtio_net: changes which RSS hash-type bits are saved for one flow type. Takes no locks. It returns -EINVAL, before changing any state, if info->data is none of exactly (RXH_IP_SRC|RXH_IP_DST), exactly (RXH_IP_SRC|RXH_IP_DST|RXH_L4_B_0_1|RXH_L4_B_2_3) or has the RXH_DISCARD bit set (any value with that bit is accepted), if info->flow_type is not TCP_V4/UDP_V4/IPV4/TCP_V6/UDP_V6/IPV6_FLOW, or if the computed hash types are not a subset of vi->rss_hash_types_supported. Otherwise it starts from vi->rss_hash_types_saved and, for TCP/UDP flows, clears that flow's IPv4 or IPv6 bit and its TCP or UDP bit and, unless RXH_DISCARD is set, sets the IP bit plus the TCP/UDP bit only when the full L4 combination was requested; for IPV4_FLOW/IPV6_FLOW it clears only the IPv4/IPv6 bit and, unless RXH_DISCARD is set, replaces the whole value with just that bit. If the result differs from vi->rss_hash_types_saved it stores it there and in vi->rss_hdr->hash_types (little-endian); then only when NETIF_F_RXHASH is set in vi->dev->features it calls virtnet_commit_rss_command, and if that returns false it returns -EINVAL with the new types already stored. It returns 0 when nothing changed, when changed with NETIF_F_RXHASH clear (no commit), or when the commit succeeds.
note: [rev:right] r15 (return 0 when types change but NETIF_F_RXHASH clear, omitted) right: virtio_net.c:4446-4454; r1 (no update when unchanged / commit failure leaves mutation) right; r2 (any data with RXH_DISCARD bit accepted) right at 4395,4399. slice cut head, real body 4389-4455

name: vmxnet3_probe_device
prose: PCI probe for the vmxnet3 NIC. It sets enable_mq to 0 if MSI is unavailable, picks Tx/Rx queue counts from the number of online CPUs when enable_mq is set (Rx count 1 when RSS support is not compiled in), and allocates the net_device with alloc_etherdev_mq (failure: returns -ENOMEM immediately, with no cleanup). After that pci drvdata is set to the netdev, and it stays set on the failure paths as well. It then, in order: sets a 64-bit DMA mask (on failure it returns that error via err_set_mask); maps the adapter structure for DMA (mapping error: -EFAULT via err_set_mask); allocates the shared structure (-ENOMEM via err_alloc_shared); calls vmxnet3_alloc_pci_resources (negative result returned via err_alloc_pci); negotiates the hardware revision by trying revisions from VMXNET3_REV_9 down to REV_1 and the UPT version through VMXNET3_REG_UVRS (no match or UPT bit 0 clear: -EBUSY via err_ver); for version >= 7 reads the device and passthrough capability registers, writes the device-capability register and issues the GET_DCR0_REG command under cmd_lock, chooses the producer register offsets, determines the queue counts (querying the device when the version is >= 6), allocates the coherent queue-descriptor area (-ENOMEM via err_ver), pm_conf (-ENOMEM via err_alloc_pm), rss_conf if VMXNET3_RSS is compiled in (via err_alloc_rss), and coal_conf for version >= 3 (via err_coal_conf). It then sets up features, interrupt resources (vmxnet3_alloc_intr_resources has no return value that is checked), RSS flag, MAC address, ops, MTU range, the reset work item, NAPI instances, and queue counts, and calls register_netdev; failure there goes to err_register. On success it calls vmxnet3_check_link and returns 0. The err_register path frees coal_conf (version >= 3), then the interrupt resources, and then falls through freeing rss_conf, pm_conf, the queue-descriptor memory, the PCI resources, the shared structure, unmapping the adapter mapping and free_netdev; later labels skip the earlier frees. Note the unwinding is not strictly the reverse of allocation order (coal_conf is freed before the interrupt resources although it was allocated before them).
note: [rev:right] r15 (cleanup frees coal_conf before interrupt resources, not reverse order) right: vmxnet3_drv.c:4292-4297 vs alloc 4201-4214, 4234; old prose also claimed drvdata set only on success and omitted the dma_set_mask error; slice cut head, real body 3974-4321

name: vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf
prose: Fills receive descriptors of one Rx command ring of a vmxnet3 queue, starting at ring->next2fill, and returns the number of descriptors made available to the device (the slice cut the head; the function is vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf(rq, ring_idx, num_to_alloc, adapter)). The loop runs while num_allocated <= num_to_alloc. For each slot it sets comp_state to PENDING and prepares a buffer according to rbi->buf_type: an XDP buffer is taken from the queue's page pool; an skb buffer is allocated with __netdev_alloc_skb_ip_align and DMA-mapped only if rbi->skb is NULL; a page buffer (BUG_ON if the type is not PAGE or len is not PAGE_SIZE) is allocated with alloc_page(GFP_ATOMIC) and DMA-mapped only if rbi->page is NULL. An existing skb or page is reused without remapping. An allocation or DMA-mapping failure (the mapped skb or page is freed first in the mapping-failure cases) increments rq->stats.rx_buf_alloc_failure and stops the loop. The descriptor address, length, buffer type and the inverted generation bit are written; when num_allocated has reached num_to_alloc the slot is marked COMP_DONE and the loop ends without setting the generation bit (the last slot is filled but not handed to the device and next2fill is not advanced); otherwise the generation bit is set, num_allocated is incremented and next2fill is advanced. After the loop it logs, executes BUG_ON(num_allocated != 0 && ring->next2fill == ring->next2comp) and returns num_allocated, which can be 0 on an immediate failure.
note: slice cut head; real name vmxnet3_rq_alloc_rx_buf at vmxnet3_drv.c:673-775; old drop was wrong (listed name vmxnet3_alloc_rx_buf does not exist in source) and old prose said 'never leaves non-empty ring with next2fill==next2comp' which is only a BUG_ON assertion (line 773)

name: vrf_ip6_rcv
prose: Receive hook for IPv6 packets arriving on a VRF slave (defined at vrf.c:1323 when CONFIG_IPV6 is enabled; the stub at 1381 for non-IPv6 builds just returns skb). It saves orig_iif = skb->skb_iif and computes need_strict (rt6_need_strict on the destination) and is_ndisc (neighbour-discovery ICMPv6). Branch 1, taken when skb->pkt_type is PACKET_LOOPBACK or (need_strict and not NDISC): sets skb->dev = vrf_dev, skb->skb_iif = vrf_dev->ifindex and IP6SKB_L3SLAVE in IP6CB; if the packet was loopback it sets pkt_type = PACKET_HOST and does no dst lookup, otherwise it calls vrf_ip6_input_dst(skb, vrf_dev, orig_iif); it then returns skb without running netfilter. Otherwise (not loopback and either not strict or NDISC): if the frame is not NDISC it adds vrf_dev rx stats, sets skb->dev and skb->skb_iif to the VRF, taps the packet through dev_queue_xmit_nit when vrf_dev->ptype_all is non-empty and the mac header could be added, and sets IP6SKB_L3SLAVE; an NDISC frame keeps its dev, skb_iif and flags. If need_strict (including strict NDISC) it then calls vrf_ip6_input_dst. Finally it returns vrf_rcv_nfhook(NFPROTO_IPV6, NF_INET_PRE_ROUTING, ...), which is NULL unless nf_hook returned 1 (when NULL the netfilter code has taken over the skb). vrf_ip6_input_dst first drops the skb's existing dst (skb_dst_drop) and sets a new dst only if the VRF-table lookup returns a non-NULL entry that is not the ip6 null entry, so on a failed lookup the skb is left without a dst.
note: [rev:mixed] r1 (NDISC keeps original dev/iif, no L3SLAVE) right for non-strict-or-strict non-loopback NDISC (1349-1370); r2 (loopback NDISC takes branch 1 and gets dev/iif/L3SLAVE) right (1335-1338); r15 (existing dst dropped first, not left unchanged on failed lookup) right: vrf.c:1310-1318

name: vxlan_snoop
prose: Learns or updates the VXLAN FDB entry for a received packet's source (called with RCU read lock held; it uses vxlan_find_mac_rcu). Returns SKB_DROP_REASON_MAC_INVALID_SOURCE with no other effect if src_mac is not a valid unicast Ethernet address (vxlan_core.c:1447). It computes ifindex = src_ifindex only when src_ip is an IPv6 link-local address (CONFIG_IPV6), else 0. If an entry for (src_mac, vni) exists: it writes f->updated = jiffies if it differs; then returns SKB_DROP_REASON_VXLAN_ENTRY_EXISTS if the entry has a nexthop; else returns SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET if the first remote's remote_ip equals *src_ip and its remote_ifindex equals ifindex (this test comes before the static check, so a static entry with the same address also returns NOT_DROPPED_YET); else returns SKB_DROP_REASON_VXLAN_ENTRY_EXISTS if f->state has NUD_PERMANENT or NUD_NOARP; else (migration) it logs under net_ratelimit, sets the first remote's remote_ip = *src_ip (remote_ifindex is not changed), sends an RTM_NEWNEIGH notification and falls through to return SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET. If no entry exists it takes vxlan->hash_lock (spin_lock), and only when netif_running(dev) calls vxlan_fdb_update to create a NUD_REACHABLE entry with NLM_F_EXCL|NLM_F_CREATE (its result is ignored), releases the lock and returns SKB_NOT_DROPPED_YET, whether or not an entry was created.
note: [rev:right] r15 (equality check precedes static check, so static entry w/ matching remote returns NOT_DROPPED_YET) right: vxlan_core.c:1468-1474; r1 (no entry & !netif_running still returns NOT_DROPPED_YET) right and already in prose; slice cut head, real body 1437-1500

name: vxlan_fdb_update_existing
prose: Applies a netlink add/replace/append request to an existing vxlan FDB entry f (rtnl lock held; uses rtnl_dereference/rcu_access_pointer on f->nh). It first returns -EOPNOTSUPP, with f unchanged, if nhid is non-zero but f has no nexthop, if nhid is non-zero together with NLM_F_APPEND, or if f has a nexthop and state lacks NUD_PERMANENT and NUD_NOARP. Unless the request carries NTF_EXT_LEARNED while f->flags has NTF_VXLAN_ADDED_BY_USER, it copies state into f->state and (ndm_flags & ~NTF_USE) into f->flags, noting a change if either differed. With NLM_F_REPLACE: for a unicast, non-zero key MAC it calls vxlan_fdb_nh_update when nhid is non-zero (a negative result is returned immediately; it returns 0 without change if f already uses that nexthop id, 1 after switching to it taking a reference and dropping the old one, or -EINVAL for an unknown, deleted, non-fdb or non-multipath nexthop, or -EAFNOSUPPORT for a family mismatch with vxlan->default_dst.remote_ip, releasing the reference it took), or else vxlan_fdb_replace, which rewrites the first remote (ip, port, vni, ifindex) unless an identical remote already exists; for a multicast or all-zero key MAC it returns -EOPNOTSUPP. With NLM_F_APPEND and a multicast or all-zero key MAC it calls vxlan_fdb_append, which adds a new remote unless an identical one exists (-ENOMEM if the allocation fails, returned immediately). With NTF_USE it sets f->updated to jiffies. If anything changed it sets f->updated, and calls vxlan_fdb_notify(RTM_NEWNEIGH, swdev_notify) on the appended or else first remote; if the notify fails with a non-zero nhid it returns that error, otherwise it restores the replaced remote (REPLACE) or removes the appended one (APPEND) before returning the error. Otherwise it returns 0. State/flags changes made earlier are not reverted on any error path after they were stored, and without NLM_F_REPLACE/NLM_F_APPEND the remotes are not touched.

name: qmc_hcld_recv_complete
prose: RX-completion callback of the Freescale QMC HDLC driver (the source spells it qmc_hcld_recv_complete, fsl_qmc_hdlc.c:248; the slice cut its head). The context is the qmc_hdlc_desc that was queued for receive. It first unmaps the descriptor's DMA buffer (dma_unmap_single, desc->dma_size). If flags has any QMC_HDLC_RX_ERROR_FLAGS bit it increments rx_errors, plus rx_over_errors for OVF, rx_frame_errors once for UNA and once more for ABORT, and rx_crc_errors for CRC, frees desc->skb and goes to re-queue. Otherwise, with crc_size 4 if is_crc32 else 2, if length < crc_size it increments rx_length_errors, frees the skb and goes to re-queue; else it subtracts the CRC, increments rx_packets, adds the reduced length to rx_bytes, skb_put()s that length, sets skb->protocol with hdlc_type_trans and passes the skb to netif_rx (ownership passes to the stack). In all three paths it then calls qmc_hdlc_recv_queue(qmc_hdlc, desc, desc->dma_size). That call allocates a new skb into desc->skb; if dev_alloc_skb fails desc->skb is NULL and nothing needs freeing; if the DMA mapping or qmc_chan_read_submit fails it unmaps (submit failure only) and frees the new skb and sets desc->skb to NULL. On any non-zero result this callback logs an error and increments rx_errors, and the descriptor is then not queued for receive. The callback returns nothing.
note: [rev:right] r15 (on dev_alloc_skb failure there is no new skb to free) right: fsl_qmc_hdlc.c:304-306 vs 324-326; function name was spelled differently in source (qmc_hcld_)

name: raw_eth_ioctl
prose: ioctl handler for the HDLC Ethernet-emulation protocol, switching on ifs->type. IF_GET_PROTO: returns -EINVAL if the device's current HDLC protocol is not this one; otherwise sets ifs->type to IF_PROTO_HDLC_ETH, and if ifs->size is smaller than sizeof(raw_hdlc_proto) sets ifs->size to that size and returns -ENOBUFS; else copies the protocol state (hdlc->state) to the user buffer, returning -EFAULT if the copy fails and 0 otherwise. IF_PROTO_HDLC_ETH: returns -EPERM without CAP_NET_ADMIN, -EBUSY if IFF_UP is set, -EFAULT if the settings cannot be copied from user space; it replaces ENCODING_DEFAULT with ENCODING_NRZ and PARITY_DEFAULT with PARITY_CRC16_PR1_CCITT, then calls hdlc->attach(dev, encoding, parity) and returns its result if non-zero, then attach_hdlc_protocol(dev, &proto, sizeof(raw_hdlc_proto)) and returns its result if non-zero. attach_hdlc_protocol first calls detach_hdlc_protocol, which on success drops the previous protocol, frees its state and resets the device; if that detach fails (for example a netdev notifier refuses NETDEV_PRE_TYPE_CHANGE) the previous protocol stays; after a successful detach it can still fail with -ENOSYS (module reference) or -ENOBUFS (state allocation), leaving no protocol attached. On success it copies the new settings into hdlc->state, runs ether_setup while keeping tx_queue_len, clears IFF_TX_SKB_SHARING, assigns a random hardware address, sends NETDEV_POST_TYPE_CHANGE, calls netif_dormant_off and returns 0. Any other ifs->type returns -EINVAL with no side effects.
note: [rev:mixed] r2 (attach_hdlc_protocol detaches the previous protocol before it can fail) right for the -ENOSYS/-ENOBUFS failures (hdlc.c:277-289); r15 (returns -EBUSY without detaching) wrong about the code (-EBUSY is not returned there; the detach-error return is the notifier's error, hdlc.c:303-307) but right that a failure can leave the old protocol attached; hdlc_raw_eth.c:51-110

name: n2_run
prose: Probes and registers one RISCom/N2 card (n2.c:321, __init). Arguments io, irq and winbase are range-checked first and the function returns -ENODEV, with nothing allocated and without calling n2_destroy_card, if io is outside 0x200-0x3FF or not a multiple of N2_IOPORTS, if irq is outside 3-15 or equals 6, or if winbase is outside 0xA0000-0xFFFFF or not 4 KiB aligned. It then allocates a zeroed card_t (failure: -ENOBUFS, nothing to release and no n2_destroy_card call). Every later failure calls n2_destroy_card(card) and returns: -ENOMEM if either hdlc net device allocation fails; -EBUSY if request_region, request_irq or request_mem_region fails; -EFAULT if ioremap fails; -ENODEV if USE_WINDOWSIZE is not 16384, 32768 or 65536; -EIO if the RAM test leaves tx_ring_buffers below 1; -ENOBUFS if register_hdlc_device fails for a port (that port's card pointer is cleared first so n2_destroy_card does not unregister it, ports already registered are unregistered). n2_destroy_card releases the IRQ, I/O region, ioremap and memory region only when card->irq, card->io or card->winbase respectively are set; because card->winbase is NULL after a failed ioremap, the memory region from request_mem_region is not released on the -EFAULT path. The function divides by (valid0 + valid1) when sizing the rings, so callers must pass at least one non-zero valid flag. On success it programs the PCR/BAR/PSR registers, sizes the RAM, computes the TX/RX ring counts, starts the SCA, initialises and registers an hdlc device for each enabled port, stores the card in *new_card, advances new_card to &card->next_card and returns 0.
note: [rev:right] r15 (not every failure path calls n2_destroy_card: validation and kzalloc failures return directly) right: n2.c:328-345; r1 (ioremap failure leaks request_mem_region) right: 375-380 with n2_destroy_card 299-302; r2 (contract-only complaint) n/a; slice began at 260 so full function is 321-474

name: n2_init
prose: Module init for the N2 driver (n2.c:476, __init). If the module parameter string hw is NULL it returns -EINVAL (after logging 'no card initialized' only when built as a module). Otherwise it prints the version and parses hw, advancing the global hw pointer, as a sequence of specifications io,irq,ram,ports separated by ':' where ports is a run of the characters '0' and '1' (each at most once). A missing comma after io, irq or ram ends the loop (break), as does a specification that enables neither port. For a specification that enabled at least one port and is followed by ':' or the end of the string it calls n2_run(io, irq, ram, valid[0], valid[1]) and ignores its return value, so n2_run errors are not propagated. If the string ends right after a specification it returns first_card ? 0 : -EINVAL immediately, without printing the error. When the loop is left in any other way (break, or the character after the specification is neither ':' nor NUL) it logs 'invalid hardware parameters' and returns first_card ? 0 : -EINVAL. first_card is non-NULL only if some earlier n2_run call succeeded, so the function returns 0 whenever at least one card was registered, even if a later specification was malformed or failed. An n2_run failure on the ioremap path leaves its memory region requested.

name: ath10k_bmi_set_start
prose: Sends a BMI set-application-start command to the target. The listed name bmi_set_app_start does not exist; the function in bmi.c:501 is ath10k_bmi_set_start(ar, address). It builds the command locally (cmd.id = BMI_SET_APP_START, little-endian, and the address) so the caller supplies no command buffer. If ar->bmi.done_sent is already set it logs a warning and returns -EBUSY without sending anything. Otherwise it calls ath10k_hif_exchange_bmi_msg(ar, &cmd, cmdlen, NULL, NULL) with cmdlen = sizeof(cmd.id) + sizeof(cmd.set_app_start); if that returns non-zero it logs a warning and returns that value; otherwise it returns 0. It takes no locks itself and does not modify ar->bmi.

name: ath10k_core_fetch_firmware_api_n
prose: Loads an ath10k 'firmware-N.bin' file by name and parses its IE (information element) list into *fw_file. It calls ath10k_fetch_fw_file(ar, ar->hw_params.fw.dir, name) and stores the result in fw_file->firmware; if that is an error pointer it returns the negative errno (the error pointer stays in fw_file->firmware, nothing is released). Otherwise it returns -EINVAL if the file is shorter than the magic string (including its NUL), if the magic does not match, or if an IE's declared length exceeds the remaining data; in these cases it goes to err, which calls ath10k_core_free_firmware_files(ar) (this releases the firmware files held in ar, namely ar->normal_mode_fw.fw_file.firmware, the cal and pre-cal files and the code-swap segments, rather than naming the fw_file argument). It walks IEs (each padded to 4 bytes, while more than one IE header of bytes remains): FW_VERSION (copied as a string when it fits), FEATURES (sets bits in fw_file->fw_features up to ATH10K_FW_FEATURE_COUNT), FW_IMAGE, OTP_IMAGE and FW_CODE_SWAP_IMAGE (pointers into the firmware buffer and lengths), WMI_OP_VERSION and HTT_OP_VERSION (only when the length is 4), and TIMESTAMP (log only); unknown IEs only produce a warning. After the walk, if the NON_BMI feature bit is not set and the firmware image pointer or length is zero it warns and returns -ENOMEDIUM via the same err path (not -ENOENT or -EINVAL). Otherwise it returns 0 and the firmware reference stays held in fw_file->firmware for the caller.

name: ath10k_add_interface
prose: mac80211 add_interface callback of ath10k (the slice cut the head; real body mac.c:5556-5919). Takes ar->conf_mutex, and releases it on every return path. It zeroes and initialises arvif, then returns -ENOBUFS if ar->num_peers >= ar->max_num_peers and -EBUSY if ar->free_vdev_map is 0; it picks the lowest free vdev id and maps vif->type to a WMI vdev type/subtype (a mesh point without the MESH_11S service and without raw mode returns -EINVAL; an unknown type only triggers WARN_ON and keeps the zero type). For ADHOC, MESH_POINT and AP it allocates a beacon buffer (kmalloc for HL devices, dma_alloc_coherent otherwise; failure -ENOMEM). If software crypto is required (HW_CRYPTO_DISABLED) without raw mode it returns -EINVAL. It then creates the firmware vdev with ath10k_wmi_vdev_create (failure returns the error through err, which only frees the beacon buffer); a failure of the optional 'disable 4addr src learning' set-param is only warned about (-EOPNOTSUPP is silent) and is not returned. It clears the vdev's bit in free_vdev_map and links arvif into ar->arvifs under data_lock. After that, a failure of keepalive disable, the NSS set-param (when cfg_tx_chainmask is set and the vif is not monitor), AP/IBSS peer creation, the peer lookup (-ENOENT), the AP kickout setup, the STA power-save parameters and recalculations, txbf, RTS, txpower recalc, or monitor recalc is returned and unwound: err_peer_delete (AP/IBSS only: delete the peer and wait) then err_vdev_delete (ath10k_wmi_vdev_delete, set the free_vdev_map bit again, unlink arvif under data_lock) then err (free the beacon buffer, drop the mutex). The FTM responder set-param result is only warned about. For monitor interfaces ar->monitor_arvif is set before ath10k_monitor_recalc, and it is not cleared if that fails. On success it wakes the vdev's mac80211 queue unless ar->tx_paused (checked under htt.tx_lock), releases the mutex and returns 0.
note: [rev:right] r15 (disable_4addr_src_lrn failure only warned, not propagated) right: mac.c:5730-5739; old prose also said any set-param error propagates and described mesh -EINVAL too broadly

name: ath10k_sdio_mbox_rxmsg_pending_handler
prose: Services pending HTC receive messages on the ath10k SDIO mailbox (sdio.c:733; the slice cut the head). It sets *done = true on entry, seeds lookaheads[0] with msg_lookahead (n_lookaheads = 1) and loops while time_before(jiffies, timeout). Each pass calls ath10k_sdio_mbox_rx_alloc; if that returns non-zero the loop breaks with that value as ret. If ar_sdio->n_rx_pkts >= 2 it sets *done = false; it then calls ath10k_sdio_mbox_rx_fetch_bundle (n_rx_pkts > 1) or ath10k_sdio_mbox_rx_fetch, but that result is immediately overwritten by the following ret = ath10k_sdio_mbox_rx_process_packets(...), so a fetch error is not returned by itself. If processing leaves n_lookaheads == 0 or ret non-zero the loop breaks; otherwise it sets *done = false and runs again with the new lookaheads, until the timeout expires. After the loop it logs a warning when ret is non-zero and not -ECANCELED, and returns ret, which is the rx_alloc error, the last process_packets result, or the value left from the last iteration (0 if the loop ended on timeout after successful processing). *done is only ever set to false after entry, in the two places above.

name: ath11k_mac_op_bss_info_changed
prose: mac80211 bss_info_changed callback of ath11k (real name ath11k_mac_op_bss_info_changed, mac.c:3527-3879; the listed name ath11k_bss_info_changed does not exist). It returns nothing; it takes ar->conf_mutex at the start and releases it at the end (there is no early return). It handles each bit of 'changed' independently, in this order: BEACON_INT (stores arvif->beacon_interval and sets the vdev beacon-interval param); BEACON (sets the pdev beacon-tx-mode param to staggered, sets up the beacon template if !do_not_send_tmpl or !bcca_zero_sent, sets do_not_send_tmpl from bcca_zero_sent, and for HE-capable BSS sets the BA mode to 256-buffer); BEACON_INFO or BEACON (stores dtim_period and sets the vdev DTIM param); SSID for AP vifs (copies the SSID when its length is non-zero and the hidden_ssid flag); BSSID when the new address is non-zero; BEACON_ENABLED (HE txbf config if enabling, ath11k_control_beaconing, and an HE-operation vdev param when the vdev is up and HE parameters exist); ERP_CTS_PROT (sets the protection mode only if arvif->is_started, otherwise defers); ERP_SLOT; ERP_PREAMBLE; ASSOC (ath11k_bss_assoc if vif->cfg.assoc, else ath11k_bss_disassoc); TXPOWER (stores it and recalculates txpower); PS (stores arvif->ps and calls ath11k_mac_config_ps, only if hw_params.supports_sta_ps); MCAST_RATE (when a channel context for the vif exists, computes a legacy rate and sets the multicast and broadcast data-rate params); BASIC_RATES (recalculates the management rate if a channel context exists); TWT (sends enable or disable TWT command); HE_OBSS_PD; HE_BSS_COLOR (AP: collision-detection config and BSS-color param; station: color-change enable and collision config); FTM_RESPONDER (only if it differs, the RTT service is present and the vif is AP or mesh); FILS_DISCOVERY/UNSOL_BCAST_PROBE_RESP; ARP_FILTER (copies up to ATH11K_IPV4_MAX_COUNT addresses and the MAC into arvif->arp_ns_offload). Failures of the WMI commands are logged as warnings and do not stop later bits from being processed. Not every changed bit leads to a command: each is subject to the extra conditions noted above.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewer (name not in slice); real function ath11k_mac_op_bss_info_changed

name: ath11k_mac_update_vif_chan
prose: Moves the vdevs of a channel-context switch to their new channel contexts (ath11k mac.c:7471, caller holds ar->conf_mutex; returns nothing). For each of the n_vifs entries in order: if arvif->is_started is false it issues WARN_ON and skips the entry. If arvif->is_up it calls ath11k_mac_vdev_restart(arvif, new_ctx); a failure is logged and the entry is skipped (no beacon template and no vdev_up for it). If the vdev is not up it calls ath11k_mac_vdev_stop; on failure it logs and skips; otherwise it calls ath11k_mac_vdev_start on the new context, logs a failure, and in either case moves on to the next entry (a vdev that was not up is never brought up here). For a vdev that was up and restarted successfully it calls ath11k_mac_setup_bcn_tmpl (a failure is only logged and processing continues), then ath11k_wmi_vdev_up with the vdev's aid, bssid and the transmitting vdev's bssid if any; a vdev_up failure is logged. After the loop, if ATH11K_FLAG_MONITOR_VDEV_CREATED is set in ar->monitor_flags (the local monitor_vif is never set, so only the flag matters) it calls ath11k_mac_monitor_stop and, if that fails, logs and returns without attempting the start (the monitor was therefore not stopped); otherwise it calls ath11k_mac_monitor_start and on failure logs and returns (the monitor having been stopped by the preceding call).

name: ath11k_tm_wmi_event

name: ath12k_le32hilo_to_u64
prose: Static inline helper (ath12k core.h:110) that combines two 32-bit little-endian fields into one 64-bit value: it converts hi and lo with le32_to_cpu into u64 values and returns (hi64 << 32) | lo64, so the converted hi value occupies the upper 32 bits and the converted lo value the lower 32 bits, on any byte order. It has no side effects.

name: ath12k_dbring_buffer_release_event
prose: Handler for a WMI direct-buffer-release event (ath12k dbring.c:231; the slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL, before taking the RCU read lock, if the event's pdev_id is >= ab->num_radios or if num_buf_release_entry differs from num_meta_data_entry. Otherwise it takes rcu_read_lock and returns -EINVAL if ab->pdevs_active[pdev_idx] is NULL. It then switches on the module id: for WMI_DIRECT_BUF_SPECTRAL it just breaks without assigning anything, and for other modules it sets ring to NULL and warns; since ring is initialised to NULL and no code in the function assigns it otherwise, the following if (!ring) check is always true, so it jumps to rcu_unlock and returns -EINVAL. The RCU read lock is released on every path after it was taken. As written, everything after that check (looking up buffers in the idr, dma_unmap_single, calling ring->handler, memset and ath12k_dbring_bufs_replenish under srng->lock) is unreachable, and the function returns -EINVAL in every case.

name: ath12k_dp_alloc
prose: Sets up the SoC-level datapath state of an ath12k device (real name ath12k_dp_alloc, dp.c:1735-1841; the listed name ath12k_dp_init does not exist). It initialises the REO command lists and locks, then does the WBM idle ring and link-descriptor setup itself: ath12k_wbm_idle_ring_setup and ath12k_dp_link_desc_setup; a failure of either returns the error directly (no further cleanup in this function). It then calls ath12k_dp_cc_init (failure: goto fail_link_desc_cleanup), ath12k_dp_init_bank_profiles (failure: fail_hw_cc_cleanup), ath12k_dp_srng_common_setup (fail_dp_bank_profiles_cleanup), ath12k_dp_reoq_lut_setup (fail_cmn_srng_cleanup), then for each of hw_params->max_tx_ring rings sets tcl_data_ring_id, tx_status_head = 0, tx_status_tail = DP_TX_COMP_RING_SIZE(ab) - 1 and kmalloc's the tx_status array (failure: ret = -ENOMEM, jump to fail_cmn_reoq_cleanup; the arrays already allocated for earlier rings are not freed, as the FIXME says). It then fills the DSCP-to-TID map tables and calls ath12k_dp_rx_alloc (failure: fail_dp_rx_free). Returns 0 on success. On failure it returns the failing step's errno after falling through the cleanup labels in order: ath12k_dp_rx_free (rx alloc failure only), ath12k_dp_reoq_lut_cleanup, ath12k_dp_srng_common_cleanup, ath12k_dp_deinit_bank_profiles, ath12k_dp_cc_cleanup, ath12k_dp_link_desc_cleanup, each label running everything below it. The caller is not required to have set up the link descriptors or WBM idle ring: this function does that.

name: ath12k_dp_tx
prose: Enqueues one 802.11 data frame on a TCL ring (ath12k dp_tx.c:222; the slice cut the head). Early returns with no statistics change: -ESHUTDOWN if ATH12K_FLAG_CRASH_FLUSH is set, -EOPNOTSUPP if the frame lacks IEEE80211_TX_CTL_HW_80211_ENCAP and is not a data frame, -ENOMEM if ath12k_dp_tx_assign_buffer returns no tx descriptor. It picks a TCL ring from the hw ring selector modulo max_tx_ring (recording it in ring_map), fills the hal_tx_info (encryption for raw mode with software crypto, checksum offload, GSN metadata when gsn_valid, TID, encap type) and handles the encap type: native WiFi (either uses an MSDU extension descriptor and possibly a different encap for EAPOL/null frames, or re-encaps via ath12k_dp_tx_encap_nwifi), RAW (-EINVAL unless ATH12K_FLAG_RAW_MODE), Ethernet (nothing), 802.3 or unknown (-EINVAL and misc_fail stat). It realigns the payload if iova_mask requires (a failure there is only warned about), DMA-maps the skb (failure: -ENOMEM), optionally allocates and maps an MSDU extension-descriptor skb (-ENOMEM on allocation failure; a negative HTT metadata result or the DMA mapping error is returned), then under tcl_ring->lock takes the next TCL entry. If none is available it counts desc_na, sets ret = -ENOMEM and, only if not all rings have been tried (ring_map) and hw_params->tcl_ring_retry is set, increments ring_selector and sets tcl_ring_retry. Every failure after the tx descriptor was assigned unwinds as applicable (ext-desc unmap, free ext skb, unmap data, ath12k_dp_tx_release_txbuf) and increments arvif->link_stats.tx_dropped; the retry jump back to tcl_ring_sel happens only after the TCL-ring-full failure, not for DMA, ext-skb, HTT-metadata, encap or alignment failures, which return their error. On success it updates link and device statistics, writes the TCL descriptor, increments ar->dp.num_tx_pending and returns 0, with the skb recorded in tx_desc->skb for the completion path. The skb may have been modified in place (nwifi encap, MIC length added, realignment); on failure the function does not free the skb.

name: ath12k_htc_connect_service
prose: Connects an HTC service to an endpoint (ath12k htc.c:557; the slice cut the head). For ATH12K_HTC_SVC_ID_RSVD_CTRL it skips the handshake: it uses endpoint 0, max message size ATH12K_HTC_MAX_CTRL_MSG_LEN, disables credit flow control, and goes to setup (conn_resp->connect_resp_code is not written in this case). Otherwise it builds a connect-service control skb (-ENOMEM if allocation fails), sends it on endpoint 0 with ath12k_htc_send (on failure it frees the skb and returns the error), and waits up to ATH12K_HTC_CONN_SVC_TIMEOUT_HZ for the control response (-ETIMEDOUT on timeout). It returns -EPROTO if the response message id is wrong or the response is shorter than the response struct (nothing written to conn_resp yet); it then stores the response status in conn_resp->connect_resp_code and returns -EPROTO if it is not success. At setup it returns -EPROTO, before writing to the endpoint or conn_resp, if the assigned endpoint id is >= ATH12K_HTC_EP_COUNT or the max message size is zero. It then sets ep->eid and returns -EPROTO if the endpoint's service_id is already in use (at that point ep->eid has been written, conn_resp has not). Otherwise it writes conn_resp->eid and ->max_msg_len, and ep->service_id, max_tx_queue_depth, max_ep_message_len, tx_credits (the credit allocation, 0 for the control service) and ep_ops, then calls ath12k_hif_map_service_to_pipe; if that fails it returns that error, leaving the endpoint fields written above in place. On success it disables credit flow (tx_credit_flow_enabled = false) when it was requested (control service or any service other than the WMI control services) and the flag was set, and returns 0.

name: ath12k_peer_assoc_h_he
prose: Fills the HE (802.11ax) fields of a WMI peer-assoc argument (ath12k mac.c:2447; the slice cut the head). It returns without writing to arg when the vif link channel lookup fails (WARN_ON), when the link bss conf or the link sta cannot be obtained (warning), when the peer has no HE capability, or when every entry of arvif->bitrate_mask.control[band].he_mcs is zero (ath12k_peer_assoc_h_he_masked returns true only when all entries are zero; a mask with any non-zero entry lets processing continue). Otherwise it sets arg->he_flag (there is no earlier check of he_flag), copies the peer's HE MAC and PHY capability bytes, sets peer_he_ops from link_conf->he_oper.params masked to 24 bits, sets peer_max_mpdu only when the HE max-AMPDU exponent extension is non-zero and the peer is VHT or HT capable, decodes the PPE threshold table into peer_ppet when the PPE-threshold-present bit is set, and sets twt_responder / twt_requester from the MAC capability bits. If the mask's highest NSS exceeds link_sta->rx_nss and no mask entry at or below rx_nss - 1 is non-zero, it overwrites he_mcs_mask[rx_nss - 1] (the caller's bitrate mask) with the highest entry. It then stores the rx/tx HE MCS-NSS maps for 80 MHz and, when link_sta->bandwidth is 160 MHz, for 160 MHz too (peer_he_mcs_count counts the sets written) and computes arg->peer_nss from the maximum NSS (limited by ar->num_tx_chains and link_sta->rx_nss). If arg->peer_phymode is MODE_11AX_HE160 it recomputes peer_nss as min(rx_nss, ar->num_rx_chains), sets peer_bw_rxnss_override to ATH12K_BW_NSS_MAP_ENABLE, and, if the computed 160 MHz rx_nss is zero, warns 'invalid max_nss' and returns without adding the encoded rx_nss - 1 to the override; otherwise it ORs it in. Returns nothing; takes no locks.
note: [rev:wrong] r15 (omits early return when arg->he_flag already set) wrong: mac.c:2447-2691 has no he_flag test, he_flag is only assigned at 2500; also fixed an old-prose error: ath12k_peer_assoc_h_he_masked (2435-2445) returns true only when ALL mask entries are zero, the old prose said it returned when the mask was non-empty; slice cut head

name: ath12k_mac_get_rate_hw_value
prose: Returns the WMI fixed-rate code for a legacy bitrate in units of 100 kbit/s (mac.c:3763). It classifies the bitrate as CCK (10, 20, 55, 110 selects preamble WMI_RATE_PREAMBLE_CCK = 1) or otherwise OFDM (preamble 0), then looks the bitrate up in the ath12k_legacy_rates table; on a match it returns ATH12K_HW_RATE_CODE(hw_value, 0, preamble) = (1 << 28) | (preamble << 8) | hw_value, with hw_value taken from the table (CCK long-preamble 11M=0, 5.5M=1, 2M=2, 1M=3; OFDM 48M=0, 24M=1, 12M=2, 6M=3, 54M=4, 36M=5, 18M=6, 9M=7). So for example 10 gives 0x10000103, 110 gives 0x10000100, 60 gives 0x10000003, 540 gives 0x10000004. If the bitrate matches none of 10, 20, 55, 110, 60, 90, 120, 180, 240, 360, 480, 540 it returns -EINVAL converted to u32 (4294967274). It reads the static rate table and has no side effects.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; old prose gave wrong codes (64..67 and 0..7): the macro in wmi.h:4791 adds bit 28 and the preamble at bit 8, and the table values are not in rate order; contract removed since it was wrong and the function reads a global table

name: ath12k_mac_vdev_create
prose: Creates a firmware vdev for a link vif and registers it on ar (ath12k mac.c:9677; the slice cut the head; caller holds the wiphy mutex). It returns, with no state modified, -EINVAL if vif is a monitor interface and ar->monitor_vdev_created is set, -ENOSPC if ar->num_created_vdevs has reached TARGET_NUM_VDEVS, and -ENOLINK if link_id is below IEEE80211_MLD_MAX_NUM_LINKS but the link conf is NULL. It then sets arvif->bssid, arvif->ar and arvif->vdev_id from the lowest free bit of ab->free_vdev_map (and ar->monitor_vdev_id for monitor vifs) and calls ath12k_mac_setup_vdev_create_arg and ath12k_wmi_vdev_create; a failure of either returns the error through the err label, which only sets is_created = false and arvif->ar = NULL (no vdev rollback; ar->monitor_vdev_id stays set). After a successful vdev creation it increments ar->num_created_vdevs, sets is_created, updates allocated_vdev_map and free_vdev_map, adds arvif to ar->arvifs under data_lock, and sets the NSS param. Failure of that param goes to err_vdev_del. By vdev type: AP creates a peer (failure: err_vdev_del) and sets kickout parameters (failure: err_peer_del); STA sets four power-save settings (failure: err_peer_del) and may prepare the 11d scan state; MONITOR sets ar->monitor_vdev_created. It then sets arvif->txpower, calls ath12k_mac_txpower_recalc (failure: err_peer_del), stores the RTS threshold in ar->rts_threshold and sets it on the vdev (a failure there is only warned about but its error is the value returned), calls ath12k_dp_vdev_tx_attach and returns ret (0 unless the RTS command failed; the vdev stays created in that case). err_peer_del, for AP vdevs only, sends a peer delete and waits for it (failure of either goes to err_vdev_del, otherwise it decrements ar->num_peers); err_vdev_del resets the monitor id/created flags for monitor vdevs, calls ath12k_wmi_vdev_delete, decrements num_created_vdevs, clears the allocated_vdev_map and free_vdev_stats_id_map bits, sets the free_vdev_map bit again, unlinks arvif under data_lock, and falls into err, which clears is_created and arvif->ar and returns ret (the error that triggered the rollback).
note: [rev:right] r15 (setup_vdev_create_arg and wmi_vdev_create failures go to err without vdev rollback, so not 'any other failure') right: mac.c:9737-9749, 9903-9906; also the old prose said the AP rollback errno could come from peer delete: that is right (9877, 9883) but then returns that value; slice cut head, real body 9677-9907

name: ath12k_mac_assign_vif_to_vdev
prose: Chooses the radio (struct ath12k) for a link vif and makes sure its vdev exists (ath12k mac.c:9984; the slice cut the head; wiphy lock held and stays held). Radio selection: ah->radio if there is one radio, otherwise the radio resolved from ctx; it returns NULL if there are several radios and ctx is NULL, or if no radio resolves. For an MLD vif it first looks for a scan link whose arvif->ar is this radio and, if found, clears ar->scan.arvif and removes and unassigns that scan link. If arvif->ar is already set: it returns NULL (clearing arvif->ar) if arvif->is_created is false (WARN_ON); on a single-radio hw it returns arvif->ar immediately, without flushing the cache; on a multi-radio hw with a different radio it returns NULL if arvif->is_started (WARN_ON), else removes and unassigns the old link vif. It then calls ath12k_mac_assign_link_vif to get the (existing or newly allocated) arvif, whose NULL return on allocation failure is not checked. For an AP vif with ar->num_peers > max_num_peers - 1 it warns and returns arvif->ar without creating a vdev and without flushing the cache. If arvif->is_created it skips creation; otherwise it calls ath12k_mac_vdev_create and, on failure, warns and returns arvif->ar without flushing (that function clears arvif->ar after a failure past its early checks). In the other cases it calls ath12k_mac_vif_cache_flush(ar, arvif) and returns arvif->ar.
note: [rev:right] r1/r2/r15 (early single-radio return skips cache flush; AP peer-resource failure and vdev_create failure skip flush) all right: mac.c:10034-10035, 10056-10060, 10065-10069 vs 10076; slice cut head, real body 9984-10079; one detail: unchecked NULL from ath12k_mac_assign_link_vif at 10055

name: TRACE_EVENT(ath12k_htt_pktlog,
prose: Tracepoint definition for ath12k_htt_pktlog(ar, buf, buf_len, pktlog_checksum); the TRACE_EVENT macro generates the function trace_ath12k_htt_pktlog (trace.h:24). When CONFIG_ATH12K_TRACING is not set the local TRACE_EVENT macro makes it an empty static inline function that does nothing. When tracing is enabled, the generated tracepoint call invokes the registered probes (nothing is recorded if the event is not enabled); when an event is recorded its TP_fast_assign copies the device name and driver name strings of ar->ab->dev, buf_len (stored as u16), pktlog_checksum and a copy of buf_len bytes from buf into the trace record, and the text format prints the driver, device, size and checksum. It returns nothing and does not modify its arguments; buf must be readable for buf_len bytes when an event is recorded.

name: ath5k_hw_phy_init
prose: Initialises the ath5k PHY during reset, or performs a fast channel change (phy.c:3741-3952; the slice shows only the tail, the function is ath5k_hw_phy_init(ah, channel, mode, fast); it assumes the PHY is in warm reset). It returns -EINVAL if fast is set and channel->hw_value differs from the current channel's hw_value. When fast it requests the RF bus and polls up to 100 times (5 us apart) for the grant (-EIO if not granted), sets the channel with ath5k_hw_channel (error returned) and waits for the synthesizer. Next, for all callers, it sets TX power with ath5k_hw_txpower (error returned) and, on AR5212 for channels whose hw_value is not AR5K_MODE_11B, writes the OFDM timings (error returned) and, if the MAC revision is at least AR5424, sets the spur mitigation filter. If fast it then releases the RF bus request, starts noise-floor calibration (AGCCTL_NF) and returns 0. When not fast: for chips other than AR5210 it initialises RF gain and RF registers (each error returned) and sets or clears the 5111 B-mode bit in TXCFG; for AR5210 it only disables the PHY with delays; then it sets the channel (error returned), enables the PHY, waits for the synthesizer, runs a bounded ADC-test wait (no error reported), starts AGC and noise-floor calibration, starts I/Q calibration unless mode is AR5K_MODE_11B (setting ah->ah_iq_cal_needed accordingly), waits for AGC calibration to finish (a timeout is only logged, not returned), restores the antenna mode and returns 0.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers (name not in slice): the slice is the tail of ath5k_hw_phy_init (phy.c:3741-3952), fixed under that name; old prose said 'gain-calibration timeout only reported' which is right

name: ath5k_hw_setup_tx_queue
prose: Allocates and sets up an ath5k TX queue of the given type and returns its index (qcu.c:202). The queue number depends on the hardware: if cap_queues.q_tx_num is 2, DATA maps to AR5K_TX_QUEUE_ID_NOQCU_DATA, BEACON and CAB to AR5K_TX_QUEUE_ID_NOQCU_BEACON and any other type returns -EINVAL; otherwise DATA uses queue_info->tqi_subtype as the index (queue_info is dereferenced here, so it must be non-NULL for DATA, and the index is not range-checked), UAPSD, BEACON and CAB use their fixed ids, and other types return -EINVAL. It then zeroes ah->ah_txq[queue] and sets its tqi_type to queue_type (before any bounds check). If queue_info is non-NULL it sets queue_info->tqi_type = queue_type and calls ath5k_hw_set_tx_queueprops; a non-zero return (that function returns -EIO if the entry is AR5K_TX_QUEUE_INACTIVE) is returned unchanged, after the entry has already been cleared. Note ath5k_hw_set_tx_queueprops returns false (0) when the queue index is not below q_tx_num, so an out-of-range index does not produce an error here. Finally it enables the queue's bit in ah_txq_status and returns the queue index.
note: [rev:right] r15 (set_tx_queueprops error is -EIO passed through, not -EINVAL) right: qcu.c:163-164, 252-254; r2 (missing precondition that tqi_subtype is a valid index; indexing before validation) right: 228, 247; r1 (queue_info may be NULL) right

name: ath5k_hw_reset
prose: Main (re)initialisation function of the ath5k hardware (reset.c:1145-1380; the slice cut the head): ath5k_hw_reset(ah, op_mode, channel, fast, skip_pcu). Fast channel change is kept only when ah->ah_radio is AR5K_RF2413 or AR5K_RF5413, otherwise fast is cleared. On AR5212 it then writes the hardware (ath5k_hw_set_sleep_clock(ah, false)) before validating the channel. It returns -EINVAL, logging an error, if channel->hw_value is not 11A, 11G or 11B, is 11G on AR5210/AR5211, or is 11B on AR5210. If fast is set it calls ath5k_hw_phy_init(..., true): on success it returns 0 immediately; on failure it falls back to the full reset (the error is not returned). The full reset saves the frame sequence counters (all 10 DCU counters before AR5211, DCU 0 only after), the TSF on AR5211 and the LED/GPIO state, runs gain calibration on AR5212 with RF <= 5112 when !fast and RF banks exist, then calls ath5k_hw_nic_wakeup (error returned), enables PHY access, calls ath5k_hw_write_initvals(ah, mode, skip_pcu) (error returned), initialises the core clock, tweaks initvals, commits EEPROM settings, restores the saved sequence/TSF/LED/GPIO values, calls ath5k_hw_pcu_init(ah, op_mode), ath5k_hw_phy_init(..., false) (error returned) and ath5k_hw_init_queues (error returned), then initialises DMA. On AR5212 with ah_use_32khz_clock and op_mode other than AP it enables the 32 kHz sleep clock. Finally it disables beacons, resets the TSF and returns 0. op_mode is only used by ath5k_hw_pcu_init and the 32 kHz decision; it is not validated. On the failure returns after the hardware was touched, earlier register writes are not undone.
note: [rev:right] r15 (touches hardware before validating channel mode) right: reset.c:1169-1170 before 1172-1194; r1/r2 about op_mode: op_mode is used (1335, 1371) but never validated, so the claim that invalid op_mode returns -EINVAL is wrong in the old text; slice cut head, real body 1145-1380

name: ath5k_hw_commit_eeprom_settings
prose: Static helper in ath5k reset.c (975-1123; the slice shows only its tail) that programs PHY registers from the EEPROM data for the channel. It returns immediately for AR5210 (no EEPROM support). Otherwise it derives ee_mode from the channel, computes the CCK/OFDM power delta (using the scaled CCK delta for channel 14, 2484 MHz), and on PHY revisions from AR5212A writes AR5K_PHY_TX_PWR_ADJ (the negated gain delta and power delta for 11G channels, 0 otherwise) while on older revisions it stores the deltas in ah->ah_txpower for software scaling. It then sets the antenna switch for ee_mode, writes the noise-floor threshold, and, if the bandwidth mode is 40 MHz and the EEPROM version is at least 5.0, writes the turbo variants of switch settling, TX/RX attenuation, ADC/PGA desired size and TX/RX margin; otherwise it writes the normal variants (the TX/RX margin only for EEPROM version >= 4.1). It then writes the XPA delays, XLNA delay, the ANI threshold and the cyclic-power RSSI threshold (with the EEPROM false-detect backoff added if the channel has spur noise), for EEPROM version >= 4.0 the I/Q correction values and its enable bit, and for version >= 5.1 clears the heavy-clipping enable register. It returns nothing and takes no locks.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; the slice is the tail of ath5k_hw_commit_eeprom_settings (reset.c:975-1123), fixed under that name

name: SIMPLE_SHOW_STORE(ani_mode, ah->ani_state.ani_mode, ath5k_ani_init)
prose: Generated function ath5k_attr_show_ani_mode (from the SIMPLE_SHOW_STORE macro in ath5k sysfs.c) is the sysfs show callback for the 'ani_mode' attribute. It takes the ieee80211_hw from dev_get_drvdata(dev), ah = hw->priv, and returns sysfs_emit(buf, "%d\n", ah->ani_state.ani_mode), that is the current ANI mode as a decimal integer with a newline written into buf, and the number of characters written. It does not modify any state and takes no locks of its own; dev must have drvdata set to a valid ieee80211_hw whose priv is an ath5k_hw.

name: SIMPLE_SHOW_STORE(ani_mode, ah->ani_state.ani_mode, ath5k_ani_init)
prose: Generated function ath5k_attr_store_ani_mode (from the SIMPLE_SHOW_STORE macro in ath5k sysfs.c) is the sysfs store callback for the 'ani_mode' attribute. It takes ah = ((struct ieee80211_hw *)dev_get_drvdata(dev))->priv and parses buf with kstrtoint(buf, 10, &val); if parsing fails it returns that negative errno and does not call anything else. Otherwise it calls ath5k_ani_init(ah, val) (the value is passed on without any range check in this function) and returns count. The return value of ath5k_ani_init is not used.

name: ath6kl_htc_mbox_conn_service
prose: Connects an HTC service and configures its endpoint (ath6kl htc_mbox.c:2420; the slice cut the head). For the pseudo control service HTC_CTRL_RSVD_SVC it uses ENDPOINT_0 with max message size HTC_MAX_CTRL_MSG_LEN and sends nothing (conn_resp->resp_code is not written). Otherwise it takes a control tx buffer (-ENOMEM if none), builds and issues a connect-service message with ath6kl_htc_tx_issue (a non-zero status is returned), waits for the response control packet (-ENOMEM if none arrives), and returns -ENOMEM if the message id is wrong or the response is too short; it then copies the response status to conn_resp->resp_code and returns -ENOMEM if the status is not HTC_SERVICE_SUCCESS, otherwise it takes the assigned endpoint and max message size from the response. Common part: -ENOMEM if the endpoint is ENDPOINT_UNUSED or >= ENDPOINT_MAX or max_msg_sz is 0 (before anything is written); it then writes endpoint->eid and returns -ENOMEM if endpoint->svc_id is already set (conn_resp is not yet written at that point, though resp_code may have been). Otherwise it sets conn_resp->endpoint and ->len_max, marks the endpoint in use by setting svc_id, then max_txq_depth, len_max, ep_cb, the cred_dist fields, and tx_drop_packet_threshold (MAX_DEF_COOKIE_NUM / 3 for WMI_DATA_BK_SVC, else MAX_HI_COOKIE_NUM). If conn_req->max_rxmsg_sz is non-zero and larger than max_msg_sz it returns -ENOMEM at that point, leaving the endpoint marked in use with cred_per_msg and conn_flags not set; otherwise cred_per_msg is max_rxmsg_sz (or max_msg_sz) divided by target->tgt_cred_sz (which must be non-zero), raised to at least 1, and conn_flags is set from conn_req->flags and the function returns 0. On every path after the buffers were taken (success or failure) the tx control buffer is reclaimed and the rx packet, if any, is reset and returned; the function takes no locks itself. Many non-memory failures are reported as -ENOMEM.
note: [rev:right] r15 (on the max_rxmsg_sz-too-large path resp_code is also set) right: htc_mbox.c:2484 sets resp_code before the checks for non-reserved services, 2542-2545 returns after 2511-2512; r1 (omits return paths/side effects) right; slice cut head, real body 2420-2568

name: ath_ant_comb_scan
prose: Per-received-frame step of the ath9k antenna-diversity combining algorithm (antenna.c:721-849; the slice shows only its tail). It derives the current/main antenna from rs->rs_rssi_ctl[2], picks antcomb->ant_ratio/ant_ratio2 from whether the alt RSSI is at least low_rssi_thresh, accumulates packet count, RSSI totals and main/alt receive counters only when both main and alt RSSI are positive, updates the debug counters and runs ath_ant_short_scan_check. It returns immediately, changing nothing further, if fewer than ATH_ANT_DIV_COMB_MAX_PKTCOUNT packets have been counted (or rs->rs_moreaggr is set) and no short scan is due. Otherwise it computes the alt ratio and the main/alt average RSSI (when total_pkt_count is non-zero), reads the hardware configuration and increments antcomb->count; when count reaches ATH_ANT_DIV_COMB_MAX_COUNT it sets alt_good (calling ath_lnaconf_alt_good_scan if alt_ratio exceeds ant_ratio), resets count and sets scan and scan_not_start. When no scan is active it tries ath_ant_try_switch (if that returns true it skips to the end), and also skips to the end if alt_rssi_avg is below main_rssi_avg plus lna1_lna2_delta. Otherwise it either runs ath_ant_try_scan, or, if scan_not_start is set, either (alt not good) clears scan_not_start and sets main/alt LNA to the current main LNA's pairing, or selects the antenna from the quick scan and increments quick_scan_cnt. Every path that got past the early return reaches the end block, which applies fast diversity bias, writes the configuration with ath9k_hw_antdiv_comb_conf_set, updates debug stats, sets scan_start_time to jiffies and zeroes total_pkt_count, the main/alt RSSI totals and the main/alt receive counts.
note: [rev:n/a] only mechanical reviewers; real function ath_ant_comb_scan (antenna.c:721); the old prose said every path reaches the done label, but there is an early return at 768-770 before it

name: ar5008_hw_ani_control_new
prose: Applies one ANI (adaptive noise immunity) control command on AR5008-family hardware (ar5008_phy.c:953-1135) and returns a bool. It switches on (cmd & ah->ani_function). For ATH9K_ANI_OFDM_WEAK_SIGNAL_DETECTION it rewrites the SFCORR/SFCORR_LOW/SFCORR_EXT threshold fields (INI defaults when param is non-zero, fixed 'off' values otherwise) and sets or clears USE_SELF_CORR_LOW; for ATH9K_ANI_FIRSTEP_LEVEL it writes FIND_SIG firstep fields with level*2; for ATH9K_ANI_SPUR_IMMUNITY_LEVEL it writes the CYCPWR_THR1 fields with (level+1)*2 and (level+1)*2-1. In these three cases the registers are written every time; the logging of the change, the matching ast_ani_* statistic and the update of the stored aniState value (ofdmWeakSigDetect, firstepLevel, spurImmunityLevel) happen only when the new value differs from the stored one. ATH9K_ANI_MRC_CCK only executes WARN_ON(1). For any other masked value it logs 'invalid cmd' and returns false without touching registers or state. After the three supported cases and MRC_CCK it logs the ANI parameters and returns true.

name: ar9002_hw_init_cal
prose: Initial calibration for AR9002-family chips (ar9002_calib.c:845-935). Returns false, before PA/NF calibration and before touching cal_list, if on AR9271 ar9285_hw_cl_cal fails or on AR9285 rev 1.2+ ar9285_hw_clc fails, or, for other chips, if the AGC offset calibration does not clear AR_PHY_AGC_CONTROL_CAL within AH_WAIT_TIMEOUT. In that last case the AGC CAL bit stays set, and on AR_SREV_9280_20_OR_LATER chips AR_PHY_AGC_CONTROL_FLTR_CAL stays set and, unless AR_SREV_9287_11_OR_LATER, AR_PHY_ADC_CTL_OFF_PWDADC stays cleared (not restored). On those other chips the AGC calibration is started by setting AR_PHY_AGC_CONTROL_CAL; the FLTR_CAL set/clear and the OFF_PWDADC clear/set steps around it are done only on AR_SREV_9280_20_OR_LATER chips (OFF_PWDADC additionally not on 9287 1.1+), and on timeout-free completion they are reverted. On success it does PA calibration (ar9002_hw_pa_cal), loads the noise floor, starts NF calibration and sets cal_list, cal_list_last and cal_list_curr to NULL. For AR9100 or AR9160 1.0+ (and later) it then sets ah->supp_cals to IQ_MISMATCH_CAL, plus ADC_GAIN_CAL and ADC_DC_CAL from AR9160 1.0 on, minus ADC_GAIN_CAL on AR9287; it inserts the ADC-gain, ADC-DC and IQ calibration entries into cal_list for those that ar9002_hw_is_cal_supported accepts for the channel, points cal_list_curr at the first entry and resets it if the list is non-empty. Finally it clears ah->caldata->CalValid if ah->caldata is non-NULL and returns true.
note: [rev:right] r15 (FLTR_CAL set/cleared only on AR_SREV_9280_20_OR_LATER) right: ar9002_calib.c:856-862, 879-885; r1 (on timeout returns false without restoring ADC_CTL/FLTR_CAL) right: 870-877; slice cut head, real body 845-935

name: ar9002_hw_get_isr
prose: Reads and decodes the AR9002 interrupt status into *masked (ar9002_mac.c:32-209; masked must be non-NULL, sync_cause_p may be NULL). Non-AR9100: it reads the async cause and, only if the MAC IRQ bit is set and the RTC reports on, reads AR_ISR; it reads the sync cause masked with AR_INTR_SYNC_DEFAULT; it sets *masked = 0 and returns false if both are zero. AR9100: it sets *masked = 0 and reads AR_ISR. If isr is non-zero: for BCNMISC it decodes AR_ISR_S2 into TIM/DTIM/DTIMSYNC/CABEND/GTT/CST/TSFOOR bits (and, without the RAC capability, writes ISR_S2 back and clears BCNMISC from isr); with RAC capability isr is re-read from AR_ISR_RAC; if isr is 0xffffffff it sets *masked = 0 and returns false (the sync cause is then neither reported nor cleared); otherwise *masked = isr & ATH9K_INT_COMMON, plus ATH9K_INT_RX for RX bits, ATH9K_INT_TX for TX bits (reading S0/S1, writing them back without RAC, and setting ah->intr_txqs) and the BCNMISC-derived bits. On non-AR9100 chips with the generic-timer bit it reads ISR_S5, sets ah->intr_gen_timer_trigger and _thresh, adds GENTIMER and TIM_TIMER bits to *masked as applicable and writes S5 back without RAC. Without RAC it writes the remaining isr back to AR_ISR. On AR9100 it then returns true (even if isr was zero). On other chips, if the sync cause is non-zero it stores it in *sync_cause_p (if non-NULL), adds ATH9K_INT_FATAL for HOST1_FATAL, HOST1_PERR or RADM_CPL_TIMEOUT (the latter also pulses AR_RC_HOSTIF in AR_RC), clears the sync cause in AR_INTR_SYNC_CAUSE_CLR; it returns true.

name: ath_chanctx_set_next
prose: Switches the ath9k driver from sc->cur_chan to sc->next_chan (channel.c:1222-1315; the slice cut the head). It takes sc->chan_lock with spin_lock_bh and returns without changes, with the lock released, if sc->next_chan is NULL or if force is false and ath_chanctx_defer_switch(sc) returns true. (If cur_chan equals next_chan none of this is done.) Under the lock it then makes next_chan the current one (cur_chan = next_chan, stopped = false, next_chan = NULL), zeroes sched.offchannel_duration unless an offchannel change is pending, sets sched.state to ATH_CHANCTX_STATE_IDLE unless it is ATH_CHANCTX_STATE_FORCE_ACTIVE (in which case it is left alone), and releases the lock. If the chip is in full sleep or the current chandef differs from the new context's chandef it calls ath_set_channel (recording the channel switch time if measured) and does not wake the queues itself; otherwise it wakes the old context's queues if they were stopped. If send_ps is set it sends the power-save-off frame. In all cases that got this far it finally calls ath_offchannel_channel_change and ath_chanctx_event(ATH_CHANCTX_EVENT_SWITCH).

name: ath_chanctx_event
prose: State machine of the ath9k channel-context scheduler (channel.c:489-770; the slice cut the head). It sets avp from vif when vif is non-NULL (avp stays NULL otherwise and is dereferenced by BEACON_PREPARE and AUTHORIZED), takes sc->chan_lock with spin_lock_bh, handles ev and releases the lock at the single exit (there is no early return). BEACON_PREPARE: clears avp->offchannel_duration and any one-shot NoA; if avp->chanctx is not sc->cur_chan it stops there. Otherwise it may set next_chan to the offchannel context (offchannel_pending and not wait_switch) or to the next active context (state IDLE) and move to WAIT_FOR_BEACON (also from WAIT_FOR_TIMER, or when mgd_prepare_tx), clears a stale NoA when the next context is inactive and the state is not WAIT_FOR_BEACON, and if the state is not WAIT_FOR_BEACON it stops. When WAIT_FOR_BEACON it sets beacon_pending, next_tbtt, switch_start_time = next_tbtt + beacon_interval/4 and cur_chan->last_beacon, and then programs an offchannel NoA if next_chan is the offchannel context, else handles beacon-miss, sets a one-shot NoA when mgd_prepare_tx is set, else clears a wrapped noa_duration and starts a periodic NoA when the next context is active and no NoA is set or force_noa_update is set (clearing that flag). BEACON_SENT: nothing if no beacon is pending; else clears beacon_pending, and if mgd_prepare_tx is set clears it and completes sc->go_beacon, otherwise if the state is WAIT_FOR_BEACON moves to WAIT_FOR_TIMER and arms the timer for switch_start_time. TSF_TIMER: only in WAIT_FOR_TIMER: counts a beacon miss if not switch_after_beacon and a beacon is pending, moves to SWITCH and queues chanctx_work. BEACON_RECEIVED: only with ATH_OP_MULTI_CHANNEL and cur_chan not offchannel: clears beacon_pending and beacon_miss and, unless FORCE_ACTIVE, beacon_adjust is unset or tsf_val is 0, adjusts the TBTT delta, re-arms the timer and clears beacon_adjust. AUTHORIZED: only if the state is FORCE_ACTIVE and avp->chanctx == cur_chan: state becomes IDLE and processing continues as SWITCH. SWITCH: only with ATH_OP_MULTI_CHANNEL, state not FORCE_ACTIVE, cur_chan not switch_after_beacon and not offchannel: selects next_chan, state WAIT_FOR_TIMER, clears wait_switch, computes and arms the switch timer (half a beacon interval, three times that with extend_absence, minus the channel switch time), and sets beacon_pending and beacon_adjust. ENABLE_MULTICHANNEL: unless cur_chan is offchannel or switch_after_beacon, selects next_chan and queues chanctx_work. UNASSIGN: if cur_chan is still assigned, sets state IDLE only when next_chan exists, is unassigned and is not the offchannel context; if cur_chan is unassigned it sets state IDLE, and if the next context is assigned selects it as next_chan and queues chanctx_work. ASSIGN and CHANGE do nothing.

name: ath9k_calculate_summary_state

Otherwise it wakes the chip (ath9k_ps_wakeup), gathers iter_data with ath9k_calculate_iter_data, copies hw_macaddr into common->macaddr when has_hw_macaddr, copies the mask to common->bssidmask and applies it. If naps > 0 it enables tsfadjust and sets ah->opmode to AP; otherwise it disables tsfadjust, calls ath9k_beacon_ensure_primary_slot when beacons is set, and sets the opmode to MESH_POINT, OCB, ADHOC or STATION in that order of preference (nmeshes, nocbs, nadhocs, else station). name: ath_isr
prose: Hard interrupt handler of ath9k (real name ath_isr, main.c:488-603; the listed name ath9k_interrupt does not exist). dev is the ath_softc. It returns IRQ_NONE, before any hardware access, if sc->sc_ah is NULL or ATH_OP_INVALID is set (note ath9k_hw_common(ah) is computed before the NULL test), and IRQ_NONE if ath9k_hw_intrpend reports nothing pending. It then calls ath9k_hw_getisr, which reads and clears the hardware interrupt status (and the sync cause, which is passed to the debug code), and masks the status with ah->imask. If ATH_OP_HW_RESET is set it kills the hardware interrupts and returns IRQ_HANDLED (the ISR has already been read at that point). If no status bits remain it returns IRQ_NONE, after the hardware status was already read and cleared. Otherwise it ORs the status into sc->intrstatus under sc->intr_lock and marks sched if any SCHED_INTR bit (FATAL, BB_WATCHDOG, RXORN, RXEOL, RX/RXLP/RXHP, TX, BMISS, CST, GTT, TSFOOR, GENTIMER, MCI) is set. A FATAL status, or BB_WATCHDOG when HW_BB_WATCHDOG hang checks are configured, skips the per-bit handling. Otherwise: SWBA schedules the beacon tasklet; TXURN raises the TX trigger level; RXEOL clears RXEOL and RXORN from ah->imask and rewrites the interrupt mask; and, if the chip lacks autosleep capability, TIM_TIMER with sc->ps_idle set (WARN once) skips the rest, while without ps_idle it wakes the chip, clears RX abort and sets PS_WAIT_FOR_BEACON under sc->sc_pm_lock. At the end, if sched is set it kills all hardware interrupts and schedules sc->intr_tq, and it returns IRQ_HANDLED.

name: ath_mci_intr
prose: Handles an AR9003 MCI (Bluetooth coexistence) interrupt (real name ath_mci_intr(sc), mci.c:485-631; the interrupt and rx-message bitmasks are read inside with ar9003_mci_get_interrupt, not passed in; returns nothing). Otherwise: for RX_MSG_REQ_WAKE it sends MCI_REMOTE_RESET (16-byte payload) and MCI_SYS_WAKING, clears that bit in its local copy, resets the req-wake state and sets BT awake; for SYS_WAKING it sets BT awake if bt_state is sleep and the remote is not asleep; for SYS_SLEEPING it sets bt_state to MCI_BT_SLEEP if it was awake and the remote is not awake; for RX_INVALID_HDR or CONT_INFO_TIMEOUT it recovers RX and sets skip_gpm; for SCHD_INFO it records the last schedule message offset; for RX_MSG_GPM it loops while more GPM data is indicated: it returns immediately (without recycling or processing further messages) if ATH_OP_HW_RESET is set, stops the loop on an invalid offset, and for each message dispatches calibration messages to ath_mci_cal_msg and COEX_AGENT messages to ath_mci_msg unless skip_gpm is set, recycling every GPM it read (including skipped ones). It then clears the handled hardware-message bits from the local mask (logging CONT_INFO) and, if RX_INVALID_HDR or CONT_INFO_TIMEOUT was set, calls ath_mci_msg(sc, MCI_GPM_COEX_NOOP, NULL). Local copies of the masks are modified, not the hardware status.

name: wil_suspend_keep_radio_on
prose: Suspends a wil6210 device while keeping the radio on (pm.c:179-297; the slice cut the head). It tries down_write_trylock(&wil->mem_lock); on failure it increments suspend_stats.rejected_by_host and returns -EBUSY with no other change. Otherwise it sets wil_status_suspending (under the lock, then released) and stops all net queues. If TX is not idle, RX is not idle or WMI is not idle it increments suspend_stats.rejected_by_host, clears wil_status_suspending, wakes the connected net queues and returns -EBUSY; a failure of wmi_suspend takes the same reject path (-EBUSY) without incrementing that counter. It then, if NAPI is enabled, waits for RX to become idle until WIL_DATA_COMPLETION_TO_MS has passed; a timeout, or WMI events still pending afterwards, increments suspend_stats.r_on.failed_suspends and goes to the resume-after-failure path. It masks the IRQ, sets the PERST-reset-disable bit (BIT_USER_CLKS_RST_PWGD), and, if wil->platform_ops.suspend exists, calls it; on failure it increments failed_suspends, clears that bit, unmasks the IRQ and goes to the resume-after-failure path. On success it saves bus_request_kbps in bus_request_kbps_pre_suspend, sets the bus request to 0, sets wil_status_suspended, clears wil_status_suspending and returns 0. The resume-after-failure path sets wil_status_resuming, clears wil_status_suspending, calls wmi_resume and returns its error if it failed, or, if it succeeded, wakes the connected net queues and returns -EBUSY.
