name: __wil_tx_vring_tso
prose: Builds a TSO (TCP segmentation offload) descriptor chain for a GSO skb on a wil6210 TX ring (txrx.c:1725-2024; the slice shows only the second half). Early returns with no ring changes: -EINVAL if the ring's txdata is not enabled, -ENOMEM if the available descriptors are fewer than nr_frags + 1, -EINVAL if skb_shinfo(skb)->gso_type masked with TCPV4|TCPV6 is neither exactly TCPV4 nor exactly TCPV6 (for TCPv4 it first zeroes ip_hdr tot_len and check, for TCPv6 the payload_len, in the skb's headers) and -EINVAL if skb->ip_summed is not CHECKSUM_PARTIAL (the header zeroing has already happened by then). It then DMA-maps the headers (skb_tcp_all_headers bytes); a mapping failure returns the initial rc (-EINVAL) with nothing to undo. It then walks the linear remainder and the page fragments, mapping each piece in at most mss-sized chunks and filling descriptors, setting the first/mid/last TSO types and fragment counts; if the ring runs out of descriptors (descs_used reaches avail) it sets rc = -ENOMEM and jumps to mem_error; a mapping error or finishing with no data descriptor goes to mem_error with rc still -EINVAL. mem_error walks back over every descriptor used so far (including the header), copies it, sets TX_DMA_STATUS_DU, unmaps it and zeroes its context, then returns rc; vring->swhead is not changed and no skb reference is taken. On success it sets the last data descriptor and the total descriptor count in the header descriptor, stores skb_get(skb) in the context of the last descriptor, updates idle statistics, executes write barriers, advances swhead by descs_used, records the tx latency timestamp (or clears skb->cb), writes vring->swhead to the hardware tail and returns 0.

name: b43_radio_2057_rcal
prose: Runs the radio 0x2057 resistor calibration (RCAL) on a b43 N-PHY device and returns the result as a u8 (phy_n.c:810-919). It saves twelve PHY RF-control registers and six RF override registers, zeroes the twelve, writes 0x07ff (OVER0, OVER1, OVER3, OVER4) or 0x007f (OVER5, OVER6) to the overrides, then does radio-revision specific setup: rev 5 clears bit 1 of REV7_RF_CTL_OVER3, sets bit 0 of R2057_IQTEST_SEL_PU and sets bit 0 and clears bit 1 of R2057v7_IQTEST_SEL_PU2; rev 9 sets OVER3 and MISC_REG3 bit 1, saves R2057_IQTEST_SEL_PU and writes 0x11 to it; rev 14 saves IQTEST_SEL_PU and PU2, sets MISC_REG3 and OVER3 bit 1 and writes 0x2 to PU2 and 0x1 to PU. It then sets the RCAL enable bit (0x1), the start bit (0x2), and clears the start bit, and waits (up to 1 s, polling every 100 us) for bit 0 of R2057_RCAL_STATUS (mask 1, value 1) to become set. On timeout it logs an error and returns 0 immediately, with the enable bit still set, the start bit cleared, the saved PHY registers not restored and the revision-specific changes left in place. On success it reads R2057_RCAL_STATUS & 0x3E, clears the enable bit, restores the six override and then the twelve control registers, and by radio rev: revs 0-4 and 6 update R2057_TEMPSENSE_CONFIG (mask ~0x3C) and R2057_BANDGAP_RCAL_TRIM (mask ~0xF0, value shifted left by 2); rev 5 clears bit 0 of R2057_IPA2G_CASCONV_CORE0 and bit 1 of PU2 and does not restore R2057_IQTEST_SEL_PU (it stays with bit 0 set); rev 9 restores IQTEST_SEL_PU; rev 14 restores both; other revisions get no radio writes. It returns the masked status value (an even number in 0 to 62).

name: get_integer
prose: Static helper in b43 sysfs.c (lines 23-35) that parses a decimal integer from a sysfs write buffer. It returns -EINVAL if count is 0. Otherwise it copies at most min(count, 10) bytes of buf into a zero-initialised 11-byte local buffer (so at most 10 bytes of buf are read) and returns simple_strtol(tmp, NULL, 10) converted to int. simple_strtol accepts an optional leading '-', stops at the first non-digit and yields 0 when there are no leading digits; the long result is not saturated or range-checked before the conversion to int, so values outside the int range are truncated by the conversion, and a legitimately negative parsed value cannot be told apart from the -EINVAL error. It takes no locks and has no side effects.

name: b43_generate_txhdr
prose: Builds the b43 hardware TX header for one 802.11 fragment (xmit.c:235-568; the slice cut the head). It zeroes *txhdr, picks the main rate (from ieee80211_get_tx_rate, default 1 Mb CCK) and fallback rate, and sets phy_rate, mac_frame_ctl, tx_receiver and the fallback duration (the original duration_id if the rates are equal or duration_id is 0 or has bit 0x8000, else a computed duration). If info->control.hw_key is set it takes dev->key[hw_key_idx] (the index is only checked with B43_WARN_ON, not enforced); if that key has no keyconf it returns -ENOKEY at once, leaving the header only partly filled and the fragment not to be transmitted. Otherwise it adds the ICV length to the PLCP length, sets the key index/algorithm in mac_ctl, and copies either the TKIP phase-1 key plus three IV bytes or min(iv_len, sizeof iv) IV bytes into txhdr->iv. It then writes the main and fallback PLCP headers (layout by firmware header format 598/351/410), fallback and PHY rate flags, the channel radio code, the PHY control word (encoding, short preamble, antenna) and MAC control bits (ACK, hardware sequence, first fragment, 5 GHz). It overwrites info->control.rates[0].count with the long (and sets LONGFRAME, also for RTS/CTS use) or short retry limit. For RTS/CTS or CTS-to-self protection it generates the RTS or CTS frame into the header with its PLCP headers, fallback rate, duration and rate flags (phy_ctl1 words only for RTS and LP/N/HT PHYs). It stores the cookie by header format, fills phy_ctl1 and phy_ctl1_fb for LP, N and HT PHYs, stores the mac_ctl, phy_ctl and extra frame type words and returns 0.

name: b43legacy_radio_interference_mitigation_disable
prose: Turns off one b43legacy interference-mitigation mode (radio.c:1217-1313; static, returns nothing). Saved values are fetched from phy->interfstack by (register type, offset) key through _stack_restore, not in push order; if no entry matches, _stack_restore executes B43legacy_BUG_ON(1) and returns 0. NONWLAN with phy->rev != 1: clears bit 0x0800 of PHY 0x042B and sets bit 0x4000 of B43legacy_PHY_G_CRS; nothing is restored. NONWLAN with rev == 1: restores PHY 0x0078 (looked up as a PHY-register entry, while the enable function saved 0x0078 as a radio-register entry, so that lookup finds no match and reaches the B43legacy_BUG_ON), recalculates the NRSSI threshold, restores 0x0406, clears 0x0800 in 0x042B, clears bit 11 of PHY_RADIO_BITFIELD only if dev->bad_frames_preempt is false, sets 0x4000 in G_CRS, and restores 0x04A0, 0x04A1, 0x04A2, 0x04A8, 0x04AB, 0x04A7, 0x04A3, 0x04A9, 0x0493, 0x04AA, 0x04AC. MANUALWLAN: returns without any change if bit 0x0800 of PHY 0x0033 is clear; otherwise sets phy->aci_enable = false and restores PHY_RADIO_BITFIELD, G_CRS, 0x0033, 0x04A3, 0x04A9, 0x0493, 0x04AA, 0x04AC, 0x04A0, 0x04A7, then 0x04C0 and 0x04C1 (rev >= 2) or 0x0406, then 0x04A1, 0x04AB, 0x04A8, then for rev 2 0x04AD and 0x04AE, for rev >= 3 0x04AD, 0x0415, 0x0416, 0x0417 and ILT 0x1A02 and 0x1A03, then 0x04A2, 0x04A8 again, 0x042B and 0x048C; it clears bit 0x800 of the ucode flags in shared memory if it was set and calls b43legacy_calc_nrssi_slope. Any other mode value runs B43legacy_BUG_ON(1).

name: b43legacy_radio_interference_mitigation_enable
prose: Turns on one b43legacy interference-mitigation mode (radio.c:971-1215; static, returns nothing). Registers it changes are saved on phy->interfstack (keyed by register type and offset) before being overwritten. NONWLAN with phy->rev != 1: sets bit 0x0800 of PHY 0x042B and clears bit 0x4000 of B43legacy_PHY_G_CRS, saving nothing. NONWLAN with rev == 1: saves radio register 0x0078 and rewrites it with a bit-flipped adjusted value, recalculates the NRSSI threshold, saves and sets PHY 0x0406 to 0x7E28, sets 0x0800 in 0x042B and 0x1000 in PHY_RADIO_BITFIELD, saves and rewrites 0x04A0, 0x04A1, 0x04A2, 0x04A8, 0x04AB (low bits replaced under a 0xC0C0 mask) and saves and sets 0x04A7, 0x04A3, 0x04A9, 0x0493, 0x04AA, 0x04AC to fixed values. MANUALWLAN: returns with no change if bit 0x0800 of PHY 0x0033 is already set; otherwise sets phy->aci_enable = true, saves a list of PHY registers (including 0x048A, 0x042B, 0x048C and, by PHY revision, 0x0406 or 0x04C0/0x04C1, and 0x04AD/0x04AE or 0x04AD/0x0415-0x0417 with ILT 0x1A02/0x1A03 for rev 2 or >= 3), then rewrites many PHY registers with fixed values and masked fields (revision-dependent for 0x0406/0x04C0/0x04C1 and the 0x048A/0x0415-0x0417 group); for rev < 3 it sets bit 0x800 of the shared-memory ucode flags if it was clear, for rev >= 2 sets 0x0800 in 0x042B, modifies 0x048C, for rev 2 modifies 0x04AE/0x04AD and for rev >= 6 writes ILT 0x1A03 and 0x1A02 and clears the low byte-masked 0x04AD; finally it calls b43legacy_calc_nrssi_slope. Any other mode value runs B43legacy_BUG_ON(1).

name: brcmf_cfg80211_start_ap
prose: cfg80211 start_ap callback of brcmfmac (cfg80211.c:5120-5367; the slice cut the head). It reads the current regulatory (11d) setting into ifp->vif->is_11d. If settings->ssid is NULL or empty it takes the SSID from the beacon head and returns -EINVAL if there is no SSID IE or it is longer than IEEE80211_MAX_SSID_LEN. For a non-MBSS interface it then disables MPC and ARP/ND offload and sets regulatory, beacon interval, DTIM period, (for AP role, when ifidx is 0 or neither RSDB nor MCHAN is enabled) BRCMF_C_DOWN and the INFRA mode, any failure going to exit; for an MBSS interface it instead returns -EINVAL (after WARN_ON) if 11d is supported and differs from the vif's setting. For the AP role it sets the mbss iovar (result ignored when the feature is enabled), AP mode, the chanspec (non-MBSS), brings the interface up, optionally configures PSK and SAE offload, calls brcmf_parse_configure_security, reconfigures WEP, sets the SSID and the closednet iovar; for the P2P GO role it sets the chanspec, security, the bsscfg ssid and enables the bss; each of these failures goes to exit with the negative error. For any other role it only executes WARN_ON(1) and continues. It then configures the management IEs, sets BRCMF_VIF_STATUS_AP_CREATED in sme_state and enables the carrier. At exit, if err is non-zero and the interface is not MBSS, it re-enables MPC and ARP/ND offload; it returns err. err starts as -EPERM and is overwritten by the results of the calls made, so for a non-MBSS interface with an unsupported role (after INFRA succeeded) it returns 0 with the AP_CREATED bit set and the carrier enabled, while for an MBSS interface with an unsupported role it returns -EPERM with those bits set too. On error returns before the AP_CREATED bit is set, the bit is not set; previous firmware changes are not rolled back.

name: brcms_c_update_beacon_hw
prose: Installs a beacon into the brcmsmac hardware beacon templates (main.c:7281-7328; static, returns nothing). If both MCMD_BCN0VLD and MCMD_BCN1VLD are set in the maccommand register it first writes MI_BCNTPL to macintstatus (clearing a previous status). If wlc->beacon_template_virgin is true it clears that flag, writes the beacon into both templates (brcms_c_beacon_write with bcn0 and bcn1 true), sets MCMD_BCN0VLD in maccommand (it does not clear MCMD_BCN1VLD) and returns. Otherwise it re-reads maccommand: if both valid bits are still set it sets MI_BCNTPL in wlc->defmacintmask and returns without writing a template. Otherwise, if MCMD_BCN0VLD is clear it writes only template 0 and sets MCMD_BCN0VLD; else, if MCMD_BCN1VLD is clear it writes only template 1 and sets MCMD_BCN1VLD. Each brcms_c_beacon_write call computes the PLCP for the beacon's tx rate, updates the beacon PHY tx control, writes the beacon (rounded up to 4 bytes, at most BCN_TMPL_LEN) and its length to the selected template(s), and writes the TIM position and DTIM period (or the beacon end and 0 when tim_offset is 0) to shared memory.

name: wlc_phy_cal_txiqlo_nphy
prose: Runs (or continues, in multi-phase mode) the N-PHY TX IQ/LO calibration (phy_n.c:25624-25984; the slice cut the head). It stays in carrier search, for PHY revs >= 4 saves and clears pi->phyhang_avoid, saves the RFSEQ gain table entries, sets the calibration gains per core, runs the TX calibration radio and PHY setup, loads the LOFT/IQ-imbalance ladders for the channel bandwidth (only for PHY revs below 6 and not rev 5 with iPA on 2 GHz) and then plays a tone (wlc_phy_tx_tone_nphy) or, when the multi-phase state is past TXPHASE0, samples. If the tone cannot be started its error is kept in bcmerror and the calibration loop is skipped. Otherwise it loads start coefficients (multi-phase coefficients, the previous best coefficients when !fullcal and they are valid, otherwise defaults with fullcal forced true), selects the full or recal command list by PHY revision, determines which commands to run (all, or the next pi->mphase_txcal_numcmds in multi-phase mode starting at mphase_txcal_cmdidx), and for each command writes it, waits up to 20000 us for the busy bits to clear, and copies the resulting coefficients; if the hardware is still busy it executes WARN and returns -EIO immediately, without the cleanup below (carrier search stays suspended, phyhang_avoid stays cleared on rev >= 4, the RFSEQ gain table and the radio/phy setup are not restored, playback is not stopped). After the loop it updates mphase_txcal_cmdidx (wrapping to 0), and when not in multi-phase mode or at the last phase stores the final coefficients in pi->nphy_txiqlocal_bestc with nphy_txiqlocal_coeffsvalid set and nphy_txiqlocal_chanspec updated, otherwise stores them in pi->mphase_txcal_bestcoeffs; then it stops playback. In all paths other than the -EIO return it runs the PHY and radio cleanup, restores the RFSEQ gain table, applies the tx-iq workaround on PHY rev < 2 when appropriate, restores phyhang_avoid on rev >= 4, leaves carrier search and returns bcmerror (0 or the tone error).

name: wlc_phy_rc_sweep_nphy
prose: Static helper of brcmsmac (phy_n.c:27065-27302; the slice cut the head) that calibrates the RX low-pass-filter RC value of an N-PHY radio 2056 core and returns the result as a u8. If pi->pubpi.phy_rev is 7 or greater it returns 0 at once without touching any register. Otherwise it selects tone, bandwidth and target power ratio by whether the channel is 40 MHz, picks the RX/TX radio register offsets from core_idx and loopback_type, saves the TXLPF RCCAL and RXLPF RCCAL_HPC radio registers, the DC-bypass bit (phy 0x48 bit 8), the RX strain-filter registers 0x267-0x270 and the rfctrl override, aux and rssi registers (0xe7, 0xec, 0xf8, 0xfa, and 0x7a or 0x7d), and programs fixed values for the sweep. It then does a binary-style search of the RXLPF_RCCAL_LPC value starting at 128+16: on the first iteration it plays a reference tone (wlc_phy_tx_tone_nphy, result ignored) and measures its I/Q power, then plays the target-bandwidth tone, and each iteration measures I/Q power, forms a power ratio and steps the value up or down, finishing with a final comparison between the last two candidates. The best value is reset to 138 (40 MHz) or 140 (20 MHz) if it lies outside 135..140 (40 MHz) or 137..142 (20 MHz); it is not clamped to the nearest limit. That value is written to RADIO_2056_RX_RXLPF_RCCAL_LPC. It then stops playback, restores all saved radio and PHY registers, sets pi->nphy_anarxlpf_adjusted to false and returns best_rccal_val - 0x80.

name: qm_shr16
prose: Arithmetic shift helper in brcmsmac phy_qmath.c (lines 147-150): it returns qm_shl16(op, -shift). qm_shl16 clamps its shift argument to the range -15..15 and, for a positive shift, doubles the value that many times with saturating 16-bit addition (qm_add16 limits to the s16 range), while for a negative shift it does an arithmetic right shift. So qm_shr16 with a positive shift arithmetically right-shifts op (by at most 15), with a negative shift it left-shifts op with saturation (by at most 15), and with 0 it returns op. If shift is INT_MIN the negation -shift overflows (undefined behaviour in C), which a caller must avoid. It has no side effects.

name: ipw2100_pci_init_one
prose: PCI probe of the ipw2100 driver (real name ipw2100_pci_init_one, ipw2100.c:6125-6322; the listed name ipw2100_pci_probe_one does not exist). It returns -ENODEV, with nothing to undo, if BAR 0 is not a memory resource. It maps BAR 0 (failure: -EIO through the fail label), allocates the net_device with ipw2100_alloc_device (failure: -ENOMEM via fail), enables the PCI device (on failure it frees the libipw device, unmaps and returns the error directly), sets bus master and drvdata, sets a 32-bit DMA mask, requests the regions, adjusts the PCI config retry-timeout byte, checks the adapter is present (-ENODEV), disables interrupts, allocates and initialises the queues (-ENOMEM on allocation failure), requests the shared IRQ, calls ipw2100_up and ipw2100_wdev_init (registered = 1 afterwards) and register_netdev (registered = 2); each failure returns its errno through fail. It then locks priv->action_mutex, creates the sysfs group and, if the RF-kill bit is clear, enables the adapter (failure: stop the adapter, -EIO) and starts a scan; it sets STATUS_INITIALIZED, unlocks the mutex and returns err (0 when everything succeeded). Failures after the mutex was taken go through fail_unlock, which unlocks it. The fail label, if dev is non-NULL, unregisters the netdev when registered >= 2, unregisters the wiphy and frees the band channels when registered is non-zero, stops the adapter, disables interrupts, frees the IRQ if dev->irq is set, kills works, frees the queues, removes the sysfs group and frees the libipw device; regardless of dev it then unmaps the I/O memory, calls pci_release_regions and pci_disable_device (also when the regions were never requested or the device never enabled, for example after a failed ioremap or device allocation) and returns the error.

name: il3945_tx_skb
prose: Queues one frame for transmission on the iwl3945 device (3945-mac.c:444-635; the slice cut the head). It takes il->lock (spin_lock_irqsave) at entry. If RF-kill is active or the frame's tx rate is IL_INVALID_RATE it releases the lock and returns -1 (drop_unlock). Otherwise it releases the lock, looks up the station id (-1 and no enqueue if it is IL_INVALID_STATION), for QoS data frames extracts the TID (-1 if it is >= MAX_TID_COUNT) and returns -1 if the queue space is below high_mark; none of these drops frees the skb. It then retakes il->lock, stores skb in txq->skbs[q->write_ptr], builds the Tx command in the command buffer slot (copies the MAC header, builds crypto, basic and rate fields), DMA-maps the command + MAC header and, when there is a payload, the payload; a mapping failure goes to drop_unlock, releasing the lock and returning -1 without advancing q->write_ptr (txq->skbs[write_ptr] still holds the skb and a mapping that already succeeded is not unmapped here). On success it attaches the buffers to the TFD, records the mapping in the command meta, sets need_update (or wait_write_ptr for fragments with more-fragments set), updates statistics, advances q->write_ptr, updates the device write pointer, releases the lock and, if the queue space is then below high_mark and il->mac80211_registered is set, updates the write pointer again under the lock when wait_write_ptr was set and stops the queue with il_stop_queue; it returns 0.

name: il3945_rs_get_rate
prose: Rate-control callback of iwl3945 that picks the TX rate for one frame (3945-rs.c:604-800; returns nothing; the slice cut the head). rs_sta (il_sta) must be non-NULL: if rs_sta->il is NULL the code only sets its local il_sta = NULL and keeps using rs_sta. It derives the supported-rate mask from the station and band (shifted for 5 GHz) and the user's maximum rate index, starts from idx = min(rs_sta->last_txrate_idx & 0xffff, RATE_COUNT_3945 - 1), and under rs_sta->lock lowers idx to rs_sta->start_rate if that is lower than idx and in the mask (clearing start_rate to RATE_INVALID whenever it was set) and then to the user's maximum rate if that is lower and in the mask. If the window of the resulting idx has fewer than RATE_MIN_FAILURE_TH failures and fewer than RATE_MIN_SUCCESS_TH successes it releases the lock, sets that window's average_tpt to IL_INVALID_VALUE and goes to the common exit with idx unchanged from that point (it may therefore already be start_rate or the user maximum, not necessarily last_txrate_idx). Otherwise it reads the window's throughput and those of the adjacent lower and higher rates allowed by the mask (higher rate disallowed above the user maximum), releases the lock, decides to decrease, keep or increase based on success_ratio against RATE_DECREASE_TH / RATE_INCREASE_TH and the throughput comparisons, cancels a decrease if the success ratio exceeds RATE_HIGH_TH or the throughput exceeds 100 * expected_tpt[low], and moves idx to the lower or higher rate when one exists. At the exit, for 5 GHz it clamps idx up to IL_FIRST_OFDM_RATE (WARN_ON_ONCE), stores idx in rs_sta->last_txrate_idx and sets info->control.rates[0].idx to idx - IL_FIRST_OFDM_RATE; for 2.4 GHz it stores idx in both; it sets rates[0].count to 1. The lock is released before the exit on both paths.

name: __il4965_up
prose: Brings the iwl4965 device up (4965-mac.c:5503-5603; static; the slice cut the head; the caller provides any required locking). It returns -EIO, allocating nothing, if S_EXIT_PENDING is set or if il->ucode_data_backup.v_addr or il->ucode_data.v_addr is NULL. It allocates the broadcast station (a non-zero error is returned after il_dealloc_bcast_stations), calls il4965_prepare_card_hw and returns -EIO after deallocating the broadcast stations if il->hw_ready is false. If the CSR_GP_CNTRL HW_RF_KILL_SW bit is clear it sets S_RFKILL, tells wiphy the hardware rfkill state is true, deallocates the broadcast stations, enables the rfkill interrupt and returns 0. Otherwise it clears S_RFKILL, clears CSR_INT, sets il->cmd_queue to IL_DEFAULT_CMD_QUEUE_NUM, calls il4965_hw_nic_init (a non-zero error is returned after deallocating the broadcast stations), clears the rfkill handshake bits, clears CSR_INT again and enables interrupts, and copies il->ucode_data into il->ucode_data_backup. It then loops up to MAX_HW_RESTARTS times calling il->ops->load_ucode; a load_ucode error is logged and the loop continues with the next attempt (it is not returned immediately); on the first success it calls il4965_nic_start (which returns nothing) and returns 0, leaving the broadcast station allocated. If every attempt fails it sets S_EXIT_PENDING, calls __il4965_down, clears S_EXIT_PENDING and returns -EIO.

name: il4965_rs_move_legacy_other
prose: Chooses the next rate-scaling search table while on a legacy (non-HT) rate (real name il4965_rs_move_legacy_other, 4965-rs.c:1252-1366; the listed name il4965_rs_move_legacy_to_other does not exist; static, returns int). It first sets tbl->action (the active table's action) to IL_LEGACY_SWITCH_SISO and remembers it as start_action, then loops over the actions starting there; each loop pass increments lq_sta->action_counter. ANTENNA1/ANTENNA2: skipped if the number of TX chains is too small or the window success_ratio is at least IL_RS_GOOD_RATIO; otherwise it copies the table into search_tbl, toggles the antenna in search_tbl and, if that succeeds, marks update_search_tbl_counter, sets the expected throughput table and finishes. SISO: copies the table, clears is_SGI and calls il4965_rs_switch_to_siso; on success (return 0) it resets lq_sta->action_counter to 0 and finishes. MIMO2_AB/AC/BC: copies the table, clears is_SGI, sets the antenna pair, skips if that pair is not valid, else calls il4965_rs_switch_to_mimo2 and on success resets action_counter to 0 and finishes. An unsuccessful action advances tbl->action by one (wrapping from MIMO2_BC to ANTENNA1) and the loop ends when it returns to start_action. When finishing after a success it sets lq_sta->search_better_tbl = 1, advances tbl->action by one with the same wrap, and sets search_tbl->action to that value only on the antenna path. If no action succeeded it sets search_tbl->lq_type = LQ_NONE (tbl->action is back at SISO and search_better_tbl is unchanged). It returns 0 on every path; search_tbl may have been overwritten by the attempts either way.

name: il4965_rs_rate_scale_perform
prose: Core of the iwl4965 rate-scaling algorithm for one transmitted frame (real name il4965_rs_rate_scale_perform, 4965-rs.c:1719-2109; static, returns nothing; the listed name il4965_rs_rate_scale does not exist). It returns at once, changing nothing, if the frame is not a data frame or has NO_ACK. It records lq_sta->supp_rates, updates the traffic-load record and sets lq_sta->is_agg from the TID's aggregation state, selects the active table (or the other one while search_better_tbl is set), sets lq_sta->is_green, and computes the usable rate mask. It returns early, without updating last_txrate_idx, if the current rate index is not in the mask (after logging; if a search was in progress it marks the search table LQ_NONE, clears search_better_tbl and reprograms the uCode with the active table's current rate) or if tbl->expected_tpt is NULL. If lq_sta->max_rate_idx is set and lower than the current index it forces that index and goes to the table update. If the window of the current rate has too little history (fewer than RATE_MIN_FAILURE_TH failures and fewer than RATE_MIN_SUCCESS_TH successes) it marks its average_tpt invalid, calls il4965_rs_stay_in_table and goes to the exit. Otherwise, if a better modulation mode was being searched it compares window throughput with lq_sta->last_tpt: better means the search table becomes active (and enable_counter is set for HT modes); otherwise the search table is marked LQ_NONE, the active table's rate is restored and the uCode table is updated; either way search_better_tbl is cleared and the later search is skipped. If not searching, it compares the throughput of the current and adjacent rates and success ratio to decide to decrease, keep or increase the rate (with a sanity check that cancels a decrease when success is good) and updates the uCode rate table if the index changed. After lq_update it calls il4965_rs_stay_in_table, and, unless the rate changed, a search just finished or staying in the table is set, and the window has counted packets, it saves last_tpt and calls the legacy, SISO or MIMO2 'move_to_other' helper; if that selects a search table it clears that table's history and sends a new link-quality command. It may then set the stay-in-table state (legacy without HT after enough actions, or HT after all actions, also starting aggregation for a high-throughput TID). At the exit it stores the current rate in tbl->current_rate and the index in lq_sta->last_txrate_idx. It acquires no locks.

name: iwl_dbgfs_ucode_general_stats_read
prose: debugfs read handler of iwlwifi dvm (real name iwl_dbgfs_ucode_general_stats_read, debugfs.c:1296-1414; the slice shows only its tail, which is not a separate function named iwl_dbgfs_statistics_read_tail). It does not send a statistics request itself.

name: iwl_op_mode_dvm_start
prose: op_mode start callback of iwlwifi's dvm driver (main.c:1233-1524; the slice cut the head). It allocates the ieee80211_hw with iwl_alloc_all (NULL: returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM), nothing to free), stores trans, dev, cfg and fw in priv, selects priv->lib from trans->mac_cfg->device_family (an unsupported family leaves it NULL; WARN_ON then returns ERR_PTR(-ENODEV) after only ieee80211_free_hw). It fills the transport configuration (no-reclaim command list, rx buffer size from the amsdu_size parameter, command groups, cmd FIFO, cb data offset, command queue and key limits depending on the PAN ucode flag, rx MPDU command and header size), calls iwl_trans_op_mode_enter, sets up locks, starts the hardware (iwl_trans_start_hw), reads the EEPROM (iwl_read_eeprom), stops the device, parses the NVM data (-ENOMEM if NULL), checks the NVM version, initialises the hw params, copies the MAC address (a second address with the last byte incremented if more than one is available), sets hw params, adjusts the command queue if the EEPROM disables PAN, initialises queue maps, calls iwl_init_drv, iwl_setup_deferred_work, sets up rx handlers, power and thermal throttling, firmware version string and contexts, calls iwlagn_mac_setup_register and registers debugfs; on success it returns op_mode. On failure it returns ERR_PTR(err) with unwinding by label: iwlagn_mac_setup_register failure runs out_destroy_workqueue (iwl_tt_exit, cancel deferred work, destroy the workqueue) then the labels below; iwl_setup_deferred_work failure starts at out_uninit_drv (iwl_uninit_drv); iwl_init_drv, iwl_nvm_check_version and iwl_eeprom_init_hw_params failures start at out_free_eeprom (kfree priv->nvm_data then priv->eeprom_blob); an iwl_parse_eeprom_data failure starts at out_free_eeprom_blob (frees only the blob); iwl_trans_start_hw and iwl_read_eeprom failures go to out_leave_trans and so skip freeing nvm_data and eeprom_blob (neither is allocated at that point, but the blob pointer may be set by a partial iwl_read_eeprom); every path from there on calls iwl_trans_op_mode_leave and ieee80211_free_hw.

name: rs_move_mimo2_to_other
prose: Chooses the next rate-scaling search table while on a MIMO2 rate in iwlwifi dvm (rs.c:1716-1879; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). First it may force the active table's action to IWL_MIMO2_SWITCH_SISO_A: for a HIGH or CONTINUOUS BT traffic load, for LOW load when the action is SISO_B or SISO_C, when iwl_tx_ant_restriction is IWL_ANT_OK_SINGLE and the action is not a SISO one, and when bt_full_concurrent is set and the action is not a SISO one. It then loops from that action (start_action); every pass increments lq_sta->action_counter. ANTENNA1/ANTENNA2: skipped if tx_chains_num <= 2 or the window success_ratio is at least IWL_RS_GOOD_RATIO; otherwise copies the table to search_tbl and calls rs_toggle_antenna, which returns non-zero on success (then update_search_tbl_counter is set and the loop finishes). SISO_A/B/C: copies the table, sets ant_type ANT_A/B/C, skips an invalid antenna, and calls rs_switch_to_siso, finishing if it returns 0. GI: skipped if the peer does not support short GI at the current width; otherwise copies the table with is_SGI toggled, sets the expected throughput table, skips if the table already uses SGI and last_tpt / 100 reaches the expected throughput, else sets the new current_rate, marks update_search_tbl_counter and finishes. MIMO3_ABC: copies the table, sets ANT_ABC, skips an invalid antenna and calls rs_switch_to_mimo3, finishing if it returns 0 (rs_switch_to_mimo2 is not called here). An unsuccessful action advances tbl->action with wrap from MIMO3_ABC to ANTENNA1 and the loop ends when it is back at start_action, after which search_tbl->lq_type = LQ_NONE. On success it sets lq_sta->search_better_tbl = 1, advances tbl->action with the same wrap and, only if the antenna or GI path was taken, copies the new action to search_tbl->action.

name: rs_rate_scale_perform
prose: Core of the iwlwifi dvm rate-scaling algorithm for one transmitted frame (real name rs_rate_scale_perform, dvm/rs.c:2157-2591; static, returns nothing; the listed name rs_rate_scale does not exist). It returns at once, changing nothing, for non-data frames and NO_ACK frames. It records supp_rates, updates the traffic-load record and lq_sta->is_agg, selects the active table (or the other one while search_better_tbl is set), sets lq_sta->is_green and computes the usable rate mask. It returns early, without updating last_txrate_idx, if the current index is not in the mask (after reverting an in-progress search by setting the search table to LQ_NONE, clearing search_better_tbl and reprogramming the active table's rate) or if tbl->expected_tpt is NULL. A user max rate lower than the current index forces that index and goes to the table update. With too little history in the current window it invalidates the average throughput, calls rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, false) and goes to the exit. When a search is in progress and iwl_tx_ant_restriction is IWL_ANT_OK_MULTI it adopts the search table if its throughput beats last_tpt (setting enable_counter for HT modes) or reverts to the active table and marks the uCode update needed, clears search_better_tbl and skips mode switching. Otherwise it looks at the throughputs of the adjacent rates to choose decrease, keep or increase, forces a decrease for HT modes when HT is disabled and for MIMO modes when the antenna restriction is not MULTI, applies BT-coex handling (with high BT traffic on MIMO it may force a decrease and call rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, true), skipping the rate change) and updates last_bt_traffic. It programs the uCode rate table if the index changed, calls rs_stay_in_table when the restriction is MULTI, and, if the rate did not change, no search just ended, the table is not pinned and the window has counted packets, saves last_tpt, calls the legacy, SISO, MIMO2 or MIMO3 move-to-other helper and, if a search table was chosen, clears its history and sends a new link-quality command. It may then set the stay-in-table state and start TID aggregation. At the exit it stores the current rate in tbl->current_rate and the index in lq_sta->last_txrate_idx. It acquires no locks.

name: iwlagn_rxon_connect
prose: Applies an associated RXON configuration for one iwlwifi dvm context (rxon.c:440-507; static; the caller holds priv->mutex; the slice cut the head). For the BSS context it first sends the RXON timing command and returns its error if it fails. It then calls iwlagn_update_qos (result not checked), and for an AP interface sends the beacon with iwlagn_update_beacon, returning its error on failure. All of these failures leave ctx->active unchanged. It then clears priv->start_calib and sends the RXON command from ctx->staging; if that fails it returns the error with ctx->active unchanged but priv->start_calib already cleared. On success it copies ctx->staging into ctx->active, sends the beacon for an IBSS (ADHOC) interface (a failure is only logged), calls iwl_init_sensitivity, and calls iwl_set_tx_power(priv, priv->tx_power_next, true); if that fails it returns the error although the active configuration and start_calib were already updated. It returns 0 when everything succeeded.

name: iwl_advance_tt_handler
prose: Advances the thermal-throttling state machine for a temperature reading (dvm/tt.c:335-456; static; returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It saves old_state = tt->state and scans the (IWL_TI_STATE_MAX - 1) transaction entries of the table for old_state, taking the first with tt_low <= temp <= tt_high; under CONFIG_IWLWIFI_DEBUG a match also logs a large temperature rise and records temp in tt_previous_temp (nothing is recorded when no entry matches or when the option is off), and if that entry's next_state differs from old_state it sets tt->state to it and marks the state changed. Whether or not anything changed, it then calls timer_delete_sync on ct_kill_waiting_tm. If the state changed: for a new state of IWL_TI_1 or higher it sets tt->tt_power_mode to IWL_POWER_INDEX_5 and either clears the HT channel-mode and protection RXON flags in every context's staging RXON (if HT is disabled) or calls iwl_set_rxon_ht(priv, &priv->current_ht_config); for a lower state (IWL_TI_0) it only calls iwl_set_rxon_ht (tt_power_mode is not set). It then takes priv->mutex, clears STATUS_CT_KILL if old_state was IWL_TI_CT_KILL, and if the new state is not IWL_TI_CT_KILL and iwl_power_update_mode(priv, true) fails it logs an error, restores STATUS_CT_KILL if old_state was CT_KILL and restores tt->state to old_state. Otherwise it logs the new state and, on entering CT_KILL from another state, with force true sets STATUS_CT_KILL and calls iwl_perform_ct_kill_task(priv, true), with force false sets tt->state back to old_state and calls iwl_prepare_ct_kill_task; on leaving CT_KILL it calls iwl_perform_ct_kill_task(priv, false). It releases the mutex before returning.

name: iwl_parse_tlv_firmware
prose: Parses a TLV-format iwlwifi firmware image into drv->fw, *pieces and *capa (iwl-drv.c:788-1465; the slice is only a fragment from its NUM_OF_CPU case, the enclosing function being iwl_parse_tlv_firmware(drv, ucode_raw, pieces, capa, usniffer_images)). It returns -EINVAL if the image is shorter than the header or the magic is not IWL_TLV_UCODE_MAGIC (logged). It then records the ucode version, the human-readable string and builds drv->fw.fw_version, and walks the TLVs while at least a TLV header remains: -EINVAL if a TLV's length (or its 4-byte aligned length) exceeds the remaining data, otherwise it dispatches on the TLV type: the instruction/data/boot/sec images and wowlan/usniffer pieces are stored in *pieces, scalar capability TLVs (probe length, PAN, flags, API/capability bitmaps, log pointers and sizes, calibration sizes, PHY SKU, scan channels, station/link/beacon counts, debug addresses) are copied into capa or drv->fw after checking the expected size (a wrong size jumps to invalid_tlv_len, which logs and returns -EINVAL, as do tlv_error cases such as bad DEF_CALIB or out-of-range station/link counts); the NUM_OF_CPU TLV marks the images dual-CPU when it equals 2 and returns -EINVAL for a value outside 1..2; debug destination/config/trigger, memory-segment, IML, recovery info, command-version, PHY integration version, current-PC and PNVM TLVs are copied with allocations whose failure returns -ENOMEM (a duplicate PHY integration string or existing PNVM data is ignored); unknown TLV types are only logged. After the loop it returns -EINVAL if a usniffer image was requested but is not present (and the unified usniffer capability is not set) or if bytes remain after parsing, otherwise 0. Output structures may be partly filled when it returns an error.

name: iwl_mld_rx_monitor_no_data
prose: Handles an RX_NO_DATA notification from the iwlwifi MLD firmware for monitor mode (real name iwl_mld_rx_monitor_no_data(mld, napi, pkt, queue), mld/rx.c:2034-2147; returns nothing; the listed name iwl_mld_rx_no_data does not exist). It returns without doing anything if mld->fw_status.in_hw_restart is set, or (via IWL_FW_CHECK, which logs) if the packet payload is smaller than struct iwl_rx_no_data_ver_3. Otherwise it extracts the channel and chain energies from the descriptor's rssi field, builds a phy_data (phy info words, GP2 on-air rise time, rate_n_flags converted from the v2/v3 rate, with_data false, a copy of rx_vec), and allocates a 128-byte skb with alloc_skb(GFP_ATOMIC); on failure it logs and returns, with nothing delivered. It sets RX_FLAG_NO_PSDU, adds RX_FLAG_FAILED_PLCP_CRC when the descriptor's error field is not RX_NO_DATA_INFO_ERR_NONE, sets zero_length_psdu_type to SOUNDING for NDP, NOT_CAPTURED for MU/TB unmatched and VENDOR otherwise, sets the band (5 GHz if channel > 14, else 2.4 GHz) and frequency, calls iwl_mld_rx_fill_status with link id -1 and a NULL header, sets the mac header at skb->len, and overrides rx_status->nss from rx_vec for VHT, HE and EHT modulation (for other formats nss is left as filled). It then calls ieee80211_rx_napi under rcu_read_lock, which takes ownership of the skb.

name: iwl_mvm_pre_channel_switch
prose: Prepares for a channel switch announcement on a vif in iwlwifi MVM (mvm/mac80211.c:5502-5620; static; the caller holds mvm->mutex; the slice cut the head). It clears mvmvif->csa_failed and csa_blocks_tx and, per vif type: AP: returns -EBUSY (WARN_ONCE) if another CSA is active on mvm->csa_vif, -EBUSY if mvm->csa_tx_blocked_vif is set, then assigns mvm->csa_vif = vif, returns -EBUSY (WARN_ONCE) if mvmvif->csa_countdown is still set (csa_vif stays assigned), records csa_target_freq and, only when chsw->block_tx is set and the hardware has HANDLES_QUIET_CSA, sets csa_blocks_tx, the STOP_AP_CSA state bit on the vif's txq and stops the other stations' TX queues. Station: sets csa_blocks_tx = chsw->block_tx first; if the firmware supports the CHANNEL_SWITCH_ERROR_NOTIF flow it breaks out and skips the rest; otherwise returns -EBUSY if not associated or no DTIM period, may schedule csa_work, runs iwl_mvm_old_pre_chan_sw_sta (its error returned) or iwl_mvm_schedule_client_csa depending on the CHANNEL_SWITCH_CMD capability, and then sets csa_count and clears csa_misbehave. name: rs_rate_scale_perform
prose: Core of the iwlwifi MVM rate-scaling algorithm for one station (real body mvm/rs.c:2052-2332; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It sets lq_sta->is_agg from mvmsta->agg_tids and selects the active table (or the search table while search_better_tbl is set); if aggregation changed it resets the expected throughput table and clears that table's windows. If the current rate index is not in the supported mask it logs an error and returns; before returning, if a search was in progress, it marks the search table's rate LQ_NONE, clears search_better_tbl and reprograms the uCode rate table from the active table. It also returns if tbl->expected_tpt is NULL. With too little history in the current window (fewer than the failure and success thresholds) it invalidates the window's average_tpt, calls rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, false) and returns without changing the rate or turning on aggregation. If a search was in progress it adopts the search table when its throughput exceeds lq_sta->last_tpt, otherwise it reverts to the active table's rate and marks the uCode table for update; it then clears search_better_tbl, marks the search done and skips mode switching. Otherwise it picks an action with rs_get_rate_action (downscale to the adjacent lower rate, upscale to the higher, or stay, in which case rs_tpc_perform may request an update when staying in the column), but if the rate is MIMO and BT coex forbids MIMO it forces a search with rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, true). If the rate changed it stores the new index, optionally tweaks the table, sets the A-MSDU length and sends the new rate table. It then calls rs_stay_in_table(lq_sta, false); if the rate did not change, no search just ended, the state is RS_STATE_SEARCH_CYCLE_STARTED and the window has counted packets it saves last_tpt and selects the next column to try (switching to it and setting search_better_tbl and programming the search table, or moving to RS_STATE_SEARCH_CYCLE_ENDED when no column is left). If ndp is false it calls rs_tl_turn_on_agg, and at the end, when a search is done and the state is SEARCH_CYCLE_ENDED, it sets the stay-in-table state.

name: iwl_mvm_pass_packet_to_mac80211
prose: Static helper in iwlwifi MVM rx.c (lines 45-94; the slice cut the head) that builds an skb from a received frame and passes it to mac80211. With hdrlen = ieee80211_hdrlen(hdr->frame_control) it calls skb_reserve(skb, hdrlen & 3) to align the later IP header. It then recomputes the number of bytes to copy: len if len <= skb_tailroom(skb) (after the reserve), otherwise hdrlen + crypt_len + 8. It appends that many bytes from hdr to the skb with skb_put_data (the caller must ensure the skb has room for them and that hdr is readable for them). If fraglen = len - copied bytes is non-zero it steals the rxb page with rxb_steal_page and adds it to the skb as fragment 0 at the offset of the rest of the frame within the page, with length fraglen and the rxb truesize. Finally it calls ieee80211_rx_napi(mvm->hw, sta, skb, napi), which takes ownership of the skb. It returns nothing.

name: iwl_trans_pcie_removal_wk
prose: Work function (pcie/gen1_2/trans.c:2182-2267; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head) that removes an inaccessible iwlwifi PCIe device. wk is the work_struct embedded in a heap-allocated struct iwl_trans_pcie_removal (pdev, mode, integrated); the caller has taken a module reference and a pci_dev reference on pdev. Otherwise it emits a KOBJ_CHANGE uevent 'EVENT=INACCESSIBLE'. If mode is IWL_RESET_MODE_PROD_RESET it looks for the companion Bluetooth device: for a non-integrated device, function 1 of the same slot via pci_get_slot when pdev is function 0 (otherwise it logs 'Unexpected function'); for an integrated device by scanning all PCI devices on the same bus for one matching a list of Intel device ids; if found it logs, stops and removes it and drops its reference. name: iwl_trans_pcie_dump_data
prose: Collects a firmware-error dump for the iwlwifi PCIe transport into a newly allocated buffer (pcie/gen1_2/trans.c:3530-3681; the slice cut the head). It returns NULL if dump_mask is 0. It computes dump_rbs = (iwl_trans_is_fw_error(trans) and the device is not mq_rx_supported and the RB bit is set in dump_mask), then sizes the dump: the header; the host-command queue (TXCMD bit set and the command queue exists); the FW monitor (via iwl_trans_get_fw_monitor_len); CSR registers; FH registers (the gen2 or gen1 range); when dump_rbs is set, the closed receive buffers of rxq[0] (counted under rxq[0].lock with spin_lock_bh); and on gen2 with the PAGING bit set, each paging block. name: iwl_trans_pcie_alloc
prose: Allocates and initialises the iwlwifi PCIe transport (pcie/gen1_2/trans.c:3747-3947; static; the slice cut the head). It allocates the iwl_trans (failure: ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM)), initialises the command wait queue and allocates the TX command pool (error: out_free_trans). It sets the TFD parameters for gen2 or gen1, the supported DMA mask and max skb frags, allocates the per-CPU TSO header pages (-ENOMEM: out_free_txcmd_pool) and computes the byte-count table size; only for gen2 devices does it create the byte-count DMA pool (-ENOMEM: out_free_tso). It allocates a dummy NAPI netdev (-ENOMEM: out_free_tso), initialises locks and wait queues, and creates the 'rb_allocator' workqueue (-ENOMEM: out_free_ndev). It may disable PCIe L0s/L1/CLKPM, sets a DMA mask of the TFD address size, falling back to 32 bits, and fails through out_no_pci if neither works; it writes the PCI retry-timeout config byte, disables interrupts, computes hw_rev_step, calls iwl_pcie_set_interrupt_capa and allocates the invalid-TX command buffer (error: out_no_pci). It then either sets up MSI-X handlers (error: out_no_pci) or allocates the ICT table and requests a shared threaded IRQ (ICT allocation error: out_no_pci; IRQ error: out_free_ict). On success it initialises debugfs monitor state and the debug TLV data and returns trans. The error labels run in a fall-through chain: out_free_ict frees the ICT, out_no_pci destroys the workqueue, out_free_ndev frees the NAPI netdev, out_free_tso frees the per-CPU pages, out_free_txcmd_pool destroys the command pool and out_free_trans frees the transport, then ERR_PTR(ret) is returned; the invalid-TX command buffer is not freed explicitly by these labels.

name: capability_store

name: mwifiex_cfg80211_authenticate
prose: cfg80211 authenticate callback of mwifiex (real name mwifiex_cfg80211_authenticate, cfg80211.c:4265-4425; the slice shows only its tail, which is not mwifiex_cfg80211_mgmt_tx). It returns -EFAULT if the interface role is UAP, -EINVAL if the wdev type is not STATION, and -EBUSY if an auth is pending (HOST_MLME_AUTH_PENDING) while the current auth algorithm is not SAE. It registers the host-MLME management-frame mask with the firmware on first use, maps req->auth_type to an auth algorithm (open, shared key, FT, LEAP or SAE; any other type returns -EOPNOTSUPP), and, if no auth is pending, sets a remain-on-channel on the BSS channel (failure: -EFAULT; success: stores a random cookie and the channel in priv->roc_cfg). It then fills the skb's tx_info (bss_num, bss_type, pkt_len), reserves and pushes the packet length, tx_control and pkt_type, builds an authentication management frame (da and bssid from req->bss->bssid, sa from priv->curr_addr, broadcast addr4); when auth_data_len >= 4 it takes the transaction number and status code from the first four bytes of auth_data only for SAE and copies auth_data + 4 (auth_data_len - 4 bytes) into the variable part, then sets auth_alg, auth_transaction (default 1) and status_code (default 0), and appends req->ie (ie_len bytes) after the auth data. It sets priv->auth_flag = HOST_MLME_AUTH_PENDING and priv->auth_alg, sets the skb priority to WMM_HIGHEST_PRIORITY, timestamps it, passes it to mwifiex_queue_tx_pkt (which takes ownership) and returns 0.

name: mwifiex_send_rgpower_table
prose: Parses a regulatory-power table text and sends it to the firmware as host commands (real name mwifiex_send_rgpower_table(priv, data, size), sta_cmd.c:1509-1597; the slice shows only the second part of it). It allocates a zeroed mwifiex_ds_misc_cmd and a copy of data (-ENOMEM if either allocation fails; both are freed automatically on return). It loops while the position is inside the copy: it first calls mwifiex_rgpower_table_advance_to_content, which skips whitespace, NULs and '#' comment lines (it returns -EINVAL if a comment has no terminating newline), and that error is returned. When it sees '}' while inside a command block it sets hostcmd->len from the 16-bit little-endian value at cmd[2], sends it with mwifiex_send_cmd (a failure is returned), clears the command buffer and starts over. Outside a block it looks for '=' and then '{' to start a block, and returns -EINVAL ('syntax error in hostcmd') if either is missing. Inside a block it splits the line on spaces and converts each token with kstrtou8(token, 16) into the command buffer; a hex parse error is returned, and -ENOMEM is returned if the command would exceed MWIFIEX_SIZE_OF_CMD_BUFFER. When the whole text has been consumed it returns 0 (a block that was opened but not closed with '}' is not sent).

name: mwifiex_usb_aggr_tx_data
prose: Decides whether to aggregate, send or defer a TX data packet on a mwifiex USB data port (usb.c:951-1121; static; the slice cut the head; the caller must not free skb afterwards, it is either queued, attached to a URB context, or, on some failure paths, completed). It computes the alignment padding and sets decision flags: if tx_param says another packet is queued it either flushes the pending aggregate and postcopies the current packet (when it would exceed the maximum size), or precopies the current packet and flushes the aggregate if the next packet would not fit (size or packet-count limits); if it is the last packet it precopies it and flushes the aggregate if packets are pending (sending the current packet separately first if it does not fit), otherwise sends it immediately. A null power-management packet is redirected to be sent separately (flushing the aggregate first when it is non-empty). Precopy: the skb is appended to port->tx_aggr.aggr_list (aggr_len, aggr_num updated) and, unless the aggregate is being flushed, the hold timer is armed or its timeout extended. Flushing: mwifiex_usb_prepare_tx_aggr_skb stops the timer, builds one aggregate skb from the list, completing each queued skb; if that allocation fails it completes all queued skbs with -1 and resets aggr_num and aggr_len (its -EBUSY result is not returned by this function); on success the aggregate is sent with mwifiex_usb_construct_send_urb, and if that returns -1 the aggregate is completed with error -1 (the return value is otherwise ignored). Sending the current packet alone: if an aggregate was just sent and the pending data-URB count has reached MWIFIEX_TX_DATA_URB it sets port->block_status, recomputes adapter->data_sent and instead postcopies the packet; otherwise it writes the interface header and returns directly the result of mwifiex_usb_construct_send_urb, which is -EINPROGRESS on submission, -ENOSR if the pending count reached the maximum, or -1 if usb_submit_urb failed (in which case the URB counters and tx_data_ix are rolled back). Postcopy: the packet is appended to the aggregation list and the hold timer is started if not set. In all other cases the function returns -EINPROGRESS.

name: mt7603_mac_fill_rx
prose: Parses the RX descriptor of a received frame for the mt7603 driver into the mt76_rx_status stored in skb->cb (mt7603/mac.c:504-684; the slice cut the head). It zeroes the status, then reads descriptor words 0, 1 and 2 unconditionally and fills wcid, band, frequency (when the channel index is within the band's channel count), FCS error, MIC error, ICV-error (monitor only) and decrypted/IV-stripped flags. It returns -EINVAL for a max-length error or when the band has no channel table. It then walks the optional descriptor groups, returning -EINVAL whenever, after advancing, the descriptor pointer is at or beyond skb->len: group 4 (skips 4 words), group 1 (IV bytes copied for decrypted CCMP/TKIP/GCMP frames; may request CCMP header insertion), group 2 (timestamp, A-MPDU reference handling), and group 3 (it reads words 0 and 3 of the group before the bounds check; maps the PHY mode: CCK/OFDM rate lookup, HT MCS above 15 or any other mode returns -EINVAL; short GI, LDPC, STBC, rate index, chains, chain signals, 40 MHz bandwidth). A missing group 3 also returns -EINVAL. On -EINVAL skb->data is not pulled, though the status may be partly filled. Otherwise it pulls the descriptor (plus 2 padding bytes when requested) from the skb, inserts the CCMP header if requested, and returns 0 immediately if there is no wcid or the frame is not QoS data; for QoS data frames it also sets aggr (unicast and not QoS-null), qos_ctl and seqno, and returns 0.

name: mt7615_mcu_set_protection
prose: Sends an HT/ERP protection configuration to the mt7615 MCU (real name mt7615_mcu_set_protection(phy, vif, ht_mode, use_cts_prot), mt7615/mcu.c:2568-2613; the slice shows only the second part). It builds a request with prot_idx 2 and band set to whether phy is not the primary phy of the device. For the HT operation protection mode NONMEMBER or NONHT_MIXED it sets prot_mm, prot_gf and prot_bw40; for 20 MHZ protection it sets prot_bw40; it also sets prot_gf when the NON_GF_STA_PRSNT bit is set. If use_cts_prot is true it sets prot_erp_mask to the bit of the vif's omac index (or HW_BSSID_0 when the index is above HW_BSSID_MAX). It returns the result of mt76_mcu_send_msg(MCU_EXT_CMD(PROTECT_CTRL), &req, sizeof(req), true), i.e. 0 on success or a negative errno from the MCU send. The other protection fields stay false/0.

name: mt7915_register_device
prose: Registers an mt7915 device (init.c:1219-1297; the slice cut the head). It initialises work items, lists, the reset wait queue and dump mutex, determines dbdc_support and calls mt7915_alloc_ext_phy; if that returns an error it returns it at once with nothing to undo. It then calls mt7915_init_hardware (error: free_phy2), mt7915_init_wiphy, mt76_register_device (error: stop_hw), mt7915_thermal_init (error: unreg_dev) and, if a second phy exists, mt7915_register_ext_phy (error: unreg_thermal). It queues dev->init_work, sets dev->recovery.hw_init_done = true and calls mt7915_init_debugfs and mt7915_coredump_register; a failure of either goes to unreg_ext_phy and returns that error. The unwinding falls through unreg_ext_phy (unregister the external phy if any), unreg_thermal, unreg_dev (mt76_unregister_device), stop_hw (mt7915_stop_hardware) and free_phy2 (ieee80211_free_hw of the second phy if still present). The unwinding does not cancel the already queued init_work and does not reset recovery.hw_init_done. On success it returns 0.

name: mt7915_mac_sta_event
prose: Handles a station lifecycle event for the mt7915 driver (mt7915/main.c:834-877; the slice cut the head). ASSOC: calls mt7915_mcu_add_sta(CONN_STATE_CONNECT, true) and returns its error if it fails; otherwise writes 0xa0 to bits 7:0 of the WTBL LMAC register for the station (mt76_rmw_field), calls mt7915_mcu_add_rate_ctrl(false) and returns its error if it fails, else sets MT_WCID_TX_INFO_SET in msta->wcid.tx_info, msta->wcid.sta = 1, msta->wcid.sta_disabled = 0 and returns 0. name: mt7921_pci_probe
prose: PCI probe of the mt7921 driver (mt7921/pci.c:233-399; the slice cut the head). It returns the error directly, with nothing to release, if pcim_enable_device, pcim_iomap_regions or pci_alloc_irq_vectors(1, 1) fails. It sets the memory-space bit and bus mastering, sets a 32-bit DMA mask (error: err_free_pci_vec), optionally disables ASPM, gets the mac80211 ops (NULL: -ENOMEM via err_free_pci_vec) and allocates the mt76 device (-ENOMEM via err_free_pci_vec). From there it sets drvdata and device fields, initialises MMIO and the IRQ tasklet and makes a devm copy of the bus ops with the mt7921 register accessors (-ENOMEM: err_free_dev). It then calls mt792xe_mcu_fw_pmctrl and __mt792xe_mcu_drv_pmctrl, reads the chip id and revision, calls mt792x_wfsys_reset (each error goes to err_free_dev), masks the interrupts, requests the shared IRQ with devm_request_irq (error: err_free_dev), calls mt7921_dma_init and mt7921_register_device (errors: err_free_irq), enables wakeup if the OF node has 'wakeup-source', and returns 0. The error labels fall through: err_free_irq calls devm_free_irq, err_free_dev calls mt76_free_device, err_free_pci_vec calls pci_free_irq_vectors; the other resources (device enable, BAR mapping, the bus-ops copy) are device-managed. name: mt7921s_wfsys_reset
prose: Resets the WiFi subsystem of an mt7921 SDIO device (sdio_mac.c:35-77; the slice cut the head). It returns 0 immediately without touching the hardware if dev->mt76.bus_hung is set. Otherwise it calls mt7921s_mcu_drv_pmctrl, claims the SDIO host, clears WF_WHOLE_PATH_RSTB in MCR_WHCR, sleeps 50 ms, clears WF_SDIO_WF_PATH_RSTB (this bit is cleared and not set again in this function), sleeps 1-2 ms, sets WF_WHOLE_PATH_RSTB again and polls MCR_WHCR for WF_RST_DONE (50 ms interval, 2 s timeout; a timeout is ignored). It releases the SDIO host, clears MT76_STATE_MCU_RUNNING in dev->mphy.state and then calls mt7921s_mcu_drv_pmctrl, clears MT_WIFI_PATCH_DL_STATE in MT_CONN_STATUS, calls mt7921s_mcu_fw_pmctrl and finally mt7921s_mcu_drv_pmctrl again (the results of these power-control calls are ignored). It returns 0 in every case.

name: mt7921s_mac_reset
prose: Performs a MAC reset of an mt7921 SDIO device (sdio_mac.c:147-199; the slice cut the head). It frees pending TX skbs and runs mt7921s_host_reset (its result is ignored). If dev->mt76.bus_hung is then set it returns 0 without doing the rest. Otherwise it schedules all TX queues, disables the tx worker, sets MT76_MCU_RESET, wakes the MCU wait queue, purges the MCU response queue, waits up to 5 s for the SDIO TX queues to drain, disables the txrx, status, net and stat workers, disables the SDIO IRQ once and runs mt7921s_wfsys_reset, then re-enables the four SDIO workers, clears dev->fw_assert and MT76_MCU_RESET and enables the SDIO IRQ. It then calls mt7921_run_firmware, mt7921_mcu_set_eeprom, mt7921_mac_init and __mt7921_start in order, stopping at the first non-zero result; it re-enables the tx worker and returns that result (0 on success). The tx worker is re-enabled on every path that disabled it.

name: mt7925_load_clc
prose: Loads the country-listing (CLC) data from the mt7925 firmware file into dev->phy.clc[] (real name mt7925_load_clc(dev, fw_name), mt7925/mcu.c:732-819; the slice starts at request_firmware). It sets dev->phy.clc_chan_conf = 0xff, and returns 0 without doing anything more if mt7925_disable_clc is set or the device is USB. For MMIO devices it reads the hardware encapsulation type from the EEPROM (an error is returned). It requests the firmware (error returned); an invalid firmware (NULL data or smaller than the trailer) gives -EINVAL. It walks the trailer's regions backward from the trailer, accumulating offsets, and returns -EINVAL if a region extends past the file; the first region that has the NON_DL feature and type FW_TYPE_CLC supplies the CLC base. If none is found it returns 0 without loading. Otherwise it iterates the CLC entries in that region: it stops if an entry's idx is beyond the phy->clc array, skips entries already present (after a chip reset), skips entries whose header encapsulation type (or the BE-control table's type) differs from hw_encap, and copies each remaining entry with devm_kmemdup (failure: -ENOMEM). It releases the firmware on every path after it was obtained and returns 0 on success.

name: get_own_mld_idx
prose: Static helper in mt7996/main.c (lines 144-164) that picks a free own-MLD index from a 64-bit occupancy mask (bit set = in use). It has no side effects. With group_mld true it searches bits 0 to 15 for the lowest clear bit; with group_mld false it searches bits 16 to 63 for the lowest clear bit and, only if none is clear there, bits 0 to 15. It returns the zero-based index of the lowest clear bit found in the range it searched, or -EINVAL if no clear bit exists in the searched range(s) (for group_mld true: bits 0-15 all set; for false: all 64 bits set).

name: mt7996_ampdu_action
prose: mac80211 ampdu_action callback of mt7996 (mt7996/main.c:1466-1526; static; the slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL, before taking dev->mt76.mutex, if sta->txq[params->tid] is NULL. Otherwise it takes dev->mt76.mutex and switches on params->action: RX_START calls mt76_rx_aggr_start on msta->deflink.wcid and then mt7996_mcu_add_rx_ba(..., true), RX_STOP calls mt76_rx_aggr_stop and mt7996_mcu_add_rx_ba(..., false); TX_OPERATIONAL sets mtxq->aggr = true and send_bar = false and calls mt7996_mcu_add_tx_ba(..., true); TX_STOP_FLUSH and TX_STOP_FLUSH_CONT clear mtxq->aggr and the tid bit of msta->deflink.wcid.ampdu_state and call mt7996_mcu_add_tx_ba(..., false); TX_STOP_CONT does the same and then also calls ieee80211_stop_tx_ba_cb_irqsafe(vif, sta->addr, tid) whatever the firmware call returned; TX_START sets the tid bit in ampdu_state and returns IEEE80211_AMPDU_TX_START_IMMEDIATE. name: handle_rcvd_ntwrk_info
prose: Work handler of the wilc1000 driver (hif.c:538-571; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head) that reports a received scan result frame. msg is the host_if_msg containing the work item; msg->body.net_info holds the received management frame (mgmt, frame_len) and the scan request is taken from msg->vif->hif_drv->usr_scan_req. If the frame is a probe response or a beacon it sets the offset of the information elements for that type; any other frame skips the reporting. It takes the IE pointer through the u.beacon.variable member for both frame types (the offsets only coincide because both layouts start with the same fixed fields) and the IE length as frame_len minus the type's offset; a non-positive length skips the reporting. Otherwise it finds the DS-parameter-set IE and, if present with a non-zero length, stores its channel byte in rcvd_info->ch, and, if scan_req->scan_result is non-NULL, calls it with SCAN_EVENT_NETWORK_FOUND, rcvd_info and scan_req->priv. On every path it frees the mgmt buffer and the msg.

name: qtnf_parse_variable_mac_info
prose: Parses the TLV part of a qtnfmac 'get MAC info' response (real name qtnf_parse_variable_mac_info(mac, resp, tlv_buf_size), commands.c:1007-1214; static; the slice starts at its beginning of the regulatory handling). It returns -E2BIG (after WARN_ON) if resp->n_reg_rules exceeds NL80211_MAX_SUPP_REG_RULES, allocates mac->rd for the rules (-ENOMEM on failure; it is not freed on later error returns here), copies the rule count and alpha2 and maps the DFS region. It then walks the TLVs: interface-limit records require an existing interface-combination array (-EINVAL if none), are counted but not stored past macinfo.n_if_comb (a warning), must have a length matching their n_limits (-EINVAL) and are converted into an allocated limits array (-ENOMEM on failure); extended-capability and mask TLVs must be at most 255 bytes (-EINVAL) and are remembered by pointer; WoWLAN capability TLVs shorter than the header or with a mismatched length return -EINVAL, an empty one is skipped, and otherwise the old WoWLAN info is freed and re-parsed; regulatory-rule TLVs return -EINVAL if there are more than resp->n_reg_rules, if the length is wrong, and otherwise fill mac->rd->reg_rules[rule_idx++]; unknown TLV types only log. After the walk it returns -EINVAL if the TLV buffer was malformed, if the parsed combination count differs from macinfo.n_if_comb, if the ext-capability and mask lengths differ, or if rule_idx differs from n_reg_rules. If extended capabilities are present it duplicates them and the mask (-ENOMEM on failure, freeing the first copy), frees the previous ones with qtnf_mac_ext_caps_free and stores the new copies in macinfo; it returns 0 on success.

name: rt2x00lib_antenna_diversity_sample
prose: Evaluates the RSSI samples gathered while sampling antennas (rt2x00link.c:67-106; static, returns nothing; the slice cut the head). It takes sample_current = the averaged RSSI of the antenna in use if the link has received frames (link.qual.rx_success non-zero), otherwise DEFAULT_RSSI, and sample_other = link.ant.rssi_history if it is non-zero, otherwise DEFAULT_RSSI. It copies the active antenna setup, clears ANTENNA_MODE_SAMPLE in link.ant.flags and, if sample_current >= sample_other, stores sample_current in rssi_history and returns without changing the antenna configuration. Otherwise it leaves rssi_history unchanged, picks the antenna opposite to the active RX antenna (ANTENNA_B if active.rx is ANTENNA_A, else ANTENNA_A), sets new_ant.rx to it when ANTENNA_RX_DIVERSITY is set and new_ant.tx to the same antenna (derived from active.rx) when ANTENNA_TX_DIVERSITY is set, and calls rt2x00lib_config_antenna with the new setup.

name: rt73usb_config_shared_key
prose: Configures a shared (group) key in an RT73 USB device (rt73usb.c:256-351; static; the slice cut the head). For SET_KEY it computes mask = 0xf << crypto->bssidx, reads SEC_CSR0 and keeps only the masked bits, and returns -ENOSPC (no register written, key unchanged) if that value is non-zero and equal to the whole mask. Otherwise it adds to key->hw_key_idx the value ffz() of the masked value (0 if the masked value is 0), which is the index of the lowest zero bit of the masked value and so may lie outside the BSS's four-bit window when bssidx is not 0. It writes the key and the TX/RX MIC from crypto to SHARED_KEY_ENTRY(key->hw_key_idx), stores the cipher in a 3-bit field of SEC_CSR1 if hw_key_idx < 8 or of SEC_CSR5 otherwise, and sets IEEE80211_KEY_FLAG_GENERATE_IV in key->flags. For both SET_KEY and DISABLE_KEY (and for any other command) it then reads SEC_CSR0, sets bit (1 << key->hw_key_idx) for SET_KEY or clears it for DISABLE_KEY, writes SEC_CSR0 back and returns 0. The shifts are only well defined if the resulting hw_key_idx is within the register widths (callers must keep it in range).
note: [rev:n/a] fixed-unreviewed; read rt73usb.c:256-351; the earlier reviewer notes about ffz outside the BSS mask and out-of-range indices were right and are now stated

name: rt73usb_config_pairwise_key
prose: Configures a pairwise key in an RT73 USB device (rt73usb.c:353-455; static; the slice cut the head). For SET_KEY it reads SEC_CSR2; if it is non-zero and all ones it sets key->hw_key_idx to 32 and reads SEC_CSR3; if that is also non-zero and all ones it returns -ENOSPC (key->hw_key_idx has by then been set to 32, nothing is written to the hardware and key->flags is unchanged). It adds ffz() of the register value read last (SEC_CSR2 when it was not full, else SEC_CSR3; 0 if that value is 0) to key->hw_key_idx (when SEC_CSR2 was not full the old index is used as the base and SEC_CSR3 is not examined). It writes the key and MICs to PAIRWISE_KEY_ENTRY(hw_key_idx), the peer address and cipher to PAIRWISE_TA_ENTRY(hw_key_idx), sets bit (1 << crypto->bssidx) in SEC_CSR4 and sets IEEE80211_KEY_FLAG_GENERATE_IV. For every command it then updates the valid bit for hw_key_idx in SEC_CSR2 (hw_key_idx < 32) or SEC_CSR3 (bit hw_key_idx - 32): set for SET_KEY, cleared for DISABLE_KEY, unchanged for any other value, writes the register back and returns 0. The shifts are only well defined for hw_key_idx within the register widths.
note: [rev:n/a] fixed-unreviewed; read rt73usb.c:353-455; earlier reviewer notes (SEC_CSR3 not checked when SEC_CSR2 not full; out-of-range final index) right and now stated

name: rtl8180_detect_rf
prose: Detects which RTL8225 RF variant an rtl8180 device has (real name rtl8180_detect_rf(dev), rtl818x/rtl8180/rtl8225.c:744-767; the slice shows only its end). It writes RFPinsOutput (0x0480), RFPinsSelect (0x0488) and RFPinsEnable (0x1FFF), reads EEPROM_CMD, sleeps 100 ms, writes 0x1B7 to RF register 0, reads RF registers 8 and 9, writes 0x0B7 to RF register 0 (restoring it), and returns a pointer to rtl8225_ops if register 8 is not 0x588 or register 9 is not 0x700, otherwise a pointer to rtl8225z2_ops. It returns no error values.

name: btc8723b2ant_is_common_action
prose: Applies the 'common' Bluetooth-coexistence action of the RTL8723B 2-antenna manager when a simple case matches and reports whether it did (halbtc8723b2ant.c:1669-1777; static; the slice cut the head). It reads the BT HS operation, WiFi connected and WiFi busy states. If WiFi is not connected it sets low-power-disable false, applies limited-RX, writes RF register 0x1, sets coex table type 0, turns TDMA off, sets the firmware DAC swing level to 6, sets decrease-BT-power 0 and the software mechanism (all off), and returns true. If WiFi is connected and coex_dm->bt_status is NON_CONNECTED_IDLE it does the same with DAC swing 0xb and returns true. If bt_status is CONNECTED_IDLE it sets low-power-disable true and returns false at once when BT HS is on; otherwise it applies limited-RX, RF register, coex table 0, TDMA off, DAC swing 0xb, decrease-BT-power 0 and the software mechanism with its first flag set, and returns true. prose: Handles an NVMe-oF AUTH_SEND command on the target side (real name nvmet_execute_auth_send(req), nvme/target/fabrics-cmd-auth.c:251-423; returns nothing). name: parport_negotiate
prose: Negotiates an IEEE 1284 transfer mode with the peripheral on a parallel port (parport/ieee1284.c:317-527). Without CONFIG_PARPORT_1284 it returns 0 for IEEE1284_MODE_COMPAT and otherwise logs and returns -1 without touching the port. Otherwise it works on port->physport and returns 0 if the current mode already equals mode, or if mode differs from it only in the IEEE1284_ADDR bit (setting ieee1284.mode = mode). Otherwise it terminates any non-COMPAT mode (parport_ieee1284_terminate) and returns 0 if mode is COMPAT. It maps ECPSWE to ECP and EPPSL/EPPSWE to EPP for the negotiation byte and returns -ENOSYS for IEEE1284_MODE_BECP (after the termination), or uses the extensibility-link request byte for IEEE1284_EXT_LINK. It sets the phase to NEGOTIATION and drives the 1284 handshake: it returns -1 (setting the phase to FWD_IDLE and restoring the control lines) if the peripheral does not respond at event 2; it returns 1, after terminating, if nAck does not go high at event 6, if the peripheral rejects a non-nibble mode (X-flag low), or if the extensibility-link handshake times out or reports no support. On success it stores mode in ieee1284.mode and sets the phase: for ECP without an extension link it goes through ECP_SETUP (a timeout at event 31 is only logged) to FWD_IDLE; otherwise REV_IDLE for NIBBLE and BYTE and FWD_IDLE for the other modes; it returns 0.

name: parport_ieee1284_ecp_read_data
prose: Reads data from an ECP-mode peripheral into buffer (parport/ieee1284_ops.c:474-615; returns the number of bytes stored). Without CONFIG_PARPORT_1284 it returns 0. Otherwise, if the physical port's phase is not REV_IDLE it calls ecp_forward_to_reverse and returns 0 on failure (the phase is then left as that helper left it). It sets the phase to REV_DATA, drops HostAck and loops while fewer than len bytes are stored: it waits for the peripheral to pull nAck low (event 43); if that does not happen within the wait it leaves the loop if some bytes were already read or the device timeout (dev->timeout) has expired, otherwise yields the port (releasing it, sleeping 40 ms and re-claiming with parport_claim_or_block, whose result is not checked, when the port has an IRQ, or waiting for an event otherwise) and leaves the loop if a signal is pending. It reads the status BUSY bit to tell a command byte from data and reads the data byte; a command byte with bit 7 set (a channel command) ends the loop without being accepted; otherwise a command is an RLE count, and if the count exceeds the remaining room the loop breaks leaving it for the next call. On all paths that leave the loop it sets the phase to REV_IDLE and returns count. It does not itself guarantee the port is still claimed if parport_claim_or_block fails during the yield.

name: ibmphp_hpc_readslot
prose: Issues a read command to an IBM hot-plug controller (HPC) (ibmphp_hpc.c:503-634; the slice cut the head). It returns -EINVAL, before taking the HPC access mutex, if pslot is NULL, if pstatus is NULL for any command other than READ_ALLSTAT and READ_BUSSTATUS, if (for READ_BUSSTATUS) the bus index of pslot->bus is negative, or if hpc_readcmdtoindex rejects the command. Otherwise it takes the access mutex (get_hpc_access) and, for controller types 2 and 4, ioremaps the controller's I/O memory; it waits for the controller to be idle (hpc_wait_ctlr_notworking) and, only if that wait succeeded, dispatches: READ_ALLSTAT stores the controller status in pslot->ctrl->status, reads the slot status into pslot->status, waits again and, only if that second wait succeeded, reads the extended status into pslot->ext_status; READ_SLOTSTATUS, READ_EXTSLOTSTATUS, READ_REVLEVEL, READ_HPCOPTIONS and READ_SLOTLATCHLOWREG store the register value in *pstatus without updating the slot; READ_CTLRSTATUS stores the controller status in *pstatus; READ_BUSSTATUS stores the value in pslot->busstatus; READ_ALLSLOT (unused) walks all slots reading status and extended status (a failed first wait gives -EINVAL and ends the loop; a failed second wait sets rc but later iterations overwrite it); any other command sets -EINVAL. It always unmaps the I/O memory (types 2 and 4) and releases the mutex once, then returns rc: 0, the failure value of the wait helper if the controller stayed busy (nothing is read or updated then), or -EINVAL as above.

name: configure_bridge
prose: Configures a PCI-to-PCI bridge function for the IBM hot-plug driver (real name configure_bridge(func_passed, slotno), ibmphp_pci.c:543-1038; static; the slice cut the head). It uses *func_passed as func and the global ibmphp_pci_bus. It writes the primary bus number and finds a secondary bus number (returning -EINVAL if none is available, 0xff), writes the secondary and subordinate bus numbers, cache line size and latency timers, then probes the bridge's own BARs by writing 0xFFFFFFFF and reading back, allocating I/O, memory and prefetchable resources for them and registering them with ibmphp_check_resource / ibmphp_add_resource; a resource that cannot be allocated returns -EIO (freeing the temporary resource), an allocation failure returns -ENOMEM, and a failure to build the needed-resources record goes to the error exit. It computes the resources needed behind the bridge (find_sec_number/amount_needed); if amount_needed->not_correct is set it removes the bus resources it added, frees amount_needed and returns -ENODEV. It allocates and registers the I/O, memory and prefetchable window resources, finds or creates the bus node for the secondary bus (add_new_bus; on failure after creation it removes the bus, frees amount_needed and returns that error), and programs the bridge's I/O, memory and prefetchable base and limit registers, interrupt line, bridge control and command registers. On success it marks func->devices for every device in amount_needed->devices, sets func->bus = 1, assigns the local variable func_passed = &func (which does not change the caller's pointer), frees amount_needed and returns 0. The shared error exit frees amount_needed, removes the io/mem/pfmem window resources added so far and the per-BAR bus resources (clearing the matching func->io, pfmem and mem entries) and returns the error value.

name: ibmphp_check_resource
prose: Finds a free address range for a requested I/O, memory or prefetchable-memory resource in the IBM hot-plug driver's per-bus resource lists (real name ibmphp_check_resource(res, bridge), ibmphp_res.c:952-1332; the slice shows a middle fragment of its gap search). It returns -EINVAL if res is NULL, if no bus node exists for res->busno, or (through the default of its type switch) for an unknown resource type. The alignment is res->len for ordinary devices, or IOBRIDGE (I/O) or MEMBRIDGE (memory) for bridges. It temporarily decrements res->len (and restores the +1 when it succeeds), selects the bus's list for the type and walks the resource nodes of each range, looking at the gap before the first node of a range, between consecutive nodes and after the last node (the part in the slice): a gap is usable when it is at least the requested length and a start address that is a multiple of the alignment fits (with adjustment of the start inside the gap); it remembers the smallest usable gap (len_cur, start_cur) and returns 0 immediately, after setting res->start, restoring res->len and setting res->end = start + len - 1, when a gap exactly matches the requested length. After the walk it uses the best remembered gap, or searches ranges that have no resource nodes yet, and returns 0 with res->start/end set, or -EINVAL if nothing fits. The function modifies res (start, end and the temporary length) but does not insert it into the lists.

name: pciehp_handle_presence_or_link_change
prose: Handles a presence-detect or data-link-layer change on a PCIe hot-plug slot (pciehp_ctrl.c:231-296; returns nothing; the slice cut the head; the caller must not hold ctrl->state_lock, which it takes and releases itself). Step 1, under state_lock: if the slot state is BLINKINGOFF_STATE it cancels button_work and falls through with ON_STATE: the state becomes POWEROFF_STATE, the lock is released, 'Link Down' and/or 'Card not present' are logged according to events (DLLSC, PDC) and pciehp_disable_slot(ctrl, SURPRISE_REMOVAL) is called; in every other state it just unlocks. Step 2, under state_lock again: it reads the card-present and link-active status; if neither is positive it handles only BLINKINGON_STATE (state becomes OFF_STATE, button_work cancelled, power indicator turned off, 'Card not present' logged), unlocks and returns. Otherwise, for BLINKINGON_STATE (after cancelling button_work) or OFF_STATE it sets POWERON_STATE, releases the lock, logs 'Card present' and/or 'Link Up' and stores pciehp_enable_slot(ctrl) in ctrl->request_result; in any other state it unlocks and does nothing. state_lock is not held on return.
