name: virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg(ver, v_opcode, msg, msglen) (virtchnl.h:1661-1892), static inline, with msglen a u16; the name virtchnl_validate_op_msg does not exist. Precondition: ver points to a valid version info (it is read only for VIRTCHNL_OP_GET_VF_RESOURCES); msg is readable for msglen bytes; fields inside msg are read only when msglen is at least the legacy size of the structure for that opcode. Postcondition: it computes the expected length valid_len for v_opcode: a fixed sizeof for most opcodes, zero for opcodes without payload (for example RESET_VF, GET_QOS_CAPS, DISABLE_CHANNELS), sizeof(u32) for GET_VF_RESOURCES when VF_IS_V11(ver) and 0 otherwise, msglen itself for VIRTCHNL_OP_RDMA (a zero msglen is a format error), and for the variable-length messages (VSI queue config, IRQ map, ethernet address list, VLAN lists v1 and v2, RSS key and LUT, RDMA IRQ map, channels, queue bandwidth) the full size computed from the count or length field inside msg when msglen reaches the legacy size. A format error is flagged when num_queue_pairs, num_vectors, num_elements, num_tc or num_queues is zero for the opcodes that test it, or when quanta_size or queue_select.num_queues is zero for CONFIG_QUANTA. VIRTCHNL_OP_EVENT, VIRTCHNL_OP_UNKNOWN and any opcode not listed return VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_PARAM (-5) at once. Otherwise it returns VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_OPCODE_MISMATCH (-38) if a format error was flagged or valid_len differs from msglen, and 0 if not. It only reads its arguments, allocates nothing and takes no locks.
note: slice cut head; real function virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg; the old prose gave the mismatch code as -53 but VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_OPCODE_MISMATCH is -38 (virtchnl.h:50)

name: field_multiplier
prose: field_multiplier(field) (bitfield.h, static __always_inline, taking and returning u64); no side effects. Postcondition: the condition (field | (field - 1)) & ((field | (field - 1)) + 1) is nonzero exactly when field is neither 0 nor a contiguous run of set bits (a run reaching bit 63 passes because the u64 addition wraps to 0, and field == 0 passes the same way). In that nonzero case the code calls __bad_mask(), which is declared __compiletime_error, so a build in which that call remains after constant folding fails to compile; at run time of a call that is reached the function would not return normally. Otherwise it returns field & -field, the lowest set bit of field (0 when field is 0).
note: reviewer R15 unreviewed; prose verified: field==0 and masks that include bit 63 do not call __bad_mask, and the call is a compile-time error only when it survives optimisation

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32_encode_bits(v, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32) in bitfield.h), static __always_inline __must_check, with u32 parameters and a u32 result. Precondition: field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits (a run may include bit 31); for field == 0, field_mask divides by field_multiplier(0) == 0. If v is a compile-time constant with bits outside field_mask(field), the call to __field_overflow() makes the build fail. Postcondition: it returns (v & field_mask(field)) * field_multiplier(field) converted to u32 (no byte swap for the u32 variant): the low bits of v that fit in the field, moved to the field's position, with all other bits zero. It has no side effects.
note: name is the macro invocation that generates the function; division by zero for field 0 added to the precondition

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32_replace_bits(old, val, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32)), static __always_inline __must_check; u32 parameters and result. Precondition: field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits; a constant val that does not fit makes the build fail through __field_overflow(). Postcondition: it returns (old & ~field) | u32_encode_bits(val, field): the bits of old selected by field are replaced by the low bits of val that fit, moved into position, and all other bits of old are unchanged. It has no side effects.
note: name is the macro invocation that generates the function

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32p_replace_bits(p, val, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32)), static __always_inline, returning void. Precondition: p points to a writable u32; field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits; a constant val that does not fit makes the build fail through __field_overflow(). Postcondition: it stores (*p & ~field) | u32_encode_bits(val, field) in *p, so only the bits selected by field change, and returns nothing. The read and write of *p are not atomic.
note: name is the macro invocation that generates the function

name: __MAKE_OP(32)
prose: Generated function u32_get_bits(v, field) (____MAKE_OP(u32,u32,,) expanded by __MAKE_OP(32)), static __always_inline __must_check; u32 parameters and result. Precondition: field is nonzero and a contiguous run of set bits (for field == 0 the division by field_multiplier(0) == 0 is undefined). Postcondition: it returns (v & field) / field_multiplier(field): the bits of v selected by field shifted down so the lowest bit of the field is bit 0. It has no side effects.
note: contract simplified to the formula with the lowest set bit; the contiguity requirement is stated in prose

name: btree_merge128
prose: Inline wrapper that calls btree_merge(&target->h, &victim->h, &btree_geo128, gfp) and returns its result. btree_merge BUG()s if target == victim. If target is empty (target->node is NULL) it takes over victim's root node and height and re-initialises victim to empty, returning 0 without allocating. Otherwise it repeatedly takes victim's last entry, inserts it into target with gfp, and removes it from victim, so entries are moved, not copied; it returns 0 once victim is empty. If an insertion fails it returns that error (btree_insert returns -ENOMEM) immediately: entries already moved are in target, the entry that failed and all remaining entries are still in victim.
note: btree_merge in lib/btree.c:634 moves entries (btree_remove(victim, ...) after each btree_insert) and has BUG_ON(target == victim); reviewer rounds 1 and 15 were right about the BUG_ON precondition and about victim being modified; the round 2 claim that victim keeps all entries on failure is wrong (moved entries are removed from victim).

name: static inline int BTREE_FN(init)(BTREE_TYPE_HEAD *head)
prose: Generated typed wrapper (the function btree_init<suffix> once BTREE_FN and BTREE_TYPE_HEAD are expanded) that returns btree_init(&head->h). btree_init (lib/btree.c:188) initialises the head as empty, then creates the node mempool with mempool_create(0, btree_alloc, btree_free, NULL); it returns -ENOMEM if mempool_create returns NULL and 0 otherwise. The wrapper itself only forwards that result.
note: Reviewer (round 15) said there is no -ENOMEM path: wrong, lib/btree.c:188-195 returns -ENOMEM when mempool_create fails. The old prose said 'initial node allocation', which was imprecise (it is the mempool creation); corrected.

name: __can_cc_frame_bits
prose: Function-like macro, an expression with no side effects of its own (it evaluates its arguments, some more than once). Let n = (is_eff ? CAN_FRAME_HEADER_EFF_BITS (39) : CAN_FRAME_HEADER_SFF_BITS (19)) + data_len * BITS_PER_BYTE + CAN_FRAME_CRC_FIELD_BITS (16). If bitstuffing is nonzero the stuffed part is n + (n - 1) / 4 (integer division), otherwise n. The macro yields that stuffed part plus CAN_FRAME_FOOTER_BITS (9), plus CAN_INTERMISSION_BITS (3) if intermission is nonzero. No range check is done on data_len.
note: Macro, not a function: kept as a described macro; the earlier contract used an unbound logic function so none is given.

name: __can_fd_frame_bits
prose: Function-like macro, an expression with no side effects of its own (it evaluates its arguments, some more than once). Let n = (is_eff ? CANFD_FRAME_HEADER_EFF_BITS (41) : CANFD_FRAME_HEADER_SFF_BITS (22)) + data_len * BITS_PER_BYTE. If bitstuffing is nonzero the stuffed part is n + (n - 1) / 4 (integer division), otherwise n. The macro yields that stuffed part plus a CRC field of CANFD_FRAME_CRC17_FIELD_BITS (28) when data_len <= 16 or CANFD_FRAME_CRC21_FIELD_BITS (33) otherwise (the CRC field is not itself stuffed), plus CAN_FRAME_FOOTER_BITS (9), plus CAN_INTERMISSION_BITS (3) if intermission is nonzero. No range check is done on data_len.
note: Macro, not a function: kept as a described macro; no contract (unbound logic function in the earlier attempt).

name: can_frame_bits
prose: Function-like macro: if is_fd is nonzero it evaluates to __can_fd_frame_bits(is_eff, bitstuffing, intermission, data_len), otherwise to __can_cc_frame_bits(is_eff, bitstuffing, intermission, data_len). Only one branch of the conditional is evaluated. Its doc comment describes the result as the number of bits on the wire of a CAN frame; no sanitising of data_len is done.
note: Macro that selects between two other macros; described rather than dropped because the selection is its whole behaviour.

name: can_frame_bytes
prose: Function-like macro that evaluates to DIV_ROUND_UP(can_frame_bits(is_fd, is_eff, bitstuffing, true, data_len), BITS_PER_BYTE): the frame bit count with the intermission always included (intermission is passed as true), rounded up to a whole number of bytes. data_len is not range checked.
note: Macro; no contract (unbound logic function in the earlier attempt).

name: CIRC_CNT
prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((head) - (tail)) & ((size) - 1), the number of occupied slots of a circular buffer. It gives the intended count only if size is a power of two; with that, the result is (head - tail) modulo size. It does not check that head and tail are in range.
note: Macro; contract dropped (bit operations on a bool-typed result tripped Frama-C earlier, and a macro has no parameters types).

name: CIRC_SPACE
prose: Function-like macro: expands to CIRC_CNT(tail, head + 1, size), i.e. ((tail) - ((head) + 1)) & ((size) - 1), the number of free slots. With a power-of-two size this is (tail - head - 1) modulo size, in the range 0 to size - 1: one slot is always kept unused so that a full buffer is distinguishable from an empty one. It does not check that head and tail are in range.
note: Macro; no contract.

name: CIRC_CNT_TO_END
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression that declares locals end = size - tail and n = ((head) + end) & (size - 1) and yields n < end ? n : end. With a power-of-two size, n is the occupied count (head - tail) modulo size, so the result is the smaller of the occupied count and size - tail: the number of occupied slots that can be read contiguously from tail without wrapping. Arguments head and tail are each read once.
note: Macro; no contract (CIRC_CNT unbound in the earlier attempt).

name: CIRC_SPACE_TO_END
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression that declares locals end = size - 1 - head and n = (end + tail) & (size - 1) and yields n <= end ? n : end + 1. With a power-of-two size, n is the free space (tail - head - 1) modulo size; the result is n when n <= size - 1 - head, otherwise size - head. That is the number of free slots that can be written contiguously from head without wrapping. Arguments head and tail are each read once.
note: Macro; no contract. Checked by example: size 8, head 5, tail 2 gives 3; size 8, head 5, tail 0 gives 2.

name: static inline void class_##_name##_destructor(_type *p)
prose: Generated by DEFINE_CLASS(_name, _type, _exit, _init, ...): copies *p into a local variable _T of type _type and then evaluates the _exit expression, which may use _T; it returns nothing. Whatever release happens is whatever _exit does; the function itself performs no other action. It is the cleanup function attached to variables declared with CLASS()/guard() via __cleanup, so it runs when such a variable leaves scope. EXTEND_CLASS and __DEFINE_UNLOCK_GUARD generate other functions of the same name pattern.
note: Old prose said the release happens 'exactly once' and that the instance came from the matching constructor; neither is checkable from the macro. Named by the definition head in DEFINE_CLASS.

name: static inline _type class_##_name##_constructor(_init_args)
prose: Generated by DEFINE_CLASS(_name, _type, _exit, _init, _init_args...): declares a local _type t initialised from the _init expression, using the _init_args parameters, and returns t. It reports no error by itself; for guards generated by DEFINE_GUARD the _init expression is ({ _lock; _T; }), so it runs the lock statement and returns the passed value, and DEFINE_GUARD_COND_4 variants may return ERR_PTR(_RET) as the value when the condition fails. __DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_1 and __DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_0 generate differently shaped constructors.
note: Named by the definition head in DEFINE_CLASS. Old claim of error handle on failure holds only for conditional guard variants.

name: static inline void *class_##_name##_lock_ptr(class_##_name##_t *_T)
prose: Generated by __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR(_name, _exp): reads the pointer stored at *(_exp) into _ptr; if IS_ERR(_ptr) it returns NULL, otherwise it returns _ptr unchanged. So the result is NULL both for an error-encoded pointer and for a stored NULL, and non-NULL only for a stored non-error pointer. It changes no state. DEFINE_CLASS_IS_UNCONDITIONAL generates a variant of the same name that simply returns (void *)1, and DEFINE_GUARD_COND_4 generates an _ext variant that forwards to the base one.
note: Old prose said 'NULL iff the guard holds an error', which is wrong: a stored NULL also gives NULL. Named by the head in __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR.

name: static inline int class_##_name##_lock_err(class_##_name##_t *_T)
prose: Generated by __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR(_name, _exp): converts the stored value *(_exp) to a long _rc. If _rc is 0 it is replaced by -EBUSY; then, if _rc is not an error value (IS_ERR_VALUE false) it is replaced by 0. It returns 0 when the stored value is a non-error value other than 0, -EBUSY when the stored value is 0, and the stored negative errno itself when the stored value is in the error range. It changes no state. DEFINE_GUARD_COND_4 generates an _ext variant that forwards to the base one.
note: Old prose was right on 0 and -EBUSY but missed that the stored errno is returned as is. Named by the head in __DEFINE_GUARD_LOCK_PTR.

name: cnt32_to_63
prose: Function-like macro (a GNU statement expression) that keeps a function-local static u32 __m_cnt_hi at each expansion site. It reads that value as the high word, issues smp_rmb(), then evaluates cnt_lo once as the low word. If the top bits of the high and low words differ ((s32)(hi ^ lo) < 0) it stores (hi ^ 0x80000000) + (hi >> 31) into both the static and the local high word. Its value is the 64-bit combination of the high and low words, so the low 32 bits equal cnt_lo, and bit 63 is documented as garbage. The header comment states the conditions for the extension to work (called at least once per half period of the counter, not preempted for too long, cnt_lo read directly from the counter); the macro does not enforce them. It uses no lock; concurrent updaters may store the same value.
note: Prose-style contract dropped (it named identifiers not in the file and called the result monotonic unconditionally).

name: comedi_check_trigger_is_unique
prose: Returns -EINVAL if (src & (src - 1)) is nonzero, which is the case exactly when more than one bit of src is set, and returns 0 otherwise, which includes src == 0 and any value with a single bit set. It does not modify anything.

name: fsleep
prose: Sleeps using one of three mechanisms chosen by usecs. If usecs <= 10 it calls udelay(usecs) (busy wait). Else if usecs < USLEEP_RANGE_UPPER_BOUND, which is (TICK_NSEC << 2) / NSEC_PER_USEC, it calls usleep_range(usecs, usecs + (usecs >> 2)), which sleeps in TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE. Otherwise it calls msleep(DIV_ROUND_UP(usecs, USEC_PER_MSEC)); msleep takes an unsigned int, so on a 64-bit unsigned long a rounded-up millisecond count above UINT_MAX is truncated by the call. It returns nothing and may sleep except in the udelay branch.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose said at least usecs microseconds with only an overflow precondition on usecs + (usecs >> 2); the msleep argument truncation is not excluded. Rewritten without a duration guarantee.

name: static inline bool dev_##accessor_name(const struct device *dev)

name: FIELD_PREP_WM16
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression. It copies _val into a local __val and _mask into a local __mask (each argument is evaluated once), runs __BF_FIELD_CHECK(__mask, (u16)0U, __val, ...), which only contains compile-time build checks (mask constant and non-zero, mask contiguous, mask not wider than 16 bits, and, for a constant value, that the value fits in the field) and no runtime check, and then yields (((typeof(__mask))__val << __bf_shf(__mask)) & __mask) | (__mask << 16), where __bf_shf is the trailing-zero count of the mask. The result has the type of the mask: the value shifted into the field position and masked, ORed with the mask shifted up by 16 bits.
note: Macro; no contract (unbound __bf_shf in the earlier attempt). Checked __BF_FIELD_CHECK in include/linux/bitfield.h.

name: FIELD_PREP_WM16_CONST
prose: Function-like macro that is a constant expression. It evaluates to FIELD_PREP_CONST(_mask, _val) | (BUILD_BUG_ON_ZERO(const_true((u64)(_mask) > U16_MAX)) + ((_mask) << 16)). FIELD_PREP_CONST yields the value shifted into the mask position and masked, with its own compile-time checks (non-zero mask, contiguous mask, value fits). The second part is a compile-time error if the mask is larger than U16_MAX and otherwise contributes the mask shifted up by 16 bits. There is no runtime check; _mask and _val are expanded more than once.
note: Macro; no contract (unbound FIELD_PREP_CONST in the earlier attempt).

name: ITSTATIC void ITPREFIX ## _insert(ITSTRUCT *node, struct rb_root_cached *root)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_insert for ITPREFIX = interval_tree). Walks down from root->rb_root.rb_node. At each visited node it raises that node's ITSUBTREE to last = ITLAST(node) if it is smaller, then goes left if ITSTART(node) < ITSTART(visited) and otherwise goes right (clearing the leftmost flag; equal starts go right). It sets node->ITSUBTREE = last, links the node at the found position with rb_link_node, and calls rb_insert_augmented_cached(&node->ITRB, root, leftmost, &ITPREFIX_augment), which rebalances and updates the cached leftmost pointer. Returns nothing. node must not already be in a tree. It takes no lock; callers must serialise access to the tree.
note: Unreviewed before (mechanical name-only rejections); rewritten from the macro body. Named by the generated definition head.

name: ITSTATIC void ITPREFIX ## _remove(ITSTRUCT *node, struct rb_root_cached *root)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_remove). It is a single call rb_erase_augmented_cached(&node->ITRB, root, &ITPREFIX_augment), which unlinks the node from the cached augmented rbtree, rebalances, and runs the augment callbacks to recompute the ITSUBTREE maxima and updates the cached leftmost pointer. Returns nothing. node must be in the tree rooted at root; no lock is taken here.
note: Named by the generated definition head. Behaviour of the augmented erase itself is in the rbtree code, not re-derived here.

name: static ITSTRUCT * ITPREFIX ## _subtree_search(ITSTRUCT *node, ITTYPE start, ITTYPE last)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_subtree_search); static, not governed by ITSTATIC. Loops with node as the current subtree root. If node has a left child and start <= left->ITSUBTREE it moves to the left child. Otherwise, if ITSTART(node) <= last: if start <= ITLAST(node) it returns node, else it moves to node's right child (taken without a NULL check, relying on the loop invariant start <= node->ITSUBTREE). If ITSTART(node) > last it returns NULL. So for a subtree satisfying the invariant it returns the leftmost node whose interval intersects [start, last], or NULL. It reads the tree and changes nothing.
note: Named by the generated definition head. The right-child step has no NULL test; correctness depends on the caller establishing start <= node->ITSUBTREE (iter_first checks it, iter_next checks start <= right->ITSUBTREE).

name: ITSTATIC ITSTRUCT * ITPREFIX ## _iter_first(struct rb_root_cached *root, ITTYPE start, ITTYPE last)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_iter_first). Returns NULL if the tree is empty (root->rb_root.rb_node is NULL), or if the root node's ITSUBTREE is less than start, or if ITSTART of root->rb_leftmost is greater than last. Otherwise it returns ITPREFIX_subtree_search(root node, start, last), i.e. the leftmost node whose interval intersects [start, last], or NULL if none does. It only reads the tree.
note: Named by the generated definition head. All three early NULL returns checked against scratch-dump lines 312-334.

name: ITSTATIC ITSTRUCT * ITPREFIX ## _iter_next(ITSTRUCT *node, ITTYPE start, ITTYPE last)
prose: Generated by INTERVAL_TREE_DEFINE (instance interval_tree_iter_next). Given a node already known to satisfy ITSTART(node) <= last, it looks for the next intersecting node in start order. Loop: if node has a right child whose ITSUBTREE >= start it returns ITPREFIX_subtree_search on that child (which may itself return NULL). Otherwise it climbs through rb_parent until it arrives from a left child, returning NULL if it reaches the root. At that ancestor it returns NULL if last < ITSTART(ancestor), returns the ancestor if start <= ITLAST(ancestor), and otherwise repeats from the ancestor. Only reads the tree.
note: Named by the generated definition head. Returns checked against scratch-dump lines 342-374.

name: ipmi_demangle_device_id
prose: Parses an IPMI Get Device ID response in data (data_len bytes) into *id. Returns -EINVAL, leaving *id untouched, if data_len < 7, or if netfn is not IPMI_NETFN_APP_RESPONSE or cmd is not IPMI_GET_DEVICE_ID_CMD, or if data[0] (the completion code) is nonzero. Otherwise it skips the first byte and sets device_id, device_revision, firmware_revision_1, firmware_revision_2, ipmi_version and additional_device_support from original bytes 1 to 6. If at least 12 bytes were given it sets manufacturer_id (original bytes 7 to 9, little endian) and product_id (bytes 10 and 11), otherwise both are set to 0. If at least 16 bytes were given it copies original bytes 12 to 15 into aux_firmware_revision and sets aux_firmware_revision_set to 1, otherwise it sets that flag to 0 (aux_firmware_revision is not written). Then returns 0. It takes no locks.

name: nf_hook
prose: Inline entry point that runs the registered netfilter hooks for (pf, hook). It returns 1 when the caller should continue by calling okfn itself; any other value means the packet was consumed. Steps: (1) with CONFIG_JUMP_LABEL, if pf and hook are compile-time constants and static_key_false(&nf_hooks_needed[pf][hook]) is false, it returns 1 at once. (2) It takes rcu_read_lock and picks hook_head by pf: net->nf.hooks_ipv4[hook] for NFPROTO_IPV4, hooks_ipv6[hook] for NFPROTO_IPV6, hooks_arp[hook] for NFPROTO_ARP (only with CONFIG_NETFILTER_FAMILY_ARP, and with WARN_ON_ONCE and no hook list if hook is out of range), hooks_bridge[hook] for NFPROTO_BRIDGE (only with CONFIG_NETFILTER_FAMILY_BRIDGE), and WARN_ON_ONCE with no hook list for any other pf; the IPv4, IPv6 and bridge indexes are not range checked here. (3) If a hook list was found it fills a struct nf_hook_state with nf_hook_state_init(hook, pf, indev, outdev, sk, net, okfn) and sets ret = nf_hook_slow(skb, &state, hook_head, 0). (4) It releases the RCU read lock and returns ret, which is still 1 if there was no hook list. nf_hook_slow returns 1 when every hook accepted; a negative errno when a hook returned NF_DROP (skb freed, -EPERM if the verdict encodes no errno); NF_DROP_GETERR(verdict), 0 or a negative errno encoded by the hook, for NF_STOLEN; nf_queue's result for NF_QUEUE (1 if queueing failed with -ESRCH and the verdict carries the queue-bypass flag, in which case processing continues with the next hook; otherwise 0, whether the packet was queued or queueing failed and nf_queue freed the skb); and 0 after a WARN_ON_ONCE for an unknown verdict, leaving the skb to the caller. nf_hook itself never calls okfn.
note: Reviewers mixed: round 1 right (return is nf_hook_slow's errno/0/1 rather than a raw verdict); round 2 wrong direction (an unknown verdict returns 0, not 1 or a negative errno); round 15 right that unknown verdict returns 0 but wrong that nf_hook_slow does not WARN (net/netfilter/core.c nf_hook_slow default: WARN_ON_ONCE(1); return 0;). The old prose said an unknown verdict gives 1: corrected. Slice cut the tail: rest of nf_hook read from include/linux/netfilter.h.

name: __ONCE_LITE_IF
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression with a function-local static bool __already_done (placed in section .data..once) separate for each place where the macro is expanded. It evaluates condition once into __ret_cond; if __ret_cond is true and __already_done is false it sets __already_done to true and the macro yields true, otherwise it yields false (without touching the flag when the condition is false). The test and the set are plain, not atomic, so concurrent callers may both see the flag clear. The yield is wrapped in unlikely().
note: Reviewer right that the old contract omitted the flag being set; contract dropped. Old prose said 'permanently' and did not mention the non-atomic test-and-set.

name: DO_ONCE_LITE_IF
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression. It evaluates condition once into __ret_do_once (as !!condition); if __ONCE_LITE_IF(__ret_do_once) is true it calls func(__VA_ARGS__). The macro yields unlikely(__ret_do_once), the truth value of the condition, whether or not func was called. Because the guard is a per-expansion-site static flag tested and set without atomics, func is called at most once per expansion site only when callers do not race; concurrent first callers may each call it. DO_ONCE_LITE(func, ...) is the same with condition true.
note: Reviewer right: the old claim that func runs at most once across all calls was too strong (per expansion site, and not atomic). Contract dropped.

name: adjust_by_scaled_ppm
prose: Returns base adjusted by scaled_ppm parts per million with a 16-bit binary fraction. It calls diff_by_scaled_ppm(base, scaled_ppm, &diff): if scaled_ppm is negative it negates it (undefined behaviour for the most negative long), and diff = mul_u64_u64_div_u64(base, (u64)|scaled_ppm|, 1000000ULL << 16), which in the generic implementation uses a 128-bit intermediate and returns U64_MAX when the quotient does not fit in 64 bits (an architecture may supply its own version). If scaled_ppm was negative the result is base - diff, otherwise base + diff, both in u64 arithmetic, so the result wraps modulo 2^64 if diff exceeds base or the sum overflows. No locks or memory are involved.
note: Reviewers right about the contract (hardcoded LONG_MIN / INT_MIN exclusions, and the underflow requirement); contract removed rather than patched. Prose now says what the u64 arithmetic does instead of excluding overflow inputs. mul_u64_u64_div_u64 read in lib/math/div64.c.

name: DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_1(srcu, struct srcu_struct, _T->idx = srcu_read_lock(_T->lock), srcu_read_unlock(_T->lock, _T->idx), int idx)
prose: Macro invocation (DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_1 in cleanup.h) that generates the guard type class_srcu_t, a struct holding struct srcu_struct *lock and int idx, plus class_srcu_destructor and class_srcu_constructor, class_srcu_lock_ptr and class_srcu_lock_err. class_srcu_constructor(l) stores l in .lock, runs idx = srcu_read_lock(lock), and returns the guard by value. class_srcu_destructor calls srcu_read_unlock(lock, idx) unless the stored lock pointer is NULL or an error pointer (__GUARD_IS_ERR). Used through guard(srcu)(...) or scoped_guard(srcu, ...), the unlock runs when the guard variable leaves scope.
note: The earlier prose used invented names srcu_guard_init / srcu_guard_exit; the generated names are class_srcu_constructor / class_srcu_destructor (DEFINE_LOCK_GUARD_1 at cleanup.h:506).

name: __svc_print_addr
prose: Formats a socket address into buf with snprintf(buf, len, ...) and returns buf. For sa_family AF_INET it prints "%pI4, port=%u" with the IPv4 address and ntohs of the port; for AF_INET6 it prints "%pI6, port=%u" with the IPv6 address and port; for any other family it prints "unknown address type: %d" with the family number. snprintf writes at most len bytes including the terminating NUL, truncating longer output, and nothing if len is 0. The address is cast to struct sockaddr_in or sockaddr_in6 only in the matching case. The function returns buf in all cases and does not check that buf is non-NULL.
note: slice cut the head: the real name is __svc_print_addr (verified in include/linux/sunrpc/svc_xprt.h); the old name format_addr does not exist in the file.

name: ssh_tid_is_valid
prose: Returns ssh_tid_to_index(tid) < SSH_NUM_TARGETS. ssh_tid_to_index returns the u8 value tid - 1u (so tid 0 gives 255) and SSH_NUM_TARGETS is 2, so the function returns true exactly when tid is 1 or 2 and false for every other u8 value including 0. It has no side effects.
note: Old prose said it returns true for every tid and that ssh_tid_to_index returns -EINVAL: both wrong (include/linux/surface_aggregator/serial_hub.h: ssh_tid_to_index is `return tid - 1u;` with u8 return, SSH_NUM_TARGETS is 2). The round 1 reviewer claim (invalid tids map to -EINVAL and give true) is also wrong for the same reason.

name: static ssize_t __struct##_##__name##_store(struct config_item *item, const char *page, size_t len)
prose: Generated by GS_STRINGS_W(__struct, __name); the generated function is named <struct>_<name>_store. It takes gs = to_<struct>(item) and calls usb_string_copy(page, &gs-><name>). If that returns nonzero the store returns that value; otherwise it returns len. usb_string_copy (drivers/usb/gadget/configfs.c) returns -EOVERFLOW if strlen(page) exceeds USB_MAX_STRING_LEN, -EINVAL if page is empty, and -ENOMEM if it needs a new buffer and kmalloc fails; on any of these the field pointer is unchanged and nothing is freed. On success it copies page into the existing buffer of the field if there is one, otherwise into a newly kmalloc'ed buffer of USB_MAX_STRING_WITH_NULL_LEN bytes, strips one trailing newline, and sets the field to that buffer. len is used only as the return value.
note: Reviewer wrong: usb_string_copy never frees the old field (lib code at drivers/usb/gadget/configfs.c:113-135 has no kfree), so the field is unchanged on -ENOMEM. The old prose missed the -EINVAL path for an empty string; added.

name: find_closest
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression yielding an index of type typeof(as). With __fc_as = as - 1, it scans i from 0 while i < as - 1: mid = (a[i] + a[i+1]) / 2 (integer division, in the element type); at the first i with x <= mid it computes left = x - a[i] and right = a[i+1] - x, increments i if right < left (so a tie keeps the lower index), and stops. If no such i is found the loop ends with i = as - 1. The array a is expected to be sorted ascending; x, a and as are each evaluated once, and x is converted to long. For as == 1 it yields 0; as == 0 is not handled and would read out of bounds. It reads the array and changes nothing.
note: Macro; contract was prose, dropped. Result described by what the loop does; 'closest' is the documented intent but midpoints use truncating integer division.

name: find_closest_descending
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression yielding an index of type typeof(as). With __fc_as = as - 1, it scans i downward from as - 1 while i >= 1: mid = (a[i] + a[i-1]) / 2 (integer division, in the element type); at the first i with x <= mid it computes left = x - a[i] and right = a[i-1] - x, decrements i if right < left (so a tie keeps index i), and stops. If no such i is found the loop ends with i = 0. The array a is expected to be sorted descending; x, a and as are each evaluated once, and x is converted to long. For as == 1 it yields 0; as == 0 is not handled. It reads the array and changes nothing.
note: Macro; contract was prose, dropped.

name: wait_event_interruptible_locked
prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 0, do_wait_intr). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, and repeats: call do_wait_intr(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. So the value is 0 when condition was seen true and -ERESTARTSYS when a signal was pending while condition was false. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. wq is the waitqueue head object, not a pointer.
note: Checked against __wait_event_interruptible_locked (wait.h:779-793) and do_wait_intr / do_wait_intr_irq (kernel/sched/wait.c:333-365). Macro; the earlier contracts were prose and are dropped.

name: wait_event_interruptible_locked_irq
prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 0, do_wait_intr_irq). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, and repeats: call do_wait_intr_irq(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr_irq adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock_irq(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock_irq(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. So the value is 0 when condition was seen true and -ERESTARTSYS when a signal was pending while condition was false. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. Because spin_unlock_irq enables interrupts around the sleep, the caller must be in a context where that is allowed.
note: Checked against __wait_event_interruptible_locked (wait.h:779-793) and do_wait_intr / do_wait_intr_irq (kernel/sched/wait.c:333-365). Macro; the earlier contracts were prose and are dropped.

name: wait_event_interruptible_exclusive_locked
prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 1, do_wait_intr). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, sets WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE on it, and repeats: call do_wait_intr(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. So the value is 0 when condition was seen true and -ERESTARTSYS when a signal was pending while condition was false. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. Being exclusive means a wake-up walking the queue stops after waking this entry (documented in the header comment).
note: Checked against __wait_event_interruptible_locked (wait.h:779-793) and do_wait_intr / do_wait_intr_irq (kernel/sched/wait.c:333-365). Macro; the earlier contracts were prose and are dropped.

prose: Function-like macro (an expression of type int). It evaluates condition once first and yields 0 without sleeping if it is true; otherwise it yields __wait_event_interruptible_locked(wq, condition, 1, do_wait_intr_irq). That loop declares a wait entry with DEFINE_WAIT, sets WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE on it, and repeats: call do_wait_intr_irq(&wq, &wait), stop if it returns nonzero, else stop when condition is true. do_wait_intr_irq adds the entry to the tail of the waitqueue if not already queued, sets TASK_INTERRUPTIBLE, returns -ERESTARTSYS if a signal is pending, and otherwise releases the lock with spin_unlock_irq(&wq->lock), calls schedule(), retakes it with spin_lock_irq(&wq->lock) and returns 0. After the loop it removes the entry from the queue, sets the task state to TASK_RUNNING and yields the loop's value. The caller must hold wq.lock (taken the matching way) on entry; condition is evaluated with the lock held and the lock is held again when the macro finishes. Because spin_unlock_irq enables interrupts around the sleep, the caller must be in a context where that is allowed. Being exclusive means a wake-up walking the queue stops after waking this entry (documented in the header comment).

name: wait_event_killable
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int. It calls might_sleep(), then if !(condition) it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, TASK_KILLABLE, 0, 0, schedule()), which repeatedly queues the task, sleeps in TASK_KILLABLE until woken, and re-tests condition each time; it yields 0 once condition is seen true and -ERESTARTSYS if prepare_to_wait_event reports that a fatal signal is pending while condition is false. If condition is true at the start it yields 0 without sleeping. The result is stored in an int. condition is expanded more than once. The task is dequeued (finish_wait) on the normal exit; wake_up must be called by whoever changes the condition.
note: Checked against ___wait_event (wait.h:302-327) and prepare_to_wait_event (kernel/sched/wait.c:290). Macro; earlier contract was prose and is dropped.

name: wait_event_state
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int. It calls might_sleep(), then if !(condition) it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, state, 0, 0, schedule()), sleeping in the task state given by state and re-testing condition on each wake-up. It yields 0 once condition is seen true (also immediately if it is true at the start) and -ERESTARTSYS if the state is one a signal can interrupt (a non-constant state is always treated as possibly interruptible) and prepare_to_wait_event reports a pending signal for that state while condition is false. condition is expanded more than once.
note: Checked against ___wait_event (wait.h:302-327), ___wait_is_interruptible (wait.h:284). Macro; contract dropped.

name: wait_event_state_exclusive
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int, the same as wait_event_state except the wait entry is queued with WQ_FLAG_EXCLUSIVE (exclusive argument 1 of ___wait_event): after might_sleep(), if !(condition) it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, state, 1, 0, schedule()). It yields 0 once condition is seen true and -ERESTARTSYS if a signal that is able to interrupt the given state is pending while condition is false. Exclusive means a wake-up walking the queue stops after waking this entry.
note: Checked against ___wait_event; the exclusive flag only changes how the entry is queued and woken. Macro; contract dropped.

name: wait_event_lock_irq_cmd
prose: Function-like macro (a do { } while (0) statement, no value). If condition is already true it does nothing. Otherwise it runs ___wait_event(wq_head, condition, TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE, 0, 0, ...), whose wait step is spin_unlock_irq(&lock); cmd; schedule(); spin_lock_irq(&lock). It therefore returns only when condition is true (uninterruptible, so no signal exit). The caller must hold lock on entry; it is held on return, and is released, with interrupts enabled, while cmd runs and the task sleeps. condition is tested with the lock held (and after every wake-up).
note: Checked against __wait_event_lock_irq (wait.h:226-231). Macro; contract was prose, dropped.

name: xz_crc32
note: Only a declaration in this header (uint32_t xz_crc32(const uint8_t *buf, size_t size, uint32_t crc); inside #if XZ_INTERNAL_CRC32); there is no body in the slice, so nothing to describe here.

name: __FP_FRAC_SRS_1
prose: Function-like macro that assigns to X (so X must be an lvalue, and is evaluated several times) and yields the assigned value: X = (X >> N) | sticky. sticky is (X & 1) when N is a compile-time constant equal to 1, and otherwise ((X << (_FP_W_TYPE_SIZE - N)) != 0), i.e. 1 if any of the N bits shifted out of X was set and 0 if not. The sz argument is not used. Meaningful only for 0 < N < _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE; a shift by the full word width or more is not defined by this macro.
note: Macro; contract was prose, dropped. Precedence: the sticky ternary is parenthesised, the shift binds tighter than |.

name: _FP_FRAC_SLL_1
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) that shifts the one-word fraction X_f (token-pasted from X) left: if N is a compile-time constant equal to 1 it does X_f += X_f, otherwise X_f <<= N. Bits shifted out of the word are lost; N is expected to be less than the word size.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_MUL_MEAT_1_imm
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value). It sets R_f = X_f * Y_f as a single word multiply (truncated to the word size, so correct only if the host word is at least twice the fraction width, as the header comment assumes) and then applies _FP_FRAC_SRS_1(R, wfracbits - 1, 2 * wfracbits), a right shift of R_f by wfracbits - 1 that ORs a sticky bit for any shifted-out bits. It modifies R_f only.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_MUL_MEAT_1_hard
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) that multiplies the one-word fractions X_f and Y_f into a two-word product using half-word pieces: it splits each into high and low halves of _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE/2 bits, forms the four partial products, adds the two cross products (adding a carry of 1 << (word/2) into the high word if that sum wraps), splits the cross sum across the two words and adds it to the low-by-low and high-by-high products with _FP_FRAC_ADD_2. It then applies _FP_FRAC_SRS_2(_z, wfracbits - 1, 2 * wfracbits), a sticky right shift of the two-word product, and sets R_f = _z_f0, the low word. Its locals _xh, _xl, _yh, _yl, _z_f0, _z_f1, _a_f0, _a_f1 are declared inside the block.
note: Old prose said '16-bit-half partial products'; the code uses half-words of _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE/2 bits. Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_DIV_MEAT_1_udiv
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) that divides one-word fractions using the udiv_qrnnd double-word primitive. If X_f < Y_f it decrements R_e and forms the dividend nh:nl = (X_f >> _FP_WFRACXBITS_fs) : (X_f << _FP_WFRACBITS_fs); otherwise nh:nl = (X_f >> (_FP_WFRACXBITS_fs + 1)) : (X_f << (_FP_WFRACBITS_fs - 1)). It calls udiv_qrnnd(_q, _r, _nh, _nl, Y_f) and sets R_f = _q | (_r != 0), the quotient with the low bit set as sticky when the remainder is nonzero. X_f is left unchanged; R_e may change. There is no test for Y_f being zero here.
note: Macro; contract was prose, dropped.

name: _FP_SQRT_MEAT_1
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) implementing a bit-at-a-time square root on one-word fractions. While q != _FP_WORK_ROUND it sets T_f = S_f + q; if T_f <= X_f it sets S_f = T_f + q, X_f -= T_f and R_f += q; then it shifts X left by one (_FP_FRAC_SLL_1) and halves q. When the loop ends, if X_f is nonzero it sets the _FP_WORK_ROUND bit of R_f if S_f < X_f and always sets the _FP_WORK_STICKY bit of R_f. So R_f accumulates the root bits and the round and sticky bits report an inexact result. The loop ends only if q reaches exactly _FP_WORK_ROUND by repeated halving; q, X, S, T and R are all modified.
note: Macro; contract was prose and the 'floor of the square root' claim was imprecise (R_f carries extra round/sticky bits); rewritten from the body.

name: _FP_FRAC_GE_1
prose: Function-like macro: expands to (X##_f >= Y##_f), a comparison of the one-word fractions X_f and Y_f as _FP_W_TYPE values, yielding 1 if X_f is at least Y_f and 0 otherwise. X and Y are names that are pasted with _f, not general expressions; nothing is modified.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_SQRT_MEAT_2
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) implementing a bit-at-a-time square root on two-word fractions (words f1 high, f0 low). Loop 1, while q is nonzero: T_f1 = S_f1 + q; if T_f1 <= X_f1 then S_f1 = T_f1 + q, X_f1 -= T_f1, R_f1 += q; then _FP_FRAC_SLL_2(X, 1) and q >>= 1. It then reloads q with the top bit of a word. Loop 2, while q != _FP_WORK_ROUND: T_f0 = S_f0 + q, T_f1 = S_f1; if T <= X as a two-word value it sets S_f0 = T_f0 + q, adds the carry to S_f1, subtracts T from X with _FP_FRAC_DEC_2 and adds q to R_f0; then shifts X left by one and halves q. Finally, if X_f0 | X_f1 is nonzero it sets the _FP_WORK_ROUND bit of R_f0 if S < X (two-word compare) and always sets _FP_WORK_STICKY in R_f0. q, X, S, T and R are modified; the second loop ends only if q reaches exactly _FP_WORK_ROUND.
note: Macro; contract named identifiers that are not in the file and is dropped. Rewritten from the body.

name: _FP_FRAC_ASSEMBLE_2
prose: Function-like macro, an expression of type void. If rsize <= _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE it assigns r = X_f0; otherwise it assigns r = X_f1, shifts r left by _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE, and adds X_f0, so r gets (X_f1 << word) + X_f0 in r's own type (r must be wider than one word for that to hold). It has no value, only assigns r, and the header comment says no shifting or overflow handling is done.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_FRAC_DISASSEMBLE_2
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value). It assigns X_f0 = r (converted to the word type) and X_f1 = 0 if rsize <= _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE, otherwise X_f1 = r >> _FP_W_TYPE_SIZE. r is evaluated more than once.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_FRAC_CONV_1_2
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) converting a two-word source fraction S to a one-word destination fraction D. If S_c != FP_CLS_NAN it applies _FP_FRAC_SRS_2(S, _FP_WFRACBITS_sfs - _FP_WFRACBITS_dfs, _FP_WFRACBITS_sfs), a right shift by the difference in fraction widths that sets a sticky bit for shifted-out bits; if S is a NaN it applies _FP_FRAC_SRL_2 with the same shift count, a plain right shift without sticky. Then it sets D_f = S_f0. The source S is shifted in place.
note: Old prose called the shift 'arithmetic'; it is a sticky right shift (SRS) for non-NaN and a logical right shift (SRL) for NaN. Macro; contract dropped.

name: _FP_FRAC_CONV_2_1
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value) converting a one-word source fraction S to a two-word destination D: D_f0 = S_f, D_f1 = 0, then _FP_FRAC_SLL_2(D, _FP_WFRACBITS_dfs - _FP_WFRACBITS_sfs), a left shift by the difference of the fraction widths. S_f is unchanged.
note: Macro; contract dropped.

name: __FP_FRAC_SUB_3
prose: Function-like macro (do { } while (0), no value), compiled only if not already defined (#ifndef __FP_FRAC_SUB_3). It sets r0 = x0 - y0 and _c1 = (r0 > x0); r1 = x1 - y1 and _c2 = (r1 > x1); then r1 -= _c1 and _c2 |= (r1 > _c1); finally r2 = x2 - y2 - _c2. The borrow test in the third step compares the already decremented r1 with _c1 rather than testing whether subtracting _c1 wrapped r1, so it sets _c2 (and subtracts an extra 1 from r2) in cases with no borrow: for example x = (0, 5, 3), y = (0, 0, 1) gives _c1 = 0, r1 = 5, _c2 = (5 > 0) = 1 and r2 = all ones instead of 0. So the macro does not compute the three-word difference modulo 2^(3W) for all inputs; an architecture may provide its own definition.
note: Reviewer right: round 15 pointed at the borrow condition r1 > _c1; confirmed with the counterexample above (compare __FP_FRAC_ADD_3, which uses r1 < _c1 correctly). The old prose claimed the correct modular difference.

name: LM3560_FLASH_BRT_uA_TO_REG
prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((a) < 62500 ? 0 : (((a) - 62500) / 62500)). It yields 0 if a is below 62500, and otherwise the integer-division quotient of (a - 62500) by 62500, i.e. the number of whole steps of 62500 above the minimum. The argument a is evaluated twice and its type decides the arithmetic; there is no upper-limit clamp.
note: Macro; no contract (macro, earlier contracts were rejected for syntax). Old prose assumed a non-negative a; for a below the minimum (including negative a) the result is 0.

name: LM3560_FLASH_TOUT_ms_TO_REG
prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((a) < 32 ? 0 : (((a) - 32) / 32)). It yields 0 if a is below 32, and otherwise the integer-division quotient of (a - 32) by 32, i.e. the number of whole steps of 32 above the minimum. The argument a is evaluated twice and its type decides the arithmetic; there is no upper-limit clamp.

prose: Function-like macro: expands to ((a) < 31250 ? 0 : (((a) - 31250) / 31250)). When CONFIG_NETLABEL is defined the header only declares void calipso_exit(void) and the real function is defined elsewhere, so none of this describes that version.

name: inet_steal_sock
prose: Calls sk = skb_steal_sock(skb, refcounted, &prefetched), which takes skb->sk away from the skb and sets *refcounted and prefetched; if that gives NULL it returns NULL. If the socket was not prefetched or is not a full socket it returns sk. If sk_protocol is IPPROTO_TCP and the state is not TCP_LISTEN, or IPPROTO_UDP and the state is not TCP_CLOSE, or the protocol is any other, it returns sk. Otherwise it calls inet_lookup_reuseport(net, sk, skb, doff, saddr, sport, daddr, ntohs(dport), ehashfn); if that returns NULL it returns sk, else it executes WARN_ON_ONCE(*refcounted) (it does not itself clear *refcounted; it expects it to be false) and returns the reuseport socket. In this tree neither skb_steal_sock nor inet_lookup_reuseport returns an error pointer. It takes no locks itself.
note: Reviewer mixed: right that the old text said *refcounted is false for reuse_sk (the code only warns if it is true); wrong that skb_steal_sock can return an ERR_PTR (include/net/request_sock.h:94-123 returns NULL or a socket; inet_lookup_reuseport, net/ipv4/inet_hashtables.c, returns NULL or a socket).

name: __inet_lookup_skb
prose: Gets net = skb_dst_dev_net_rcu(skb) and iph = ip_hdr(skb), then sk = inet_steal_sock(net, skb, doff, iph->saddr, sport, iph->daddr, dport, refcounted, inet_ehashfn). If sk is an error pointer it returns NULL; if sk is non-NULL it returns it (whether or not it was prefetched); otherwise it returns __inet_lookup(net, skb, doff, iph->saddr, sport, iph->daddr, dport, inet_iif(skb), sdif, refcounted), the established-then-listener lookup, which can return NULL. *refcounted is whatever inet_steal_sock left for a stolen socket (false when nothing was stolen), and __inet_lookup then sets it true for an established match and false for a listener match or NULL. The caller needs the RCU protection that skb_dst_dev_net_rcu requires.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose said a stolen socket is returned only if prefetched; the code returns any non-NULL non-error stolen socket (include/net/inet_hashtables.h __inet_lookup_skb). Tail of the function was cut in the slice; read from the header.

name: key32_to_tunnel_id
prose: Converts a 32-bit big-endian tunnel key into the 64-bit big-endian tunnel id: on a big-endian build it returns (__force __be64)key, i.e. the numeric value of key zero-extended; on a little-endian build it returns the numeric value (u64)key << 32, so the key sits in the upper 32 bits of the 64-bit value and the low 32 bits are zero. No state is touched.
note: Reviewer mixed. Rounds 1 and 2 objected to earlier wordings; the current text matches scratch-dump lines 1627-1631 (#ifdef __BIG_ENDIAN: (__be64)key, else (u64)key << 32). Round 15 was right that the contract (either result on any host) was too weak; contract removed because endianness cannot be stated in it.

name: __netif_txq_completed_wake
prose: Function-like macro, a GNU statement expression of type int; its arguments (including get_desc, pkts and down_cond) may be evaluated more than once. It first calls netdev_txq_completed_mb(txq, pkts, bytes) unconditionally, which reports the completion to BQL (netdev_tx_completed_queue) when CONFIG_BQL is enabled and otherwise does an smp_mb() if bytes != 0. It then sets _res = -1, and only if pkts is nonzero and get_desc >= start_thrs does it set _res = 1 and, if netif_tx_queue_stopped(txq) and !(down_cond), call netif_tx_wake_queue(txq) and set _res = 0. The value is 0 if the queue was woken, 1 if pkts was nonzero and get_desc reached start_thrs but the queue was not woken (already running or down_cond true), and -1 if pkts is 0 or get_desc < start_thrs.
note: Reviewer right: the old prose said -1 only when start_thrs was not reached; the code also gives -1 when pkts == 0. Macro; contract dropped (it did not type-check).

Without CONFIG_RV_REACTORS the generated body is just return, doing nothing. Returns void.
note: Old prose described only the CONFIG_RV_REACTORS variant; the #else variant added.

name: da_event_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon, enum events_##name event)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_MODEL_HANDLER_IMPLICIT as da_event_<name>(da_mon, event), returning bool. It reads da_mon->curr_state with READ_ONCE, then up to MAX_DA_RETRY_RACING_EVENTS times: next_state = model_get_next_state_<name>(curr_state, event). If that is INVALID_STATE it calls cond_react_<name>, calls trace_error_<name> with the state and event names, and returns false without changing the state. Otherwise it tries try_cmpxchg(&da_mon->curr_state, &curr_state, next_state); if that succeeds it calls trace_event_<name> with the old state name, event name, new state name and whether the new state is final, and returns true. If the compare-and-exchange fails, curr_state is refreshed with the current value and the loop retries. After all retries fail it calls trace_rv_retries_error and pr_warn (whose text says the monitor is reset, but no reset is performed here) and returns false.
note: Checked against scratch-dump lines 2031-2058; there is no da_monitor_reset call in the function.

name: da_event_##name(struct da_monitor *da_mon, struct task_struct *tsk, enum events_##name event)
prose: Generated by DECLARE_DA_MON_MODEL_HANDLER_PER_TASK as da_event_<name>(da_mon, tsk, event), returning bool. It does the same as the implicit variant: READ_ONCE of da_mon->curr_state, then up to MAX_DA_RETRY_RACING_EVENTS attempts of next_state = model_get_next_state_<name>(curr_state, event); on INVALID_STATE it calls cond_react_<name> and trace_error_<name>(tsk->pid, state name, event name) and returns false with no state change; on a successful try_cmpxchg of curr_state it calls trace_event_<name>(tsk->pid, old state, event, new state, is-final) and returns true; a failed compare-and-exchange retries with the refreshed state. After all retries fail it calls trace_rv_retries_error and pr_warn (whose text says the monitor is reset, but no reset is performed) and returns false. tsk is used only for tsk->pid in the traces.

name: snd_hdac_regmap_encode_verb
prose: Function-like macro: expands to (((verb) << 8) | 0x80000 | ((unsigned int)(nid) << 20)). It puts the verb shifted left by 8 bits, the constant bit 0x80000 (bit 19) and the NID shifted left by 20 bits into one pseudo register value. The NID is cast to unsigned int first, so the result is unsigned int; the verb is not cast. Neither argument is masked or range checked, so a verb wider than 12 bits or a NID wider than 12 bits would overlap other fields.
note: Macro; no contract (earlier ones failed on bit operations). The old prose assumed nid < 256 and verb < 65536; the macro enforces neither, and the field widths implied by the shifts are not those numbers.

name: snd_hdac_regmap_encode_amp
prose: Function-like macro: expands to snd_hdac_regmap_encode_verb(nid, AC_VERB_GET_AMP_GAIN_MUTE) | ((ch) ? AC_AMP_GET_RIGHT : AC_AMP_GET_LEFT) | ((dir) == HDA_OUTPUT ? AC_AMP_GET_OUTPUT : AC_AMP_GET_INPUT) | (idx). So the pseudo register for the amp gain/mute get verb of NID nid, with the right-channel bit if ch is nonzero (else the left-channel bit), the output bit if dir equals HDA_OUTPUT (else the input bit), and idx ORed in unchanged. idx is not masked or range checked.
note: Macro; the old contract hard-coded numeric constants (0x843, 0x4000, 0x8000) instead of the AC_* names; dropped.

name: snd_hdac_regmap_encode_amp_stereo
prose: Function-like macro: expands to snd_hdac_regmap_encode_verb(nid, AC_VERB_GET_AMP_GAIN_MUTE) | AC_AMP_SET_LEFT | AC_AMP_SET_RIGHT | ((dir) == HDA_OUTPUT ? AC_AMP_GET_OUTPUT : AC_AMP_GET_INPUT) | (idx). It is the same encoding as snd_hdac_regmap_encode_amp but sets both the left and the right amp bits (AC_AMP_SET_LEFT and AC_AMP_SET_RIGHT) instead of selecting one channel. idx is not masked or range checked.
note: Macro; the old contract hard-coded numeric constants; dropped.

When the tracing core's probe is attached, the entry it writes is filled by the event's TP_fast_assign, which records rc, sport = ntohs(uh->source) and dport = ntohs(uh->dest) where uh = udp_hdr(skb), family = sk->sk_family, and two zero-initialised sockaddr_in6-sized byte arrays saddr and daddr that TP_STORE_ADDR_PORTS_SKB then fills: if CONFIG_IPV6 is enabled and the network header version of skb is 6, as sockaddr_in6 values (family AF_INET6, the UDP source and destination ports as stored in the header, and ipv6_hdr(skb) source and destination addresses), otherwise as sockaddr_in values taken from ip_hdr(skb). skb must have a valid UDP header and network header and sk must be non-NULL.
note: Unreviewed before (mechanical name-only rejections). The old prose described a 'data' or '__data' first argument that the wrapper does not have (that is the probe's signature), and put the record contents into the wrapper; rewritten from include/linux/tracepoint.h (__DECLARE_TRACE) plus the event's TP_STRUCT__entry/TP_fast_assign. The old item was dropped with a one-line prose; rewritten.
