It finally checks, with EXPECT_EQ (failures are recorded, not fatal), that opening s1d41/f1 through the fd returns variant->expected_read_result, renaming s1d41/f1 to s1d42/f1 returns expected_rename_result, exchanging s1d41/f2 with s1d42/f3 returns expected_exchange_result, and renaming s1d42/f4 to s1d42/f5 returns expected_same_dir_rename_result.

name: TEST_F(protocol, bind_unspec)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(protocol, bind_unspec) (net_test.c:796-885); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture provides self->srv0 (a service with a port) and the unspec_any0 and unspec_srv0 address templates; variant describes the protocol domain/type and whether the TCP sandbox (variant->sandbox == TCP_SANDBOX) is active. Postcondition: when the sandbox is TCP_SANDBOX it creates a ruleset handling LANDLOCK_ACCESS_NET_BIND_TCP, adds a rule allowing bind on srv0.port (ASSERT_EQ 0) and enforces it. It opens a socket (ASSERT_LE) and expects, as EXPECT_EQ checks that only record failures, a bind with an address length one byte short to return -EINVAL and a bind to AF_UNSPEC/INADDR_ANY to return 0 for AF_INET, -EAFNOSUPPORT for AF_INET6 and -EINVAL for any other domain (this first bind is allowed by the rule, so it does not depend on whether the protocol is restricted), then closes the socket. When sandboxed it enforces a second ruleset handling bind with no rule (bind denied), opens a fresh socket, and expects the same AF_UNSPEC/INADDR_ANY bind to return -EACCES for AF_INET when the protocol is restricted and 0 when it is not, -EAFNOSUPPORT for AF_INET6 and -EINVAL otherwise, then closes it. Finally, with a third fresh socket, it expects a bind with AF_UNSPEC and the loopback address to return -EAFNOSUPPORT for AF_INET and AF_INET6 and -EINVAL otherwise, and closes it.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); corrected: the first bind (with the allow rule enforced) expects 0 for AF_INET, not -EACCES for a restricted protocol (net_test.c:829-840); the -EACCES/0 split applies only to the second, denied, bind (857-863). Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(protocol, connect_unspec)
prose: Precondition: the fixture provides a valid srv0 endpoint and the unspec_any0 sockaddr template, and variant describes the protocol domain/type and whether the TCP sandbox is active. Postcondition: the parent binds a socket to srv0 (listening with backlog for SOCK_STREAM) and forks a child that closes the listening descriptor, connects a new socket to srv0, expects a second connect to return -EISCONN for SOCK_STREAM and 0 otherwise, when sandboxed installs, enforces and closes a ruleset allowing LANDLOCK_ACCESS_NET_CONNECT_TCP on srv0.port, expects a connect to unspec_any0 to return -EINVAL for AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM and 0 otherwise, expects a reconnect to srv0 to return -EISCONN for AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM and 0 otherwise, when sandboxed installs, enforces and closes an empty ruleset denying connect, expects a connect with a truncated address length to return -EINVAL and a connect with a minimal AF_UNSPEC sockaddr to return -EINVAL for AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM and 0 otherwise, then closes the socket and exits with _metadata->exit_code; the parent accepts a connection for SOCK_STREAM, waits for the child, asserts it exited normally with EXIT_SUCCESS, closes the accepted and listening descriptors, and returns void, recording mismatches only as test failures.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); prose re-checked against net_test.c:887-1009 and kept; named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function)

name: TEST_F(protocol, tcp_fastopen)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(protocol, tcp_fastopen) (net_test.c:1011-1106); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture provides self->srv0; variant describes the protocol and whether the TCP sandbox is active; 'restricted' is true only for TCP_SANDBOX with a SOCK_STREAM TCP/IP protocol on AF_INET or AF_INET6. Postcondition: the parent binds a socket to srv0 and listens when it is a stream socket, then forks a child. The child closes the listening socket, opens a socket and, when sandboxed, enforces a ruleset handling LANDLOCK_ACCESS_NET_CONNECT_TCP with no rule (connect denied). It sends with MSG_FASTOPEN and no address and expects -ENOTCONN for AF_UNIX, -EDESTADDRREQ for datagram sockets and -EINVAL otherwise; then sends 'A' with MSG_FASTOPEN to srv0 and expects -EACCES when restricted, -EOPNOTSUPP for AF_UNIX stream sockets and 0 otherwise; it closes the socket and exits with _metadata->exit_code. The parent accepts a connection when the protocol is an unrestricted non-AF_UNIX stream; reads one byte from the accepted (or the bound) socket expecting -1/ENOTCONN when restricted, -1/EINVAL for AF_UNIX stream, and otherwise one byte equal to 'A'; waits for the child and expects a normal exit with EXIT_SUCCESS, closes the accepted socket if distinct, and closes the bound socket. All checks are EXPECT_* (failures are recorded) except the socket creation ASSERTs.
note: slice cut; the dropped item had a one-line truncated prose; written from net_test.c:1011-1106. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc/argv are the command line: argv[1] is the path of a file on the fuse_mnt mount (a FUSE file whose read is delayed by 1 s) and the optional argv[2] is 'hugetlbfs'. Postcondition (main, fuse_test.c:228-331; slice cut the head): it prints a message and calls abort() if argc < 2, if argv[2] is given and is not 'hugetlbfs', or (for 'hugetlbfs') if the default huge page size cannot be determined; with 'hugetlbfs' it sets the memfd size to twice the huge page size. It allocates a zero-filled comparison buffer with calloc (the result is not checked), opens argv[1] read-only (abort() on failure), creates a sealable memfd of that size and maps it shared (the mfd_assert_* helpers abort on failure), and starts a sealing thread that, after 200 ms, unmaps the mapping and tries to add F_SEAL_WRITE (expecting it to fail while the FUSE read is pending and succeed after one more second). It then read()s the FUSE file into the memfd mapping, aborting if read fails or returns 0, records whether F_SEAL_WRITE was already set, waits for the sealing thread and asserts that the memfd has F_SEAL_WRITE. It maps the memfd privately and aborts if the memfd was sealed during the read but its data is not all zero, or if it was not sealed but its data is all zero. Otherwise it closes the memfd and the file descriptor, prints 'fuse: DONE', frees the comparison buffer and returns 0. Every checked failure ends in abort(); the only unchecked failure is the calloc result.
note: slice cut the head. Reviewer (round15) right: the calloc result is not checked (fuse_test.c:258), so not every failure path aborts; the rest of the old prose re-read against fuse_test.c:228-331 and kept in substance.

Postcondition: it asserts that the pagemap entry of each of the 10 pages has PM_GUARD_REGION clear before any guard is installed, then installs a guard region with MADV_GUARD_INSTALL on each even-indexed page and asserts that the pagemap entry has PM_GUARD_REGION set exactly for the even-indexed pages and clear for the odd-indexed pages, and finally closes the pagemap file descriptor and unmaps the 10-page mapping; any failed assertion aborts the test immediately, in which case the close and munmap may be skipped.

Postcondition: the function returns true if and only if every one of the first size bytes at buf equals chr (trivially true when size is 0) and false otherwise; it does not modify the buffer and does not acquire, release or leave behind any lock, reference or allocation.

name: TEST_F(guard_regions, split_merge)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(guard_regions, split_merge) (guard-regions.c:701-829); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture is set up and the mmap_ helper can create a 10-page PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE mapping. Postcondition: it maps 10 pages, installs guards over the whole range and asserts that all ten pages fault on read/write. It unmaps pages 2, 5 and 8 (splitting the VMA) and asserts that the remaining pages (0-1, 3-4, 6-7, 9) are still guarded; it maps pages 2, 5 and 8 again with MAP_FIXED and asserts that exactly those three pages are now readable and writable (the unmap cleared their guards). It installs guards over the whole range again and asserts that all ten fault; it splits the VMA with mprotect(PROT_READ) on pages 0-2 and 7-9 and asserts that all ten are still unreadable, restores PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE on them and asserts that all ten still fault for read/write; it splits again, removes all guards with MADV_GUARD_REMOVE and asserts that all ten pages are readable, merges again with mprotect(PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE) and asserts that all ten are readable and writable. It ends with munmap of the 10 pages. Every check is an ASSERT_*, which stops the test on failure.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); the old prose stopped after the remapping step (guard-regions.c:748-757) although the test continues with the re-guard, mprotect split/merge and GUARD_REMOVE checks through line 828; rewritten. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(hmm, anon_teardown)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(hmm, anon_teardown) (hmm-tests.c:1413-1469); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->fd is open on the dmirror device and self->page_size and page_shift are set. Postcondition: it computes npages from HMM_BUFFER_SIZE and then repeats NTIMES times: it allocates an hmm_buffer and its mirror with malloc (ASSERT_NE NULL), maps npages anonymous private pages and fills them with ptr[i] == i + c (c is the iteration number), and only then creates a thread running unmap_buffer, which sleeps for a pseudo-random time (below 32 ms), unmaps the second half of the buffer and sets buffer->ptr to NULL. Concurrently it issues HMM_DMIRROR_READ on the buffer; if that returns 0 it asserts that cpages equals npages, faults equals 1 and every mirror entry equals i + c, and if it returns nonzero it makes no further checks. In both cases it joins the thread and frees the buffer and mirror with hmm_buffer_free. Failures of the ASSERT_* checks stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the buffer is filled before the thread is created (hmm-tests.c:1446-1450); the thread only sleeps and then unmaps the second half concurrently with the device read. Named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function).

name: TEST_F(hmm, exclusive)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(hmm, exclusive) (hmm-tests.c:1784-1836); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the fixture is initialized (self->fd open on the dmirror device, page_size and page_shift set) and the dmirror device supports exclusive access. Postcondition: it allocates an hmm_buffer and its mirror (ASSERT_NE NULL), maps npages anonymous private pages and fills them with ptr[i] = i; it maps them exclusively for the device with HMM_DMIRROR_EXCLUSIVE (ASSERT_EQ 0 and cpages == npages) and asserts that the device mirror holds i. It then faults the pages back by reading and incrementing each entry in system memory (asserting the old value i), asserts every entry is now i + 1, asserts that HMM_DMIRROR_CHECK_EXCLUSIVE returns 0 (the device's exclusive access has been revoked) and frees the buffer with hmm_buffer_free. A failed ASSERT_* runs the harness teardown and aborts the test process (it does not return from the body), so the buffer is not freed on that path.
note: reviewer (round15) right: a failed ASSERT_* calls __bail, which runs the teardown and abort()s (kselftest_harness.h:962-972), it does not return early from the body. Named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function).

name: TEST_F(hmm, exclusive_mprotect)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(hmm, exclusive_mprotect) (hmm-tests.c:1838-1886); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the fixture is initialized (self->fd open on the dmirror device, page_size and page_shift set) and the dmirror device supports exclusive access. Postcondition: it allocates an hmm_buffer and mirror, maps npages anonymous private pages filled with ptr[i] = i, maps them exclusively with HMM_DMIRROR_EXCLUSIVE (ASSERT_EQ 0, cpages == npages) and asserts that the mirror holds i. It then calls mprotect(PROT_READ) on the whole mapping (asserted to return 0), asserts that a device write with HMM_DMIRROR_WRITE returns -EPERM, and frees the buffer with hmm_buffer_free. A failed ASSERT_* runs the harness teardown and aborts the test process (it does not return from the body), so the buffer is not freed on that path.
note: reviewer (round15) right (same reason as hmm_exclusive): failed ASSERT_* aborts the process. Named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function).

name: TEST_F(hmm, exclusive_cow)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(hmm, exclusive_cow) (hmm-tests.c:1891-1966); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the fixture is initialized (self->fd open on the dmirror device, page_size and page_shift set) and the dmirror device supports exclusive access. Postcondition: it allocates an hmm_buffer and mirror, maps npages anonymous private pages filled with ptr[i] = i and maps them exclusively with HMM_DMIRROR_EXCLUSIVE (ASSERT_EQ 0, cpages == npages). It forks (a failed fork fails ASSERT_EQ(pid, 0)). The child increments every entry asserting the old value i, asserts every entry is i + 1 and calls _exit(0) without running the test teardown; if one of its assertions fails, the harness aborts the child. The parent does the same increment-and-verify on its own copy, then waits for the child (ASSERT_EQ(waitpid, pid)), asserts that it exited normally (WIFEXITED) with status 0, and frees the buffer. A failed ASSERT_* in the parent runs the harness teardown and aborts the test process (it does not return from the body), so the buffer is not freed on that path.
note: reviewer (round15) right: a failed ASSERT_* (parent or child) aborts via __bail rather than returning early (kselftest_harness.h:962-972; hmm-tests.c:1934-1938 comment says the same for the child). Named by the TEST_F invocation (generated function).

name: main
prose: Precondition: the program runs on a Linux system with hugetlb support; argv[0] is used as the memfd_create name. Postcondition (main, hugetlb-madvise.c:60-367; slice cut the head): it reads the default huge page size and calls exit(1) with a message if it is 0 (the following 'base page size' check repeats the test of huge_page_size, so a zero base page size is not detected); it reads the number of free huge pages and calls exit(KSFT_SKIP) if fewer than MIN_FREE_PAGES (20) are free; it creates a hugetlb memfd (exit(1) on failure). It then runs a sequence of tests of MADV_DONTNEED, MADV_REMOVE, fallocate and fallocate(PUNCH_HOLE) on anonymous and memfd hugetlb mappings (NR_HUGE_PAGES = 10 pages each), after each step comparing the free huge page count with the expected value through validate_free_pages, which prints a message and calls exit(1) on a mismatch. Each mmap, the paired munmap calls at the beginning, each madvise and fallocate call whose success or failure is being tested prints a message and calls exit(1) when the result is not the expected one. The intermediate cleanups and the final two munmap calls are written '(void)munmap(...)' and close(fd) is called without checking, so a failure of those calls does not change the outcome. If every check passes it returns 0.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the (void)munmap calls (hugetlb-madvise.c:133, 170, 195, 254, 294, 362-363) and the final close(fd) (365) are not checked, so main can return 0 even if they fail; the old prose said it returns 0 only if every syscall succeeded. Slice cut the head; real function main.

name: main
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: main never returns to its caller; it sets a 9-test plan, obtains a free base address via find_base_addr (whose mmap or munmap failure exits with a failure message without dumping maps), then runs eight MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE mmap checks that require success for the 5-page mapping at base, the 3-page mapping at base+page_size, and the 1-page mappings at base and base+4*page_size, and require MAP_FAILED (without checking errno) for the 5-page mapping at base, the 1-page mapping at base+2*page_size, the 2-page mapping at base+3*page_size, and the 2-page mapping at base, dumping the process maps and exiting with failure on any unexpected mmap result or on any munmap failure in main, then performs the ninth check by munmapping the 5-page base range (dumping maps and exiting with failure if that munmap fails), and finally calls ksft_finished, which exits the process with overall success if all checks passed.
note: prose re-checked against map_fixed_noreplace.c:41-201 (8 mmap calls, 2 of main's own munmap calls, find_base_addr failure paths, ksft_finished exit) and kept; reviewer points from rounds 0/2 (errno not checked; 9th check is munmap; find_base_addr exits without dump_maps) are already in the prose. Contract dropped: main exits through ksft_finished and touches the process address space, outside method rule 4.

name: TEST_F(mdwe, mprotect_WRITE_EXEC)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mdwe, mprotect_WRITE_EXEC) (mdwe_test.c:259-272); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture setup has set self->size and self->flags and, for enabled variants, the memory-deny-write-execute prctl state (executable_map_should_fail(variant) is variant->enabled && (!variant->forked || variant->inherit)). Postcondition: it maps self->size bytes of PROT_WRITE memory into self->p (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED, which stops the test on failure), then calls mprotect(self->p, self->size, PROT_WRITE | PROT_EXEC) and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_LT or EXPECT_EQ) unless the result is negative when executable_map_should_fail(variant) is true, or 0 when it is false. The mapping stays in self->p and is unmapped by the fixture teardown.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against mdwe_test.c:168-171 and 259-272; the prose is kept in substance, with the gtest-style 'TestBody' wording replaced by the real TEST_F-generated function. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(mdwe, mmap_FIXED)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mdwe, mmap_FIXED) (mdwe_test.c:274-285); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture setup has set self->size and self->flags. Postcondition: it maps self->size bytes of PROT_READ memory into self->p (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), then maps self->size bytes at the same address with PROT_READ | PROT_EXEC and flags | MAP_FIXED, replacing the existing mapping, and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_EQ) unless the returned address equals self->p. self->p is unchanged and the mapping is unmapped by the fixture teardown.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against mdwe_test.c:274-285; kept in substance. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(mdwe, arm64_BTI)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mdwe, arm64_BTI) (mdwe_test.c:287-301); it takes _metadata, the fixture self and the variant, and returns void. Precondition: the fixture setup has set self->size and self->flags. Postcondition: on a build for aarch64 it skips the test and returns if getauxval(AT_HWCAP2) does not report HWCAP2_BTI; on any other architecture the HWCAP test is compiled out and the SKIP statement (SKIP(return, "HWCAP2_BTI not supported")) then executes unconditionally, so the test always skips and returns before doing anything. When it does not skip it maps self->size bytes with PROT_EXEC into self->p (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), calls mprotect(self->p, self->size, PROT_EXEC | PROT_BTI) and records a non-fatal failure (EXPECT_EQ) unless it returns 0.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); corrected: outside __aarch64__ the SKIP is unconditional (mdwe_test.c:291-294), so the old precondition (which required HWCAP2_BTI only for aarch64 builds and implied a run elsewhere) was incomplete. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(merge, mprotect_faulted_left_unfaulted_right)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(merge, mprotect_faulted_left_unfaulted_right) (merge.c:266-323); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->carveout is a reserved address range of at least 11 pages and self->procmap is an open PROCMAP_QUERY handle. Postcondition: it maps 9 anonymous private pages (PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_NORESERVE, MAP_FIXED) at carveout + 2 * page_size (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), makes the last 3 pages read-only (splitting the VMA), faults in only the first page by writing ptr[0] = 'x' (which gives the left VMA an anon_vma), makes the first 3 pages read-only, then makes the middle 3 pages read-only too (each mprotect asserted to return 0), so that the three VMAs should merge. It then asserts through find_vma_procmap/PROCMAP_QUERY that a VMA containing ptr exists and that it spans exactly [ptr, ptr + 9 * page_size). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: only the first page (ptr[0]) is written, not the first six pages (merge.c:299); the other pages stay unfaulted. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(merge, mprotect_unfaulted_left_faulted_right)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(merge, mprotect_unfaulted_left_faulted_right) (merge.c:325-382); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->carveout is a reserved address range of at least 11 pages and self->procmap is an open PROCMAP_QUERY handle. Postcondition: it maps 9 anonymous private pages (PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE, MAP_NORESERVE, MAP_FIXED) at carveout + 2 * page_size (ASSERT_NE MAP_FAILED), makes the first 3 pages read-only (splitting the VMA), faults in only page 3 by writing ptr[3 * page_size] = 'x' (which gives the right VMA an anon_vma), makes the last 3 pages read-only, then makes the middle 3 pages read-only (each mprotect asserted to return 0), so that the three VMAs should merge. It then asserts through find_vma_procmap/PROCMAP_QUERY that a VMA containing ptr exists and spans exactly [ptr, ptr + 9 * page_size). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: only ptr[3 * page_size] is written, not the last six pages (merge.c:358). Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(merge, mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(merge, mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted) (merge.c:748-831; the packet name mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted_faulted does not exist and the slice starts mid-test); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: self->carveout is a reserved address range and self->procmap is an open PROCMAP_QUERY handle. Postcondition: it maps three 5-page anonymous private read/write areas ptr, ptr2 and ptr3 with MAP_FIXED at carveout offsets 1, 7 and 14 pages, moves ptr3 2000 pages further away and ptr2 1000 pages further away with mremap(MREMAP_MAYMOVE | MREMAP_FIXED), faults in ptr and ptr3 by writing their first byte (ptr2 stays unfaulted), moves ptr3 back to &ptr[10 * page_size] and moves ptr2 to &ptr[5 * page_size] (each mremap asserted not to fail), so that ptr and ptr2 should merge but ptr3 should stay separate. It then asserts through find_vma_procmap/PROCMAP_QUERY that the VMA containing ptr spans exactly [ptr, ptr + 10 * page_size) and that the VMA containing ptr3 spans exactly [ptr3, ptr3 + 5 * page_size). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: slice cut the head; named by the real test TEST_F(merge, mremap_unfaulted_between_faulted). The old prose (a 'still-rejected' item) described this test but called its mappings preconditions of the caller; the whole setup is in the test itself (merge.c:763-822).

name: get_sqrt
prose: Precondition: val is an unsigned long less than 1099511627776 (1TB), so that mid*mid (mid <= 2^19) fits in unsigned long and the initial high bound 2^20 covers the square root of val. Postcondition: because high is decremented unconditionally on every iteration (there is no else branch), the function returns 1 when val is 0; when val equals m*m for some power of two m (1 <= m <= 524288) it returns that m; in every other case it returns m+1, where m is the largest power of two with m*m < val and val < 4*m*m — so the result is generally not the integer square root of val.
contract: /*@ requires 0 <= val && val < 1099511627776; ensures (val == 0 ==> result == 1) && (val >= 1 ==> ((result * result == val && (result & (result - 1)) == 0) || (((result - 1) & (result - 2)) == 0 && (result - 1) * (result - 1) < val && val < 4 * (result - 1) * (result - 1)))); */
note: reviewer (round15) wrong: for val = 16 the code returns 4 (mid takes the values 2^19, 2^18, ... so mid = 4 gives temp == 16 and the function returns mid, mremap_test.c:91-92), which satisfies the first disjunct of the contract; I also simulated the loop for 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 15, 16, 17, 63, 64, 65, 1e9, 2^38, 2^38+1 and 2^40-1 and all results match the prose and the contract. Prose and contract kept.

name: syscall_raw
prose: Precondition: n is a system call number and a1..a6 are its arguments (arguments the call does not use are ignored by the kernel); the file builds only for x86_64, i386 or aarch64 (any other architecture hits an #error). Postcondition (syscall_raw, pkey_sighandler_tests.c:45-78; static inline, always inlined): it issues the system call directly with inline assembly (the 'syscall' instruction on x86_64 with a1..a6 in rdi, rsi, rdx, r10, r8, r9; 'int $0x80' on i386, where a6 is not passed; 'svc #0' on aarch64 with the number in x8) instead of going through glibc's syscall(), so no PLT or library code protected by memory protection key 0 is touched, and returns the raw value left in the return register as a long: a non-negative result, or a negative errno value as set by the kernel (errno itself is not set). The function has no other effects of its own; the effects are those of the system call (for example SYS_exit terminates the calling thread).
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:39-78; added the per-architecture argument passing and that errno is not set. Contract left empty (arbitrary system calls).

name: pkey_reg_restrictive_default
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition (pkey_reg_restrictive_default, pkey_sighandler_tests.c:103-111; static inline, returns u64): it returns set_pkey_bits(PKEY_REG_ALLOW_NONE, 0, PKEY_DISABLE_ACCESS), i.e. the architecture's 'allow nothing' protection-key register value with the access-disable setting for key 0 applied, which the tests use as their most restrictive register value (the source comment says execution on pkey 0 stays possible so callers need not enable it). It only computes a value, with no side effects.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:99-111. Contract left empty (depends on the macros PKEY_REG_ALLOW_NONE and set_pkey_bits).

name: sigsegv_handler
prose: Precondition: the function is installed as the SIGSEGV handler with SA_SIGINFO and invoked by the kernel with signo == SIGSEGV, a valid info pointer and a valid ucontext. Postcondition: it locks the global mutex, copies *info into the global siginfo, signals the global condition variable, unlocks the mutex, and then issues SYS_exit(0), so the calling thread (SYS_exit ends only the thread) terminates with status 0 and the function does not return; no locks, references or memory remain held.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:113-123 and kept; note SYS_exit ends only the calling thread

name: sigusr1_handler
prose: Precondition: the function is installed as the SIGUSR1 handler with SA_SIGINFO and invoked by the kernel with signo == SIGUSR1, a valid info pointer and a valid ucontext. Postcondition: it locks the global mutex, copies *info into the global siginfo, signals the global condition variable, unlocks the mutex, and returns normally to the interrupted thread, leaving no locks held and no memory allocated.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:125-133 and kept

name: sigusr2_handler
prose: Precondition: the function is installed as the SIGUSR2 handler with SA_SIGINFO and invoked by the kernel with signo == SIGUSR2, a valid info pointer and a valid ucontext, with the pkru register at the init_pkru value that enables MPK 0 so library calls work. Postcondition: it prints its invocation message to stdout and returns normally to the interrupted thread, leaving no locks held and no memory allocated.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:135-142 and kept

name: raise_sigusr2
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: the function obtains the caller's thread id via SYS_gettid and sends SIGUSR2 to that thread via SYS_tkill; if a SIGUSR2 handler is installed it runs and the signal returns, so this function returns normally to its caller; if no handler is installed the default disposition for SIGUSR2 terminates the process and the function does not return.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:144-156 and kept

name: thread_segv_with_pkey0_disabled
prose: Precondition: the function is run as a pthread start routine whose thread stack is accessible when it begins, and a SIGSEGV handler is installed. Postcondition: it writes the most restrictive pkey register value, disabling access on every protection key including pkey 0, and then dereferences a NULL pointer, causing a SIGSEGV with SEGV_MAPERR at address NULL that invokes the SIGSEGV handler, which copies the siginfo and terminates the thread via SYS_exit(0); the function therefore does not return in the tests (its 'return NULL' is only reached if the store does not fault).
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:158-166 and kept: the function never returns only when the SIGSEGV handler runs and ends the thread

name: thread_segv_pkuerr_stack
prose: Precondition: the function is run as a pthread start routine whose thread stack is protected by pkey 0, and a SIGSEGV handler is installed. Postcondition: it writes the most restrictive pkey register value, disabling access on every protection key including pkey 0, and then returns NULL; the test expects that returning requires accessing the now-inaccessible stack and so raises a SIGSEGV with SEGV_PKUERR that invokes the SIGSEGV handler, which copies the siginfo and terminates the thread via SYS_exit(0); the function therefore does not return in the tests (it is terminated by the handler's SYS_exit).
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:168-175 and kept; the SEGV_PKUERR outcome is what the test expects (source comment), not something the C code itself guarantees

name: thread_segv_maperr_ptr
prose: Precondition: the function is run as a pthread start routine and its ptr argument points to a valid, allocated stack_t describing an alternate signal stack that is pkey_mprotect()ed with pkey 0; a SIGSEGV handler is installed. Postcondition: it installs that alternate signal stack via the SYS_sigaltstack syscall, writes a pkey register value that disables every key except pkey 1 (so pkey 0, protecting the thread and signal stacks, is inaccessible), and then dereferences a NULL pointer, causing a SIGSEGV with SEGV_MAPERR at address NULL that invokes the SIGSEGV handler, which copies the siginfo and terminates the thread via SYS_exit(0); after the faulting store the source would call SYS_exit(0) and return NULL, but the SIGSEGV handler ends the thread first.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:177-198 and kept; added that the SYS_exit after the faulting store would run only if the fault were not delivered

name: test_sigsegv_handler_with_pkey0_disabled
prose: Precondition: none beyond a working ksft framework. Postcondition: the function installs sigsegv_handler as the SIGSEGV handler with SA_SIGINFO (if sigaction fails it prints an error and calls exit(EXIT_FAILURE), so it does not return on that path), clears the global siginfo, creates a detached thread running thread_segv_with_pkey0_disabled, waits on the global condition variable until siginfo.si_signo is non-zero, and then reports a ksft test result that passes exactly when siginfo.si_signo == SIGSEGV, siginfo.si_code == SEGV_MAPERR and siginfo.si_addr == NULL; it changes the SIGSEGV disposition, leaves the global siginfo filled with the fault's siginfo, and leaves the detached thread terminated.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against pkey_sighandler_tests.c:205-236 and kept; pthread_create's result is not checked

name: FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(migrate)
prose: Fixture teardown generated by FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(migrate) (rmap.c:195-220), void; it takes the fixture data self. Precondition: self->data was filled in by FIXTURE_SETUP(migrate) (which sets expected_pfn, semid, pipefd and backend but does not initialize data->region; the fixture data starts zeroed, so region is NULL, not MAP_FAILED, unless a test set it). Postcondition: it calls munmap(data->region, data->mapsize) if data->region is not MAP_FAILED (so also when it is still NULL, in which case munmap fails harmlessly) and sets it to MAP_FAILED; it unmaps data->expected_pfn if it is not MAP_FAILED and sets it to MAP_FAILED; it removes the semaphore set with semctl(IPC_RMID) and sets data->semid to -1; it closes the read end data->pipefd[0] (the write end is not closed here); and according to data->backend it calls shm_unlink(data->filename) for SHM, unlink(data->filename) for NORM_FILE and does nothing for ANON. Return values of these calls are ignored.
note: reviewer (round15) right: setup leaves data->region uninitialized/zero (rmap.c:159-193), so the old precondition 'region valid or MAP_FAILED' was inaccurate and region may be NULL at teardown. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: merge_and_migrate
prose: Precondition: data points to a struct global_data whose expected_pfn field points to a writable unsigned long; data->region may be any value (MAP_FAILED is handled). Postcondition (merge_and_migrate, rmap.c:389-408): it returns FAIL_ON_WORK at once if data->region is MAP_FAILED, and returns FAIL_ON_WORK if ksm_start() fails (negative result); neither case needs KSM to be available beforehand since both failures are handled. Otherwise it calls try_to_move_page(data->region) and keeps its result (0 on success or FAIL_ON_WORK), then opens /proc/self/pagemap; if that open fails it returns FAIL_ON_WORK (the try_to_move_page result is discarded), otherwise it stores the PFN of data->region read from pagemap in *data->expected_pfn and returns the try_to_move_page result. The pagemap descriptor is opened only after the page was moved and is never closed (leaked).
note: reviewer (round15) right: the function handles a MAP_FAILED region and a failing ksm_start itself (rmap.c:394-398), so the old precondition requiring a valid region and KSM was unnecessary; the pagemap descriptor leak and the ordering (move first, then pagemap) from the old prose were right and are kept.

name: uffd_wp_unpopulated_test
prose: Precondition: gopts->uffd is a valid userfaultfd and gopts->area_dst is a mapping of at least gopts->nr_pages * gopts->page_size bytes (it need not be registered; the function registers it). Postcondition (uffd_wp_unpopulated_test, uffd-unit-tests.c:338-382; returns void): it registers the whole area with uffd_register for write-protect mode (err() terminates the test on failure) and opens a pagemap descriptor (never closed). On the first page it then: write-protects it with wp_range and checks that the pagemap entry has the wp bit set; unprotects it and checks the bit is clear; write-protects it again, zaps it with MADV_DONTNEED (err() on failure) and checks the bit is clear; writes to the page (fault-in) and checks the bit is clear, then drops it with MADV_DONTNEED; write-protects it again, reads it (the read of the zero page, with no pagemap check) and drops it with MADV_DONTNEED. It ends with uffd_test_pass(). The range stays registered and the pagemap descriptor stays open.
note: reviewer (round15) right: no pagemap check follows the read-zero-page step (uffd-unit-tests.c:374-379); the wp bit is checked after protect, unprotect, zap and fault-in only. Round-0 reviewer's point (the function registers the area itself) was already right in the old prose.

name: uffd_wp_fork_pin_test_common
prose: Precondition: gopts->uffd is a valid userfaultfd and gopts->area_dst is a mapping of at least gopts->page_size bytes (the function registers the first page itself); with_event selects whether fork events are used in the child checks. Postcondition (uffd_wp_fork_pin_test_common, uffd-unit-tests.c:464-515; returns void): it registers the first page for write-protect mode (err() on failure), opens a pagemap descriptor, touches the page and write-protects it. It tries to pin the page (pin_pages): if that fails it marks the test skipped, closes the pagemap descriptor, calls uffd_unregister (its result is ignored on this path) and returns. Otherwise it runs pagemap_test_fork(gopts, with_event, false) (fork after pinning, the early-copy path); if that reports a wrong child wp bit it calls uffd_test_fail, unpins and goes to the out label; otherwise it unpins and runs pagemap_test_fork(gopts, with_event, true) (pin in the child); a failure there calls uffd_test_fail and goes to out, and success calls uffd_test_pass. At out it unregisters the page (err() terminates the test if that fails) and closes the pagemap descriptor.
note: reviewer (round15) right: on the skip path the uffd_unregister result is not checked (uffd-unit-tests.c:488), so 'on every path it unregisters the page, aborting via err() if that fails' was too broad; round-0 reviewer's point (it registers the area itself) was already right.

name: default_huge_page_size
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition (default_huge_page_size, vm_util.c:294-313): if /proc/meminfo cannot be opened it returns 0 immediately (nothing has been allocated or opened at that point). Otherwise it reads the file line by line with getline until the first line that matches 'Hugepagesize: <number> kB', takes that number shifted left by 10 (kB to bytes) as the result and stops reading; if no line matches the result is 0. On every path that opened the file it frees the getline buffer and closes the stream before returning the result.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong in substance but right on precision: on fopen failure there is no buffer to free and no stream to close (line is NULL, f is NULL, vm_util.c:297-302), so the old prose is true on the paths that opened the file; the prose now states the early return explicitly.

name: get_free_hugepages
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition (get_free_hugepages, vm_util.c:399-416): if /proc/meminfo cannot be opened it returns 0 immediately (nothing has been allocated or opened at that point). Otherwise it reads the file line by line with getline until the first line that matches 'HugePages_Free: <number>', stores that number as the result and stops reading; if no line matches the result is 0. On every path that opened the file it frees the getline buffer and closes the stream before returning the result.
note: reviewer (round15) wrong in substance but right on precision: nothing is allocated or opened when fopen fails (vm_util.c:402-407); the prose now states the early return explicitly.

name: FIXTURE_SETUP(mount_setattr_idmapped)
prose: Fixture setup generated by FIXTURE_SETUP(mount_setattr_idmapped) (mount_setattr_test.c:994-1052; the packet slices split it at line 1024), void. Precondition: the process can unshare a mount namespace and mount filesystems (CAP_SYS_ADMIN); /tmp, /mnt and the tools mkfs.ext4 and mount exist. Postcondition: it unshares CLONE_NEWNS and makes / recursively private (ASSERT_EQ 0 each), lazily unmounts /mnt and /tmp (results ignored), then mounts a tmpfs (NOATIME, NODEV, size=100000, mode=700) on /tmp and creates /tmp/B with a root-owned regular file /tmp/B/b, mounts a tmpfs on /tmp/B, creates /tmp/B/BB with a root-owned file /tmp/B/BB/b and mounts a tmpfs on /tmp/B/BB. It mounts a tmpfs (size=256m, mode=700) on /mnt and creates /mnt/A with a tmpfs mounted on it, /mnt/A/AA with a recursive bind mount of /tmp on it, /mnt/B with a ramfs mounted on it (NOATIME, NODEV, NOSUID) and /mnt/B/BB (just a directory), mounts a read-only devpts (RELATIME, NOEXEC, RDONLY) on /tmp/B/BB (not on /mnt/B/BB), creates /mnt/C and /mnt/D, creates /mnt/C/ext4.img of 2 GiB, formats it with mkfs.ext4 and loop-mounts it as ext4 on /mnt/D through system() calls (each asserted to return 0), and closes the image descriptor. Every step except the two umount2 calls is an ASSERT, so a failure aborts the test instead of returning.
note: reviewer (round15) right: devpts is mounted at /tmp/B/BB (mount_setattr_test.c:1041), not /mnt/B/BB, and /tmp/B/BB is first a tmpfs and then a devpts is mounted over it; /mnt/B/BB is only a directory. Named by the macro invocation (method rule 5).

name: TEST_F(mount_setattr, mount_detached_mount_on_detached_mount_and_attach)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mount_setattr, mount_detached_mount_on_detached_mount_and_attach) (mount_setattr_test.c:1817-1864); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the mount_setattr fixture setup has built its mount layout (a testing tmpfs on /mnt, /mnt/A with its tree, /mnt/B a ramfs, /tmp/B a tmpfs) and /tmp/target1 exists. Postcondition: it opens a detached (non-recursive) clone of /mnt (fd_tree_base) and asserts through statx that its subdirectory A is not a mount root; it opens a second detached clone from fd_tree_base itself (fd_tree_subdir, with AT_EMPTY_PATH) and makes the same check. It moves fd_tree_subdir onto fd_tree_base with move_mount (asserted to succeed), asserts that fd_tree_subdir is now a mount root with a unique mount id and records that id, and asserts that a second identical move_mount fails. It then attaches fd_tree_base to /tmp/target1 (asserted to succeed) and asserts that /tmp/target1 is a mount root whose unique mount id equals the recorded id. Finally it closes both tree fds (EXPECT_EQ 0, recorded failures only). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: unreviewed (round15 fixed-unreviewed); re-read against mount_setattr_test.c:1817-1864; added the statx checks and made clear that the second clone is made from the first descriptor. Named by the TEST_F invocation.

name: TEST_F(mount_setattr, basic_recursive)
prose: Test function generated by TEST_F(mount_setattr, basic_recursive) (mount_setattr_test.c:565-657); it takes _metadata and the fixture self and returns void. Precondition: the mount_setattr fixture built its layout (/mnt/A, /mnt/A/AA, /mnt/A/AA/B, /mnt/A/AA/B/BB); if the mount_setattr syscall is not supported the test skips and returns. Postcondition: it reads the flags of /mnt/A, then calls sys_mount_setattr on /mnt/A with AT_RECURSIVE setting RDONLY, NOEXEC and RELATIME and clearing the atime bits (ASSERT_EQ 0), and asserts that all four mounts have the expected flags. It then calls it again recursively with only MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY cleared and propagation MS_SHARED (ASSERT_EQ 0) and asserts that all four mounts have the expected flags without RDONLY and are shared. It opens /mnt/A/AA/B/b for writing (O_CREAT | O_EXCL), calls the recursive setattr once more with attr_set = MOUNT_ATTR_RDONLY and asserts that it fails (return < 0, because a writer is open) and that the flags and shared state of all four mounts are unchanged, then closes the file (EXPECT_EQ 0). ASSERT_* failures stop the test.
note: reviewer (round15) right: the RDONLY-clearing/MS_SHARED call succeeds before the file is opened, and the call made while the file is open must fail (mount_setattr_test.c:600-634); the old prose had the order reversed.

name: main
prose: Precondition: argc is 1 or 2 (any other count is treated like the default case, because only argc == 2 selects a queue name); argv[1], if given, is the message-queue name. Postcondition (main, mq_open_tests.c:239-502; slice cut the head; it never returns): it chooses the queue path: the default path, or argv[1] (with a leading '/' added when missing; a malloc failure calls exit(1) and the result of strdup is not checked). If the user is not root it calls ksft_exit_skip, which exits. It opens the msg_max and msgsize_max /proc/sys files (and the default-setting files when present); if msg_max or msgsize_max cannot be opened it calls shutdown(2, ...). It saves the current sysctl values and RLIMIT_MSGQUEUE (the helpers it uses call shutdown with a nonzero status on read, write or rlimit errors), prints the initial and the adjusted system state, and runs test series 1 (mq_open without an attr struct, with different cases depending on whether default settings are supported) and test series 2 (mq_open with attr structs that exceed limits, first with euid 0 and then, after seteuid(99), with euid 99; a failing seteuid(99) calls exit(1) directly), printing PASS or FAIL lines; the test_queue helpers call shutdown(1, ...) if an mq call fails unexpectedly. It ends with shutdown(0, "", 0), which restores euid 0, closes and unlinks the queue, restores the saved sysctl and rlimit values and calls exit(0); a nonzero shutdown status instead reports the error with error(status, ...) and exits with that status.
note: slice cut the head. Reviewer (round15) right: the early fopen failures call shutdown(2, ...) and other helper failures call shutdown(1/4-7, ...) (mq_open_tests.c:123-213, 279-281), so main does not always end in shutdown(0); the old prose also implied exit(1) for 'seteuid or malloc' only.

name: TEST(nsfs_user_time_namespace_isolation)
prose: Test function generated by TEST(nsfs_user_time_namespace_isolation) (file_handle_test.c:1226-1373; the packet name nsfs_open_by_handle_from_user_ns does not exist and the slice starts mid-test); it takes _metadata and returns void. Precondition: the kernel provides time namespaces and nsfs file handles, otherwise the test skips and returns (after freeing the handle and closing its descriptors). Postcondition: it allocates a file handle (ASSERT_NE NULL), creates a pipe, opens /proc/self/ns/time and gets its handle with name_to_handle_at (EOPNOTSUPP skips; any other failure fails ASSERT_EQ(ret, 0)), then forks. The child unshares a user namespace, maps the current uid and gid to 0 (after writing 'deny' to setgroups), unshares a time namespace, forks a grandchild and waits for it, then exits 0; if the user-namespace unshare fails it writes 'U' to the pipe, if opening or writing the maps fails it writes 'M' (the write calls themselves are unchecked), if the time-namespace unshare or the inner fork fails it writes 'N', and exits 0 in each of those cases. The grandchild calls open_by_handle_at on the parent's time-namespace handle and writes 'S' if that unexpectedly succeeds, 'P' if it fails with ESTALE and 'F' for any other error, then exits 0. The parent closes the write end, reads one byte (ASSERT_EQ 1), reaps the child and asserts that it exited normally with status 0, skips on 'U', 'M' or 'N', and otherwise asserts that the byte is 'P'. It then closes the pipe and frees the handle.
note: slice cut the head; real test is TEST(nsfs_user_time_namespace_isolation); the old prose was essentially right (it also correctly listed the 'U'/'M'/'N' skips) and is expanded with the setup and parent-side checks.

The return values are ignored.

name: main
prose: Test program entry point (cmsg_sender.c:470-583); the packet slice cut the head, so the function is main, not send_packets. Parameters argc and argv are handed to cs_parse_args, which fills the global opt (cs_parse_args can exit the process on bad arguments). It then malloc()s opt.size bytes (the result is not checked) and fills them with memrnd, resolves opt.host/opt.service with getaddrinfo (hints.ai_family = opt.sock.family), and, if the result is AF_INET6 and the protocol is IPPROTO_ICMP, switches opt.sock.proto to IPPROTO_ICMPV6. It opens a socket(ai_family, opt.sock.type, opt.sock.proto). For ICMP/ICMPv6 it sets buf[0] to the echo-request type and buf[1] to 0; for another protocol on a SOCK_RAW socket it copies a udphdr built from {1, 2, htons(opt.size), 0} into buf and overwrites the sin6_port of ai_addr (cast to sockaddr_in6) with htons(opt.sock.proto). It then calls ca_set_sockopts(fd), reads CLOCK_REALTIME and CLOCK_MONOTONIC (a failure calls error(ERN_GETTIME, ...), which terminates the process), builds one iovec/msghdr addressed to ai_addr, calls cs_write_cmsg, and loops opt.num_pkt times calling sendmsg (MSG_MORE if opt.msg_more). Return values: ERN_SOCK_CREATE if getaddrinfo fails (jumping to err_free_buff, so only buf is freed; note the code uses ERN_SOCK_CREATE for the resolve failure and ERN_RESOLVE for the socket failure); ERN_RESOLVE if socket() fails (freeaddrinfo and free, no close); ERN_SEND if sendmsg returns a negative value; ERN_SEND_SHORT if sendmsg returns a value different from (int)opt.size; ERN_SEND_MORE if the follow-up write(fd, NULL, 0) returns a negative value (all three close fd, then free ai and buf); otherwise ERN_SUCCESS (0), after an optional loop of up to 40 iterations of cs_read_cmsg (stopping early when the SCM_TSTAMP_SND bit is seen, else usleep(opt.txtime.delay / 20)) when opt.ts.ena is set, then close, freeaddrinfo, free. Not covered: the malloc result is not checked, and cs_parse_args, ca_set_sockopts, cs_write_cmsg and cs_read_cmsg can end the process through error().
note: Slice cut the head; function is main at cmsg_sender.c:470 (the old prose called it send_packets and said clock_gettime failure never returned, which holds, but the ERN code mapping of the two early failures is swapped relative to their names: lines 494 and 504). No reviewer claim to check (mechanical rejection only).

name: TEST_F(epoll_busy_poll, test_set_invalid)
prose: Test body (epoll_busy_poll.c:166-267; the slice started at line 255 and showed only its tail, so test_invalid_params is not a separate function). It uses the fixture's epoll fd, params struct and capability state, and records non-fatal EXPECT_* failures rather than aborting. Steps in order: (1) zero self->params, set __pad = 1, ioctl(fd, EPIOCSPARAMS, &params) and expect -1 with errno EINVAL; (2) __pad = 0, busy_poll_usecs = (uint32_t)INT_MAX + 1, expect -1 / EINVAL; (3) busy_poll_usecs = 32, prefer_busy_poll = 2, expect -1 / EINVAL; (4) prefer_busy_poll = 1, busy_poll_budget = UINT16_MAX, check via cap_get_flag that CAP_NET_ADMIN is effective, then expect the ioctl to return 0; (5) clear CAP_NET_ADMIN from the effective set with cap_set_flag and cap_set_proc and expect the same ioctl to return -1 with errno EPERM; (6) restore the capability the same way, then call ioctl(fd, EPIOCSPARAMS, (struct epoll_params *)0xdeadbeef) and expect -1 with errno EFAULT. The function returns nothing; what the kernel returns is asserted by the test, not guaranteed by it.

name: TEST_F(epoll_busy_poll, test_set_and_get_valid)

It then zeroes the struct again, calls ioctl(fd, EPIOCGPARAMS, &params), expects return 0 and expects the struct to hold busy_poll_usecs 25, busy_poll_budget 16, prefer_busy_poll 1 and __pad 0. The checks are non-fatal EXPECT_* macros, so the test continues after a failed expectation; nothing is returned. The test does not itself set up capabilities (the fixture does).
note: Old prose did not mention that the struct is zeroed between the set and the get, or that the checks are non-fatal. No reviewer claim.

name: add_standard_tcp_options
prose: add_standard_tcp_options(buf, no_ext, ts, order) (gro.c:484-512) writes TCP option bytes after the base header and then calls recompute_packet(buf, no_ext, TCPOLEN_TSTAMP_APPA) (that constant comes from the system netinet/tcp.h, where it is TCPOLEN_TIMESTAMP + 2 = 12; the header is not in this repository, so the 12 is assumed). Writes depend on order, relative to buf + total_hdr_len: order 0 writes NOP at +0, NOP at +1 and a timestamp option at +2; order 1 writes NOP at +0, timestamp at +1 and NOP at +11; order 2 writes timestamp at +0, NOP at +11 and NOP at +12. Any other order calls error(1, 0, "unknown order"), which terminates the process, and recompute_packet is not reached. tcp_write_options for the timestamp kind memsets sizeof(struct tcp_option_ts) bytes (the struct is uint8 kind, uint8 len, uint32 tsval, uint32 tsecr, so with normal alignment 12 bytes, not the 10 of TCPOLEN_TIMESTAMP), sets kind, len = TCPOLEN_TIMESTAMP, tsval = ts and tsecr = 0, so the byte at +10 in order 2 is cleared by that memset rather than left as is, and tsval is stored at struct offset 4 under that layout. recompute_packet then copies the first total_hdr_len bytes of no_ext over buf, moves PAYLOAD_LEN bytes from no_ext + total_hdr_len to buf + total_hdr_len + 12 (so any option-area byte at +12 or beyond, namely the order 2 NOP at +12 and the end of the timestamp memset area in orders 0 and 1, is overwritten by the payload), adds 12/4 to tcphdr->doff, zeroes and recomputes the TCP checksum over PAYLOAD_LEN + 12 bytes, and for PF_INET adds 12 to iph->tot_len and recomputes the IPv4 header checksum (also for the second IPv4 header when ipip is set), while for other protocols it adds 12 only to the outer IPv6 payload_len. Buffer requirement: buf must be writable at least up to total_hdr_len + 14 bytes for order 0 (timestamp memset ends at +13), total_hdr_len + 13 for orders 1 and 2, and up to total_hdr_len + 12 + PAYLOAD_LEN for the payload move; no_ext must hold total_hdr_len + PAYLOAD_LEN bytes.
note: Reviewer 1 (order 2 writes NOPs at 11 and 12, offset 10 unwritten) is mixed: NOPs are at +11 and +12 (gro.c:502-505) but the TS memset of sizeof(struct tcp_option_ts) (gro.c:469, 12 bytes with padding) zeroes +10, and the layout is still TS, NOP, NOP. Reviewer 2 (buffer minimum understated, writes past total_hdr_len+12) is right (order 0 reaches +13, orders 1/2 reach +12). Tally 1 right 0 wrong, 1 mixed.

name: main
prose: Test program entry point of ioam6_parser.c (the slice showed only the tail of main, lines 1071-1101, and no function named unnamed_ioam6_hbh_layout_check exists). main(argc, argv) returns the unsigned int ret, initialised to 1, and returns 0 only when check_ioam_trace returns 0. Steps in order: if argc != 9 it returns 1; it maps argv[2] through str2id, parses argv[3] and argv[4] as IPv6 addresses (src, dst), argv[5] as a hex u32 (tr_type), argv[6] as u8 (tr_size) and argv[7] as u16 (ioam_ns), returning 1 on any failure; nexthdr is IPPROTO_IPV6 when argv[8] equals "encap" and IPPROTO_ICMPV6 otherwise; hoplen is sizeof(hbh) + 2 + sizeof(ioam6 header) + sizeof(trace header) + tr_size + (tr_size % 8). It opens an AF_PACKET/SOCK_DGRAM socket for ETH_P_IPV6, binds it to the device named in argv[1] with SO_BINDTODEVICE and sets a 1 second SO_RCVTIMEO; a failure of any of those calls returns 1 (after closing the socket once it exists). It then recv()s into a 512-byte buffer; a recv result <= 0 (including the timeout) returns 1 after closing. Packets whose IPv6 source or destination differ from src/dst, or whose nexthdr is not hop-by-hop, are skipped by receiving again. For the first matching packet it checks the hop-by-hop next header and hdrlen against nexthdr and (hoplen >> 3) - 1, the 2 padding bytes (the test is ptr[0] != IPV6_TLV_PADN && ptr[1] != 0, so it fails only when both are wrong), the IOAM option type, its opt_len and IOAM6_TYPE_PREALLOC, and, when tr_size % 8 is nonzero, the trailing padding bytes (a conjunction of four != tests, so it fails only when all four differ); any failing check jumps to close and returns 1. Finally ret = check_ioam_trace(testname_id, trace, tr_type, tr_size, ioam_ns), the socket is closed, and ret is returned (check_ioam_trace returns 1 on a header mismatch or when the test id is in neither range, otherwise the result of check_data). The header reads are not checked against the received size, only against the 512-byte buffer.
note: Slice cut the head; fixed under real name main (ioam6_parser.c:1002-1101). Old record said dropped; the fragment is the tail of main. No reviewer claim (mechanical rejection only).

name: build_packet_udp
prose: Static function build_packet_udp(_uh) in csum.c fills the UDP header at _uh from the cfg_* globals and returns a pointer just past the header (uh + 1). It sets source to htons(cfg_port_src), dest to htons(cfg_port_dst), len to htons(sizeof(struct udphdr) + cfg_payload_len) and check to 0. If cfg_zero_sum is set it sets source to 0, then to the value of checksum(uh, IPPROTO_UDP, sizeof(struct udphdr) + cfg_payload_len), prints the old and new source ports to stderr and stores ntohs(source) into cfg_port_src. Then check becomes 0 when cfg_zero_disable is set, otherwise checksum(uh, IPPROTO_UDP, sizeof(struct udphdr) + cfg_payload_len); if cfg_bad_csum is set the check value is then replaced by its bitwise complement (so with cfg_zero_disable and cfg_bad_csum both set it becomes 0xFFFF). It prints "tx: sending checksum: 0x%x" with the check value to stderr and returns uh + 1. The helper checksum() reads the pseudo-header addresses through the global iph_addr_p (8 bytes for PF_INET, 32 for PF_INET6, selected by cfg_family) and, when cfg_do_tx and cfg_send_pfpacket are both set, returns only the complemented folded pseudo-header sum without covering the UDP data; otherwise it sums the header and payload over len bytes. Preconditions: _uh points to a writable udphdr followed by cfg_payload_len payload bytes already in place, and iph_addr_p was set by the IP header builder. The buffer stays with the caller.
note: Reviewer claims: round 1 (cfg_bad_csum flips check even when cfg_zero_disable is set, so not 0) right (csum.c:249-250); round 1 (precondition omits iph_addr_p) right since checksum() uses it (csum.c:176); round 2 (annotation says void) wrong, function returns void * (csum.c:225,253); round 15 (claims a print of the final checksum but code has none) wrong, fprintf at csum.c:252. Also the old prose said checksum(uh,...) without qualification; in the PF_PACKET tx case it is pseudo-header only (csum.c:181-182). Tally 2 right 2 wrong.

name: recv_prepare_packet
prose: Static function recv_prepare_packet() takes no parameters and returns a file descriptor. It creates a socket(PF_PACKET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0), sets SO_RCVBUF to cfg_rcvbuf, enables PACKET_AUXDATA, calls recv_prepare_packet_filter(fd) and recv_prepare_packet_bind(fd), then returns fd. The filter is a classic BPF program attached with SO_ATTACH_FILTER that accepts a packet (returns 0xFFFF) only when the packet type is PACKET_HOST, the IP protocol/next-header byte equals IPPROTO_UDP when cfg_encap is set (otherwise cfg_proto), and the 16-bit destination port equals cfg_port_dst; cfg_family only selects whether those two offsets are taken from an IPv4 header (cfg_family == AF_INET) or an IPv6 header. The bind step sets sll_protocol to ETH_P_IP when cfg_family == PF_INET and ETH_P_IPV6 otherwise, resolves cfg_ifname with if_nametoindex and binds. If socket creation, either setsockopt (including the filter attach), if_nametoindex returning 0, or bind fails, error(1, ...) is called with a nonzero status, which terminates the process, so the function does not return in those cases. Globals read: cfg_rcvbuf, cfg_family, cfg_proto, cfg_encap, cfg_port_dst, cfg_ifname.
note: Reviewers: round 1 and round 2 (claims about an fd parameter / returning nothing) wrong, the function takes no argument and returns fd (csum.c:546-569) and the old prose already said so; round 15 (precondition omits cfg_proto/cfg_port_dst; filter checks protocol and port, not address family) right (csum.c:497-506, 515-525), rewritten. Tally 1 right 2 wrong.

name: copyfd_io_poll
prose: Static function copyfd_io_poll(infd, peerfd, outfd, in_closed_after_out, winfo) in mptcp_connect.c (lines 634-767; the packet slice began inside earlier functions). It puts peerfd into non-blocking mode (the fcntl result is ignored) and loops on poll() of peerfd for POLLIN|POLLOUT with poll_timeout. The loop exits and the function returns 0 (after usleep(cfg_wait) when cfg_remove is set and quit is not) when the event mask becomes 0 or the global quit is set, when a read of peerfd returns 0 while POLLOUT is already cleared (in that case *in_closed_after_out is set to true first), when reading infd returns 0 bytes while POLLIN is already cleared, or when cfg_truncate > 0 and both the total written and the total read have reached cfg_truncate. Other returns: 0 immediately (without the cfg_remove sleep) when a read from peerfd fails, with any errno, while cfg_rcv_trunc is set; 1 when poll() fails with errno other than EINTR (EINTR retries); 2 on poll timeout; 3 when reading peerfd fails and cfg_rcv_trunc is not set; 4 when reading infd fails with errno other than EINTR; 5 when revents has POLLERR or POLLNVAL and cfg_rcv_trunc is not set (when it is set the loop simply continues); 111 when do_rnd_write to peerfd fails, except that when cfg_rcv_trunc is set and errno is ECONNRESET or EPIPE, POLLOUT is cleared and the loop continues (so 111 is returned for any write failure when cfg_rcv_trunc is not set, and for other errnos when it is). Data movement: bytes read from peerfd are written to outfd with do_write (its result is ignored); bytes to send come from winfo->buf/off/len, refilled with read(infd, ...) when winfo->len is 0; when infd reaches EOF and POLLIN is still enabled it calls shut_wr(peerfd), which sleeps cfg_wait microseconds if set and then does shutdown(peerfd, SHUT_WR). peerfd is left non-blocking.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (returns 0 on read error when cfg_rcv_trunc, not only clean completion) right (mptcp_connect.c:689-691); round 15 (111 also when cfg_rcv_trunc is false) right (lines 714-724, the exception is conditioned on cfg_rcv_trunc). Tally 2 right 0 wrong. Slice began inside other functions; checked against the whole function.

name: client
prose: Static function client(pipefd) in mptcp_sockopt.c (lines 771-793; the packet slice began inside test_ip_tos_sockopt). It calls alarm(15), then, depending on the global pf, connects an MPTCP socket to 127.0.0.1:15432 (AF_INET) or ::1:15432 (AF_INET6) with sock_connect_mptcp(..., IPPROTO_MPTCP); any other pf calls xerror, which prints a message and calls exit(1). It then calls test_ip_tos_sockopt(fd) and connect_one_server(fd, pipefd) and returns 0. It has no other return statement, so it returns 0 whenever those calls return; sock_connect_mptcp, test_ip_tos_sockopt (die_perror/xerror, both of which exit(1)) and connect_one_server (die_perror/xerror, asserts) can end the process instead. Relevant behaviour of test_ip_tos_sockopt: it exits when setsockopt/getsockopt IP_TOS fail, when the value read back differs, when the returned length is not 1, when a getsockopt with length 0 fails or leaves a nonzero length, when the final getsockopt with length (socklen_t)-1 returns something other than -1 while errno is not EINVAL (die_perror), and when that length is changed from -1 (xerror); these checks are independent, and a final getsockopt returning -1 passes without errno being checked. connect_one_server closes fd and pipefd itself; client closes neither.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (formal requires weaker than prose) moot, no contract now; round 2 (test_ip_tos_sockopt can fail without terminating, r == -1 and errno != EINVAL, so client may return 0) right (mptcp_sockopt.c:765); round 15 (die_perror triggers on r != -1 && errno != EINVAL regardless of s; xerror on s != -1) right, and the old prose's nested 'only if s != -1' was wrong. Tally 2 right 0 wrong (1 moot).

name: do_server
prose: Static function do_server(args, ipc_fd) in nettest.c (lines 1562-1666). ipc_fd is -1 when there is no parent to signal (ipc_write then does nothing; otherwise it writes the int message to ipc_fd and only logs a failure). Steps: if args->serverns is set it calls switch_ns (failure logs and goes to err_exit); it sets args->dev = args->server_dev and args->expected_dev = args->expected_server_dev; resolve_devices or validate_addresses failing goes to err_exit; it uses a timeout of prog_timeout seconds when prog_timeout is nonzero; it creates the listening socket with msock_server when args->has_grp, otherwise lsock_init, and a negative result goes to err_exit. err_exit does ipc_write(ipc_fd, 0) and returns 1. With bind_test_only it closes the listening socket, calls ipc_write(ipc_fd, 1) and returns 0. For a non-SOCK_STREAM type it calls ipc_write(ipc_fd, 1), returns msg_loop(0, lsd, addr, alen, args) after closing the listening socket. For SOCK_STREAM: if args->password is set and tcp_md5_remote fails it closes the listening socket and goes to err_exit (returns 1); otherwise it calls ipc_write(ipc_fd, 1) and loops on select() with the listening socket. The loop ends with close(lsd) and return of rc in these cases: select returns 0 (rc = 2); select fails with errno other than EINTR (EINTR retries; rc is select's negative return); accept fails (rc is select's positive return value); show_sockstat or check_device returns nonzero (rc is that value, and the accepted socket csd is not closed on these two paths); or msg_loop has run on the accepted socket, csd was closed, and interactive is false (rc is msg_loop's return value). When interactive is set the loop repeats after every msg_loop call whatever its return value, so it returns only through the other exits. Every exit from the stream loop closes the listening socket; the accepted socket is closed only after msg_loop.
note: Reviewers: original (csd not closed on show_sockstat/check_device failure; select/accept returns omitted) right (nettest.c:1644-1650); round 2 (accept failure returns select's positive rc, not -1) right (lines 1638-1641, rc still holds select's return); round 15 (interactive loop repeats after any msg_loop return, not only successful) right (lines 1653-1657); the old prose said 'successful msg_loop'. Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(proc_net_pktgen, ctrl_cmd)
prose: Test body (proc_net_pktgen.c:161-181) using the fixture's ctrl_fd, which the fixture setup opened on /proc/net/pktgen/pgctrl. It writes "stop", "start" and "reset" to ctrl_fd, each twice: once with sizeof(string) bytes (including the NUL) and once with sizeof(string) - 1 bytes. After each write it expects (EXPECT_EQ) the returned length to equal the number of bytes written. A mismatch is recorded as a non-fatal failure and the test continues with the next write, so the function returns normally after the sixth write, and the test fails if any expectation was violated.
note: Name is the TEST_F invocation. No reviewer claim; prior prose checked and kept.

name: TEST_F(proc_net_pktgen, wrong_thr_cmd)
