name: build_packet
prose: Static function build_packet(payload_len) in psock_snd.c (lines 153-168) builds a test frame in the global tbuf and returns its length. It appends in order: build_vnet_header (sizeof(struct virtio_net_hdr), 10 bytes, with csum and GSO fields set from cfg_use_csum_off, cfg_use_csum_off_bad and cfg_use_gso; flags are OR-ed in, not cleared), build_eth_header (ETH_HLEN, or ETH_HLEN + 4 with a VLAN tag when cfg_use_vlan), build_ipv4_header (20 bytes, with tot_len from payload_len) and build_udp_header (8 bytes), so off is 52 bytes without VLAN and 56 with VLAN. It then checks off + payload_len > sizeof(tbuf) (the comparison is done as size_t); if true it calls error(1, 0, "payload length exceeds max"), which exits the process. Otherwise it fills tbuf + off with payload_len bytes of DATA_CHAR and returns off + payload_len, that is payload_len + 52 or payload_len + 56 with VLAN. tbuf is sizeof(struct virtio_net_hdr) + ETH_HLEN + ETH_MAX_MTU + 1 bytes (65560), so payload_len up to 65508 (65504 with VLAN) is accepted. The headers are written into tbuf before the length check. Negative payload_len is outside the intended domain: if off + payload_len is negative, the size_t comparison makes error() fire; for payload_len between -off and -1 the check passes and memset receives payload_len converted to a huge size_t.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (non-VLAN 65505-65508 returns, negative lengths do not abort) right (psock_snd.c:162-167); round 2 (formal requires payload_len <= 1481) wrong/moot, that contract is removed; round 15 (returned length is payload_len + 54/58, bounds off by two) wrong: virtio_net_hdr is 10 bytes (flags, gso_type, hdr_len, gso_size, csum_start, csum_offset), plus 14 + 20 + 8 = 52, VLAN +4 = 56 (psock_snd.c:76-151). Contract dropped because the function writes the global tbuf and reads cfg_* globals. Tally 1 right 1 wrong (1 moot).

name: main
prose: Test program entry point of reuseport_bpf.c (lines 458-639); main takes no parameters and ignores the command line. It prints section headers to stderr and runs these scenarios in order, each as a call with a struct test_params: IPv4 UDP: test_reuseport_ebpf with 10 and with 20 receive sockets, test_reuseport_cbpf with 10 and with 20, test_extra_filter, test_filter_no_reuseport; IPv6 UDP: the same six calls; IPv6 UDP with mapped IPv4 (recv AF_INET6, send AF_INET): test_reuseport_ebpf with 20 and 10 sockets and test_reuseport_cbpf with 10 and 20 sockets only; then enable_fastopen() (which may write the tcp_fastopen sysctl and calls error(1, ...) if it cannot open, read or write it); IPv4 TCP: ebpf (10), cbpf (10), test_extra_filter, test_filter_no_reuseport; IPv6 TCP: the same four; IPv6 TCP with mapped IPv4: ebpf (10) and cbpf (10) only; finally test_filter_without_bind(), prints "SUCCESS" to stderr and returns 0. The helpers return void and report failures by calling error(1, ...) (which exits with status 1), so main has no failing return path of its own; main returns 0 only when it reaches the end. A constructor and destructor outside main raise and restore RLIMIT_MEMLOCK around the whole program.
note: Slice cut the head; main is at reuseport_bpf.c:458. Reviewer round 15 (the formal contract only ensures result == 0 and omits side effects) right as a criticism of the old contract; contract removed since the function does I/O on stderr, sysctl files and sockets. The old prose said it ran 'every' scenario; extra_filter and no_reuseport tests are not run for the mapped-IPv4 sections (lines 539-567, 619-633). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: sk_peek_offset_test
prose: Static function sk_peek_offset_test(af, proto) in sk_so_peek_off.c (lines 57-168) returns 1 when every step passes and 0 otherwise (the only assignment of res = 1 is at line 159, after all checks). It creates two sockets s[0] and s[1] (SOCK_STREAM for IPPROTO_TCP, SOCK_DGRAM otherwise) with recv_sock initially equal to s[0], binds s[0] to a zeroed sockaddr of family af (wildcard address, port 0) with sizeof(union) as the length, reads the address back with getsockname, calls listen(s[0], 0) for TCP, connects s[1] to the address, and for TCP sets recv_sock = accept(s[0], NULL, NULL), treating a result <= 0 as failure. Then, on recv_sock: SO_PEEK_OFF read must be -1; after setting it to 0 (a failed setsockopt is only reported with ksft_perror) the read must be 0; send(s[1], "ab", 2) must return 2; recv(recv_sock, buf, 1, MSG_PEEK) must return 1 with 'a' and the offset must read 1; recv(buf, 2, MSG_PEEK) must return 1 with 'b' and the offset must read 2; recv(buf, 2, MSG_TRUNC) must return 2 and the offset must read 0. Each failed step prints with ksft_perror and jumps to out, returning 0. Note sk_peek_offset_get ignores a getsockopt failure (after ksft_perror) and returns an uninitialised int, so a failed read could by chance match the expected value. Cleanup at out: for TCP and recv_sock >= 0 it closes recv_sock; then closes s[1] if >= 0 and s[0] if >= 0. Consequences: on early failures after the sockets were created but before a successful accept, recv_sock is still the same descriptor as s[0], so for TCP s[0] is closed twice; and when accept returns 0 the failure path closes descriptor 0. A successful path prints a message with printf and returns 1.
note: Reviewers: round 2 (cleanup double-closes s[0] on early TCP failures; accept returning 0 treated as failure) right (sk_so_peek_off.c:75, 99-103, 161-166); round 15 (sk_peek_offset_get ignores getsockopt failure and returns an uninitialised value) right (lines 47-55). The old prose had both facts in a long sentence; rewritten with the exact conditions. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: try_accept
prose: Static function try_accept(tst_name, port, md5_addr, md5_prefix, ao_addr, ao_prefix, set_ao_required, sndid, rcvid, vrf, cnt_name, cnt_expected, needs_tcp_md5, inj) in tcp_ao/unsigned-md5.c (lines 37-121); it returns nothing, and vrf is unused. If needs_tcp_md5 is nonzero and should_skip_test(tst_name, KCONFIG_TCP_MD5) is true it returns immediately, before creating a socket and before any synchronize_threads call. Otherwise it creates a listening socket with test_listen_socket(this_ip_addr, port, 1) and, if given, installs an MD5 key for md5_addr/md5_prefix (test_set_md5), an AO key for ao_addr/ao_prefix (test_add_key) and the AO-required flag (test_set_ao_flags); each of these failing, or test_get_tcp_counters failing, calls test_error. If cnt_name is set it reads the netstat counter before; if ao_addr is set it reads the TCP counters into cnt1. It calls synchronize_threads, then test_skpair_wait_poll(lsk, 0, poll_cnt, &sk_pair) where poll_cnt is 0 when cnt_expected is TEST_CNT_GOOD and cnt_expected otherwise, then synchronize_threads again. A result of -ETIMEDOUT stores it in sk_pair and calls test_fail unless inj == FAULT_TIMEOUT; -EKEYREJECTED calls test_fail unless inj == FAULT_KEYREJECT; any other negative result calls test_error; on success it calls test_fail if inj == FAULT_TIMEOUT, then accept()s (a failed accept calls test_error; a successful one with inj == FAULT_TIMEOUT calls test_fail). inj is compared for equality with a single fault value, not tested as a bit mask. It then reads the TCP counters again into cnt2 when ao_addr is set and closes the listening socket. If cnt_name is NULL it reports test_ok ("no counter checks") and skips the counter checks, including the AO counter assertion. Otherwise it reports test_fail when the netstat counter did not increase (after <= before) and test_ok when it did, and, when ao_addr is set, calls test_assert_counters(tst_name, &cnt1, &cnt2, cnt_expected). Finally it calls synchronize_threads once more and, if an accepted socket exists (sk >= 0), test_kill_sk(sk). The netstat counter is only compared for an increase; the expected count cnt_expected is used only for the poll and the AO counter assertion.
note: Reviewers: original (FAULT_KEYREJECT success is not failed; counter only checked for increase) right on both points (unsigned-md5.c:78-80, 107-113); round 15 (AO counter assertion is skipped when cnt_name is NULL) right (lines 100-103, 114-115); the old prose said 'fault bit', but the code compares with == (line 6). Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: main
prose: Entry point main(argc, argv) of tcp_mmap.c (lines 445-616). getopt parses "46p:svr:w:H:zxkP:M:C:a:i": -4/-6 set cfg_family and cfg_alen, -p port, -H host, -s server flag, -r/-w rcvbuf/sndbuf, -z zerocopy, -M mss, -x hash flag, -k keepflag, -P max pacing rate, -C chunk_size, -a map_align, -i integrity; any other result (including -v, which is in the option string but has no case, and unknown options) hits the default case and calls exit(1). If map_align is 0 it uses default_huge_page_size(), or 2 MiB if that returns 0. With -s it creates a listening socket (socket failure exits 1; SO_REUSEADDR failure is ignored), calls setup_sockaddr, optionally sets TCP_MAXSEG (failure exits 1), binds and listens with backlog 128 (failure exits 1), and calls do_accept, which loops forever accepting connections and starting threads, so main does not return in server mode. Client mode: mmap_large_buffer(chunk_size, &buffer_sz) (failure exits 1), creates a socket (failure exits 1), applies buffer sizes, setup_sockaddr, optional TCP_MAXSEG (failure exits 1), connect (failure exits 1); a failing SO_MAX_PACING_RATE setsockopt only calls perror, and a failing SO_ZEROCOPY setsockopt prints and sets zflg to 0 (neither exits). With -i it fills the buffer with random data, EVP_MD_CTX_new failure prints and exits 1, then initialises SHA-256. It then sends chunks with send() (MSG_ZEROCOPY if zflg) in a loop until FILE_SZ (1 << 35) bytes have been sent or a send returns <= 0, updating the digest per chunk; if integrity is on and total == FILE_SZ it sends the SHA-256 digest. It frees the EVP context if one exists, closes the socket, unmaps the buffer and returns 0 (also after a short or failed send).
note: Slice cut the head; main starts at tcp_mmap.c:445. Reviewer round 15 (SO_MAX_PACING_RATE and SO_ZEROCOPY setsockopt failures only perror, not exit(1)) right (lines 573-582); the old prose's blanket 'any ... setsockopt failure ... exit(1)' was wrong for these two, and for the ignored SO_REUSEADDR. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(tls, recv_partial)
prose: Test body (tls.c:1104-1122) using the tls fixture's connected pair (fd sends, cfd receives). It builds the string "test_read_partial" (17 characters) and sends strlen + 1 = 18 bytes, including the NUL, with send(self->fd, ...), expecting the return value 18. It then calls recv(self->cfd, recv_mem, 9, MSG_WAITALL), expecting 9 and the bytes "test_read"; clears recv_mem, calls recv(self->cfd, recv_mem, 8, MSG_WAITALL), expecting 8 and the bytes "_partial". The NUL byte is left unread. All checks are non-fatal EXPECT_EQ expectations; the body returns nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 (send length is strlen + 1 = 18, not 17) right (tls.c:1109, 1113); the old prose said 17. The slice cut the head, name fixed to the real TEST_F. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(tls, rekey_fail)
prose: Test body (tls.c:1985-2057; the slice began at line 2036, in the middle of it, so no function named tls_rekey_recv exists). It sends and receives test_message_before_rekey on the pair, then sends a TLS KeyUpdate with tls_send_keyupdate on fd. If the variant's tls_version is not TLS 1.3 it only checks that setsockopt(TLS_TX) on fd fails with -1 and errno EBUSY and returns. For TLS 1.3 it checks a valid TX rekey succeeds (0), then that three invalid updates fail with -1 and errno EINVAL (a TX update with a changed version, an RX update on cfd with a changed version, a TX update with a changed cipher), sends test_message_after_rekey (expecting the full length), and expects recv on cfd without a control message to return -1 (errno not checked). After tls_recv_keyupdate on cfd it expects recv to return -1 with errno EKEYEXPIRED, both blocking and with MSG_DONTWAIT; it installs a new RX key with setsockopt(TLS_RX) on cfd (expecting 0), and expects the next recv to return something other than -1 (EXPECT_NE) with the data equal to test_message_after_rekey. All checks are non-fatal EXPECT_* expectations.
note: Slice cut the head; the old prose described the tail of this test (and said recv returns send_len, but the code only expects not -1, tls.c:2055). No reviewer claim beyond mechanical rejection.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, timeo)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2744-2774) for the tls_err fixture. If self->notls is set it skips with SKIP(return, ...). Otherwise it sets SO_RCVTIMEO of 10 ms on self->cfd2 (ASSERT_EQ on the setsockopt result) and forks (ASSERT_GE on the fork result). The parent sleeps 1 ms, then calls recv(cfd2, buf, 128, 0) twice, expecting -1 with errno EAGAIN each time, and calls wait(); it does not check the child's status. The child calls recv(cfd2, ...) once, expecting -1 with EAGAIN, and then exit(0).
note: Reviewer round 15 (the child performs only one recv) right (tls.c:2770-2772). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, poll_partial_rec)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2776-2808; the slice began at 2790 and cut the head). It skips when self->notls is set. It polls self->cfd2 for POLLIN with a 1 ms timeout, expecting 0 events. It sends 128 random bytes on self->fd, reads the resulting TLS record from self->cfd into a 256-byte buffer (expecting a length greater than 128), sends the first 100 bytes of the record on self->fd2 (expecting 100), polls cfd2 again for 1 ms expecting 0, sends the remaining rec_len - 100 bytes, polls expecting 1, then recv(cfd2, rec, 256, 0) is expected to return 128 and the data to equal the 128 bytes sent. All are non-fatal EXPECT_* expectations.
note: Old record was dropped because the slice cut the head; the test exists at tls.c:2776 so it is fixed under the real name.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, epoll_partial_rec)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2810-2847). It skips when self->notls is set. It creates an epoll instance and adds self->cfd2 for EPOLLIN (ASSERT_GE on both calls), and expects epoll_wait(..., timeout 0) to return 0. It sends 128 random bytes on self->fd, reads the TLS record from self->cfd (length expected greater than 128), sends the first 100 bytes of the record on self->fd2 (expecting 100), and expects epoll_wait with timeout 0 to return 0; it sends the remaining bytes, expects epoll_wait to return 1, then expects recv(cfd2, rec, 256, 0) to return 128 with the data equal to the 128 bytes sent, and closes the epoll fd. The ASSERTs end the test on failure (without closing epollfd); the EXPECTs do not.
note: Prior prose checked against tls.c:2810-2847; it omitted the initial empty epoll_wait and used 'exactly one event' loosely (the check is return value 1). No reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, poll_partial_rec_async)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2849-2904). It skips when self->notls is set, creates a pipe (ASSERT_GE), sends 128 random bytes on self->fd, reads the TLS record from self->cfd (expecting more than 128 bytes), and forks (ASSERT_GE). Parent: closes p[1], sleeps 1 ms, sends the first 100 bytes of the record on self->fd2 (expecting 100), blocks reading one byte from p[0] (barrier, expecting 1), sends the remaining bytes, then wait()s and expects the returned pid to equal the child's pid and the status to be 0. Child: closes p[0], polls self->cfd2 for POLLIN with a 20 ms timeout expecting 0, writes one byte to p[1] (expecting 1), polls cfd2 again with a 20 ms timeout expecting 1, and exits with status !__test_passed(_metadata), so a failed expectation in the child makes the parent's status check fail. All checks are non-fatal EXPECT_* except the ASSERTs.
note: Prior prose checked against tls.c:2849-2904; clarified the child exit status and the barrier. No reviewer claim.

name: TEST_F(tls_err, oob_pressure)
prose: Test body (tls.c:2909-2920) for the tls_err fixture; it does not check self->notls. It fills a 64 KiB buffer with random bytes, sends 5 bytes with MSG_OOB on self->fd2 (expecting 5), sends the whole 64 KiB with flags 0 (expecting 65536), then sends 5 bytes with MSG_OOB on self->fd2 64 times, expecting 5 each time. The source comment says the large send after OOB is meant to trigger copy mode due to memory pressure; the test itself only checks the returned byte counts, via non-fatal EXPECT_EQ.
note: Prior prose checked; made the 'exercising the copy path' claim an intent from the source comment (tls.c:2906-2908), since the test only asserts return values. No reviewer claim.

name: run_printf
prose: Static function run_printf(min, max) in nolibc-test.c (lines 1687-1723). It loops test from min while test >= 0 and test <= max, with ret starting at 0 and a per-iteration line length llen. The switch is on test + __LINE__ + 1, so each CASE_TEST(name) labels one test by source line; a test number with no case does nothing (there is no default), and the case that is last in the switch executes return ret. For a matching case, CASE_TEST prints "<test> <name>" to stdout and then either EXPECT_VFPRINTF adds expect_vfprintf(...) to ret, or EXPECT_ZR(1, expr) adds expect_zr(expr, llen), which is 1 when the test function (test_scanf, test_strerror, test_printf_error) returns nonzero and 0 otherwise (the cond argument is the constant 1, so those cases are never skipped). expect_vfprintf formats with vsnprintf into a buffer limited to 21 bytes and returns 1 if the returned length differs from the expected count c, otherwise strncmp(expected, buf, c) (any sign, 0 on equal), printing the result to stdout. The function returns ret after the loop or at the sentinel case, so it returns 0 when no case ran or every executed case matched, and otherwise the accumulated sum, which can in principle be negative or cancel out because strncmp results can be negative.
note: Reviewers: original (negative strncmp result makes ret possibly negative) right (nolibc-test.c:1575-1578); round 2 (omits EXPECT_ZR contributions from scanf/strerror/printf_error) right (lines 1714-1716); both were already reflected in the old prose, rewritten with exact conditions. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(pcie_ep_doorbell, DOORBELL_TEST)

The body uses the pci_ep_ioctl macro, which stores ioctl(self->fd, cmd, arg) in ret and replaces a negative result by -errno. It calls pci_ep_ioctl(PCITEST_SET_IRQTYPE, PCITEST_IRQ_TYPE_AUTO) and asserts ret == 0 (fatal ASSERT_EQ), then pci_ep_ioctl(PCITEST_DOORBELL, 0) and expects ret to be 0 (non-fatal EXPECT_FALSE(ret)), so any nonzero return fails the expectation. Nothing is returned.

name: TEST_F(file_handle, pid_has_exited)
prose: Test body (pidfd_file_handle_test.c:274-307) for the file_handle fixture; self->pidfd is a pidfd of the test process and self->child_pidfd3/child_pid3 a child created with CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID. It allocates a struct file_handle with MAX_HANDLE_SZ bytes of handle space (ASSERT_NE), obtains the handle of child_pidfd3 with name_to_handle_at(AT_EMPTY_PATH), fstat()s child_pidfd3, opens the handle with open_by_handle_at(self->pidfd, fh, 0) and asserts the opened pidfd has the same st_dev and st_ino, then closes it. It moves child_pidfd3 out of the fixture (self->child_pidfd3 = -EBADF), sends SIGKILL through it, closes it, and waits with waitid(WEXITED | WNOWAIT) so the child has exited but is not reaped. It then calls open_by_handle_at again and only asserts that the result is >= 0 (no stat comparison and the descriptor is not closed), and finally reaps the child with waitid(WEXITED). Failures of the ASSERT_* macros end the test early; EXPECT_* ones do not. The file_handle buffer is not freed in this test.
note: Old prose claimed the handle buffer is freed, every pidfd is closed and st_dev/st_ino match after the child exited; none of that is in the code (no free(), the second pidfd is only asserted >= 0, pidfd_file_handle_test.c:303-304). Systematic: 'buffer is freed' claim wrong in 7 of 7 file_handle tests of this slice.

The file_handle buffer is not freed in this test.

name: FIXTURE_SETUP(current_nsset)
prose: Fixture setup (pidfd_setns_test.c:91-321) for current_nsset, running before each TEST_F with a zero-initialised self supplied by the harness. It first sets every element of nsfds[], child_nsfds1[], child_nsfds2[], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds[], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds1[] and child_pidfd_derived_nsfds2[] to -EBADF. It opens /proc/self/ns as a directory (ASSERT_GE 0), stores getpid() in self->pid and a pidfd of it in self->pidfd, and for each namespace in ns_info opens /proc/self/ns/<name> into nsfds[i] and derives child_pidfd_derived_nsfds[i] with the namespace ioctl on self->pidfd; a failed open records an EXPECT_EQ(errno, ENOENT) and a failed ioctl records EXPECT_EQ(errno, EOPNOTSUPP), and the array element then holds the negative return value (-1), not -EBADF. It creates a child with create_child(&child_pidfd_exited, 0) that unshares the user and net namespaces when the matching nsfds entry is >= 0 and exits right away, and the parent asserts waitid(WEXITED | WNOWAIT) succeeds (the exited child is waited for but not reaped). It then reopens self->pidfd (the earlier pidfd is overwritten, not closed), creates two socketpair-synchronised children child_pid1 and child_pid2, each created with CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID when both namespaces are available, otherwise with whichever of those is available, otherwise with 0; each child unshares the mount, cgroup, ipc, uts and net namespaces and switches the time namespace when the corresponding nsfds entry is >= 0 (exiting with EXIT_FAILURE if one fails), writes one byte to its socketpair and pause()s; the parent asserts it reads that byte (ASSERT_EQ, read_nointr == 1) for each child. Finally it reopens nsfds[i] (overwriting the earlier descriptors without closing them), opens /proc/<child_pid1>/ns/<name> and /proc/<child_pid2>/ns/<name> into child_nsfds1[i] and child_nsfds2[i], derives child_pidfd_derived_nsfds1[i]/2[i] from the two child pidfds, with the same EXPECT_EQ(errno, ENOENT/EOPNOTSUPP) on failure (failed entries hold -1), and closes proc_fd. Only the ASSERT_* failures abort the setup; EXPECT_* failures are recorded and execution continues.
note: Slice cut the head; fixed under real macro name. Reviewer round 15 (EXPECT failures do not abort; failed openat/ioctl leave -1, not -EBADF) right on both points (pidfd_setns_test.c:119-133, 269-317). Old prose also said the exited child was 'reaped with WNOWAIT'; WNOWAIT leaves it unreaped. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: FIXTURE_TEARDOWN(current_nsset)
prose: Fixture teardown (pidfd_setns_test.c:323-354) for current_nsset. It asserts (ASSERT_EQ, ending the teardown on failure) that sending SIGKILL with sys_pidfd_send_signal to self->child_pidfd1 and then self->child_pidfd2 returns 0. For every namespace index it closes, without checking the result, each of nsfds[i], child_nsfds1[i], child_nsfds2[i], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds[i], child_pidfd_derived_nsfds1[i] and child_pidfd_derived_nsfds2[i] that is >= 0. It then closes child_pidfd1 and child_pidfd2 when they are >= 0, with EXPECT_EQ(0, close(...)) (a failure is recorded, not fatal), and asserts that waitid(P_PID, ..., WEXITED) succeeds for child_pid_exited, child_pid1 and child_pid2, which reaps all three children. It does not close self->pidfd or self->child_pidfd_exited.
note: Reviewer round 15 (child_pidfd_exited is not closed, and close uses EXPECT_EQ so failures do not abort) right (pidfd_setns_test.c:347-353); the old prose said every stored fd is closed and any failure aborts. self->pidfd is not closed either. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST_F(pidfs_xattr, set_get_list_xattr_persistent)
prose: Test body (pidfd_xattr_test.c:97-130) for the pidfs_xattr fixture, whose child (created with CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID) exits immediately; the child is reaped in the fixture teardown. The body uses ASSERT_* only, so it stops at the first failed assertion. It sets "trusted.persistent" = "persistent value" on self->child_pidfd with fsetxattr (expects 0), reads it back with fgetxattr (expects the value length and identical bytes), and calls flistxattr, expecting a positive return and that the first name in the returned list equals "trusted.persistent" (strcmp on the list start only; it does not check that it is the only entry or the list length). It then closes the pidfd (asserted 0), sets self->child_pidfd = -EBADF, sleeps 2 seconds, reopens the pidfd with sys_pidfd_open(self->child_pid, 0) (expects >= 0) and repeats the same fgetxattr and first-entry flistxattr checks. Nothing is returned.
note: Reviewer round 15 (code only strcmp's the first entry, not that it is the sole entry) right (pidfd_xattr_test.c:113, 129). Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: check_all_cpu_dscr_defaults
prose: Static function check_all_cpu_dscr_defaults(val) in dscr_sysfs_test.c (lines 30-65) returns 0 or 1. It opens CPU_PATH with opendir; if that fails it prints with perror and returns 1 (there is no precondition that the directory can be opened). For each directory entry it skips entries whose d_type does not have the DT_DIR bit, the entry named "cpuidle", entries whose name does not contain the substring "cpu", entries for which snprintf of "<CPU_PATH><name>/dscr" into a LEN_MAX buffer reports a length >= LEN_MAX, and entries whose dscr file fails access(F_OK). For each remaining file it calls check_cpu_dscr_default(file, val), which reads the file as a hexadecimal unsigned long with read_ulong and returns read_ulong's nonzero error value if that read fails, 1 (after printing both values) if the value differs from val, and 0 if equal; any nonzero result makes the function close the directory and return 1 (the exact error code is not passed on, since it is only tested for truth). After all entries it closes the directory and returns 0. The directory stream is closed on every path after a successful opendir.
note: Reviewers: original (contract only bounds result to 0/1) moot, no contract; round 2 (on read_ulong failure it returns 1, not read_ulong's error code) right (dscr_sysfs_test.c:58-61); round 15 (precondition says CPU_PATH can be opened yet opendir failure is a return path; snprintf-overflow skip omitted) right on both (lines 36-40, 52-54). Tally 3 right 0 wrong (1 moot).

name: back_to_back_ebbs
prose: Test function back_to_back_ebbs() (back_to_back_ebbs_test.c:62-101), run through test_harness in a forked child whose exit status becomes the test result. It takes no parameters. SKIP_IF(!ebb_is_supported()) prints a skip message and returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99), which test_harness turns into a reported skip with status 0, before any event is opened. Otherwise it initialises an event for config 0x1001e ("cycles") as an EBB leader with exclude_kernel, exclude_hv and exclude_idle set, and FAIL_IF (which prints and returns 1) applies to: event_open failing (nothing installed yet), ebb_event_enable failing (handler installed via setup_ebb_handler, sample_period still unset, event left open), core_busy_loop returning nonzero inside the wait loop (event open, sample_period 5, PMC1 programmed, EBB globally enabled and PMCs unfrozen, none of that undone), and the final check ebb_count != NUMBER_OF_EBBS (50), which is reached after the loop, ebb_global_disable, ebb_freeze_pmcs, dump_ebb_state and event_close. Between the open and the wait loop it sets sample_period = 5, freezes the PMCs, loads PMC1 with pmc_sample_period(5), enables EBBs globally and unfreezes the PMCs. The loop runs core_busy_loop while ebb_state.stats.ebb_count < 50; the handler ebb_callee increments the count. The function returns 0 only when it ends with ebb_count exactly 50; an overshoot above 50 would return 1 through the last FAIL_IF.
note: Reviewers: round 2 (final mismatch returns after event_close and global disable, not with the event open; enable failure occurs before sample_period = 5) right (back_to_back_ebbs_test.c:79-98); round 15 (SKIP_IF returns 0 so skip path gives zero status and the function can return 0 without 50 EBBs) wrong at function level, the function returns 99 (utils.h:160-166, MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE = 99), though test_harness reports a skip with status 0 (harness.c:125-128); formal-contract claims (original, round 1) moot, no contract now. Old prose said the skip terminates 'with a nonzero status', which is wrong too. Tally 1 right 1 wrong.

name: event_alternatives_tests_p9
prose: Test function event_alternatives_tests_p9() (event_alternatives_tests_p9.c:25-111), run through test_harness in a forked child. It returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99, reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0) when platform_check_for_tests() is nonzero, when PVR_VER(mfspr(SPRN_PVR)) != POWER9, or when check_for_generic_compat_pmu() is nonzero, before opening anything. Then, five times, it initialises a leader event (PM_RUN_CYC_ALT with EventCode_1, PM_INST_DISP with EventCode_2, PM_BR_2PATH with EventCode_2, PM_LD_MISS_L1 with EventCode_3, PM_RUN_INST_CMPL_ALT with EventCode_4), opens it with event_open, opens the second event as a sibling with event_open_with_group(&event, leader.fd), and closes both with event_close. Each open is wrapped in FAIL_IF, which prints a message and returns 1 immediately, so a failing leader open leaves the earlier completed pairs closed and nothing of the current pair open, and a failing sibling open leaves that pair's leader open and not closed. The function returns 0 after all five pairs succeeded; the results of event_close are not checked.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (prose claims all opened events are closed before returning but FAIL_IF returns early without closing) right for the current pair only (earlier pairs are closed, lines 55-56, 68-69, 81-82, 94-95); round 2 (SKIP_IF returns 0, not nonzero) wrong, it returns 99 (utils.h:158-166); round 15 (SKIP_IF returns the skip value, nonzero, not 0) right in that sense; the old prose said it returned 0 on skip and that every already-opened event leaks, both wrong or overstated. Formal-contract claims moot. Tally 2 right 1 wrong.

name: group_constraint_thresh_cmp
prose: Test function group_constraint_thresh_cmp() (group_constraint_thresh_cmp_test.c:32-91), run through test_harness in a forked child. SKIP_IF(platform_check_for_tests()) returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99), reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0, before any event is opened. If have_hwcap2(PPC_FEATURE2_ARCH_3_1) it uses the power10 events: leader p10_EventCode_1 with attr.config1 = 1000 (event_open), then a sibling p10_EventCode_2 with config1 = 2000 whose event_open_with_group must fail (FAIL_IF(!...)), event_close of that sibling, then a new sibling p10_EventCode_2 with config1 = 1000 whose event_open_with_group must succeed, then it closes the leader and the sibling. Otherwise it uses the power9 events: leader p9_EventCode_1, sibling p9_EventCode_2 expected to fail, closed, then p9_EventCode_3 expected to succeed, then both closed. FAIL_IF prints a message and returns 1 at once: if the leader open fails nothing is open; if the mismatched open unexpectedly succeeds, the leader and that sibling are left open; if the matching open fails, the leader is left open. It returns 0 after the final closes (event_close results are not checked).
note: Reviewers: round 1 (prose said failures of event_init/event_close are checked and the caller closes events) moot for the current text (the code does not check them and the test closes the events itself); round 2 and 15 (contract only bounds the result) moot, contract removed because the function uses structs and system calls. The old prose said SKIP_IF returns 0 and omitted the power10 branch; fixed (utils.h:160-167). Tally 0 right 0 wrong.

name: main
prose: main() of group_constraint_thresh_cmp_test.c (lines 93-96) returns test_harness(group_constraint_thresh_cmp, "group_constraint_thresh_cmp"). test_harness forks the test, waits for it with a timeout, and returns the test's exit status: 0 on pass, 0 when the test returned the skip value (the harness maps it to 0 after reporting the skip), 1 when the test function returned 1, and 1 for harness errors (fork or waitpid failure, killed by signal, timeout). The test function itself only returns 0, 1 or the skip value, so main returns 0 or 1.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (prose says skipped returns nonzero, but SKIP_IF returns 0) wrong at main level: the test function returns 99 but test_harness converts it to 0 (harness.c:125-128), so main returns 0 on skip, as the old prose stated; rounds 2 and 15 (contract only bounds result / omits harness) moot, contract removed. Tally 0 right 1 wrong.

name: group_constraint_thresh_ctl
prose: Test function group_constraint_thresh_ctl() (group_constraint_thresh_ctl_test.c:31-59), run through test_harness in a forked child. If platform_check_for_tests() is nonzero, SKIP_IF returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99; reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0) with no event opened. Otherwise it opens leader EventCode_1 with event_open and sibling EventCode_2 with event_open_with_group(&event, leader.fd), which is expected to fail; it then event_close()s that sibling, initialises EventCode_3 as a new sibling, expects event_open_with_group to succeed, and closes the leader and the sibling. The failure checks use FAIL_IF, which prints a message and returns 1 (not -1): when the leader's event_open fails nothing is open; when the mismatched sibling open unexpectedly succeeds, the leader and that sibling stay open; when the matching sibling open fails, the leader stays open. It returns 0 after the final closes (event_close results are not checked).

name: ptrace_tm_spd_tar
prose: Test function ptrace_tm_spd_tar() (ptrace-tm-spd-tar.c:126-166), run through test_harness in a forked child; TEST_PASS is 0 and TEST_FAIL is 1 (ptrace.h:33-34). It returns MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99; test_harness reports a skip with status 0) through SKIP_IF_MSG when !have_htm() or htm_is_synthetic(); the macro returns, it does not terminate the process, and 99 is not KSFT_SKIP. Otherwise it creates a 3-int SysV shared segment with shmget(IPC_PRIVATE, ..., 0777|IPC_CREAT) (the result is not checked) and forks. The child calls tm_spd_tar(), which ends in exit(0) or exit(1) and never returns. The parent attaches the segment as pptr with shmat (unchecked), sets pptr[0] and pptr[1] to 0 and spins until pptr[2] is nonzero (the child sets it in wait_parent); if fork() failed (pid == -1) the 'if (pid)' branch is still taken and the parent spins on pptr[2] with no child, so it never returns. It then calls trace_tm_spd_tar(pid). If that returns nonzero the parent sends SIGTERM to the child, calls shmdt(&pptr), shmctl(IPC_RMID) and returns TEST_FAIL. Otherwise it calls shmdt(&pptr), wait(&status), shmctl(IPC_RMID), returns TEST_FAIL if wait() did not return pid, and otherwise TEST_FAIL when the child exited normally with a nonzero status and TEST_PASS when it exited with status 0 or ended by a signal. Note shmdt(&pptr) passes the address of the pointer variable, not the attached address pptr, so it does not detach the segment (it fails; its result is ignored); shmctl(IPC_RMID) only marks the segment for removal.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (misstates TEST_FAIL causes; SKIP_IF_MSG exiting process) mixed: the skip macro returns 99 rather than exiting (utils.h:169-176) so the 'exiting' claim is wrong, while the old prose's KSFT_SKIP (4) was indeed wrong; round 2 (omits signaled-child path returning TEST_PASS) right (lines 162-163); round 15 (shmdt(&pptr) detaches the address of the local pointer, not the segment) right (lines 148, 153). Tally 2 right 0 wrong, 1 mixed.

name: tm_vsx
prose: Function tm_vsx() (ptrace-tm-vsx.c:29-82) is the child side of the ptrace TM VSX test; it takes no parameters, uses the global shm_id, and never returns (every path ends in a loop or exit). It attaches the shared segment with cptr = shmat(shm_id, NULL, 0) (unchecked). At label trans it sets cptr[1] = 0 and runs an inline-asm block: it calls load_vsx_ckpt (loadvsx(fp_load_ckpt)) before the tbegin. instruction, i.e. outside the transaction, so the checkpointed VSX state is fp_load_ckpt; tbegin. then, inside the transaction, calls load_vsx (loads fp_load), tsuspends, stores the word 1 with stw to the address of cptr[1], tresumes, and then executes b . (an endless loop) which only ends when the transaction is aborted (the tend. after it is not reachable by normal flow). On the abort path the block sets result = 1 and reads TEXASR. After the block, if result is nonzero: if cptr[0] is still 0 it goes back to trans and retries; otherwise it calls shmdt(cptr), stores the VSX registers into fp_store with storevsx, and calls exit(1) if compare_vsx_vmx(fp_store, fp_load_ckpt_new) is nonzero and exit(0) if it is zero. If result is zero it detaches with shmdt(cptr) and calls exit(1). The parent is expected to set cptr[0] nonzero after writing new checkpointed VSX/VMX state through ptrace.
note: Reviewers: original (precondition omits that cptr[0] must be set; code loops when unset) right (lines 69-71); round 2 (code attaches via shmat and retries while cptr[0] is zero) right; round 15 (load_vsx_ckpt runs before tbegin, outside the transaction) right (lines 39-43). All three were against earlier wording; the text is rewritten from the code. Tally 3 right 0 wrong.

name: uaccess_flush_test
prose: Test function uaccess_flush_test() (uaccess_flush.c:21-153), run through test_harness in a forked child. SKIP_IF and FAIL_IF are macros that return MAGIC_SKIP_RETURN_VALUE (99, reported by test_harness as a skip with status 0) or 1 from the function; they do not terminate the process. It returns 99 when geteuid() != 0, when the CPU lacks PPC_FEATURE_ARCH_2_06, or when reading any of the debugfs files powerpc/rfi_flush, powerpc/entry_flush or powerpc/uaccess_flush fails (after perror). It then writes 0 to rfi_flush and entry_flush when their original values were nonzero (a write failure returns 1), opens an L1D read-miss perf counter (fd < 0 returns 1), allocates a buffer with memalign (its arguments are alignment zero_size and size CACHELINE_SIZE; the result is not checked or freed), enables the counter (failure returns 1) and calls set_dscr(1). It then measures in two rounds of 10 repetitions each: round one with uaccess_flush equal to its original value, round two after writing the opposite value (!uaccess_flush_orig) to powerpc/uaccess_flush (a write failure returns 1 without restoring anything). Each repetition resets the counter (failure returns 1), runs syscall_loop_uaccess(p, 100000, 24 KiB), reads the counter (a short read returns 1) and counts a pass when uaccess_flush is nonzero and L1D misses >= iterations * (zero_size / CACHELINE_SIZE - 2), or when it is zero and misses are below half that. After each round it prints PASS or FAIL and sets rc = 1 if passes < repetitions (rc is never reset). After the second round it disables and closes the counter, sets DSCR to 0, and restores rfi_flush, entry_flush and uaccess_flush to their original values, returning 1 at the first restore write that fails (so earlier restores have happened, later ones not), and finally returns rc (0 or 1). The early returns 1 taken after the counter was opened and before it is closed (failures of enable, reset, read, and of the uaccess_flush write) leave the perf counter open, DSCR at 1 once set_dscr(1) has run, and rfi_flush/entry_flush at 0 if they were changed; the failure return after perf_event_open (fd < 0) also leaves rfi_flush/entry_flush at 0 if they were changed; the restore-failure returns happen after the counter is closed.
note: Reviewers: original (returns 1 on debugfs write failures without restoring original values; omits writability) right (lines 54-66, 122-125); round 15 (restore-failure returns after the second round occur after perf_event_disable/close, so the counter is not open) right (lines 132-150). The old prose also said SKIP_IF/FAIL_IF terminate the process, which is wrong (they return). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of testptp.c (lines 156-694; the slice showed only the middle). It parses options with getopt using "cd:e:E:f:F:ghH:i:k:lL:n:o:p:P:rsSt:T:w:x:Xy:z" and stores the settings; it does not run anything until parsing is complete. During parsing it returns -1 (after usage or a message) when -L does not parse as "pin,func" (usage), when -x is outside 1..PTP_MAX_SAMPLES, when -y is not realtime, monotonic or monotonic-raw, and for an unknown option or '?'; -h prints usage and returns 0 immediately, without opening the device. It then opens the device (default DEVICE, read-only when -r, else read-write); an open failure prints a message and returns -1 (nothing to close). get_clockid failing returns -1 with fd left open. It then performs the requested operations in a fixed order, reporting per-operation errors with perror and continuing: -c capabilities, -f frequency adjust, -t/-n time shift, -o phase adjust, -g get time, -s/-S/-T set time, -L pin function, -e external timestamps (reads events, and disables the request afterwards unless -r), -z flag test, -l pin listing, then checks that -w and -H are used only together with -p (else prints a message and returns -1 with fd open), -p periodic output (a clock_gettime failure returns -1 with fd open), -P PPS, -k system/phc offset samples (n_samples outside 1..25 prints usage and returns -1 with fd open; calloc failure returns -1 with fd open), -x extended timestamps (calloc failure returns -1 with fd open), -X cross timestamp (calloc failure returns -1 with fd open), and -F channel masking (clears the mask, enables one channel and waits for getchar()). Operations already done before a -1 return are not undone. When it reaches the end it closes fd and returns 0.
note: Reviewer round 15 (omits -h returning 0 without opening the device; 'fd left open' is false when the open fails) right on both (testptp.c:313-315, 323-327). Old prose also said the -k count check is part of option parsing; it happens after the earlier operations have run (lines 553-558). Tally 2 right 0 wrong. The whole function was read.

name: run_single_test
prose: Static function run_single_test(test, uparams) in resctrl_tests.c (lines 119-156); it returns nothing. If test->disabled is set it returns at once without printing anything. If the vendor check fails (test_vendor_specific_check, true when the test has no vendor_specific mask or get_vendor() matches it) it calls ksft_test_result_skip and returns. It then reads snc_mode = snc_nodes_per_l3_cache() and prints "Starting <name> test ..."; if snc_mode == 1 and snc_unreliable is set and get_vendor() == ARCH_INTEL it reports a skip (SNC detection unreliable) and returns. Then test_prepare(test) (signal handler registration and mounting resctrl; it unregisters the handler itself if the mount fails) failing calls ksft_exit_fail_msg, which ends the process; the 'return' after it is not reached. If test->feature_check(test) is false it reports a skip and goes to cleanup. Otherwise it runs test->run_test(test, uparams) and reports ksft_test_result(!ret, ...), pass when the return value is 0. The cleanup path, reached after a feature-check skip or after a reported result, runs test_cleanup: it calls test->cleanup if that is set, umount_resctrlfs() and signal_handler_unregister().

name: TEST_F(map, data_mmap)
prose: Test body (map_test.c:214-261; the slice began at line 255 inside it, so no test named metadata_pages_protection exists) for the map fixture, whose setup maps the per-CPU ring buffer of the current CPU into self->map_desc (desc->meta, desc->cpu_fd). It computes meta_len = meta_page_size and data_len = subbuf_size * nr_subbufs and, with ASSERT_*, checks that mmap(PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED, cpu_fd, offset meta_len) succeeds for the whole data area and for data_len - subbuf_size (each unmapped again); that mapping data_len (minus one subbuf) at offset meta_len + 2 * subbuf_size fails with MAP_FAILED (size overflow); and that mapping the full data_len at offset data_len + 2 * subbuf_size fails with MAP_FAILED (offset outside the buffer). If meta_page_size is larger than getpagesize() it maps the meta page area at offset 0 (must succeed), checks with ASSERT_EQ that every int from offset meta_struct_len up to meta_page_size reads as 0 (padding), and unmaps it. The body returns nothing; the first failed ASSERT ends it.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of param_test.c (lines 1483-1660; the slice was the tail). It scans argv from index 1, ignoring arguments that do not start with '-'. For -1 to -9 it needs a following argument (otherwise usage and return -1) and stores atol of it in loop_cnt[digit]; -m, -s, -D, -t and -r also need a following argument and a non-negative value (else usage and return -1) and set opt_modulo, opt_sleep, opt_disable_mod, opt_threads, opt_reps; -y, -k, -d, -v and -M set flags (opt_yield, opt_signal, opt_disable_rseq, verbose, opt_mo = RSEQ_MO_RELEASE); -T needs an argument whose first character is one of s, l, i, b, m, r (opt_test is set to it; any other character gives usage and return -1; opt_test defaults to 's'); -h prints usage and returns 0 at once (goto end); any other option gives usage and returns -1. It then runs exactly one test selected by opt_test: s spinlock, l linked list, b buffer, m memcpy buffer, i counter increment, r membarrier. name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of cs_prctl_test.c (lines 232-359; the slice began inside it). Globals: num_processes defaults to 2 and the local num_threads to 3, delay to 0. getopt uses ":hkT:P:d:": -P and -T set the process and thread counts (strtol/strtoul, no error check), -d the delay, -k sets keypress (and later delay = -1), -h calls printf(USAGE) and exit(EXIT_SUCCESS); any other result, including a missing option argument, calls handle_usage(20, "unknown option") which exits with status 20. num_processes outside 1..MAX_PROCESSES exits through handle_usage(1, ...), num_threads outside 1..MAX_THREADS through handle_usage(2, ...). It seeds rand with time, puts itself in a new process group with setpgid(0, 0) (failure calls handle_error, which exits with EXIT_FAILURE), creates num_processes child processes each with num_threads threads (a pipe failure calls handle_error; clone failures of the processes are not checked), sets need_cleanup, and runs a fixed sequence of core-scheduling prctl calls with validate() checks of the cookies (PR_SCHED_CORE_CREATE on the process group, CREATE on a random child's TGID, SHARE_TO that pid, SHARE_FROM one of its threads, SHARE_TO the process group). Each of these five _prctl calls returning < 0 calls handle_error (which prints, SIGTERMs all children if need_cleanup is set, and exits EXIT_FAILURE). Two further _prctl calls (PR_SCHED_CORE_MAX, and SHARE_TO with a nonzero arg5) are expected to fail with EINVAL and are checked through validate(), not handle_error. validate() counts failures in errors. After the sequence it prints TESTS FAILED with the error count and sets res = 10 when errors is nonzero, else prints SUCCESS. It then waits for getchar() when -k was given, otherwise sleeps delay seconds, sends signal 15 to each child process, and returns res (0 or 10).

name: TEST_F_SIGNAL(precedence, kill_is_highest, SIGSYS)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:1280-1307) for the precedence fixture, whose setup allocates six filter programs (allow, log, trace, error, trap, kill). Each program loads the syscall number and returns SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW for every syscall except getpid, for which it returns its own action (allow: always allow). The body reads getppid, sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS (ASSERT_EQ 0), and installs, with prctl(PR_SET_SECCOMP, SECCOMP_MODE_FILTER) and ASSERT_EQ(0, ...) each, the filters in the order allow, log, trace, error, trap, kill. It then expects syscall(__NR_getppid) to equal the parent pid (EXPECT_EQ) and calls syscall(__NR_getpid) with the comment 'should never return': the kill filter has the highest precedence, so the process is expected to be killed with SIGSYS, which is what TEST_F_SIGNAL(..., SIGSYS) checks. The final EXPECT_EQ(0, res) is only reached if getpid returns, which would be a failure.
note: Generated name replaced by the real macro invocation. Old prose checked against seccomp_bpf.c:1179-1307; it was essentially right but called the death 'the call never returns' without stating that SIGSYS death is the expected outcome checked by the TEST_F_SIGNAL harness. No reviewer claim.

It expects syscall(__NR_getppid) to return the parent pid and then calls syscall(__NR_getpid): the trap filter has the highest precedence among those installed, so the kernel raises SIGSYS; the test installs no handler, so the process is expected to die from SIGSYS, which TEST_F_SIGNAL(..., SIGSYS) checks. The last EXPECT_EQ(0, ...) is only reached if getpid returned.

name: user_notif_syscall
prose: Static function user_notif_syscall(nr, flags) in seccomp_bpf.c (lines 3360-3376). It builds a four-instruction classic BPF filter on the stack that loads the syscall number and returns SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF when it equals nr and SECCOMP_RET_ALLOW otherwise, and returns the result of seccomp(SECCOMP_SET_MODE_FILTER, flags, &prog), where seccomp() sets errno to 0 and returns syscall(__NR_seccomp, ...). So it returns what the kernel returns: 0 on success; with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER in flags, the new notification listener file descriptor (non-negative) on success; and -1 with errno set by the kernel on failure (the errors depend on the kernel, for example EINVAL for unsupported flags or EACCES without no_new_privs or CAP_SYS_ADMIN, and are not produced by this code); a SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_TSYNC failure can return a positive thread id. The filter is installed for the calling thread (and, with TSYNC, its threads) and stays installed for the process lifetime; the stack filter array is copied by the kernel.
note: Reviewers: round 2 (EFAULT cannot occur because the filter pointer is a valid local array) right; round 15 (success can return a listener fd when flags include SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER, not always 0) right (seccomp_bpf.c:305-309, 3360-3375, callers at 3423). The old prose also enumerated errno values the code does not produce. The TSYNC return value is from the seccomp(2) interface, not from this file. Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: TEST(user_notification_continue)
prose: Test body (seccomp_bpf.c:3842-3926). It sets PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS (ASSERT_EQ 0), installs a user-notification filter for __NR_dup with SECCOMP_FILTER_FLAG_NEW_LISTENER through user_notif_syscall (ASSERT_GE 0 for the listener), and forks (ASSERT_GE 0). The child creates a pipe, calls dup on the read end (which is held for the supervisor), asserts the fd differs, and ASSERT_EQ(filecmp(self, self, pipe_fds[0], dup_fd), 0) before exit(0). The parent polls the listener (expecting revents == POLLIN), receives the notification with SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_RECV (expecting 0), polls again (expecting revents == POLLOUT), expects req.data.nr == __NR_dup, and sets resp.id and resp.flags = SECCOMP_USER_NOTIF_FLAG_CONTINUE. It then sends SECCOMP_IOCTL_NOTIF_SEND three times: with error 0 and val USER_NOTIF_MAGIC it expects -1 with errno EINVAL, with error USER_NOTIF_MAGIC and val 0 the same, and with error 0 and val 0 it expects 0 (if that fails with EINVAL the SKIP(goto skip, ...) jumps to the reap step). It finally expects waitpid to return the child's pid, the child to have exited normally, and its exit status to be 0; a status of 2 makes the test skip with SKIP(return, ...) (kcmp not supported). Everything uses non-fatal EXPECT_* except the ASSERTs named above; nothing is returned.

prose: Test body (sgx/main.c:616-715) for the enclave fixture. After ASSERT_TRUE(setup_test_encl(...)) and zeroing self->run, it takes data_start = encl_base + data offset + PAGE_SIZE (the second page of the .data segment). It then mprotect()s the page to PROT_READ (a failure only prints with perror), sets the put value to MAGIC2 and calls the enclave again, expecting the call to return 0 with exception_vector 14, exception_error_code 0x7 and exception_addr == data_start (a page fault reported through the vDSO); it clears the three exception fields, mprotect()s the page back to PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE (failure only perror), resumes the enclave with vdso_sgx_enter_enclave(..., ERESUME, ...) expecting 0, EEXIT and no exception, and finally reads the address again expecting MAGIC2, EEXIT and no exception. name: test4_lseek
prose: Static function test4_lseek(fd) in adi-test.c (lines 466-513). It checks a sequence of seeks on the ADI device descriptor using seek_adi, which calls lseek(fd, offset, whence), records the timing on success, and then always calls lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END) with the result ignored before returning the result of the first lseek; the test does not assume that this extra call moves the position (it expects the following SEEK_CUR calls to continue from the previous offset). Steps: (1) seek_adi(fd, 0x123456789abcdef0, SEEK_SET) must return the same offset, else ret = -1; (2) the same SEEK_SET again must return a negative value with errno == EINVAL, else ret = -2 (errno is read after seek_adi's extra lseek, which could change it); (3) seek_adi(fd, 0, SEEK_CUR) must return the original offset, else -3; (4) seek_adi(fd, 0x100, SEEK_CUR) must return offset + 0x100, else -4; (5) seek_adi(fd, 0xFFFFFFF000000000, SEEK_CUR) must return offset + 0x100 + 0xFFFFFFF000000000, else -5. A failing step prints a message with the step code to stderr and jumps to out; with all steps passing ret = 0. It returns ret (through RETURN_FROM_TEST, which may print a debug line). The fd stays open and nothing is allocated.
note: Reviewer round 15 (seek_adi does not leave fd at EOF: the SEEK_END result is ignored and the test expects the position unchanged) right (adi-test.c:308-310, 492-508); the old prose claimed each seek_adi leaves fd at end-of-file. Tally 1 right 0 wrong.

name: change_skew_test
prose: Function change_skew_test(ppm) in change_skew.c (lines 33-52). It declares an uninitialised struct timex, sets only modes = ADJ_FREQUENCY and freq = ppm << 16, and calls adjtimex. The shift is defined only for 0 <= ppm <= 32767 (a negative ppm shifts a negative value, and ppm >= 32768 overflows int); the function does not check ppm. If adjtimex returns a negative value it prints "Error adjusting freq" and returns that value without running the child programs. Otherwise it runs system("./raw_skew"), system("./inconsistency-check") and system("./nanosleep") in that order and returns the bitwise OR of the three system() results (the adjtimex result is not part of it): each is -1 if the child could not be run or the wait status otherwise, so the result is -1 if any of them failed to start, else 0 only when all three exited with status 0, and otherwise nonzero.
note: No reviewer claims on the current text (round 2 claim on negative ppm is already in the text). Checked against change_skew.c:33-52.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of change_skew.c (lines 55-93); argc and argv are unused. It first runs system("killall -9 ntpd") (result ignored), then calls adjtimex with modes = ADJ_OFFSET and offset = 0 on an uninitialised struct timex; the call's copy-back fills the whole struct from the kernel, including tx.freq. If that call returns a negative value it prints "Maybe you're not running as root?" and returns -1. Otherwise it loops over ppm values 0, 250, 500, -250, -500, printing "Using %i ppm adjustment" and calling change_skew_test(ppm), and stops at the first nonzero result (which includes a negative adjtimex result inside change_skew_test). It then calls adjtimex with modes = ADJ_FREQUENCY and tx.offset = 0 (ignored, since ADJ_OFFSET is not in modes) with tx.freq still equal to the value copied back by the first adjtimex call, so the frequency is set back to that earlier value; its return value is ignored. Finally, if the last result was nonzero it prints "[FAIL]" and calls ksft_exit_fail(); otherwise it prints "[OK]" and calls ksft_exit_pass(). Both exit the process, so main does not return normally after the first adjtimex succeeds.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of leap-a-day.c (lines 178-381; the slice began inside it). getopt uses "wti:": -w sets settime = 0 and prints a message, -i sets the iteration count (atoi, default 10), -t enables TAI output; any other option prints usage and calls exit(-1). With -t it checks clock_gettime(CLOCK_TAI): on failure it prints a message and calls ksft_exit_fail(). It installs handler for SIGINT (and tries SIGKILL, which cannot be caught) and sigalarm as the handler for SIGRTMAX; handler calls clear_time_state() and exit(0). Each loop iteration computes next_leap as the next UTC midnight, sets the system time to next_leap - 10 seconds unless -w was given, calls clear_time_state(), sets STA_INS (or STA_DEL, alternating each iteration through insert) with adjtimex, and checks it was set. adjtimex returning negative, the flag not being set, and timer_create failing each print a message and call ksft_exit_fail() without calling clear_time_state(). It arms a timer for next_leap, sleeps until 3 seconds before it, re-sets the flag if it was cleared, and prints adjtimex state every half second until the reported time reaches next_leap + 2. It then flips insert, runs test_hrtimer_failure, and if error_found is set (by sigalarm or test_hrtimer_failure) it prints a message, calls clear_time_state() and ksft_exit_fail(). The loop ends with 'if iterations != -1 and --iterations == 0 break', so iterations -1 loops until interrupted, and values 0 or below -1 also never reach zero. After the loop it calls clear_time_state() and ksft_exit_pass(). Since ksft_exit_* terminate the process, main does not return to its caller.

name: loop_queue_tgt_io
prose: Static function loop_queue_tgt_io(t, q, tag) in ublk/file_backed.c (lines 77-103) takes a ublk thread, a queue and a tag; it fetches the I/O descriptor with ublk_get_iod(q, tag). It dispatches on ublksrv_get_op(iod): UBLK_IO_OP_FLUSH calls loop_queue_flush_io, which allocates one SQE with ublk_io_alloc_sqes (not checked for failure), prepares an IORING_FSYNC_DATASYNC fsync on the registered backing file with IOSQE_FIXED_FILE and returns 1; UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE_ZEROES and UBLK_IO_OP_DISCARD give -ENOTSUP without preparing any SQE; UBLK_IO_OP_READ and UBLK_IO_OP_WRITE call loop_queue_tgt_rw_io; any other operation gives -EINVAL. loop_queue_tgt_rw_io has two shapes: when the queue is not zero-copy or uses auto zero-copy it allocates one SQE and returns -ENOMEM if the SQE pointer is NULL, otherwise prepares one read/write SQE and returns 1; when it is zero-copy without auto zero-copy it allocates three SQEs (not checked), prepares a buffer-register, a fixed read/write and a buffer-unregister SQE and returns 2. So the return value is 1 (flush, or one-SQE read/write), 2 (three-SQE zero-copy read/write), -ENOTSUP, -EINVAL, or -ENOMEM (only from the one-SQE read/write path). name: trigger_uevent
prose: Function trigger_uevent(times) in uevent_filtering.c (lines 195-218) opens "/sys/devices/virtual/mem/full/uevent" with O_RDWR|O_CLOEXEC. If the open fails it returns -1 when errno is ENOENT and -EINVAL for any other errno. Otherwise it loops i from 0 to times - 1, writing the 4 bytes "add\n" with write_nointr (which retries on EINTR and returns write()'s result: the byte count, or -1 with errno set on failure); on a negative result it prints "Failed to trigger uevent" and stops the loop. It closes the fd and returns ret, the result of the last write performed: 4 when the writes succeeded (a short write would return its smaller count), or -1 when the last write failed (the value is -1, not a negative errno). If times is 0, ret is never assigned and the returned value is indeterminate.

name: mess_with_syscall
prose: Static function mess_with_syscall(testpid, pass) in x86/syscall_numbering.c (lines 353-395); returns nothing. It first sets sh->probing_syscall = false. For pass PTP_NOTHING or PTP_DONE it returns at once without touching the child's registers. Otherwise it reads the child's registers with PTRACE_GETREGS (the result is not checked) and, if regs.orig_rax differs from regs.rbx, calls fail(), which prints a message and increments sh->nerr but does not stop. Then by pass: PTP_GETREGS returns without writing registers; PTP_WRITEBACK writes them back unchanged; PTP_FUZZRET sets rax to MODIFIED_BY_PTRACE (-9999); PTP_FUZZHIGH sets rax to MODIFIED_BY_PTRACE and ORs 0xffffffff00000000 into orig_rax; PTP_INTNUM sets rax to MODIFIED_BY_PTRACE and replaces orig_rax with (int)orig_rax (sign extension of the low 32 bits). For these three and PTP_WRITEBACK it then calls PTRACE_SETREGS (result not checked). For any other pass value (not reachable with the enum values handled above) it calls crit(), which prints a failure and a skip message and calls exit(EX_OSERR), so PTRACE_SETREGS is not reached.

prose: main(argc, argv) of x86/test_shadow_stack.c in the build variant that has CET support (lines 978-1087; when the compiler is older than GCC 8.5 a different main at line 64 just prints a skip message and returns 0). argc and argv are unused; ret starts at 0. name: enable_tracer
prose: Static function enable_tracer() in latency-collector.c (lines 1437-1446), no parameters, no return value. It is meant to run after save_and_disable_tracer() has filled save_state (the saved option values, their valid flags and the saved threshold string). It takes save_state.mutex, calls set_trace_opts(&save_state, use_options), then write_file(TR_THRESH, save_state.thresh, threshold, ERR_CLEANUP) and write_file(TR_CURRENT, NOP_TRACER, current_tracer, ERR_CLEANUP), and releases the mutex. set_trace_opts writes to the trace_options file, through set_trace_opt, each option that was found to exist (opt_valid) and whose saved value differs from the wanted use_options value, warning and calling cleanup_exit(EXIT_FAILURE) if a write fails. write_file writes the global string threshold (not the saved threshold) to the threshold file, skipped when the saved value is non-NULL and equal to it (needs_change), and writes the global current_tracer to the current_tracer file, skipped when it equals "nop" (NOP_TRACER); a failed write warns with warnx and calls cleanup_exit(EXIT_FAILURE) (ERR_CLEANUP). name: timerlat_aa_init
prose: Function timerlat_aa_init(tool, dump_tasks) in rtla/src/timerlat_aa.c (lines 1023-1056). It reads nr_cpus locally with sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_CONF), allocates a zeroed timerlat_aa_context (failure returns -1 with nothing installed), stores it in the global __timerlat_aa_ctx (overwriting any previous pointer without freeing it) and fills nr_cpus, tool and dump_tasks. It then allocates the per-CPU taa_data array with calloc(nr_cpus, ...), calls timerlat_aa_init_seqs(taa_ctx) and timerlat_aa_register_events(tool, dump_tasks). If any of those three fails it calls timerlat_aa_destroy() and returns -1; timerlat_aa_destroy frees the context (and, when taa_data was allocated, first unregisters the events, destroys the seqs and frees taa_data) but does not reset __timerlat_aa_ctx, so the global is left pointing at freed memory after a failed init. On success it returns 0.

name: timerlat_bpf_wait
prose: Function timerlat_bpf_wait(timeout) in rtla/src/timerlat_bpf.c (lines 96-107), compiled only with HAVE_BPF_SKEL. It uses the file-scope skeleton pointer bpf, which must already have been loaded by timerlat_bpf_init (there is no NULL check). It creates a libbpf ring buffer on the signal_stop_tracing map with ring_buffer__new(bpf_map__fd(...), handle_rb_event, NULL, NULL), where handle_rb_event ignores the data and returns 0, then calls ring_buffer__poll(rb, timeout * 1000), frees the ring buffer with ring_buffer__free and returns the poll result. The result of ring_buffer__new is not checked: if it returned NULL, ring_buffer__poll would dereference it (libbpf's ring_buffer__poll reads rb->epoll_fd without a NULL check), so there is no -EINVAL return for a failed creation. ring_buffer__poll returns the number of records consumed (capped at INT_MAX, 0 on timeout), or a negative errno taken from epoll_wait (for example -EINTR when a signal interrupts the wait) or from record processing. The argument is multiplied by 1000 before being passed as the millisecond timeout, so timeout is in units of 1000 ms, and a negative value makes epoll_wait wait without a timeout; the int multiplication overflows for |timeout| above 2147483.
note: Old record was still-rejected on mechanical contract-vs-prose checks only (no reviewer claim). I checked libbpf's ring_buffer__poll and ring_buffer__free in tools/lib/bpf/ringbuf.c:172-187, 336-357. The old claims that a ring-buffer creation failure returns -EINVAL and that the free means 'no reference escapes' were unsupported or wrong, and the contract is dropped because the function uses the global bpf and system calls.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of aio_multibuff.c (lines 234-380; the slice began at 256). It returns 1 after printing a message when argc != 2 and when the malloc of ep_path fails. It builds "<argv[1]>/ep0", opens it O_RDWR and writes the descriptors and then the strings structures to it; an open failure or a write returning < 0 prints with perror and returns 1 (ep_path and, once opened, ep0 are not released). It opens "<argv[1]>/ep1" (failure returns 1 without freeing ep_path or closing ep0) and then frees ep_path. After that point it zeroes ctx and calls io_setup(AIO_MAX, &ctx), and eventfd(0, 0); a failure of either prints a message and returns 1 (ep0 and ep1, and after the eventfd failure also the aio context, are not released; ep_path is already freed). It then initialises two io_buffer sets with init_bufs and loops on select over ep0 and the eventfd: select failing with errno other than EINTR (EINTR retries) breaks the loop; ep0 events go to handle_ep0, which sets the 'ready' flag; until ready is true the loop continues; for each of the two buffer sets that has no requests outstanding it prepares pwrite requests on ep1 with eventfd notification and submits them with io_submit, recording the number accepted (a failed io_submit is only printed); when the eventfd is readable it reads it (a failed read breaks the loop), reaps events with io_getevents(ctx, 1, BUFS_MAX, ...), subtracts them from the current buffer's outstanding count and advances to the other buffer when the count is 0. After a break it deletes both buffer sets with delete_bufs, io_destroy(ctx), closes ep1 and ep0 and returns 0.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) of aio_simple.c (lines 222-386; the slice began inside it). It returns 1 after a message if argc != 2 or the malloc of ep_path fails. It opens "<argv[1]>/ep0" (failure returns 1), writes the descriptors and strings to it (a write returning < 0 returns 1), then in a loop opens "<argv[1]>/ep1" and "<argv[1]>/ep2" into ep[0] and ep[1] (a failure prints 'unable to open ep%d' with the file number 1 or 2 and returns 1). It then frees ep_path, calls io_setup(2, &ctx) and eventfd(0, 0), each failure printing a message and returning 1 (descriptors open, the aio context not destroyed after an eventfd failure). It then loops on select over ep0 and the eventfd: select failing with errno other than EINTR breaks the loop; ep0 activity goes to handle_ep0, which sets the 'ready' flag; until ready is true the loop continues; when the eventfd is readable it reads it (a failed read breaks the loop), reaps events with io_getevents(ctx, 1, 2, ...) and clears req_in or req_out according to which endpoint the completed request used; if the IN transfer is not outstanding it prepares a pwrite of buf_in on ep[0] with eventfd notification and submits it, and likewise a pread of buf_out on ep[1] for OUT (a failed io_submit is only printed). name: static int enable_%%MODEL_NAME%%(void)
prose: Generated function enable_%%MODEL_NAME%% (template tools/verification/rvgen/rvgen/templates/ltl2k/main.c, lines 57-68), where %%MODEL_NAME%% is replaced by the model name when a monitor is generated; it is the .enable callback of the monitor's struct rv_monitor and takes no parameters. It calls ltl_monitor_init(); if that returns nonzero the function returns that value at once, before the %%TRACEPOINT_ATTACH%% placeholder is expanded, so no tracepoint probe of this function is attached. ltl_monitor_init (include/rv/ltl_monitor.h) gets a task monitor slot (returning its negative error if that fails), attaches a probe on task_newtask, and initialises the LTL monitor state of every existing thread and each present CPU's idle task. On success the function expands the generated tracepoint-attach code (whatever %%TRACEPOINT_ATTACH%% becomes) and returns 0; the matching disable function detaches the tracepoints and calls ltl_monitor_destroy().

Reviewer round 15 (formal contract only constrains the return sign and omits attaching and disable ownership) right as a criticism of the contract, which is removed (the function touches kernel global state and generated code). name: static int __init register_%%MODEL_NAME%%(void)
prose: Generated function register_%%MODEL_NAME%% (template ltl2k/main.c lines 87-90), the module init function (module_init) of a generated monitor, with no parameters. It returns rv_register_monitor(&rv_%%MODEL_NAME%%, %%PARENT%%), where %%PARENT%% is substituted by the generator (a parent monitor pointer or NULL). rv_register_monitor returns -EINVAL if the monitor name is too long or if the parent is itself a nested monitor, -EEXIST if a monitor of the same name is already registered, the error of create_monitor_dir if creating the monitor's directory fails, and 0 after adding the monitor to the monitor list; it takes and releases rv_interface_lock internally. On a nonzero return the monitor is not added to the list, although monitor->parent may already have been set. After a successful return the module's exit function unregister_%%MODEL_NAME%% calls rv_unregister_monitor.

name: used_empty
prose: Function used_empty() in virtio_ring_0_9.c (lines 197-208) returns bool and only reads state. It reads guest.last_used_idx (and, under RING_POLL, ring.used->ring[last_used_idx & (ring_size - 1)].id). Without RING_POLL it returns ring.used->idx == guest.last_used_idx, true when the host has published no used entry beyond last_used_idx. Under RING_POLL it returns the expression (id ^ last_used_idx ^ 0x8000) & ~(ring_size - 1) converted to bool, so it is true when that expression is nonzero (the id field at the slot does not carry the expected high bits and thus no new used entry is visible there) and false when it is zero. It requires the ring to have been set up by alloc_ring.
note: Reviewers: round 1 (contract omits the initialisation precondition) moot, contract removed; round 2 (ignores the RING_POLL branch) right; round 15 (RING_POLL returns true when the high-bit expression is nonzero, not zero as the prose said) right (virtio_ring_0_9.c:204). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: enable_call
prose: Function enable_call() in virtio_ring_0_9.c (lines 217-224), returns bool. It stores guest.last_used_idx into vring_used_event(&ring), which the virtio ring header defines as ring.avail->ring[ring.num] (the used-event slot at the end of the available ring, not a field of the used ring), executes smp_mb(), and returns used_empty(). So the return value is true when no used entry beyond last_used_idx is visible after the store (ring.used->idx == last_used_idx without RING_POLL, or, under RING_POLL, the used_empty expression (id ^ last_used_idx ^ 0x8000) & ~(ring_size - 1) being nonzero), and false when a new used entry is already available. It requires the ring to have been set up by alloc_ring.
