name: static bool run_output_check(const output_check oc, const atf::fs::path& path, const std::string& stdxxx)
prose: Static function run_output_check(oc, path, stdxxx) in atf-sh/atf-check.cpp (lines 681-761) checks the captured output file path (stdxxx names the stream, "stdout" or "stderr", in the messages) against one output_check and returns true when the check passes. By oc.type: oc_empty passes when the file is empty and oc.negated is false, or non-empty and oc.negated is true; when it fails with negated false it prints "Fail: <stream> not empty" and a diff against /dev/null, and when it fails with negated true it prints only "Fail: <stream> is empty" (no diff and no file content); oc_file compares path with the file oc.value: a failure prints "does not match golden output" and a diff, or, when negated and equal, "matches golden output" and the golden file's content; oc_ignore always passes; oc_inline writes decode(oc.value) to a temporary file and compares it the same way (diff or the temporary file's content on failure); oc_match passes when some line of path matches the regular expression oc.value (grep_file, line by line) xor oc.negated, and on failure prints "Fail: regexp <re> not in/is in <stream>" followed by the whole file content; oc_save (which requires oc.negated to be false, checked with INV) copies path's bytes to the file named oc.value, truncating it, without checking for copy errors, and returns true; any other type reaches UNREACHABLE and returns false. Diagnostics go to stderr (the diff output is also connected to stderr). The helpers compare_files, grep_file and cat_file throw std::runtime_error when a file cannot be opened or read, in which case the function does not return normally.
note: Reviewers: original (oc_save requires !oc.negated, omitted; negated and match failures cat files rather than diffs) right (atf-check.cpp:704-707, 736-740, 744); round 15 (an oc_empty failure with negated true writes a diagnostic but no diff or file content) right (lines 692-694). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: bc_lex_token
prose: Function bc_lex_token(l) in bc/src/bc_lex.c (lines 170-504, compiled when BC_ENABLED); it must be called with the signal lock held (BC_SIG_ASSERT_LOCKED). It reads c = l->buf[l->i++], so l->i is incremented before the switch and the token describes the character that was at l->i on entry plus any further characters consumed. It sets l->t by character class: whitespace and NUL characters go to bc_lex_commonTokens; '!' gives BC_LEX_OP_REL_NE with '=' or BOOL_NOT otherwise (the latter with a POSIX diagnostic); '"' calls bc_lex_string; '#' gives a POSIX diagnostic and then bc_lex_lineComment (whitespace); '%', '*', '^', '/' (unless '/*', which starts a comment), '+', '-' pick the plain or assignment operator, '++' and '--' become increment and decrement; '&' and '|' require a doubled character for BC_LEX_OP_BOOL_AND/OR (with a POSIX diagnostic) and otherwise call bc_lex_invalidChar; '.' starts a number if a number character follows, otherwise it is BC_LEX_KW_LAST with a POSIX diagnostic; digits and the capital letters A to Z call bc_lex_number; lowercase letters call bc_lex_identifier (keyword or name); '(' ')' '[' ']' '{' '}' ',' ';' map to their punctuation tokens; '<' and '>' pick the relational, shift (only with BC_ENABLE_EXTRA_MATH) and assign variants; '=' gives '==' or assignment; backslash followed by a newline is whitespace and otherwise an invalid character; '$' and '@' are the truncate and places operators when BC_ENABLE_EXTRA_MATH is set; any other character calls bc_lex_invalidChar. Errors: bc_lex_invalidChar sets BC_LEX_INVALID and raises a parse error that does not return. The diagnostics for POSIX-forbidden constructs (the BC_ERR_POSIX_* codes) are errors only in the strict POSIX mode; otherwise, per bc_vm_handleError (vm.c:350-359), they print a warning when warnings are enabled and return silently when not, so the token is still produced and the function returns normally.
note: Reviewers: original (l->i is incremented before the switch, so the token corresponds to the character at l->i - 1 after the increment, i.e. at l->i on entry) right as a wording point, the old text already said 'on entry'; round 15 (POSIX-forbidden constructs are allowed in non-POSIX mode; no error is raised and the function returns normally) right (vm.c:350-359). Tally 2 right 0 wrong. I did not read bc_lex_commonTokens, bc_lex_number, bc_lex_identifier beyond their call conditions.

The parse results are stored in the parser and lexer state p.

name: bc_history_enableRaw
prose: Static function bc_history_enableRaw(h) in bc/src/history.c (lines 821-877). On non-Windows builds it asserts BC_TTYIN, and if h->rawMode is already true it returns immediately without changing anything. Otherwise it takes the signal lock, saves the terminal attributes of stdin with tcgetattr into h->orig_termios (failure calls bc_vm_fatalError(BC_ERR_FATAL_IO_ERR), which does not return), releases the lock, copies the attributes, clears BRKINT, ICRNL, INPCK, ISTRIP and IXON from the input flags, sets CS8 in the control flags, clears ECHO, ICANON, IEXTEN and ISIG from the local flags, sets VMIN = 1 and VTIME = 0, and calls tcsetattr(STDIN_FILENO, TCSAFLUSH, &raw) with the lock held, repeating it while it fails with EINTR; a final failure calls bc_vm_fatalError(BC_ERR_FATAL_IO_ERR). On Windows nothing is done to the terminal here (the comment says raw mode is set in bc_history_init) and h->orig_termios is not touched. In every path that returns normally, h->rawMode is true afterwards.
note: Reviewers: original (on Windows rawMode is set without saving orig_termios) right (history.c:823-826, 876); round 15 (the precondition wrongly requires h->rawMode to be false, but the code returns early when it is true) right (history.c:832). Tally 2 right 0 wrong.

name: bc_program_call
prose: Static function bc_program_call(p, code, bgn) in bc/src/program.c (starting line 1787), returns nothing; it executes a function-call instruction. It reads the number of arguments nargs and the function index from the bytecode at *bgn, sets the new instruction pointer to index 0 of that function and looks the function up in p->fns. Errors are raised with bc_verr/bc_err and do not return: BC_ERR_EXEC_UNDEF_FUNC when the function has no code, BC_ERR_EXEC_PARAMS when nargs differs from the function's parameter count, and BC_ERR_EXEC_VOID_VAL (bc_err) in the argument loop when an argument is a void result. It records the current length of the results stack in the new frame (so the callee's results can be discarded later), then for each argument it copies the result into a variable with bc_program_copyToVar, which pops that argument result from the results stack (the arguments do not stay on the stack); parameters not passed are initialized as empty or default variables, and the instruction pointer of the callee is pushed on the instruction stack. The results stack depth is checked only by an assert, not at run time.
note: Reviewer round 15 (results-stack check is only an assert) right (program.c); the old prose said the arguments stay on the results stack, which is wrong because copyToVar pops each one. Tally 1 right 0 wrong. I read the whole function.

name: bc_program_reset
prose: Function bc_program_reset(p) in bc/src/program.c (starting line 3003), returns nothing. It resets the interpreter after an error or interrupt: it pops the instruction stack down to the bottom frame, resets the bottom frame's instruction index to the end of its function (so execution stops), clears the tail-call and related state, and clears the signal flag. In interactive dc mode (not bc) it also pops the results stack down to its bottom, by npop, popping the top nresults entries (not just one), so the results stack ends up with the entries that existed before the failed command removed. It does not return a status.
note: Both reviewers (original and round 15, about popping the top nresults entries in interactive dc) right. Tally 2 right 0 wrong. The description is qualified: I read the function but did not trace every state field it clears.

It returns 0 if e < 3 or e is even, or if p or q has a bit length outside the supported range (the byte length must be 5 up to BR_MAX_RSA_FACTOR/8) or is even. If d is NULL it returns dlen = (n_bitlen + 7) >> 3 without computing. It computes phi = (p-1)(q-1) = k * e + r; r == 0 returns 0. name: MakeUnmade
prose: Function MakeUnmade(gn, pgn) in bmake/compat.c (lines 519-627), returns bool. IMPSRC is set only after the children have succeeded. It returns true for MADE and for ERROR in keep-going (-k) mode; false for ABORTED and UPTODATE. In query mode it calls exit(1); otherwise it exits after PrintOnError.

name: Cond_EvalLine
prose: Function Cond_EvalLine(line) in bmake/cond.c (lines 1014-1164), returns CondResult. Names that are not if/else/endif give CR_ERROR. An endif, else or elif without a preceding if is a fatal error with CR_TRUE. For .if, a CR_ERROR from CondEvalExpression returns CR_FALSE with IFS_WAS_ACTIVE. The cond_states array is allocated and grown in steps of 32.

If the F1 help callback fails it sets retval to ERROR and the loop ends. The epilogue allocates items[i].value (owned by the caller), sets *focusitem to form.sel, frees buffers, calls delwin and end_dialog, and returns retval.

name: main
prose: main(argc, argv) in snmp/gensnmpdef.c (lines 503-588), returns int. The -c option value is parsed with strtol and errors, trailing text or out-of-range values call err(1); an empty -c is accepted as 0. -h prints usage and exits 0; an unknown option is ignored. malloc or smiLoadModule failure calls err(1). It loops over the modules, calls close_node and tdefs_cleanup, and returns 0.

name: main
prose: Entry point of gensnmptree. Precondition: argc and argv are the process arguments. It loops over getopt with the option string "dEeFfhI:i:lp:t": -d sets the debug flag; -E, -e and -t choose the operation (OP_ENUMS, OP_EXTRACT, OP_TREE; the default is OP_GEN) and call errx(1) if an incompatible operation was already chosen (-t is accepted only after OP_GEN or OP_TREE); -F and -f choose GEN_FUNCS_C or GEN_FUNCS_H and call errx(1) if the other one was already chosen; -h writes the usage text to stderr and calls exit(0); -I calls path_new(optarg); -i records the input file name; -l sets localincs; -p records the file prefix and calls errx(1) if strlen(prefix) + strlen("tree.c") exceeds MAXPATHLEN. An unknown option letter has no case in the switch (getopt itself prints a diagnostic) and parsing just continues. It then reads the input from stdin, or from the -i file (err(1) if fopen fails), parses the first top-level construct with parse_top(gettoken()), merges every further construct into root until TOK_EOF, calls check_tree(root) only if root is non-NULL, and dispatches on op: OP_EXTRACT calls errx(1) when no operands remain, otherwise calls gen_extract(stdout, root, argv[i]) for each operand and calls errx(1) at the first operand for which it returns non-zero, else returns 0; OP_ENUMS calls make_enums(argc, argv, gen_funcs) and returns 0; OP_TREE calls errx(1) if operands remain, else gen_tree(root, 0) and returns 0; OP_GEN calls errx(1) if operands remain, else make_table(root, gen_funcs == GEN_FUNCS_H) and returns 0. The switch has no default case. The callees (parse_top, merge, check_tree, gen_*) may themselves terminate the process; they were not read in detail.
note: Reviewer claim 2 (OP_EXTRACT uses extract_enum) is wrong: gensnmptree.c main calls gen_extract(stdout, root, argv[i]) in the OP_EXTRACT case (the extract_enum calls are in make_enums). Claim 1 (check_tree only if root non-NULL) is right and already reflected. Real prose error found by hand: invalid options do not errx(1) (no '?' case in the switch).

name: snmp_set
prose: SET request processor of the SNMP agent library. Precondition: pdu is a parsed SET request whose nbindings does not exceed SNMP_MAX_BINDINGS (the local context arrays node[] and scratch[] are sized by it), resp is a PDU to fill, resp_b the output buffer, data the caller's context pointer. Steps: it builds the response header with snmp_pdu_create_response and snmp_pdu_encode_header; if the header cannot be encoded it returns SNMP_RET_IGN at once, without freeing resp, without touching pdu->error_status/error_index and without calling snmp_dep_finish. Phase 1, for each binding: find_node must find a node (otherwise error_index = i+1 and error_status is SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME for SNMPv1, else SNMP_ERR_NOT_WRITEABLE if find_subnode finds an intermediate node, SNMP_ERR_NO_ACCESS if the exception is SNMP_SYNTAX_NOSUCHOBJECT, otherwise SNMP_ERR_NO_CREATION); a leaf without SNMP_NODE_CANSET gives NOSUCHNAME (v1) or NOT_WRITEABLE; a syntax mismatch gives BADVALUE (v1) or WRONG_TYPE; a failed snmp_value_copy gives GENERR; a binding that cannot be encoded gives TOOBIG (ASN_ERR_EOBUF) or GENERR. Each of these failures sets error_index = i+1, calls snmp_pdu_free(resp) and returns SNMP_RET_ERR. Phase 2 calls the node's SET action for each binding (context.ctx.code starts as SNMP_RET_OK); for SNMPv1 several error codes are mapped to BADVALUE, NOSUCHNAME or GENERR; the first non-zero result sets error_index = i+1 and error_status = that code, calls rollback() for the bindings before i (the failing binding itself is not rolled back), frees resp, sets the result code to SNMP_RET_ERR and jumps to the common exit. Phase 3 runs snmp_dep_commit; if it fails, error_status is its code and error_index is the last var_index (the last binding index, nbindings; 0 if there are no bindings); if snmp_dep_rollback then also fails and the PDU is not v1, error_status becomes SNMP_ERR_UNDO_FAILED and error_index 0; then rollback() is called for all nbindings bindings, resp is freed, the code becomes SNMP_RET_ERR and control goes to the common exit. Phase 4 calls each action with SNMP_OP_COMMIT (a failure is only logged); then snmp_fix_encoding is called and, if it does not return SNMP_CODE_OK, resp is freed and the code becomes SNMP_RET_IGN. The common exit (reached only from phases 2 to 4) calls snmp_dep_finish and returns the code, which is SNMP_RET_OK unless changed as above. The early returns of phase 1 do not pass through snmp_dep_finish (the dependency list is still empty at that point).
note: Reviewer: header-encoding failure returns IGN without freeing resp/error fields (right, snmpagent.c:681-682, already in prose). Round-15 claim 'dependency commit failure sets error_index 0' is only right when the dependency rollback also fails on a non-v1 PDU (lines 874-877); otherwise error_index is context.ctx.var_index. Old prose also wrongly said the failing binding index was used and that the dependency list is finished on every path reaching the common exit without distinguishing the phase-1 returns.

name: op_ifxtable
prose: Slice cut the head: this is the tail of op_ifxtable (defined at line 366), the handler for the ifXTable columns. Precondition: ctx and value are valid, sub is the number of OID sub-identifiers before the column, op is an snmp_op. GETNEXT returns SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME when there is no next interface, otherwise rewrites value->var to the next interface index; GET returns NOSUCHNAME if the instance suffix is not exactly one sub-identifier or the interface is unknown; SET returns SNMP_ERR_NO_CREATION for a bad suffix or unknown interface, SNMP_ERR_RES_UNAVAIL if snmp_dep_lookup fails, and for ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable and ifPromiscuousMode returns WRONG_VALUE unless the integer is 1 or 2, INCONS_VALUE if that field was already set in this request, otherwise records it in the dependency record and returns NOERROR; any other SET column returns NOT_WRITEABLE; ROLLBACK and COMMIT return NOERROR without doing anything. For GET and GETNEXT it calls mib_fetch_ifmib(ifp) (result ignored) when ifp->mibtick < this_tick and then fills value for the column: ifName and ifAlias use string_get (result NOERROR, or RES_UNAVAIL if malloc fails; ifAlias passes ifp->alias_size - 1 as the length), the multicast/broadcast/HC counters, ifLinkUpDownTrapEnable (1 or 2 from trap_enable), ifHighSpeed ((baudrate + 499999) / 1000000), ifPromiscuousMode (1 if IFF_PROMISC else 2), ifConnectorPresent (1 or 2) and ifCounterDiscontinuityTime (counter_disc - start_tick if counter_disc > start_tick, else 0) are stored in value->v; a column not in that switch leaves value unchanged and returns NOERROR.
note: Dropped by earlier rounds only because the function name was not in the slice; the real function is op_ifxtable (mibII_interfaces.c:366).

name: op_begemot_ntp
prose: Slice cut the head: this is op_begemot_ntp (defined at line 1472), the handler for the begemotNtp scalars; the leaf is value->var.subs[sub-1]. GETNEXT aborts the process (abort()). GET returns string_get of ntp_host or ntp_port, stores ntp_timeout or ntp_debug in value->v.uint32 and returns NOERROR, and for begemotNtpJitter/begemotNtpStability calls fetch_sysinfo() first when this_tick > sysinfo_tick (SNMP_ERR_GENERR if it returns -1, otherwise sysinfo_tick = this_tick) and returns SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME if the corresponding sysb_* flag is not set, otherwise stores the scaled counter64 and returns NOERROR. SET of the host or port leaf returns SNMP_ERR_NOT_WRITEABLE unless community == COMM_INITIALIZE, otherwise returns string_save's result for the new string (non-zero error code on malloc failure, leaving the old pointer in place) or NOERROR; SET of the timeout leaf first stores the old timeout in ctx->scratch->int1, then returns SNMP_ERR_WRONG_VALUE if the new value is 0 (value->v.uint32 < 1) without changing ntp_timeout, else sets ntp_timeout and returns NOERROR; SET of the debug leaf stores the old ntp_debug in scratch->int1, sets ntp_debug and returns NOERROR. ROLLBACK restores via string_rollback (host, port) or from scratch->int1 (timeout, debug) and returns NOERROR; COMMIT calls string_commit for host and port, does nothing for timeout and debug, and returns NOERROR. An op or leaf that is not handled in the relevant switch falls to abort().
note: Old prose omitted the GET branch (including GENERR/NOSUCHNAME for jitter/stability) and said the timeout rollback value is stored only when the value is valid; code stores scratch->int1 before the range check (snmp_ntp.c:1572-1574). Dropped earlier for a mechanical name reason.

name: op_snmp
prose: Handler for the mib-2 snmp group scalars; the leaf is value->var.subs[sub-1]. GETNEXT aborts the process (abort()). GET stores the value of the requested leaf (the counters in snmpd_stats, TRUTH_MK(snmpd.auth_traps) for snmpEnableAuthenTraps, silentDrops, proxyDrops) in value->v and returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR, and returns SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME for any other leaf. SET of snmpEnableAuthenTraps returns SNMP_ERR_WRONG_VALUE without side effects if value->v.integer is not a valid truth value, otherwise saves value->v.integer in ctx->scratch->int1, sets snmpd.auth_traps from TRUTH_GET(value->v.integer) and returns NOERROR. ROLLBACK of that leaf assigns ctx->scratch->int1 (the saved integer as stored, not converted with TRUTH_GET) back to snmpd.auth_traps and returns NOERROR; COMMIT of that leaf returns NOERROR. A SET, ROLLBACK or COMMIT for any other leaf, and any other op value, reaches abort().
note: Round-15 reviewer right: GET with an unsupported leaf returns SNMP_ERR_NOSUCHNAME (action.c default case), it does not abort as the old precondition claimed.

name: TestSpecParser::visitChar
prose: Precondition: none beyond the parser object being in a valid state. Postcondition: if c is a backslash and m_mode is not EscapedName it calls escape() (saves the current mode in lastMode, sets m_mode = EscapedName and pushes m_realPatternPos onto m_escapeChars), then addCharToPattern(c), which unconditionally appends c to m_substring and m_patternName and increments m_realPatternPos, and returns true. Otherwise, if c is ',' and m_mode is not EscapedName, it returns separate(): for QuotedName or Tag mode that sets m_mode = None, m_pos = m_arg.size(), clears m_substring and m_patternName and returns false; for any other mode it calls endMode(), addFilter() (which pushes the current filter if it has patterns) and returns true. Otherwise it dispatches on m_mode: None calls processNoneChar (a space returns true so the character is dropped; '~' sets m_exclusion; '[' starts Tag; '"' starts QuotedName; any other character starts Name; the last four continue below); Name calls processNameChar ('[' sets m_exclusion if m_substring is "exclude:" or else calls endMode(), then starts Tag); EscapedName calls endMode() (reverts to lastMode), addCharToPattern(c) and returns true; Tag, QuotedName and any other mode call processOtherChar, which returns false for a non-control character and, for a control character of the mode, appends c to m_substring, calls endMode() and returns true. If it did not return earlier it appends c to m_substring, appends c to m_patternName and increments m_realPatternPos only when c is not a control character of the (possibly new) mode, and returns true. So the only false result comes from separate().
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: addCharToPattern (catch.hpp:5184) unconditionally updates m_substring, m_patternName and m_realPatternPos; it does not skip control characters (that check is in the final lines of visitChar, not in the backslash branch). Prose kept, with the false-return condition made explicit.

name: operator << (ostream&, XmlEncode const&)
prose: Precondition: none. Postcondition: calls xmlEncode.encodeTo(os) and returns os. encodeTo walks m_str byte by byte and writes: '<' as < and '&' as &; '>' as > only when it has at least three characters before it and the two preceding characters are ']' (otherwise '>' unchanged); '"' as " only when the encoder was built ForAttributes (otherwise unchanged); bytes below 0x09, 0x0E to 0x1F and 0x7F as \xHH (uppercase, two hex digits, via hexEscapeChar, which saves and restores the stream's format flags but leaves the fill character '0'); other bytes below 0x7F unchanged (so tab, LF, VT, FF and CR pass through); for a byte of 0x80 or above it hex-escapes just that byte when it is below 0xC0 or at least 0xF8, when the multi-byte sequence would run past the end of the string, when a continuation byte does not match 10xxxxxx, when the decoded value is below 0x80, when it is in [0x80,0x800) but encoded in more than 2 bytes, when it is above 0x800 and below 0x10000 but encoded in 4 bytes, or when it is at least 0x110000; otherwise it copies the whole sequence unchanged. Because only the lead byte of a rejected sequence is escaped, the following bytes are examined on their own (continuation bytes then get escaped individually). The overlong test uses a strict '0x800 < value', so a 4-byte encoding of exactly U+0800 is not rejected, and surrogate values are not rejected.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the overlong check is (0x800 < value && value < 0x10000 && encBytes > 3), which misses value == 0x800 (catch.hpp:15245). The slice's operator<< itself only forwards to encodeTo.

name: value<T>
prose: Function template value<T>(T&& value) in Catch::Generators. Precondition: the argument is convertible to T, which is deduced as a forwarding reference; it is meant for rvalue arguments (T then a non-reference type). Postcondition: returns a GeneratorWrapper<T> owning (through a unique_ptr made by pf::make_unique) a newly allocated SingleValueGenerator<T> constructed from std::forward<T>(value); its get() returns the stored value and its next() always returns false, so exactly one value is produced. For an lvalue argument T would be an lvalue-reference type and the generator would hold a reference member (SingleValueGenerator stores T m_value), so the referent would have to outlive the wrapper; this function does not handle that case specially. Allocation or the copy/move of the argument may throw.
note: Unreviewed earlier; I qualified the lvalue case (the old prose said the stored reference is simply valid while the argument lives).

name: values<T>
prose: Function template values<T>(std::initializer_list<T> values) in Catch::Generators. Precondition: T is not bool (FixedValuesGenerator static_asserts this at compile time). Postcondition: returns a GeneratorWrapper<T> owning a newly allocated FixedValuesGenerator<T> that holds copies of the listed elements in a std::vector; get() returns m_values[m_idx] and next() increments m_idx and returns true while m_idx is still less than the number of elements. The initial get() on an empty list would index an empty vector. Allocation or element copies may throw.
note: Unreviewed earlier; prose confirmed against catch.hpp:3896-3912 with the empty-list remark added.

name: table<Ts...>
prose: Function template table<Ts...>(std::initializer_list<std::tuple<typename std::decay<Ts>::type...>> tuples). Postcondition: returns values<std::tuple<Ts...>>(tuples), i.e. a GeneratorWrapper<std::tuple<Ts...>> owning a FixedValuesGenerator of copies of the tuples (get() returns the current tuple, next() advances the index and returns true while elements remain). The argument type is std::initializer_list<std::tuple<decay<Ts>...>>, which can be passed on only if it is the same type as std::initializer_list<std::tuple<Ts...>>, i.e. when every Ts equals its decayed type; otherwise the call does not compile. std::tuple<Ts...> must not be bool-like for FixedValuesGenerator's static_assert (it never is a bool).
note: Unreviewed earlier; the old prose said the elements 'convert' to std::tuple<Ts...>, but an initializer_list<X> does not convert to initializer_list<Y>, so I replaced it with the same-type condition.

name: generate<L>
prose: Function template generate<L>(SourceLineInfo const& lineInfo, L const& generatorExpression). Precondition: generatorExpression() can be called with no arguments and returns a Generators-style object with a nested type UnderlyingType and a get() member. Postcondition: it calls acquireGeneratorTracker(lineInfo); only if that tracker has no generator yet does it call generatorExpression() once and install a newly allocated Generators<UnderlyingType> built from the result in the tracker (the tracker owns it); it then returns the result of get() (a const reference to the current element) of the tracker's generator cast to IGenerator<UnderlyingType>. The reference is valid only as long as the generator stays installed in the tracker.
note: Unreviewed earlier; confirmed against catch.hpp:4040-4052 (generatorExpression is invoked only when no generator exists).

name: CumulativeReporterBase::assertionEnded
prose: Member of CumulativeReporterBase (the definition at catch.hpp:5837, the only assertionEnded definition inside this slice). Precondition: m_sectionStack is not empty (checked only by assert, so not in NDEBUG builds). Postcondition: it calls prepareExpandedExpression on the AssertionResult inside assertionStats (through const_cast; this calls result.getExpandedExpression() so the expression string is built while the temporary expression object still exists, which mutates the caller's AssertionStats), appends a copy of assertionStats to the assertions of the section node at the back of m_sectionStack, and always returns true.
note: The old prose described ConsoleReporter::assertionEnded (catch.hpp:16145, outside the slice). The original rejection (omits the prepareExpandedExpression mutation) is right for the function actually in the slice; the round-15 claim ('returns false when the result is ok') belongs to the console reporter and was judged against the wrong function.

name: repeater::operator()
prose: Precondition: none; k may be any int. Postcondition: operator()(int k) const calls fun() k times when k > 0 and zero times when k <= 0, then returns. The repeater object itself is not modified by this operator (it is const), but fun is invoked as a const member and may have side effects of its own (mutable members, captured references or pointers); an exception thrown by fun propagates and stops the loop.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the old claim that the functor is 'unchanged' was too strong (a const call can still mutate mutable state or things it points to).

name: BenchmarkFunction::BenchmarkFunction(BenchmarkFunction const& that)
prose: Copy constructor of Catch::Benchmark::Detail::BenchmarkFunction (the item 'clone-based copy'; the copy assignment operator does the same with f.reset(that.f->clone())). Precondition: that.f is non-null (a moved-from BenchmarkFunction has a null f, and dereferencing it here would be undefined). Postcondition: f is initialised with that.f->clone(), a virtual call that heap-allocates a new model<Fun> copy-constructed from the stored callable, so the new object owns an independent copy through its unique_ptr; that is unchanged. Allocation or the callable's copy constructor may throw.
note: Dropped earlier because the item name did not match a function; the constructor BenchmarkFunction(BenchmarkFunction const&) exists at catch.hpp:6687.

name: count_bits
prose: Function template test::detail::count_bits<A, a...>() (constexpr); it needs at least one character in the pack (an empty braced list cannot be deduced in the range-for). It scans the characters with a small mode machine starting in BIN mode, counting bits: in BIN mode spaces, tabs and newlines are ignored, ';' enters COMMENT mode, 'x' or 'X' enters HEX mode, '!' enters CHECK mode, '@' enters GOTO mode with addr = 0, '0', '1' and '.' each add one bit, and any other character throws the string "bad character"; COMMENT mode ends at a newline; HEX mode adds 4 bits per hex digit (throws "unaligned hex digit" if the bit count is not a multiple of 4), ignores ':' and returns to BIN on any other character; CHECK mode ignores digits and returns to BIN on any other character (the address is not checked here, so "address check failed" is never thrown by count_bits); GOTO mode accumulates decimal digits into addr and, on the first non-digit, throws "cannot go backwards" if 8*addr < bits, otherwise sets bits = 8*addr and returns to BIN. The inner 'again' loop is `for (bool again = true; again; again = false)`, so the again flag set by the helpers has no effect: the character that ends a HEX, CHECK or GOTO run is consumed by that step and is not reprocessed in BIN mode. A GOTO or CHECK still open at the end of the input has no effect. It returns the final bits count; the thrown string literals are the only error reporting (in a constant expression they make the program ill-formed).
note: Reviewer round 15 right: count_bits never calls handle_check, so it cannot throw "address check failed" (that is thrown by handle_check, used by constbuf()). Also noted from the code: the terminating character of hex/check/goto runs is consumed because 'again' is reset by the for-increment.

name: matching_vector
prose: Precondition: vector is a valid index into the static array order (0 <= vector < nentries); i = order[vector] is read first, and if i >= 2*nstates the function returns -1 before reading tally[i] or width[i]; otherwise tally[i], width[i], froms[i] and tos[i] must be valid, and for every earlier entry j = order[prev] that gets examined, tally[j], width[j], froms[j] and tos[j] must be valid and froms[j], tos[j] must hold at least tally[i] entries when width[j] and tally[j] equal width[i] and tally[i]. Postcondition: returns -1 if order[vector] >= 2*nstates; otherwise it scans prev = vector-1 down to 0 and returns -1 immediately at the first prev whose j = order[prev] has a different width or a different tally than i (it does not look at smaller prev); for a j with equal width and tally it compares tos[j][k] and froms[j][k] with tos[i][k] and froms[i][k] for k in [0, tally[i]) and returns j (the vector number order[prev], not prev) at the first full match, scanning from the nearest earlier entry; it returns -1 if the scan ends without a match. It only reads the static arrays order, tally, width, froms, tos and the global nstates; it allocates and frees nothing and modifies nothing.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: output.c:797-800 does 'i = order[vector]; if (i >= 2 * nstates) return (-1);' and then indexes tally[i]/width[i]; the older round-2 claim that a tally mismatch does not stop the scan is also wrong (output.c:812-815 returns -1 at the first differing width or tally). Prose kept, with the read-only note added.

name: copy_union
prose: Precondition: cptr points just after the %union token in the current input line (begin_ainfo records cptr-6 for diagnostics). If unionized is already set it calls over_unionized(), which prints an error and ends the program through done(1); otherwise it sets unionized = 1. Postcondition: through puts_both/putc_both it writes the guard lines '#ifdef YYSTYPE', '#undef  YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED', '#define YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED 1', '#endif', '#ifndef YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED', '#define YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED 1' to text_file (and also to union_file only when dflag is set), then a line-number directive to text_file only, then the union text. Identifier characters between %union and the first '{' are collected as a tag (at most NAME_LEN characters kept) and whitespace is buffered. At the opening brace, if a tag was found it writes 'union <tag>' plus the buffered whitespace, otherwise 'typedef union YYSTYPE' plus the whitespace; the union body is copied up to the brace that brings the depth back to 0, copying string and character literals and comments through copy_string and copy_comment and reading further lines with get_line. At the closing brace it writes '; ' and then 'typedef union <tag> YYSTYPE;' for the tagged case, or ' YYSTYPE;' (completing 'typedef union YYSTYPE {...} YYSTYPE;') for the untagged case, then '#endif /* !YYSTYPE_IS_DECLARED */'. It leaves cptr just past the closing brace and returns nothing. If the input ends before the matching brace, unterminated_union() prints an error and ends the program through done(1).

name: yyySolveAndSignal
prose: Precondition: yyyRSTop points at a valid entry of the ready-set array (yyyRS) whose node is valid; the entry's node->parent is read, and parent.noderef is dereferenced (for prodNum) when the entry is inherited (whichSym nonzero, through yyyRefN) and when it is synthesized with parentIsStack == 0, so it must be valid in those cases; the tables yyyIIIEL, yyyIIEL and yyyIEL must be consistent with the node's prodNum and the attribute number. Postcondition: it pops the top ready-set entry (yyyRSTop is decremented; there is no check against the array base). The per-rule switches on yyyRefN->prodNum (cases 1 to 8) and on the symbol and attribute numbers contain no statements in this file, so no semantic action runs. Then: if the solved instance was inherited (whichSym nonzero) and yyyRSTopN->prodNum is nonzero it calls yyySignalEnts on that node with the entry range taken from yyyIEL; if it was synthesized and the node's parentIsStack is false it calls yyySignalEnts on the parent noderef with the range from yyyIEL; if it was synthesized and parentIsStack is true it does not signal anyone but takes a cell from the solved-SA free list (or the next unused cell of yyySSALspace, calling yyyHandleOverflow(yyySSALof) when the space is exhausted; that handler prints a message and exits the process), links it in front of the stack item's solvedSAlist and stores the attribute number in the cell. yyySignalEnts itself decrements reference counts and pushes newly ready entries onto the ready set, and may call yyyHandleOverflow(yyyRSof) which also exits. It returns nothing.

name: yygrowstack
prose: Precondition: data points to a valid YYSTACKDATA. For a fresh stack data->stacksize is 0 and the base pointers are NULL (the structure is zeroed by the caller); otherwise stacksize is positive, s_base and l_base point to arrays of at least stacksize elements and s_mark lies within the state array. Postcondition: returns 0 or YYENOMEM (-2). newsize is YYINITSTACKSIZE if stacksize was 0; if stacksize is already at least YYMAXDEPTH it returns YYENOMEM with data unchanged; otherwise newsize is stacksize doubled and capped at YYMAXDEPTH. i is computed as s_mark - s_base. It reallocs the state array: if that fails it returns YYENOMEM with data unchanged. Otherwise s_base and s_mark (= new base + i) are updated and the value array is reallocated; if that fails it returns YYENOMEM, and then s_base and s_mark have already been moved to the new state array while l_base, l_mark, stacksize and s_last keep their old values (s_last may therefore still point into the old state array, which is freed if realloc moved it, or be NULL for a fresh stack). On success l_base is the new value array, l_mark = l_base + i (the same index i is used for both marks), stacksize = newsize, s_last = s_base + newsize - 1, and it returns 0. The arrays stay owned through data; nothing is freed on any path.
note: Reviewer round 1 right (l_base is not leaked: realloc failure leaves the old value array in l_base); round 15 right (s_last may point into the old array, the same array, or be NULL, not necessarily a freed array); round 2 (precondition impossible for a fresh stack) is a misreading because the precondition is split by stacksize == 0 in the prose. Old prose said both marks are kept 'at the same element offsets as before'; code uses the offset of s_mark for both.

Syntax errors: a syntax error found while the error flag is 0 calls yyerror("syntax error") and increments the error count; an explicit YYERROR from an action (where the grammar uses it) jumps to yyerrlab, which increments the error count but does not call the error function. In recovery (error flag 3) states are popped until one shifts the error token, and lookahead tokens are discarded without further error reports. Return value: it returns 0 through yyaccept when, after reducing the start symbol, the lookahead is end of input; it returns 1 through yyabort when recovery has popped the state stack to its base without finding a state that shifts the error token, or when the lookahead is end of input while the error flag is 3; it also returns 1 (after calling yyerror("yacc stack overflow")) when yygrowstack returns YYENOMEM, because in this skeleton yyoverflow falls through into yyabort. No other value is returned. Cleanup: nothing is freed on return, because yyfreestack expands to nothing in this non-pure file; the stack stays allocated in the file-scope stack structure for the next call.

No other value is returned. name: mainSort
prose: Static function mainSort(ptr, block, quadrant, ftab, nblock, verb, budget) of bzip2's block sorter. Precondition: nblock > 0; block and quadrant are valid for indices 0 to nblock-1+BZ_N_OVERSHOOT with block[0..nblock-1] holding the input; ptr is valid for 0..nblock-1; ftab is valid for 0..65536; budget points to a writable Int32; and the data is such that the AssertH checks with codes 1006, 1007 and 1002 hold (a failed AssertH calls the library's internal-error handler, BZ2_bz__AssertH__fail or bz_internal_error depending on the build). With verb >= 4 it prints progress text through VPrintf. Postcondition, normal return: ftab is zeroed and filled with the 2-byte frequency counts (then cumulative bucket starts) and ends with SETMASK completion bits set for the processed buckets; block[0..BZ_N_OVERSHOOT-1] is copied to block[nblock..], quadrant[0..nblock-1] is zeroed and quadrant[nblock..nblock+BZ_N_OVERSHOOT-1] is initially zeroed; ptr[0..nblock-1] is filled by the bucket distribution, by mainQSort3 on unsorted small buckets (step 1) and by the pointer scans of step 2 so that it gives the sorted order of the cyclic rotations of block (the algorithm's goal); for every big bucket except the last one processed, step 3 stores cached ordering values into quadrant (including quadrant[a2update + nblock] when a2update < BZ_N_OVERSHOOT), so the overshoot quadrant entries are not necessarily zero at the end; *budget is reduced by the work done in mainQSort3. Early return: the function returns (with no value) from step 1 immediately after a mainQSort3 call when *budget < 0, leaving ptr, ftab and quadrant partially processed; this is the only early return. It allocates and frees no memory.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: step 3 overwrites the overshoot quadrant entries (blocksort.c:995-1000: quadrant[a2update + nblock] = qVal), so the old statement that the overshoot area is left zeroed was wrong/contradictory.

name: dialog_calendar
prose: Slice cut the head: this is dialog_calendar(title, subtitle, height, width, day, month, year) (calendar.c:672). It saves the dialog variables (dlg_save_vars) and sets dialog_vars.separate_output = TRUE, takes the current local time, overrides year (>= 1900), month (>= 1) and day (valid for that month) from the arguments when given and normalises with mktime (HAVE_MKTIME build), sizes and draws the dialog window, then draws the day, month and year boxes. Return paths: if WeekStart() < 0 or init_object/DrawObject fails for any of the three boxes, it returns CleanupResult(DLG_EXIT_ERROR, ...) at once, without adding a date to the result. Otherwise it runs the key loop until result != DLG_EXIT_UNKNOWN (or until dlg_result_key reports a result key and dlg_button_key returns false): keys are mapped to button choices, field changes, date steps (day, month or year by whole-day steps through mktime/localtime), mouse selections, or a KEY_RESIZE which rebuilds the window (goto retry); the result is set from dlg_result_key, dlg_char_to_button, dlg_enter_buttoncode or dlg_ok_buttoncode. After the loop it formats the selected date with strftime and dialog_vars.date_format when that is set and produces a non-empty string, otherwise as day/month/year with the default format "%02d/%02d/%0d" (day, month, year), adds it with dlg_add_result, calls AddLastKey() and returns CleanupResult(result, ...). CleanupResult deletes the dialog window, frees the mouse regions and the prompt, restores the saved dialog variables, frees the cached day and month name strings and returns its first argument. So the date is added to the result only on the non-error path.
note: Dropped earlier only because the name was not in the slice. Two statements of the old prose were wrong: the DLG_EXIT_ERROR returns do not format/add the date ('in every case' was false), and the default date format is dd/mm/yyyy (tm_mday, tm_mon + 1, year), not mm/dd/yyyy.

name: dlg_result_key
prose: Precondition: resultp points to a writable int; dialog_key is a curses or dialog key code and fkey tells whether it came from a function-key binding. If KEY_RESIZE is defined it first updates dialog_state.had_resize: while had_resize is set, an ERR dialog_key is replaced by 0 (the local copy) and any other key clears had_resize; otherwise, if fkey is nonzero and dialog_key == KEY_RESIZE, had_resize is set. Postcondition, when the build defines HAVE_RC_FILE: for a nonzero fkey it returns TRUE and stores DLG_EXIT_OK for DLGK_OK (unless dialog_vars.nook), DLG_EXIT_CANCEL for DLGK_CANCEL (unless nocancel), DLG_EXIT_EXTRA for DLGK_EXTRA (only if extra_button is set), DLG_EXIT_HELP for DLGK_HELP (only if help_button is set) and DLG_EXIT_ESC for DLGK_ESC, and returns FALSE for every other value; for a zero fkey it returns TRUE with DLG_EXIT_ESC if dialog_key == ESC, TRUE with DLG_EXIT_ERROR if dialog_key == ERR (after the ERR-to-0 replacement above), else FALSE. When HAVE_RC_FILE is not defined the ESC and ERR tests apply for any fkey value and the function-key switch does not exist. *resultp is written only when TRUE is returned.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: without HAVE_RC_FILE the ESC/ERR checks are not guarded by fkey (dlg_keys.c:331-339), so the old unconditional statement was wrong; the original rejection (ERR not always handled because of fkey or had_resize) is also right. The prose now covers both builds.

name: dlg_form
prose: The slice is the middle of dlg_form(title, cprompt, height, width, form_height, item_no, items, current_item), the form implementation (formbox.c:463), not of the wrapper dialog_form. Precondition: items has item_no valid DIALOG_FORMITEM entries, current_item is writable, the dialog variables are initialised. It lays out the form with make_FORM_ELTs and dlg_auto_size (height or width 0 means auto size; form_height 0 means the computed height), creates the dialog window and a form sub-window, draws the box, title, prompt and field texts, picks the initial field with set_choice, and loops reading keys until result != DLG_EXIT_UNKNOWN or dlg_result_key reports a result key. In the loop: button hotkeys (when not editing text) and DLGK_ENTER/DLGK_TOGGLE set the result from dlg_ok_buttoncode/dlg_enter_buttoncode (or DLG_EXIT_OK when the state is the text field) after dlg_del_window(dialog); DLGK_LEAVE sets the result from the current button; navigation keys move between fields, buttons, pages (scrolling) or tab through items; mouse clicks select a field or set a button result; KEY_RESIZE frees the prompt, resets the size, unregisters the form window and jumps back to retry; other keys while a text field is active are passed to dlg_edit_string, which edits current->text in place unless the item is read-only. After the loop it frees the mouse regions, unregisters the form window, deletes the dialog window (dlg_del_window(dialog) is also called inside the loop in the Enter/Toggle branches before the loop ends), frees the prompt, stores the final choice in *current_item and returns result (a DLG_EXIT_* value such as DLG_EXIT_OK, DLG_EXIT_CANCEL, DLG_EXIT_ESC, DLG_EXIT_HELP, DLG_EXIT_EXTRA, DLG_EXIT_ERROR from dlg_result_key, or a button code); that return statement is the only one in the function. It does not allocate or free the items array or write the field values to the dialog output; that is done by the callers such as dialog_form.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the old prose described the dialog_form wrapper (temporary item list, dlg_form call, output of the field texts) but the slice is dlg_form, which does none of that. The name in the packet (dialog_form) was therefore the wrong function.

name: fill_lists
prose: Precondition: current is a writable buffer of at least MAX_LEN+1 bytes holding a NUL-terminated string, input is a NUL-terminated string, d_list and f_list are initialised LISTs and keep is a bool. It finds the first position n where current and input differ. If the strings are identical it sets the result FALSE and requests a rescan only when n == 0 and d_list->length == 0 (both strings empty and the directory list empty). If they differ and neither remainder (current + n, input + n) contains '/', it does not rescan: the result is show_both_lists(input, d_list, f_list, keep), which uses the caller's keep and returns TRUE if either list's highlighted choice changed (the file list is only updated when the directory list reports no change, because of the || short-circuit). Otherwise (a '/' in either remainder) it rescans. A rescan copies input into current truncated to MAX_LEN, frees and reinitialises both lists (free_list with reinit), takes the directory part of current (or "./"), opendirs it and, when that succeeds, adds each entry of acceptable length found by stat() to d_list (directories) or, only if f_list->win is set, to f_list (other files), closes the directory and sorts non-trivial lists with qsort; if opendir fails the lists simply stay empty. It then calls show_both_lists(input, d_list, f_list, FALSE) (result ignored), sets both list offsets to their choices and the result to TRUE. Returns that result (TRUE after a rescan even if opendir failed).
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong on both points: for two empty strings with an empty directory list the code does rescan and returns TRUE (fselect.c:458-460: rescan = (n == 0 && d_list->length == 0)); FALSE is returned only for identical strings otherwise. show_both_lists is called with keep FALSE in the rescan branch and with the caller's keep in the no-slash branch, which is what the prose said. I made the keep and short-circuit details explicit.

name: digits_of
prose: Precondition: none for value (any int); the local 80-byte buffer is large enough for any int. Postcondition: returns strlen of sprintf(temp, "%d", value), the number of characters in the decimal text of value, which is the number of digits of |value| plus one when value is negative. It only uses a local buffer and has no other effects.
note: Contract assumes a 32-bit int (10 digits for INT_MAX); the earlier contract was an overlong nested conditional that did not parse. Round-1 reviewer claim (minus sign omitted) was right; later rounds were mechanical syntax rejections.

name: handle_my_getc
prose: Precondition: cb is a DIALOG_CALLBACK pointer (a MY_OBJ when it is registered), result points to a writable int. If cb is not found in dialog_state.getc_callbacks it returns FALSE and leaves *result unchanged. Otherwise, for a non-function key that dlg_char_to_button maps to button index 0 it treats the key as DLGK_ENTER. For a function key: DLGK_ENTER sets *result = DLG_EXIT_OK and done; DLGK_BEGIN sets hscroll to 0; DLGK_GRID_LEFT decrements hscroll if it is positive; DLGK_GRID_RIGHT increments it while it is below MAX_LEN; for a mouse key it sets *result = dlg_ok_buttoncode(ch - M_EVENT) (assigned even when that is DLG_EXIT_ERROR) and finishes only if the value is not DLG_EXIT_ERROR, otherwise it calls beep(); any other function key beeps. After a function key, if hscroll differs from old_hscroll it calls repaint_text. For a non-function key: ERR does clearerr(input), reads one character with getc and pushes it back with ungetc, and calls handle_input (which repaints when the file size differs from last_pos) if the character was not EOF; ESC sets *result = DLG_EXIT_ESC and finishes; any other key beeps. It returns FALSE when the dialog is finished (or the callback is not valid) and TRUE otherwise.
note: Reviewer round 15 right on both points: the invalid-callback path also returns FALSE, and the mouse path assigns *result = DLG_EXIT_ERROR before testing it (tailbox.c:264-270). The old prose also said the ERR character was consumed, but it is pushed back with ungetc, and said 'a button' matches whereas only button index 0 does.

name: find_and_hash_each_line
prose: Slice cut the head: static function find_and_hash_each_line(current) (io.c:217). Precondition: current's buffer, prefix_end, suffix_begin, buffered, linbuf, alloc_lines and linbuf_base are set up, the globals equivs, equivs_index, equivs_alloc, buckets and nbuckets are initialised (buckets[-1] must also be valid), and the options ignore_white_space, ignore_case, tabsize, output_style, context and no_diff_means_no_output are set. Behaviour: it mallocs a cureqs array of alloc_lines entries. For every line starting at prefix_end and before suffix_begin it hashes the line text (honouring ignore_case and ignore_white_space: IGNORE_ALL_SPACE, IGNORE_SPACE_CHANGE, IGNORE_TAB_EXPANSION), looks for an equal line in the hash bucket (same hash, then memcmp or lines_differ) and otherwise adds a new equivalence class to eqs (growing it by doubling with xrealloc; xalloc_die if the size would exceed PTRDIFF_MAX), stores the line start in linbuf[line] and the class index in cureqs[line] (growing linbuf and cureqs by doubling when full), and counts lines; an incomplete last line is put in buckets[-1] when whitespace is significant and the buffer end is moved back over the inserted newline. It then sets current->buffered_lines to that count. A second loop records line starts for the lines of the suffix, one start per line plus one extra entry for the end (bufend, or the start of the line at which it stops once context lines have been recorded when no_diff_means_no_output is set), growing linbuf as needed. Finally it stores linbuf, valid_lines (the index of that last entry), alloc_lines and cureqs (as current->equivs) in current and the local equivalence table, size and index back into the globals equivs, equivs_alloc and equivs_index. It returns nothing; allocation failure or size overflow ends the process through xalloc_die.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: linbuf gets one extra start entry (the end sentinel) beyond the lines (io.c:468-496), which the old prose omitted. Dropped-name issue: the packet name matches the real function; the slice just starts after its head.

name: main
prose: Entry point of sdiff. Precondition: argv is the command line. It sets exit_failure = EXIT_TROUBLE (2), initialises locale, text domain and c_stack_action(cleanup), reads the EDITOR environment variable into editor_program, and makes the first diff argument DEFAULT_DIFF_PROGRAM. Options are parsed with getopt_long and mostly forwarded to the diff child by diffarg (-a, -b, -B, -d, -E, -H, -i, -I pattern, -l, -t, -w -> -W, -W -> -w, --strip-trailing-cr, --tabsize); -o records the output file, -s sets suppress_common_lines, --diff-program replaces argument 0; -v prints version information and --help prints usage, each followed by check_stdout() (which fails fatally on a write error or on fclose failure) and returns EXIT_SUCCESS; an unknown option calls try_help (which terminates with status EXIT_TROUBLE). If the number of operands is not exactly two, try_help prints a diagnostic and terminates with EXIT_TROUBLE. Without -o it appends --suppress-common-lines (if requested), -y, -- and the two file names and calls execvp on the diff program; if execvp returns, perror_fatal ends the process (exiterr, status 2). With -o: both operands being directories is fatal; it expands the names, opens the left and right files and the output with ck_fopen (fatal on failure), starts diff --sdiff-merge-assist as a child connected by a pipe (or popen when fork/vfork is unavailable; pipe, fork, fdopen and popen failures are fatal), runs interact() on the three streams, closes left, right and out, waits for the child (waitpid retried on EINTR, other errors fatal; pclose in the popen build), removes the temporary file tmpname if any, and then: if interact() returned false it calls exiterr(), which exits with EXIT_TROUBLE; otherwise check_child_status requires a normal exit status of at most EXIT_FAILURE (anything else is reported and ends with exiterr), and the process exits with the child's exit status via exit(WEXITSTATUS(wstatus)). The trailing 'return EXIT_SUCCESS' is not reached.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: the interact_ok == false path exits through exiterr() with status 2 instead of the child's status (sdiff.c:739-740). Slice cut the head only; function name matches.

name: print_sdiff_hunk
prose: Slice cut the head: this is the tail of print_sdiff_hunk(hunk) (side.c:235); there is no function called print_1sdiff_hunk. Precondition: hunk is a change-script node chain and the global line buffers, next0/next1, outfile and the sdiff options are set. It calls analyze_hunk to get the changes kind and the line ranges first0..last0 and first1..last1; if the kind is 0 (UNCHANGED) it returns without printing. Otherwise it first calls print_sdiff_common_lines(first0, first1), which prints the common lines before the hunk (unless suppress_common_lines) and advances next0 and next1; with sdiff_merge_assist it prints a 'c<len0>,<len1>' line; for a CHANGED hunk it prints paired lines with '|' while both ranges have lines, then continues with the remaining kind (OLD or NEW) and sets next0 and next1 to the lines consumed so far; for lines only in the second file it prints them with '>' and sets next1 past them; for lines only in the first file it prints them with '<' and sets next0 past them. It returns nothing.
note: Dropped earlier only because the packet name did not match a function; the slice is the end of print_sdiff_hunk.

name: Info_Out
prose: Interprets a terminfo-style output string (the non-termcap branch of new_curse.c) and writes the result to stdout. Precondition: string is NULL or a NUL-terminated capability string; p_list is NULL or has at least place readable ints; place is at most 9 (p[] has 10 entries). If string is NULL it returns at once without touching p[], Otemp or stdout. Otherwise it clears p[0..9], and, only if p_list is not NULL, fills p[1], p[2], ... from p_list in reverse order (p[1] = p_list[place-1], p[2] = p_list[place-2], and so on, consuming place entries). It then sets the global Otemp to string and walks it: literal characters are written with putchar; '%' sequences are handed to Operation() (printing %d-style numbers, arithmetic and comparison operators on a stack, %c, %i, %p<n>, %P<v>, %g<v>, %'c', %{n} and %%); the conditional forms %? ... %t ... %e ... %; are evaluated by the code in Info_Out itself, skipping the branch that is not selected; '$<n>' computes a padding count from n milliseconds (using chars_per_millisecond) and writes that many copies of the pad character from String_table[pc__] (or 0 when there is none). At the end it calls fflush(stdout). The globals p[], variable[], Otemp, chars and the file-scope stacks are modified. For a well-formed string Otemp ends pointing at the terminating NUL; for malformed strings (an unterminated '$<', '%{' or %' sequence or an unterminated conditional) the scanning loops can read past the end of the string, and the stacks (128 entries) are not bounds-checked.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: p[] is filled from p_list only when p_list is not NULL (new_curse.c:1936-1941); the old prose also had the fill order reversed. Prose qualified for malformed strings.

name: Get_key
prose: Decodes a terminal key sequence that started with first_char (ESC or Ctrl-_), called from wgetch. Precondition: KEY_TOS is NULL or a valid KEY_STACK list of entries with NUL-terminated element->string, Max_Key_len <= 127 (the local buffer string[128]), and standard input is readable through wgetch(stdscr). It puts first_char in string[0], sets Time_Out = FALSE and Noblock = TRUE; in builds without BSD_SELECT it installs Clear as the SIGALRM handler (the old handler is not restored) and starts a one-second alarm. It then reads characters with wgetch(stdscr) (which can itself call Get_key again for another ESC) while fewer than Max_Key_len characters are collected, Time_Out is not set and no match was found; each character other than -1 is appended and the whole accumulated string is compared with every KEY_STACK entry's string with strcmp, taking the first match; the string consisting of first_char alone is never compared, so an entry equal to first_char alone is never returned. After the loop (no BSD_SELECT) it calls alarm(0) if no time-out occurred; in non-SYS5 builds it calls ioctl(0, TIOCSETP, &Terminal) on every return; in SYS5 builds the corresponding ioctl is commented out and the local Gterminal changes are never applied. It sets Noblock = FALSE. If a match was found it returns that entry's element->value; otherwise it pushes back with ungetch, from the last read back to index 1, every collected character except those equal to -1 or 255, and returns first_char.
note: Reviewer round 15 right: no comparison is made before at least one more character has been read (new_curse.c:2386-2399), so a one-character entry equal to first_char cannot match; the old prose did not say so. Old round-2 claim about SYS5 termio changes was already handled (Gterminal is a local that is never applied).

name: Delete_line
prose: Slice cut the head: the function is Delete_line(row, end_row, window) (new_curse.c:3033). Precondition: window is a valid WINDOW and the doubly linked screen-line list starting at curscr->first_line is long enough that the unchecked walks (window->SR links from the head, then row more links) never reach a NULL next_screen. Behaviour: it finds the line at index SR + row (setting the global top_of_win to the window's first line on the way; if row + SR == 0 it first sets curscr->first_line to the next line), unlinks it from the list, clears it with clear_line(tmp1, 0, window->Num_cols), sets its number to -1, and re-inserts it before the line reached by walking up to SR links from curscr->first_line (stopping early at the last line) and then up to end_row further links (again stopping early at the last line), changing only the prev_screen/next_screen fields of the line and its new neighbours (no nodes are allocated or freed). It then positions the terminal at (SR + row, 0) and calls String_Out with the dl__ string; afterwards, if the cs__ string is NULL and end_row < window->Num_lines, it positions at (SR + end_row, 0) and calls String_Out with al__, else if cs__ is non-NULL and dl__ is NULL it positions at (SR + end_row, 0) and outputs a newline. Return value: the line that followed the deleted line before re-insertion (NULL if the deleted line was the last node), except that if row == window->Num_lines - 1 the re-inserted cleared line itself is returned; when row + SR == 0 it also sets curscr->first_line and the global top_of_win to the returned pointer.
note: Dropped earlier for name reasons. Old prose errors: top_of_win is a global, not a local; 'always returns a struct _line pointer' contradicted its own NULL return.

name: HASH_JEN_MIX
prose: Function-like macro HASH_JEN_MIX(a,b,c) (not a C function): it expands to do { ... } while (0) and applies Bob Jenkins' nine-step mixing sequence in place, each step of the form x -= y; x -= z; x ^= (z >> n) or (y << n) with the shift amounts 13, 8, 13, 12, 16, 5, 3, 10, 15 on the three operands. Precondition: a, b and c are distinct modifiable lvalues of an unsigned integer type (HASH_JEN passes unsigned variables and hashv); each is evaluated several times. Postcondition: a, b and c are overwritten with mixed values that depend only on their previous values; with unsigned operands the arithmetic wraps. It returns nothing.
note: Dropped earlier (ensures \true contract). Kept as a fix because the macro performs real computation; it is not a function, so no contract is given.

name: MUR_FMIX
prose: Function-like macro MUR_FMIX(_h) (not a C function): it expands to do { ... } while(0) and applies the MurmurHash3 finalisation mix to _h in place: _h ^= _h >> 16; _h *= 0x85ebca6b; _h ^= _h >> 13; _h *= 0xc2b2ae35l; _h ^= _h >> 16. Precondition: _h is a modifiable lvalue of an unsigned 32-bit type (the shifts assume 32 bits; _h is evaluated several times). Postcondition: _h holds the mixed value, which depends only on its previous value; unsigned multiplication wraps. It returns nothing.
note: Dropped earlier (ensures \true contract). Kept as a fix because the macro performs real computation; it is not a function, so no contract is given.

name: _dwarf_arange_pro_cleanup
prose: Slice cut the head: this is _dwarf_arange_pro_cleanup(dbg) (libdwarf_arange.c:243). Precondition: dbg is non-NULL and dbg->dbg_mode == DW_DLC_WRITE (checked only by assert). If dbg->dbgp_as is NULL it returns without changing anything. Otherwise it removes every Dwarf_Arange from the arange set's as_arlist and frees each one (only the arange structures themselves), frees the arange set head and sets dbg->dbgp_as = NULL. It returns nothing.
note: Dropped earlier because the item was an unnamed fragment; the function exists under the name above.

name: _dwarf_frame_section_init
prose: The packet name _dwarf_frame_section_create does not exist; the array-building code described by the old prose is the end of _dwarf_frame_section_init(dbg, frame_sec, ds, eh_frame, error) (libdwarf_frame.c:440-547), whose tail lies in this slice. Precondition: frame_sec is non-NULL and *frame_sec is NULL (asserted), ds describes a readable section, eh_frame is non-zero for .eh_frame. It callocs a Dwarf_FrameSec (failure sets DW_DLE_MEMORY and returns DW_DLE_MEMORY). It then reads the section entry by entry: a 4-byte length (or 0xffffffff followed by an 8-byte length); a length larger than the remaining data, or a zero length when not .eh_frame, returns DW_DLE_DEBUG_FRAME_LENGTH_BAD (error set); a zero length in .eh_frame ends the loop; each entry is added with _dwarf_frame_add_cie (CIE id 0 in .eh_frame, all ones otherwise) or _dwarf_frame_add_fde, and a non-DW_DLE_NONE result is returned after cleanup. After the loop, if there are CIEs (fs_cielen > 0) it mallocs fs_ciearray and fills it from the CIE list, and likewise fs_fdearray for FDEs; malloc failure returns DW_DLE_MEMORY after cleanup. On success *frame_sec is set to the new section and DW_DLE_NONE is returned; on every failure the section is torn down with _dwarf_frame_section_cleanup (freeing CIEs, FDEs, both arrays and the structure) and *frame_sec is left NULL.
note: Dropped earlier because the name was not in the file. The slice also contains the beginning of _dwarf_frame_run_inst, which is a different function.

name: _dwarf_find_section
prose: Precondition: dbg and name are non-NULL (asserted, so unchecked in NDEBUG builds) and dbg is a valid Dwarf_Debug whose dbg_section array holds dbg_seccnt entries. Postcondition: returns a pointer to the first entry dbg->dbg_section[i], for i from 0 to dbg_seccnt - 1, whose ds_name is non-NULL and strcmp-equal to name, or NULL if there is none; the pointer refers to memory owned by dbg, nothing is allocated or freed and no lock is taken.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong for this function: _dwarf_find_section (libdwarf_sections.c:209-224) does iterate dbg_section[0..dbg_seccnt-1); the dbgp_seclist STAILQ walk the reviewer saw is the neighbouring function _dwarf_pro_find_section, which is what lies inside the packet slice 252-280. Prose kept.

name: elf_rawdata
prose: Slice cut the head: this is the tail of elf_rawdata(s, ed) (elf_data.c:203), which returns the raw (untranslated) data descriptor of a section. If s is NULL, s->s_elf is NULL or the Elf has no raw file, it sets the ARGUMENT error and returns NULL. With ed == NULL and a non-empty s->s_rawdata list it returns the first descriptor's d_data without allocating; with a non-NULL ed it returns the address of the d_data of the descriptor after ed in the list (taken without a NULL check; because d_data is the first member this is NULL when ed was the last). Otherwise it reads sh_type, sh_offset, sh_size and sh_align from the 32- or 64-bit section header; SHT_NULL sets the SECTION error and returns NULL; for a type other than SHT_NOBITS, if sh_offset exceeds e->e_rawsize or sh_size exceeds the remaining bytes it sets the SECTION error and returns NULL; if _libelf_allocate_data fails it returns NULL (error set by that helper, RESOURCE). Otherwise it fills a new descriptor: d_buf = NULL for SHT_NOBITS or sh_size 0, else e_rawfile + sh_offset; d_off 0, d_align = sh_align, d_size = sh_size, d_type ELF_T_BYTE, d_version = e->e_version, appends it to s->s_rawdata (the section owns it; the caller must not free it) and returns its d_data.
note: Dropped earlier because the packet name _libelf_getrawdata does not exist; the real function is elf_rawdata. The old prose also missed the early returns for ed != NULL and an existing descriptor.

name: elftc_reloc_type_str
prose: Slice is the middle of elftc_reloc_type_str(mach, type) (libelftc/elftc_reloc_type_str.c:35). It switches on the ELF machine (EM_386 and EM_IAMCU, EM_AARCH64, EM_ARM, EM_IA_64, EM_MIPS, EM_PPC, EM_PPC64, EM_RISCV, EM_LOONGARCH, EM_S390, EM_SPARC and EM_SPARCV9, EM_X86_64) and then on the relocation type number, returning a pointer to a string literal such as "R_X86_64_PC32" when both are known. If the machine is not handled, or the type is not listed for that machine, it formats "<unknown: %#x>" for the type into a static 32-byte buffer with snprintf and returns a pointer to that buffer. It never returns NULL; the literals are statically owned, and the buffer is overwritten by the next unknown-type call (so that case is not thread-safe). Callers must not free or modify the result.
note: Old prose said the function returns NULL for an unrecognised machine or type; the code (libelftc/elftc_reloc_type_str.c:955-957) returns the formatted static buffer. Packet name reloc_type_name does not exist.

name: libpe_write_coff_header
prose: Writes the PE COFF header and, when the optional-header size is non-zero, the optional header and data directories, for libpe_write_coff_header(pe, off) (libpe_coff.c:225). Precondition: pe is an initialised PE handle with a writable pe_fd (seekable when pe_cmd == PE_C_RDWR) and off is the file offset of the COFF header. In PE_C_RDWR mode, if neither LIBPE_F_DIRTY_COFF_HEADER nor LIBPE_F_BAD_COFF_HEADER is set it only lseeks past the existing header and skips the write; otherwise it lseeks to off. If pe_ch is NULL it callocs it and picks a default machine from pe_obj; it then sets timestamp if zero, the optional-header size and characteristics by pe_obj (PE_O_PE32, PE_O_PE32P, or optsize 0 for other objects), IMAGE_FILE_LINE_NUMS_STRIPPED, the section count, symbol pointer and count, and IMAGE_FILE_RELOCS_STRIPPED when no .reloc section exists, resets ch_optsize if LIBPE_F_BAD_OPT_HEADER is set, and writes the header with write(). On both paths it advances off past the COFF header, clears LIBPE_F_DIRTY_COFF_HEADER and LIBPE_F_BAD_COFF_HEADER and sets LIBPE_F_DIRTY_SEC_HEADER. If ch_optsize is 0 it returns off at that point. Optional header: in PE_C_RDWR mode with neither LIBPE_F_DIRTY_OPT_HEADER nor LIBPE_F_BAD_OPT_HEADER set it only lseeks forward by ch_optsize and returns off + ch_optsize (flags unchanged); in other modes the flags are not consulted and the optional header is always written. Writing allocates pe_oh (calloc) if NULL, sets the magic, default linker version 2.22, oh_ndatadir = PE_DD_MAX, default alignments and header and image sizes, then writes the fields with WRITE_OPT (a write that would exceed ch_optsize pads the rest and stops; a short write or failed pad fails), may switch pe_obj to PE_O_PE32P when the magic is PE_FORMAT_32P, allocates pe_dd if NULL, fills the base-relocation entry when a .reloc section exists, writes the data directories and pads the rest. At opt_done it advances off by ch_optsize, clears LIBPE_F_DIRTY_OPT_HEADER and LIBPE_F_BAD_OPT_HEADER, sets LIBPE_F_DIRTY_SEC_HEADER and returns off. Failure: it returns -1 with errno EIO (lseek, write or libpe_pad failed) or ENOMEM (calloc failed), leaving already-written bytes and the file position unspecified. pe_ch, pe_oh and pe_dd, once allocated, stay owned by the handle.
note: Reviewer round 15 wrong: the clean-header RDWR path only lseeks (libpe_coff.c:242-253) and jumps to coff_done without writing; the write after lseek happens only for a dirty or bad header or in non-RDWR modes. The old prose was nearly right but implied optional-header flags matter in every mode; I made the RDWR-only condition explicit.
