name: pcap_parse_source
prose: static int pcap_parse_source(const char *source, char **schemep, char **userinfop, char **hostp, char **portp, char **pathp, char *ebuf) in libpcap pcap.c (lines 1771-2116; the packet showed only the middle of it and called it an unnamed uri parser). Precondition: the five out-pointers and ebuf are writable. Postcondition: if source is NULL or empty it returns -1 with a message in ebuf and leaves the out-parameters untouched (they are set to NULL only after these two checks). Otherwise all five are set to NULL and: with no ':' in source, or a ':' not followed by '//', *pathp is a strdup of the whole source and 0 is returned (malloc failure -> -1 with a message). For a 'file' scheme (case-insensitive) *schemep is the scheme and *pathp is everything after 'file://'. For rpcap or rpcaps with no '/' after the '//', *pathp is everything after '://' and *schemep stays NULL. Otherwise it takes the authority up to the next '/', splits off 'userinfo@' if present, then the host: an IP literal in brackets (the host is returned without the brackets; a missing ']' or extra text after it other than ':' fails with a message) or everything up to ':'; the port is the rest after ':' (it may be an empty string); an empty host part gives NULL host and port. The path is everything after the '/' that ended the authority (empty string if none). On success it returns 0 with *schemep, *pathp allocated and *userinfop, *hostp, *portp each NULL or allocated (the caller frees); on any failure it returns -1 with a message in ebuf, frees every string it had allocated, and leaves the out-parameters NULL.
note: slice shows only lines 1795-2062; real function pcap_parse_source (line 1772); old prose wrongly said the out-parameters are first set to NULL in the NULL/empty-source error cases (they are untouched)

name: daemon_msg_startcap_req
prose: static int daemon_msg_startcap_req(uint8 ver, struct daemon_slpars *pars, uint32 plen, char *source, struct session **sessionp, struct rpcap_sampling *samp_param, int uses_ssl) in libpcap rpcapd/daemon.c (lines 1953-2293; slice cut head). Precondition: the control connection pars is open and the request's remaining payload length is plen. Postcondition: it receives the start-capture request (a fatal receive error jumps to fatal_error; a non-fatal one to error), rejects a datagram request when SSL is in use, allocates a session, opens the capture device with pcap_open_live, then creates the data socket either actively (connecting to the client's address and port) or passively (listening on a free port), unpacks and applies the client's filter (-1 -> fatal_error, -2 -> error), sends the start-capture reply carrying the buffer size and, for passive mode, the port (a send failure goes to fatal_error), accepts the client's data connection in passive mode, performs the TLS handshake on the data socket when uses_ssl, starts the data thread, and discards any excess request data (failure -> fatal_error). On full success it returns 0 with *sessionp pointing at the new session. In the 'error' path (non-fatal errors) it sets *sessionp = NULL, frees addrinfo and the session, sends the client an error reply (PCAP_ERR_STARTCAPTURE with the message in errmsgbuf; several error sites fill errbuf instead, so the reply can carry an uninitialised or stale message) and discards excess data; it returns 0 if both succeed, or -1 if sending the error reply or discarding the data fails. In the 'fatal_error' path it sets *sessionp = NULL, closes and frees any session, sends no error reply and returns -1.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): -1 is also returned from the error path when sending the error reply or discarding data fails, after an error reply was attempted; fatal_error itself sends none; also noted errmsgbuf/errbuf mismatch

name: pcap_next_packet
prose: static int pcap_next_packet(pcap_t *p, struct pcap_pkthdr *hdr, u_char **data) (libpcap sf-pcap.c lines 517-789; slice cut head). Precondition: p->rfile is positioned at a per-packet header; hdr and data are non-NULL. Postcondition: returns 0 only at a clean end of file (no bytes read for the header; hdr and data untouched); returns -1 with a message in p->errbuf on a header read I/O error, a truncated header, a captured length above max_snaplen_for_dlt(linktype) (the message mentions the snapshot length or the maximum), buffer growth failure, or an I/O error or EOF while reading the packet bytes or the bytes beyond the snapshot length; in the error cases *hdr may already be partly filled and *data is not set. On success it returns 1: hdr is filled from the file header (byte-swapped when p->swapped, microseconds scaled to nanoseconds or the reverse according to scale_type, caplen and len exchanged when lengths_swapped is SWAPPED, or MAYBE_SWAPPED with caplen > len); if caplen exceeds the snapshot length the buffer is grown to the snapshot length, the first snapshot bytes are read, the rest is read and discarded in 4096-byte pieces and caplen is set to the snapshot length; otherwise the buffer is grown (next power of two, capped at the snapshot length) if needed and caplen bytes are read. *data is set to p->buffer and pcapint_post_process(linktype, swapped, hdr, data) is called before returning. p->buffer may be reallocated, so earlier pointers into it become invalid.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): pcapint_post_process IS called at line 786

name: kh_resize_##name
prose: Macro-generated function kh_resize_##name(kh_##name##_t *h, khint_t new_n_buckets), defined inside __KHASH_IMPL in khash.h (lines 244-~310). Precondition: h is a valid initialised table of the generated type. Postcondition: new_n_buckets is rounded up to a power of two (minimum 4). If h->size is at least (khint_t)(new_n_buckets * 0.77 + 0.5) no rehash is done and the table is left unchanged. Otherwise it allocates and fills a new flags array (failure -> -1), and when growing reallocates the keys array (and the values array for maps); a failure frees the new flags and returns -1, with h->keys possibly already enlarged (valid, contents preserved) if only the values reallocation failed. It then rehashes every live element into the new capacity with the kick-out scheme, shrinks the keys and values arrays when shrinking (these shrinking reallocations are not checked), frees the old flags, installs the new flags and n_buckets, and (in the part after the slice) updates n_occupied and upper_bound; it returns 0 in the success and no-op cases. The caller keeps ownership of h.
note: added: shrink reallocations unchecked; verified lines 244-302 of the macro

name: TREE_ROTL_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_ROTL_##node##_##field(struct node *self) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_ROTL_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self and self->avl_right are non-NULL and the subtrees have valid heights. Postcondition: the right child r becomes the new subtree root: self takes over r's former left subtree, self is rebalanced with TREE_BALANCE and becomes r's left child, then r is rebalanced and returned as the new root. Rebalancing recomputes heights and may rotate further.

name: TREE_ROTR_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_ROTR_##node##_##field(struct node *self) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_ROTR_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self and self->avl_left are non-NULL and the subtrees have valid heights. Postcondition: the left child l becomes the new subtree root: self takes over l's former right subtree, self is rebalanced and becomes l's right child, then l is rebalanced and returned as the new root.

name: TREE_BALANCE_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_BALANCE_##node##_##field(struct node *self) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_BALANCE_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self is non-NULL and its children are valid subtrees with correct heights. Postcondition: it computes delta = (left height) - (right height), where a missing child counts as 0. If delta < -1 it first rotates the right child to the right when that child leans left (delta of the child > 0), then rotates self left and returns the new root; if delta > 1 it first rotates the left child left when that child leans right, then rotates self right and returns the new root; otherwise it sets self's avl_height to 1 plus the larger child height and returns self.

name: TREE_INSERT_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_INSERT_##node##_##field(struct node *self, struct node *elm, int (*compare)(struct node *, struct node *)) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_INSERT_<node>_<field>). Precondition: elm is non-NULL with its child pointers NULL and a valid avl_height (this function does not initialise them), compare is a valid ordering, and self is a valid AVL subtree or NULL. Postcondition: if self is NULL it returns elm; otherwise it recursively inserts elm into the left subtree when compare(elm, self) < 0, else into the right subtree (so elements that compare equal go right), and returns self after TREE_BALANCE.

name: TREE_FIND_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_FIND_##node##_##field(struct node *self, struct node *elm, int (*compare)(struct node *, struct node *)) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_FIND_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self is a valid subtree or NULL and compare is consistent with the tree's ordering. Postcondition: returns NULL if self is NULL; returns self if compare(elm, self) == 0; otherwise returns the result of searching the left subtree when compare(elm, self) < 0, else the right subtree. compare is called up to twice per node. The tree is not modified.

name: TREE_REMOVE_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_REMOVE_##node##_##field(struct node *self, struct node *elm, int (*compare)(struct node *, struct node *)) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_REMOVE_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self is a valid AVL subtree or NULL and compare is consistent with the tree's ordering. Postcondition: returns NULL if self is NULL. If compare(elm, self) == 0 it detaches self: its left subtree and right subtree are merged with TREE_MOVE_RIGHT (the right subtree is attached at the rightmost position of the left subtree, rebalancing along that path), self's avl_left and avl_right are set to NULL (its height is not reset) and the merged subtree root is returned. Otherwise it recurses into the left subtree when compare(elm, self) < 0, else the right, and returns self after TREE_BALANCE. The node matched is the one whose compare result is 0, which need not be the same pointer as elm; nothing is freed.

name: TREE_FORWARD_APPLY_ALL_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_FORWARD_APPLY_ALL_##node##_##field(struct node *self, void (*function)(struct node *, void *), void *data) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_FORWARD_APPLY_ALL_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self is a valid subtree or NULL and function is callable. Postcondition: does nothing for NULL; otherwise recursively visits the left subtree, calls function(self, data), then recursively visits the right subtree, so every node is visited once in in-order (ascending) order. It does not change the tree itself.

name: TREE_REVERSE_APPLY_ALL_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_REVERSE_APPLY_ALL_##node##_##field(struct node *self, void (*function)(struct node *, void *), void *data) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_REVERSE_APPLY_ALL_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self is a valid subtree or NULL and function is callable. Postcondition: does nothing for NULL; otherwise recursively visits the right subtree, calls function(self, data), then recursively visits the left subtree, so every node is visited once in reverse in-order (descending) order. It does not change the tree itself.

name: ucl_msgpack_consume
prose: static bool ucl_msgpack_consume(struct ucl_parser *parser) in libucl ucl_msgpack.c (lines 947-1330; the packet called it an unnamed parse loop; I read the whole function, but only skimmed the sub-parsers it calls). Precondition: parser->chunks->begin/remain describe the msgpack buffer. Postcondition: it runs a state machine over the buffer (read_type, start_assoc, start_array, read_assoc_key, read_assoc_value, read_array_value, finish states). It returns false, in every such case with parser->err set (ucl_create_err or inside the called helpers), for: an unknown msgpack type byte; not enough data for a length field; an invalid length-field size; a failure of ucl_msgpack_insert_object (no key for an object member, bad container type); a NULL result of ucl_msgpack_get_container (out of memory or a bad top-level object); a negative result from a sub-parser (the CONSUME_RET macro); a key whose type is not a string, or an empty or too long key; a value or container operation with no container on the stack; an empty container found by GET_NEXT_STATE; the error state; at the end of input, a non-empty container still starting, an unfinished value, an invalid finishing state, or a non-empty stack after rewinding ('incomplete container'). It returns true only if the whole buffer was consumed without these errors and the container stack is empty after the final rewind. In the final handling of a trailing empty container the return value of the sub-parser is not checked.
note: reviewer WRONG (R17): the NULL-container and insert failures do set parser->err (ucl_msgpack_get_container lines 777-779, 787-789, 816; ucl_msgpack_insert_object lines 855-857, 869)

name: ucl_state_machine
prose: static bool ucl_state_machine(struct ucl_parser *parser) in libucl ucl_parser.c (lines 2424-2770; slice cut head). Precondition: parser->chunks is the chunk to parse. Postcondition: if parser->top_obj is NULL the state is reset to UCL_STATE_INIT. It loops while chunk->pos < chunk->end handling the states INIT, KEY/KEY_OBRACE, VALUE, AFTER_VALUE, MACRO_NAME, MACRO and ERROR. It returns true at once from the AFTER_VALUE state when ucl_parse_after_value succeeded and the object stack is empty (the rest of the chunk is ignored); otherwise after the loop it attaches any pending last comment to the current, stacked or top object (or drops it), and then, if the stack is non-empty and the state is not ERROR, it checks the stack entries belonging to this chunk for open braces: if any was opened with a brace it appends 'unmatched open brace' text to parser->err, sets err_code to UCL_EUNPAIRED and returns false; otherwise it returns true. It returns false after setting parser->state to UCL_STATE_ERROR (and, in most cases, an error message) for: a failed comment skip or syntax error in INIT, a key where the stack is already empty, a failure of ucl_parse_key, ucl_parse_value (or a NULL current object, which sets the state but no message), ucl_parse_after_value, an invalid, unknown or malformed macro, a failure of ucl_parse_macro_value, an unknown state (internal-error message), or the error state itself. It also returns false without changing the state when creating a container fails (INIT or nested key case), and when a macro handler returns false (the state was already restored from prev_state; a missing macro sets an internal error message).
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (container allocation failures return false without setting UCL_STATE_ERROR) and R15 (UCL_STATE_VALUE with a NULL cur_obj returns false without a message, lines 2559-2563)

name: ucl_schema_validate
prose: static bool ucl_schema_validate(const ucl_object_t *schema, const ucl_object_t *obj, bool try_array, struct ucl_schema_error *err, const ucl_object_t *root, ucl_object_t *external_refs) in libucl ucl_schema.c (lines 929-1066; slice cut head). Precondition: schema and root are valid; obj is non-NULL unless try_array is true; err may be NULL, but if the schema contains a satisfied 'anyOf' or a failing 'not' subschema the code writes err->code, so err must then be non-NULL. Postcondition: returns false with UCL_SCHEMA_INVALID_SCHEMA if schema is not an object. With try_array true it checks maxValues and minValues over the sibling chain starting at obj (a violation gives UCL_SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT and false) and validates every element of that chain individually (try_array false), returning true if all pass. With try_array false it checks, in order: 'enum'; 'allOf' (each sub-schema validated with try_array true; the first failure returns false); 'anyOf' (the first sub-schema that passes ends the loop, a pass sets err->code = UCL_SCHEMA_OK, no pass returns false with the last sub-validation's error left in err; note that for an empty anyOf array 'ret' is read uninitialised); 'oneOf' (false if no sub-schema or more than one passes; when more than one passes no new error is written); 'not' (false if the subschema passes, without writing an error; if it fails err->code is reset to UCL_SCHEMA_OK); '$ref' (resolved through ucl_schema_resolve_ref, false on failure, then validated with the referenced schema); the 'type' constraint (false on mismatch); and finally returns the result of the object, array, number (int or float) or string validators according to obj->type, or true for other types.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (not/oneOf failures do not set err) and R15 (err->code is dereferenced in the anyOf success and not branches, so err may not be NULL there, lines 994, 1023)

name: ucl_load_handler
prose: bool ucl_load_handler(const unsigned char *data, size_t len, const ucl_object_t *args, void *ud) in libucl ucl_util.c (lines 1771-1930; slice cut head). Precondition: ud is the parser; when len > 0 the stack must be non-empty (parser->stack->obj is used without a check). Postcondition: returns false (no message) if parser is NULL. It reads options from args when args is an object: booleans try, multiline, escape, trim (matched with strncmp against the key's length, so a key that is a prefix of an option name also matches), strings key and target, integer priority. It returns false with message 'No Key specified in load macro' if key is NULL or empty. If len is 0 it returns false with 'Unable to parse load macro'. Otherwise it copies the file name (allocation failure -> false) and fetches the file with ucl_fetch_file: on failure it returns try_load (true when try was set, after clearing the error; false otherwise with the error left in parser->err). If the top container already has the key it sets 'Key %s already exists', unmaps the buffer and returns false. For target 'string' (case-insensitive, the default) it creates a string object from the buffer with the escape/trim flags, copies its value, and sets the multiline flag if requested; if object creation returns NULL these later steps use the NULL pointer without a check. For target 'int' it copies the buffer to a temporary string (allocation failure -> false, with a message, buffer unmapped), parses it with strtoll base 10 and creates an integer object. Any other target creates no object. It unmaps the buffer and, if an object was created, sets its key and priority and inserts it into the top container, then returns true (also when no object was created).
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the string branch dereferences the object returned by ucl_object_fromstring_common without a NULL check (lines 1887-1891), so 'returns true when object creation fails' is not what the code does

name: cbor_handler
prose: static int cbor_handler(XO_ENCODER_HANDLER_ARGS) in libxo enc_cbor.c (lines 243-102 of the excerpt; real function at lines 243-343; slice cut head). Precondition: xop is a valid handle; unless op is XO_OP_CREATE the private data (the cbor_private_t) must exist; name and value must be valid strings for the ops that use them. Postcondition: if XOF_PRETTY is set it first prints a trace line ('op <name>: [name] [value]') and flushes stdout, even when there is no private data. It then returns -1 if private is NULL and op is not XO_OP_CREATE. Otherwise, by op: XO_OP_CREATE returns cbor_create(xop); the open ops append the name as a CBOR string and an indefinite map/array start and increase c_indent (and set c_open_leaf_list for a leaf list); the close ops append a break and decrease c_indent (clearing c_open_leaf_list for leaf lists); XO_OP_OPEN_INSTANCE/CLOSE_INSTANCE do the map start/break without a name; XO_OP_STRING and XO_OP_CONTENT append the name (unless inside a leaf list) and the value as a string or, for content, as true/false/null/number through cbor_content; XO_OP_FINISH appends a break and decreases c_indent; XO_OP_FLUSH with XOF_PRETTY dumps the buffer to stdout through cbor_memdump and returns 0, otherwise it writes the buffer to descriptor 1 and returns 0 when the write returns a non-negative count or -1 when it fails; XO_OP_DESTROY, XO_OP_ATTRIBUTE, XO_OP_VERSION and any other op do nothing. Every case other than the ones above returns 0.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the pretty trace print is at lines 250-254, before the NULL-private check at 257; reviewer R1 (cbor_create and write failure returns) RIGHT

name: csv_open_level
prose: static int csv_open_level(xo_handle_t *xop, csv_private_t *csv, const char *name, int instance) in libxo enc_csv.c (lines 420-457). Precondition: csv is a valid csv_private_t with its path and name stack initialised; name is a valid string. xop is marked UNUSED in the parameter list but is in fact used: it is passed to csv_emit_record and csv_dbg. Postcondition: always returns 0. If CF_RECORD_DATA is set (a new open event ends recording) it clears that flag, emits the record with csv_emit_record and returns without pushing name or changing the path cursor. Otherwise it takes the next expected path member, csv_path_top(csv, 0): if there is none and instance is non-zero and CF_HAS_PATH is clear it sets CF_RECORD_DATA; if there is a member equal to name it advances c_path_cur by one and, when c_path_cur reaches c_path_max, sets CF_RECORD_DATA; a member that does not match leaves things unchanged. In all of these non-emitting cases it then pushes name onto the stack with csv_stack_push.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (returns before pushing when recording) and R15 (xop is used by csv_emit_record and csv_dbg)

name: xo_set_options
prose: int xo_set_options(xo_handle_t *xop, const char *input) in libxo libxo.c (lines 2261-2443; slice cut head). Precondition: xop may be NULL (the default handle is used). Postcondition: if input is NULL it returns 0 and changes nothing. If input starts with ':' each following character is a one-letter option (c f F g H I i<digits> J k n P T U u W X x set the corresponding flag, style or indent; other letters are ignored) and it returns 0. Otherwise it works on a copy and processes comma-separated tokens: '@name' and 'encoder=name' call xo_encoder_init (a missing name calls xo_failure, a failed init issues a warning, and in both cases rc is assigned the init result); 'colors=...' sets the colour map; a style name is accepted only the first time (the first style wins and later ones are ignored with a warning) and is applied after the loop only if it is greater than 0; other names are looked up as flags (set), 'no-color' (clears colour), 'indent=N' (a missing value calls xo_failure); any other token warns 'unknown libxo option value' and sets rc to -1. It returns rc, which is 0 if nothing failed, -1 after an unknown token, or the last xo_encoder_init result; a later successful encoder initialisation overwrites an earlier -1 with 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the first style wins (line 2408-2411) and a later 'rc = xo_encoder_init()' can overwrite an earlier -1

name: xo_do_format_field
prose: static ssize_t xo_do_format_field(xo_handle_t *xop, xo_buffer_t *xbp, const char *fmt, ssize_t flen, xo_xff_flags_t flags) in libxo libxo.c (lines 3309-3664; slice cut head). Precondition: xop->xo_vap holds the arguments for fmt, fmt has flen readable bytes, xbp is NULL (then xo_data is used) or a writable buffer. Postcondition: returns 0 when the whole format was processed, and -1 when a format has too many '.' qualifiers, contains an 'n' or 'v' conversion, or xo_buf_has_room fails for the per-field format copy. It walks fmt: literal runs (with '%%' and backslash escapes) are appended through xo_format_string_direct when output is wanted; each conversion is parsed into an xo_format_t, a '%@...@' prefix is skipped (a '*' inside it consumes an int argument unless XOF_NO_VA_ARG), and the field is skipped (no output) when XFF_NO_OUTPUT is set or when a hidden-field flag does not apply to the style (the tests use XOF_ISSET on the handle with XFF constants). If not skipped, string conversions (s, S, m) with no formatter go through xo_format_string and others through xo_vsnprintf with escaping appropriate to XML, HTML, JSON, SDPARAMS or encoder styles; xo_columns and xo_anchor_columns are updated when XOF_COLUMNS and XOIF_ANCHOR are set. Unless XOF_NO_VA_ARG is set, the corresponding va_arg arguments are consumed for every conversion (also for skipped fields; for a skipped 's' the string pointer is popped), so XFF_NO_OUTPUT suppresses output but not argument consumption, whereas XOF_NO_VA_ARG suppresses consumption. A missing conversion character only reports xo_failure and continues. After the loop the trailing literal is appended, and with the gettext flags xo_format_gettext post-processes the field.
note: reviewer R15 partly WRONG: with XFF_NO_OUTPUT (make_output false) no output is appended but va_arg arguments are still consumed (lines 3400, 3566-3629); only XOF_NO_VA_ARG avoids consuming

name: xo_do_close_container
prose: static int xo_do_close_container(xo_handle_t *xop, const char *name) in libxo libxo.c (lines 7043-7102; slice cut head). Precondition: xop may be NULL (the default handle is used). Postcondition: if name is NULL it is taken from the top stack entry (copied into an alloca buffer because xo_depth_change frees it); if that entry has no name and lacks XSF_DTRT a failure is reported and XO_FAILURE_NAME is used, while in DTRT mode with no stack name it stays NULL. By style: XML calls xo_depth_change (depth -1, indent -1) and prints the closing tag, returning the number of bytes printed; JSON sets the stack flags, changes depth and indent by -1, prints '}' (with newlines if pretty), marks the enclosing stack entry XSF_NOT_FIRST and returns the printed byte count; HTML and TEXT change the depth by -1 (indent unchanged) and print nothing (return 0); SDPARAMS does nothing at all, including no depth change (return 0); ENCODER changes the depth by -1 and returns xo_encoder_handle's result for XO_OP_CLOSE_CONTAINER.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (xop may be NULL; DTRT keeps name NULL) and R15 (SDPARAMS does not decrement depth, line 7092-7093)

name: xo_do_close
prose: static int xo_do_close(xo_handle_t *xop, const char *name, xo_state_t new_state) in libxo libxo.c (lines 7597-7656; slice cut head). Precondition: xop is valid. Postcondition: new_state is mapped to the open state that must be found (container, list, instance, leaf list) or, for XSS_MARKER, a marker; any other new_state returns 0 at once. It scans the stack from the top entry down (never reaching entry 0). When need_state is not a marker and it meets a marker: if name is non-NULL it reports a failure and returns 0; otherwise it reports 'close stops at marker', uses that marker as the limit and stops. When looking for a marker (new_state XSS_MARKER) markers do not stop the scan. An entry matches when its state equals the needed state and, when name is non-NULL, its name is NULL or equal to name (entries without a name are not skipped). If no limit was found it reports a failure and returns 0. Otherwise it returns xo_do_close_all(xop, limit), which closes every scope from the top down to and including the limit and always returns 0 (a negative close result is only reported with xo_failure). So the function returns 0 on every path.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): a marker does not stop the scan when new_state is XSS_MARKER, and entries with no name match any name (lines 7622, 7640)

name: xo_transition
prose: static ssize_t xo_transition(xo_handle_t *xop, xo_xof_flags_t flags, const char *name, xo_state_t new_state) in libxo libxo.c (lines 7661-7919; the slice ends at line 7903, before the flush handling). Precondition: xop may be NULL (xo_default is used); the stack is initialised. Postcondition: it finds the effective old state (skipping markers on top of the stack, remembering that it started on a marker) and dispatches on the pair (old state, new state): it opens or closes containers, lists, instances and leaf lists through the xo_do_* functions, first closing an open list or leaf list or instance when needed, returns the result of the last such call (negative on its failure), does nothing (rc 0) for the emit transitions that need nothing, logs a failure and does nothing for close-instance and close-leaf-list from the initial state, and logs 'unknown transition' for unlisted pairs (rc stays 0). If a close would have to cross a marker it logs a failure and returns -1 at once, without setting XOIF_MADE_OUTPUT. Otherwise, after the dispatch, if rc is non-negative and XOF_FLUSH is set it calls xo_flush_h and returns -1 if that fails; it then sets XOIF_MADE_OUTPUT (also when rc is negative) and returns rc.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): the XOF_FLUSH/xo_flush_h and XOIF_MADE_OUTPUT code exists at lines 7904-7910; the slice stopped at line 7903; reviewers R1/R2 (marker_prevents_close error path) RIGHT

name: yaml_parser_load_mapping
prose: static int yaml_parser_load_mapping(yaml_parser_t *parser, yaml_event_t *event, struct loader_ctx *ctx) in libyaml loader.c (lines 482-527; slice shows lines 505-544; the packet named it yaml_parser_load_mapping_start). Precondition: event is a MAPPING-START event whose tag and anchor strings are handed over to this function. Postcondition: it checks the document node stack limit, replaces a NULL tag or a '!' tag by a copy of the default mapping tag, creates an empty pairs stack and a mapping node that owns the tag and pairs, pushes the node on parser->document->nodes, registers the anchor for the new node index, records the node in its parent with yaml_parser_load_node_add, checks the loader-context stack limit and pushes the index onto *ctx; it returns 1 on success. It returns 0 on failure: if the node-stack limit check, the default tag duplication, the pairs stack initialisation, or the push of the node onto the document nodes fails, it frees the tag and the event's anchor and returns 0 (a pairs stack already allocated is not freed on the push-failure path); if registering the anchor, load_node_add, the context limit check or the context push fails after the node was pushed, it returns 0 without freeing the tag (now owned by the node on the document's node stack), with the anchor handled by yaml_parser_register_anchor, and with nothing pushed onto *ctx unless the last push itself succeeded.
note: slice cut head; real function name yaml_parser_load_mapping (line 483); old prose slightly overstated that nothing was pushed to ctx on every failure after the node push - only the final push can succeed or fail last

name: yaml_parser_parse_flow_mapping_value
prose: static int yaml_parser_parse_flow_mapping_value(yaml_parser_t *parser, yaml_event_t *event, int empty) in libyaml parser.c (lines 1169-1199). Precondition: a token can be peeked from the scanner. Postcondition: returns 0 if no token can be peeked (error set by the scanner). If empty is non-zero it sets parser->state to YAML_PARSE_FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE and returns the result of yaml_parser_process_empty_scalar (1 with an empty plain scalar event at the token's start mark, or 0 with YAML_MEMORY_ERROR if allocation fails). Otherwise, if the token is a VALUE token it is skipped and the next token is peeked (failure -> 0); if that token is neither a FLOW-ENTRY nor a FLOW-MAPPING-END it pushes YAML_PARSE_FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE on the parser's states stack (failure -> 0) and returns yaml_parser_parse_node(parser, event, 0, 0), which determines parser->state itself (for a plain scalar the pushed state is restored later, for a collection the state becomes the first-entry state of that collection). In the remaining cases (no VALUE token, or the VALUE is followed directly by a flow entry or mapping end) it sets parser->state to YAML_PARSE_FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE and returns the empty scalar event as above.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 and R15 (the node branch leaves the state to parse_node, not FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE)

name: yaml_parser_parse_block_sequence_entry
prose: Static libyaml parser state function. Returns 1 or 0 as follows. If first is nonzero it first does PEEK_TOKEN and then PUSHes that token's start_mark onto parser->marks without checking the PEEK_TOKEN result for NULL (a NULL token would be dereferenced); if the PUSH fails (parser->error set to YAML_MEMORY_ERROR) it returns 0; otherwise it skips the token. It then peeks the next token and returns 0 if none can be fetched. If that token is YAML_BLOCK_ENTRY_TOKEN it skips it and peeks again (return 0 if no token); if the new token is neither a block-entry nor a block-end token it pushes YAML_PARSE_BLOCK_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_STATE onto parser->states (return 0 if the push fails) and returns the result of yaml_parser_parse_node(parser, event, 1, 0); otherwise it sets parser->state to YAML_PARSE_BLOCK_SEQUENCE_ENTRY_STATE and returns the result of yaml_parser_process_empty_scalar (1 and an empty plain-scalar event, or 0 with YAML_MEMORY_ERROR if the one-byte malloc fails). If the token is YAML_BLOCK_END_TOKEN it sets parser->state to the popped parser->states entry, pops parser->marks, fills event with a sequence-end event using the token's marks, skips the token and returns 1. For any other token type it pops parser->marks and returns the result of yaml_parser_set_parser_error_context with problem "did not find expected '-' indicator" (an error return, 0).
note: Reviewer 1 (omits empty-scalar path) wrong: prose already had it, code lines 'else { parser->state = ...ENTRY_STATE; return yaml_parser_process_empty_scalar }'. Reviewer 2 right: with first!=0 the PEEK_TOKEN result is used as token->start_mark with no NULL check.

name: copy_event
prose: Test-helper in run-emitter.c. Switches on event_from->type and returns the value of the matching libyaml initializer called on event_to with data copied from event_from: yaml_stream_start_event_initialize, yaml_stream_end_event_initialize, yaml_document_start_event_initialize, yaml_document_end_event_initialize, yaml_alias_event_initialize, yaml_scalar_event_initialize, yaml_sequence_start_event_initialize, yaml_sequence_end_event_initialize, yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize or yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize. Those initializers return 1 on success and 0 on failure (for example allocation failure); copy_event passes that value through. For any other type value the default branch executes assert(1), which is a no-op, so control reaches the final return 0 and event_to is not touched by this function.
note: Reviewer (round 15) wrong: default branch is assert(1), which never fails, so the function falls out of the switch to 'return 0' (run-emitter.c copy_event default: / assert(1); / return 0). Original reviewer's 'opposite of stated' also wrong: prose already said 1 on success, 0 on failure.

name: main
prose: Test driver. First loop over argv from index 1: an argument equal to "-c" sets canonical, "-u" sets unicode; any other argument starting with '-' prints "Unknown option" and main returns 0 immediately. Every argument starting with '-' that was not rejected (i.e. -c and -u) is removed from argv by shifting and decrementing argc. If fewer than one file argument remains (argc < 2) it prints a usage line and returns 0. Otherwise for each file argument it prints a header, opens the file (assert(file)), initializes a parser and an emitter writing to a BUFFER_SIZE-byte in-memory buffer, then loops: yaml_parser_parse; if parsing fails it sets error=1 and leaves the loop; otherwise it stores a copy of the event with copy_event (assert(event_number < MAX_EVENTS) before the store, so up to MAX_EVENTS events fit) and emits the event, asserting that emit succeeds (or print_output, which returns 0 after printing the failure report, so the assert still fails). After the loop it deletes the parser and emitter and asserts fclose succeeded. It then frees the stored events (events 0..event_number-1), prints "PASSED (length: <written>)" and calls print_output for the file; this PASSED line is printed even when the first pass stopped on a parse error (error=1, second pass skipped). After the last file main returns 0. All the asserts (fopen, initialize, copy_event, emit, parse, compare, fclose) abort the program when they fail, and compile to nothing if NDEBUG is defined.

name: #define HEXAGON_V64_CREATE_W(w1, w0)
prose: Function-like macro in hexagon_types.h that builds a 64-bit value from two words; two definitions are selected by #ifdef __hexagon__. Under __hexagon__ it is a GNU statement expression that stores (w0) into w[0] and (w1) into w[1] of a local union {long long d; int w[2];} and yields d, so w0 occupies the low 32 bits and w1 the high 32 bits given the target's little-endian layout. Otherwise it expands to the expression ((HEXAGON_Vect64)(w1) << 32LL) | (HEXAGON_Vect64)((w0) & 0xffffffff); here w1 is not masked, and shifting a negative or large signed w1 left follows the C rules for that type.
note: macro; fixed under its definition head. Both variants read from the source (hexagon_types.h lines 554-570).

name: #define HEXAGON_V64_CREATE_H(h3, h2, h1, h0)
prose: Function-like macro in hexagon_types.h building a 64-bit value from four halfwords, two definitions selected by #ifdef __hexagon__. Under __hexagon__ it is a statement expression that stores each argument into h[0]..h[3] of a local union {long long d; short h[4];} (h0 into h[0], h3 into h[3], each converted to short) and yields d, so h0 occupies bits 0-15 and h3 bits 48-63 on the little-endian target. Otherwise it expands to ((HEXAGON_Vect64)(h3) << 48LL) | (((HEXAGON_Vect64)((h2) & 0xffff)) << 32LL) | (((HEXAGON_Vect64)((h1) & 0xffff)) << 16LL) | (HEXAGON_Vect64)((h0) & 0xffff); h2, h1 and h0 are masked to 16 bits, h3 is only cast and shifted, not masked.

name: #define HEXAGON_V64_CREATE_B(b7, b6, b5, b4, b3, b2, b1, b0)
prose: Function-like macro in hexagon_types.h building a 64-bit value from eight bytes, two definitions selected by #ifdef __hexagon__. Under __hexagon__ it stores each argument into b[0]..b[7] of a local union {long long d; char b[8];} (b0 into b[0], b7 into b[7], each converted to char) and yields d, so b0 is the lowest byte and b7 the highest on the little-endian target. Otherwise it expands to a shifted OR: (HEXAGON_Vect64)(b7) << 56LL combined with ((b6) & 0xff) << 48 ... ((b0) & 0xff); b6..b0 are masked to 8 bits, b7 is only cast and shifted, not masked.

name: DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)
prose: Generated function (from macro DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)): extern "C" uptr __asan_stack_malloc_0(uptr size) returns OnMalloc(0, size). OnMalloc obtains the fake stack through GetFakeStackFast(): the thread-local fake stack if one is set; otherwise, if __asan_option_detect_stack_use_after_return is false, nullptr; otherwise GetFakeStack(), which is nullptr when there is no current thread and otherwise creates the thread's fake stack on first use. If there is no fake stack, or FakeStack::Allocate returns nullptr (no free class-0 frame), it returns 0. Otherwise it calls SetShadow(ptr, size, 0, 0) on the frame and returns the frame address. FakeStack::Allocate may first run GC when needs_gc_ is set, and marks the chosen frame's flag byte as used; SetShadow CHECK-fails (aborts) if ptr + size is not shadow-granule aligned, and poisons the redzone from ptr+size to the end of the frame with the stack right-redzone magic.
note: Frames returned here are freed with __asan_stack_free_0. Reviewer's point concerned the free side, not this function; this prose was rewritten after reading OnMalloc/Allocate/SetShadow in asan_fake_stack.cpp.

name: DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)
prose: Generated function (from macro DEFINE_STACK_MALLOC_FREE_WITH_CLASS_ID(0)): extern "C" void __asan_stack_free_0(uptr ptr, uptr size) calls OnFree(ptr, 0, size), which (1) calls FakeStack::Deallocate(ptr, 0), writing 0 through the saved flag pointer stored in the frame, thereby marking the frame free (there is no null or validity check on ptr, so a bad ptr is dereferenced), then (2) calls SetShadow(ptr, size, 0, kMagic8), which sets the frame's shadow (for class 0 on a shadow scale of 3, one 64-bit shadow word) to the stack-after-return magic; SetShadow CHECK-fails if ptr + size is not shadow-granule aligned. It returns nothing. The frame it expects is one handed out by the fake stack, i.e. returned by either __asan_stack_malloc_0 or __asan_stack_malloc_always_0.

name: initHwProbe
prose: Static function in riscv.c that issues the Linux riscv_hwprobe system call (number 258) through syscall_impl_5_args with arguments (Hwprobes, len, 0, 0, 0), i.e. pairs = Hwprobes, pair_count = len, cpusetsize = 0, cpus = NULL, flags = 0, and returns the raw long result of the ecall. With these arguments the Linux kernel's hwprobe_get_values returns 0 after filling in the value (and key, set to -1 for unknown keys) of each of the len pairs, and returns a negative errno on failure (for example -EFAULT for a bad pointer, or -ENOSYS if the syscall is not implemented); it does not return a count of keys or entries. Hwprobes must point to len writable struct riscv_hwprobe entries with the keys already set. The caller keeps ownership of the array.

name: __fixtfdi
prose: PowerPC double-double to int64 conversion in compiler-rt; takes the long double input as hi/lo doubles (DD) and returns uint64_t carrying an int64_t value. Path 1: if the unsigned value (high 32 bits of hi with the sign cleared) minus 0x3ff00000 is below 0x03f00000, i.e. 1.0 <= |hi| < 2^63 by exponent, it builds the integer from hi's mantissa, adds the lo tail mantissa (negated when hi and lo signs differ, arithmetic-shifted by the exponent difference first) if lo != 0, shifts right by 62 minus the unbiased head exponent and restores the sign of hi; this approximates truncation toward zero of hi + lo (the tail is shifted separately, so its low bits are floored before being added). Path 2: otherwise, if fabs(hi) < 1.0, it returns 0. Path 3: otherwise, if hi == -2^63, it returns INT64_MIN, except that when lo > 0.0 it returns INT64_MIN plus the ceiling of lo's magnitude (tail mantissa negated, arithmetic-shifted right by 1075 minus lo's biased exponent, then subtracted). Path 4: otherwise it returns INT64_MAX when hi > 0.0 (|hi| >= 2^63, including +infinity) and INT64_MIN when not (NaN hi, -infinity, and hi below -2^63). No memory is accessed beyond locals.
note: Round-1 reviewer wrong (prose already said NaN gives INT64_MIN: final 'else return INT64_MIN' at fixtfdi.c:96-97). Round-15 reviewer right: hi == -2^63 with lo > 0 adds ceil(lo) (lines 80-87), not a truncation.

name: __llvm_ctx_profile_get_context
prose: Returns a ContextNode pointer (no path in this function returns null) for the function with the given Guid, and increments counters[0] of real nodes it hands out. It reads TLS __llvm_ctx_profile_current_context_root. (1) If that is null it returns getUnhandledContext(..., nullptr) without touching the two TLS slots: that may start a root context (tryStartContextGivenRoot, which sets IsUnderContext, may take the root's Taken lock via TryLock and leave it held, and returns either the root's first node or a scratch node if the lock is busy), or return the scratch buffer, or return a flat-profile node entered and marked scratch. (2) Otherwise it consumes (reads and zeroes) __llvm_ctx_profile_callsite[0]; if that is null or points into a scratch context it returns getUnhandledContext(..., root), which returns a per-root 'unhandled' node marked scratch (allocating one, possibly in a new arena, the first time that Guid is seen) after entering it; expected_callee[0] is not consumed on this path. (3) Otherwise it consumes __llvm_ctx_profile_expected_callee[0]; if it differs from Callee it returns getUnhandledContext as in (2). (4) Otherwise it walks the callsite's list of nodes for one whose guid equals Guid, allocating a new node (getCallsiteSlow, from the current root's arena) and linking it at the head of the list if none is found; if that node's callsites_size or counters_size differs from NumCallsites or NumCounters it prints a '[ctxprof] Returned ctx differs' diagnostic and still continues; it then calls onContextEnter on it and returns it (a real, unmarked node).
note: Both reviewers right: the first (round 1) that scratch is also returned for contention/not-started (via tryStartContextGivenRoot and getUnhandledContext), the second (round 15) that TLS slots are only consumed when the root is set (callsite slot) and when the callsite slot is non-null (expected-callee slot); old prose said both always consumed.

name: AddRareFeature
prose: Member function of InputCorpus; Idx must be a valid index into IsRareFeature and GlobalFeatureFreqs (not checked). First loop: while RareFeatures.size() > Entropic.NumberOfRarestFeatures and FreqOfMostAbundantRareFeature > Entropic.FeatureFrequencyThreshold, it scans RareFeatures for the entry with the highest GlobalFeatureFreqs (ties resolved toward the later entry, with Delete recording its position and a second-highest index tracked alongside; both start at RareFeatures[0], so the 'second' can be the same feature), then clears IsRareFeature[Delete] (indexed by that position in RareFeatures, not by the feature index), overwrites RareFeatures[Delete] with the last entry and pops the back, calls DeleteFeatureFreq on every input for the removed feature (setting that input's NeedsEnergyUpdate when it returns true), and sets FreqOfMostAbundantRareFeature to GlobalFeatureFreqs of the recorded second-most-abundant feature. After the loop: it pushes Idx on RareFeatures, sets IsRareFeature[Idx] = true and GlobalFeatureFreqs[Idx] = 0; for every input it calls DeleteFeatureFreq(Idx) and, if that input's Energy > 0, increments SumIncidence by 1 and adds log(SumIncidence)/SumIncidence to Energy (inputs with Energy <= 0 are not changed by this step). Finally it sets DistributionNeedsUpdate = true. It has no return value.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: Idx must be valid and the arrays sized; earlier prose said 'no precondition'. Original reviewer's Energy>0 point was already in the prose.

name: UpdateCorpusDistribution
prose: Member function of InputCorpus taking Random &Rand. If DistributionNeedsUpdate is false and (Entropic.Enabled is false, or Rand(kSparseEnergyUpdates) returns nonzero) it returns immediately; the call to Rand happens only when DistributionNeedsUpdate is false and Entropic.Enabled is true, so the random generator state advances in that case. Otherwise it clears DistributionNeedsUpdate, asserts Inputs is non-empty (N = Inputs.size()), resizes Intervals to N+1 and Weights to N, fills Intervals with 0..N, computes the average TimeOfUnit and, if Entropic.Enabled, calls UpdateEnergy on each input that has NeedsEnergyUpdate and nonzero Energy (clearing the flag) and sets each Weights[i] to 0 when the input has no features or has been fuzzed far more than average, else to its Energy; if no weight is positive (or Entropic is disabled) it assigns Weights[i] = (i+1) times 1000 if the input has a focus function else 1, or 0 for inputs with no features. It optionally prints the scores (FeatureDebug) and then rebuilds CorpusDistribution as a piecewise_constant_distribution over Intervals and Weights. It has no return value.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: Inputs must be non-empty (assert(N), FuzzerCorpus.h:507). Original reviewer wrong: the early-return condition in the old prose matched code lines 500-502.

name: MinimizeCrashInput
prose: Driver function in FuzzerDriver.cpp. If Inputs does not hold exactly one path it prints an error and calls exit(1). It builds BaseCmd from Args with the minimize_crash and exact_artifact_path flags and the input path removed (assert that the path is an argument), adds -max_total_time=600 when Flags.runs <= 0 and Flags.max_total_time == 0, and merges the child's stdout and stderr. Then it loops: it reads the current file, runs the command on it through ExecuteCommand (which returns true when the child exits with status 0; a failed popen also yields false); if the run returns true (child exited 0, i.e. no crash) it prints 'did not crash' and calls exit(1). Otherwise it records the first dedup token from the output, runs the command again with minimize_crash_internal_step=1 and exact_artifact_path set to Flags.exact_artifact_path or a 'minimized-from-<hash>' path under the artifact prefix. If that second run returns true (the child exited 0, which this code reports as 'failed to minimize beyond'), it sets CurrentFilePath and rewrites the original bytes there only when Flags.exact_artifact_path is set, and leaves the loop; the function then returns 0. If the second run exits nonzero it compares dedup tokens: if they differ it again (when exact_artifact_path is set) writes U to that path and breaks out of the loop, so the function returns 0; if equal it continues with the new artifact path as the current input. The only return is 0 after a break; exit(1) is used for the other failures.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: 'Success' is ExecuteCommand's true = child exit status 0 (FuzzerUtilPosix.cpp: pclose(Pipe) == 0), so the break means the internal step ended without a crash, not that the input stopped crashing. Original reviewer right on the exit(1) path and break conditions; old prose was ambiguous.

name: InternalGetProcAddress
prose: Windows PE export-table lookup in interception_win.cpp. It builds RVAPtr views over module and reads dos_stub->e_lfanew while constructing headers, before the '!module' test in the following if, so a null module is dereferenced there (undefined behavior) rather than returning 0. The following check returns 0 if module is null (only meaningful if the dereference above did not fault), if e_magic is not 'MZ', if the NT signature is wrong, or if SizeOfOptionalHeader is smaller than sizeof(IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER); it returns 0 if the export directory size is 0, and 0 after scanning NumberOfNames names without any equal to func_name. For the first name equal to func_name it takes the ordinal-indexed function RVA: if that RVA lies inside the export directory (a forwarder string 'module.function') it copies the string into a 256-byte buffer, splits at the first '.', calls GetModuleHandleA on the module part and returns the recursive InternalGetProcAddress(redirected_module, text after the '.'); if the forwarder string is 255 or more characters, has no '.', or GetModuleHandleA returns null, it calls ReportError and InterceptionFailed (which prints and executes __debugbreak; it is not declared noreturn, so with a debugger attached execution can continue past it). Otherwise it returns the in-memory address (module base + RVA) of the function as uptr.
note: Reviewers (rounds 1, 15) right about the null-module dereference; round 2 partially right: InterceptionFailed does report and __debugbreak() (interception_win.cpp:164-169) but is not noreturn, so it is not guaranteed to leave the function.

name: INTERCEPTORS_STRTO_BASE(long, strtol, char)

The body is INTERCEPTOR_STRTO_BODY: ENSURE_MSAN_INITED(), then res = REAL(strtol)(nptr, endptr, base), then __msan_unpoison(endptr, sizeof(*endptr)), then return res. __msan_unpoison returns without effect if the address is not in application memory (a null endptr is thus ignored). The parsed value is returned unchanged; nptr is not checked here.

name: ELFNixPlatformRuntimeState::dlopenFull
prose: Member function taking std::unique_lock<std::recursive_mutex> &JDStateLock (held on entry, by the caller's convention) and PerJITDylibState &JDS. It first calls JDStateLock.unlock(), then calls the push-initializers wrapper through JITDispatch with JDS.Header; if that call itself returns an error it returns that error with the lock still unlocked. Otherwise it re-locks JDStateLock; if DepInfo holds an error it returns that error (lock held); otherwise it calls dlopenInitialize(JDStateLock, JDS, *DepInfo) and returns its error if any (dlopenInitialize and runInits only unlock temporarily around calling initializers and re-lock before returning); if the dep-info map is still non-empty afterwards it returns a StringError 'Encountered unrecognized dep-info key headers while processing dlopen of <name>' (lock held); else it returns Error::success() with the lock held.
note: Both reviewers right: the early wrapper-call error returns with the lock released (elfnix_platform.cpp:477-481), and the success-wrapper-call path can still return an error from DepInfo or from leftover dep-info keys (lines 484-496).

name: MachOPlatformRuntimeState::dlopenFull
prose: Member function taking std::unique_lock<std::mutex> &JDStatesLock (held on entry by the caller's convention) and JITDylibState &JDS. It unlocks JDStatesLock, calls the push-initializers wrapper through JITDispatch with JDS.Header and, if that call returns an error, returns it with the lock still unlocked. Otherwise it re-locks; if DepInfo holds an error it returns that error (lock held); then it calls dlopenInitialize(JDStatesLock, JDS, *DepInfo) and returns its error if any; if the dep-info map is still non-empty it logs under ORC_RT_DEBUG and returns a StringError 'Encountered unrecognized dep-info key headers while processing dlopen of <name>'; otherwise it returns Error::success(). Whether JDS is sealed or unsealed is handled inside dlopenInitialize (sealed JITDylibs with a non-empty dependency list produce an error there, sealed already-referenced ones are skipped); this function does not test it.
note: Old preconditions (unsealed or first-time) are not checked in this function; rewritten from macho_platform.cpp:1083-1115 and dlopenInitialize 1117-1186.

name: MachOPlatformRuntimeState::dlupdateFull
prose: Member function taking std::unique_lock<std::mutex> &JDStatesLock (held on entry by the caller's convention) and JITDylibState &JDS (dlupdateImpl only calls it for an unsealed, referenced JITDylib; this function does not check that). It unlocks JDStatesLock, calls the push-initializers wrapper through JITDispatch with JDS.Header and returns that call's error, with the lock still unlocked, if it fails. Otherwise it re-locks; if DepInfo holds an error it returns it (lock held); otherwise it calls dlupdateInitialize(JDStatesLock, JDS), which runs registerObjCRegistrationObjects and runModInits for JDS only, and returns an error from it if any, else Error::success(). The contents of a successful DepInfo are not used.
note: Old prose said dlupdateInitialize 're-ran initializers' and did not mention that DepInfo's value is ignored; rewritten from macho_platform.cpp:1211-1247.

name: __llvm_write_custom_profile
prose: Function in InstrProfilingFile.c (compiled when __APPLE__ is not defined); the slice cut the head. It saves the current profile file with getProfileFile() as oldFile and calls lprofSuspendSigKill() (PDeathSig). Return paths: (1) if lprofProfileDumped() or continuous mode is enabled, it prints a note, calls lprofRestoreSigKill() when PDeathSig == 1 and returns 0; (2) if the runtime profile version does not match INSTR_PROF_RAW_VERSION it prints an error, restores SIGKILL and returns -1; (3) if getCurFilename gives no filename it prints an error, restores SIGKILL and returns -1; (4) otherwise it builds, in alloca'd buffers, the target-specific name by inserting 'Target.' before the basename of the current filename, calls fopen(name, "w") and setProfileFile(OutputFile) before checking the result; if fopen failed it prints an error, restores SIGKILL and returns -1, leaving the registered profile file as NULL (oldFile is not restored); (5) on success it sets FreeHook to free, calls setupIOBuffer(), initializes a file writer, takes Version from __llvm_profile_get_version() unless *VersionOverride is supplied (VersionOverride non-NULL), calls lprofWriteDataImpl(...) and stores its result, closes the file with closeFileObject, restores SIGKILL if PDeathSig == 1, restores the saved profile file with setProfileFile(oldFile) and returns lprofWriteDataImpl's result (nonzero value signals a write failure as defined by that function). Target is used with strlen (must be a NUL-terminated string).
note: Name from source (slice cut the head; the old name writeTargetProfileFile does not exist anywhere under compiler-rt). Prose follows InstrProfilingFile.c:1280-1387; the old prose was consistent with this except that it asserted lprofWriteDataImpl returns 0 or negative.

name: parseFilenamePattern
prose: Static function in InstrProfilingFile.c. It frees lprofCurFilename.ProfilePathPrefix if set, frees lprofCurFilename.FilenamePat if owned, then memset-zeroes the whole lprofCurFilename structure (so PNS, TmpDir, MergePoolSize, NumPids/NumHosts/NumBinaryIds and others are reset to 0), and stores FilenamePat in it: the caller's pointer when CopyFilenamePat is 0, otherwise strdup(FilenamePat) with OwnsFilenamePat = 1 (no check that strdup succeeded). It then scans the pattern, handling each '%x': %p stores the pid text on the first occurrence (return -1 with a warning if snprintf returns <= 0); %h gets the hostname on the first occurrence (return -1 if gethostname fails); %t reads TMPDIR into TmpDir on each occurrence (return -1 if unset); %b on the first occurrence checks that __llvm_write_binary_ids(NULL) > 0 (return -1 otherwise); %c returns -1 after disabling continuous mode if it is already enabled, otherwise enables continuous mode and sets the page size on Mach-O/ELF/COFF/AIX targets and returns -1 on other targets; any other character goes to getMergePoolSize: if it is a %m / %Nm specifier a second one returns -1, the first sets MergePoolSize, and a non-m character is skipped. At the end it stores NumPids, NumHosts and NumBinaryIds and returns 0. On every -1 return the new pattern is already stored, the three counts are still 0, and TmpDir, MergePoolSize or continuous mode may already have been set by earlier specifiers.
note: Round-15 reviewer right: the memset zeroes PNS as well, so the old 'leaving PNS untouched' was wrong. Rounds 1 and 2 wrong: the prose already listed the duplicate-%m and unsupported-%c returns and the success path copying the three counts (InstrProfilingFile.c:842-876).

name: RoundUp
prose: Static function (compiled only when NT_GNU_BUILD_ID is defined) in InstrProfilingPlatformLinux.c: returns (size + align - 1) & ~(align - 1) as size_t, with unsigned wraparound if size + align - 1 exceeds the size_t range. For align a power of two this is the smallest multiple of align that is at least size (when no wraparound occurs); for an align that is not a power of two the expression does not round to a multiple of align. No memory is read or written.
note: Contract cleared (reviewers right: the formal used UINT64_MAX instead of SIZE_MAX, a 64-bit-only bound, and omitted minimality). Source line 125-127.

name: TEST(TestRtsanInterceptors, IoctlBehavesWithOutputPointer)
prose: gtest test (macro TEST, body is TestBody of TestRtsanInterceptors_IoctlBehavesWithOutputPointer_Test). It opens an AF_INET stream socket; if that returns -1 it prints the error and GTEST_SKIP()s (returns from the body). It calls getifaddrs; if that returns -1 or a null list it prints the error, closes the socket and skips. Otherwise it zero-initializes an ifreq and copies the first interface's name (strncpy, at most IFNAMSIZ-1 bytes) into it and calls ioctl(sock, SIOCGIFADDR, &ifr). If ioctl returns -1 it prints the error, closes the socket, frees the list and FAIL()s. Otherwise it frees the list, closes the socket and makes two fatal assertions: ifr_addr.sa_data is not null (an array member, so its address is always non-null) and ifr_addr.sa_family equals AF_INET. It returns nothing.
note: Checked against rtsan_test_interceptors_posix.cpp:788-821.

name: pthread_create (INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_create, pthread_t *thread, const pthread_attr_t *attr, void *(*start_routine)(void*), void *arg))
prose: Interceptor defined with INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_create, ...) in safestack.cpp (named pthread_create, not pthread_create_interceptor). It calls EnsureInterceptorsInitialized(), then obtains size and guard (both initially 0): if attr is non-null from pthread_attr_getstacksize and pthread_attr_getguardsize on attr, otherwise from a temporary default pthread_attr_t initialized and destroyed locally; the return values of the getters are not checked, so a failing getter leaves the value at 0. On Solaris a size of 0 is replaced with 2 MiB (LP64) or 1 MiB. SFS_CHECK(size) then aborts the process (fprintf and abort) if size is 0. size is rounded up to 16; unsafe_stack_alloc(size, guard) aborts if size+guard overflows or mmap fails, mprotect-s the guard area PROT_NONE and returns the address after the guard. A struct tinfo is placed at the end of that mapping holding start_routine, arg and the stack parameters. The function returns REAL(pthread_create)(thread, attr, thread_start, tinfo) directly: on success the new thread runs thread_start, which installs the unsafe stack (and so overwrites tinfo's contents) and calls start_routine(arg); the stack is released later by the thread-exit cleanup handler. If the real pthread_create fails, its error code is returned and the mapped unsafe stack (which contains tinfo) is not unmapped, so it is leaked.
note: Slice cut the head: the function is INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_create, ...). Old prose wrong in claiming getter failures are returned (lines 240-250 ignore them; failure leads to SFS_CHECK abort or a default value) and that tinfo is a separate allocation (it lives inside the mapped stack, lines 269-270). Reviewer round 1 right on the leak, which the old prose already stated.

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::Handle::Handle(AddrHashMap<T, kSize> *map, uptr addr)
prose: Handle constructor (template member): sets map_ = map, addr_ = addr, remove_ = false and create_ = true, then calls map_->acquire(this), which sets created_, addidx_, bucket_ and cell_. Because create_ is true and remove_ false, acquire leaves cell_ non-null: either an existing cell (found lock-free in the bucket's embedded cells with no lock held, or in the bucket's add array with the bucket read lock held and addidx_ set), or a newly claimed cell with created_ true, addr still 0 and the bucket's exclusive lock held until the destructor (release) publishes the address. It returns nothing; the destructor calls map_->release(this).
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for this constructor: create_ is true here, so cell_ cannot be null (sanitizer_addrhashmap.h:140-146 and acquire lines 285-331).

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::Handle::Handle(AddrHashMap<T, kSize> *map, uptr addr, bool remove)
prose: Handle constructor (template member): sets map_ = map, addr_ = addr, remove_ = remove and create_ = true, then calls map_->acquire(this). If remove is false the outcome is that of the two-argument constructor (non-null cell_: existing cell with no lock or the bucket read lock, or a new cell with created_ true and the exclusive bucket lock held). If remove is true, acquire skips the lock-free search, takes the bucket's exclusive lock and, if a cell for addr exists, sets cell_ to it (created_ false) and keeps the lock; if none exists it releases the lock and leaves cell_ null (exists() is false). The destructor (release) then removes the cell and unlocks. It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for this constructor: with create_ true the only null-cell case is remove=true, which the old prose already stated.

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::Handle::Handle(AddrHashMap<T, kSize> *map, uptr addr, bool remove, bool create)
prose: Handle constructor (template member): sets map_, addr_, remove_ and create_ from the arguments and calls map_->acquire(this). With remove true: acquire takes the bucket's exclusive lock; cell_ is the existing cell for addr (created_ false, lock held until the destructor removes it and unlocks) or null if none exists (lock released). With remove false: an existing cell is found lock-free in the embedded cells (no lock held) or in the add array (bucket read lock held, addidx_ set), after a retry loop that also covers a cell inserted concurrently; if none exists and create is true, a new cell is claimed with created_ true and the bucket's exclusive lock held until the destructor publishes it; if none exists and create is false, cell_ is null, created_ is false and no lock is held. It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer right for this constructor: remove=false, create=false and absent address leaves cell_ null; the old prose omitted that case.

name: AddrHashMap<T, kSize>::acquire
prose: Member function of AddrHashMap (declared SANITIZER_NO_THREAD_SAFETY_ANALYSIS) that fills in Handle *h: it sets h->created_ = false, addidx_ = -1U, bucket_ = the bucket for hash(addr_) and cell_ = nullptr. The calling thread must not already hold that bucket's mutex. If remove_ is false it first looks lock-free in the bucket's embedded cells (found: cell_ set, nothing locked, return); then, if the bucket has an add array, it takes the read lock and scans it (found: addidx_ and cell_ set, read lock held, return; not found: read lock released). It then takes the exclusive lock and re-checks the embedded cells and the add array: if the address is found and remove_ is set it sets cell_ (and addidx_ for the add array) and returns holding the exclusive lock; if it is found and remove_ is not set (it appeared concurrently) it unlocks and goes back to the lock-free search again. If it is not found and remove_ is set or create_ is false, it unlocks and returns with cell_ null. Otherwise it sets created_ = true and claims a free embedded cell (addidx_ stays -1U) or, in the add array, a new slot at index add->size (allocating a 64-byte array with InternalAlloc the first time, or doubling it with InternalAlloc/memcpy/InternalFree when full), setting addidx_ and cell_; it returns with the exclusive lock held and the cell's addr still 0 (release() publishes it). It returns nothing.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong: the old prose already said absent-and-remove_ gives null (lines 284-288). Round-17 reviewer right in a narrow sense: the retry (unlock and search again when a non-removing lookup finds the element under the exclusive lock, lines 256-263 and 272-280) was not in the old prose; the lock-free add-array hit does return holding the read lock (lines 234-244).

name: SizeClassAllocator32<Params>::ClassID
prose: Static member function of the 32-bit primary allocator: returns SizeClassMap::ClassID(size). In SizeClassMap::ClassID, size greater than kMaxSize gives 0; size up to kMidSize gives (size + kMinSize - 1) >> kMinSizeLog, which is 0 for size 0 and at least 1 for size from 1; larger sizes give kMidClass + (l1 << S) + hbits + (lbits > 0), computed from the most-significant-bit index of size. So the result is 0 for size 0 and for size above kMaxSize, and nonzero for sizes from 1 to kMaxSize. It reads no mutable state.
note: Round-15 reviewer right (size 0 gives 0, sanitizer_allocator_size_class_map.h:158-162). Round-2 reviewer wrong: sizes above kMaxSize are handled (return 0), so there is no precondition. Upper bound by kNumClasses dropped as not verified from this code alone.

name: TgKill
prose: Function in sanitizer_linux.cpp whose body depends on the platform macro: on Linux it returns internal_syscall(SYSCALL(tgkill), pid, tid, sig), the raw kernel return (0 on success or a negative errno value); on FreeBSD it returns internal_syscall(SYSCALL(thr_kill2), pid, tid, sig), where internal_syscall maps to libc syscall/__syscall, so failure is -1 with errno set rather than -errno; on Solaris it ignores pid, assigns errno = thr_kill(tid, sig) and returns -1 if errno is then nonzero, otherwise 0; on Haiku it ignores pid and sig and returns kill_thread(tid), the status_t result. No arguments are validated.
note: Old prose wrong for FreeBSD (said -errno): sanitizer_syscall_generic.inc defines internal_syscall as syscall/__syscall there. Round-15 reviewer wrong: thr_kill returns the error number (stored into errno, then -1 is returned), as the prose said for Solaris.

name: ThreadDescriptorSizeFallback
prose: Static function in sanitizer_linux_libcdep.cpp; the file has two definitions of this name, one for SANITIZER_GLIBC and one for SANITIZER_FREEBSD (both without SANITIZER_GO), and the slice contains the FreeBSD one in full. The FreeBSD one takes no arguments and, depending on the compile-time architecture macros, returns: on s390 or sparc 524 (32-bit) or 1552 (64-bit); on mips 1152 (32-bit) or 1776 (64-bit); on loongarch64 1856; on aarch64 1776; on powerpc64 1776; and 0 if none of those macros is defined. The glibc definition (lines 224-296) returns a version-dependent size on x86, arm (reads gnu_get_libc_version and aborts via CHECK_EQ if the major version is not 2), values 1772 or 1936 on riscv64 depending on the glibc minor version, and the same constants as the FreeBSD one on s390/sparc/mips/loongarch64/aarch64/powerpc64; the glibc one has no final return for an unlisted architecture.
note: Both reviewers (rounds 1, 2, 15) right about the earlier formal contract (cleared); the file has two definitions, the riscv64 values belong to the glibc one (sanitizer_linux_libcdep.cpp lines 260-268), which the old prose did not mention.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_mutex_lock, pthread_mutex_t *m)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_mutex_lock. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It then calls MutexBeforeLock(thr, (uptr)m, true), calls REAL(pthread_mutex_lock)(m), then calls MutexAfterLock(thr, (uptr)m, true, false) whatever the real call returned (the after-lock event is recorded even if the call failed), and returns the real call's return value unchanged.

name: INTERCEPTOR(int, pthread_cond_wait, pthread_cond_t *c, pthread_mutex_t *m)
prose: Interceptor for pthread_cond_wait. The interceptor first calls InitThread() and ignores its bool result (InitThread returns false while the per-thread initing flag is set, in which case the thread pointer thr may still be null). It obtains a shadow condition variable with init_cond(c): if the slot c already holds a nonzero pointer that pointer is used; otherwise a zeroed pthread_cond_t is allocated with InternalAlloc and installed with a compare-exchange, and if another thread won the race the new block is freed and the winner's is used. It then calls MutexBeforeUnlock and MutexBeforeLock for m (both with writelock true), calls REAL(pthread_cond_wait)(shadow, m), calls MutexAfterLock(thr, (uptr)m, true, false) whatever the real call returned, and returns the real return value unchanged. The shadow stays installed in c until pthread_cond_init replaces it or pthread_cond_destroy frees it.

name: OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTORS_BITWISE(OSAtomicOr, fetch_or, OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR_PLUS_X, OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR) [OSAtomicOr32]
prose: Generated interceptor int32_t OSAtomicOr32(uint32_t x, volatile uint32_t *ptr) (macro OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR_PLUS_X with __tsan_atomic32_fetch_or and kMacOrderNonBarrier, which equals mo_acq_rel). It runs SCOPED_TSAN_INTERCEPTOR(OSAtomicOr32, x, ptr): this aborts the process if the real function was not found, and if the interceptor must be ignored (thread not initialized, ignore_interceptors set, or in an ignored library) it returns REAL(OSAtomicOr32)(x, ptr) directly. Otherwise it calls __tsan_atomic32_fetch_or((volatile a32 *)ptr, x, mo_acq_rel), which atomically sets *ptr to old | x and returns the old value, and the function returns that old value plus x (converted to int32_t). So the return value is old + x, not the new value of *ptr (old | x).
note: Round-15 reviewer right: OSATOMIC_INTERCEPTOR_PLUS_X returns tsan_atomic_f(...) + x and fetch_or returns the old value (tsan_interceptors_mac.cpp:57-62, 106-107); the old prose said (old|x)+x. The unmodified/ignored path (REAL call) was also missing.

name: dup2
prose: TSAN interceptor TSAN_INTERCEPTOR(int, dup2, int oldfd, int newfd). SCOPED_TSAN_INTERCEPTOR aborts if the real dup2 is missing; if the thread must be ignored (not initialized, ignore_interceptors or in an ignored library) it returns REAL(dup2)(oldfd, newfd) directly. Otherwise it calls REAL(dup2), stores the result as newfd2 and, if oldfd >= 0 and newfd2 >= 0 and newfd2 != oldfd, calls FdDup(thr, pc, oldfd, newfd2, false) to record the duplication; it returns newfd2 (the new descriptor, or -1 with errno set on failure of the real call).

Otherwise it calls REAL(eventfd), and if the returned fd is >= 0 it calls FdEventCreate(thr, pc, fd) to register it; it returns the descriptor, or -1 with errno set on failure of the real call (no registration then).

name: operator new (nothrow)
prose: C++ allocation operator, nothrow (macro OPERATOR_NEW_BODY with nothrow true). If in_symbolizer() it returns InternalAlloc(size) directly. Otherwise, inside a SCOPED_INTERCEPTOR_RAW scope, it sets p = user_alloc(thr, pc, size) and does not report an out-of-memory error itself; then it calls invoke_malloc_hook(p, size) (also when p is null) and returns p. p is null only if the allocator returns null for the request, which user_alloc/user_memalign do (setting errno) only when allocator_may_return_null is enabled; otherwise the allocator reports the error and does not return. A non-null result is released with operator delete.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for the nothrow forms (OPERATOR_NEW_BODY(..., true) skips ReportOutOfMemory, tsan_new_delete.cpp:31-44); the old prose was already correct for the non-nothrow aligned forms.

name: operator new[] (nothrow)
prose: C++ array allocation operator, nothrow (macro OPERATOR_NEW_BODY with nothrow true). If in_symbolizer() it returns InternalAlloc(size) directly. Otherwise, inside a SCOPED_INTERCEPTOR_RAW scope, it sets p = user_alloc(thr, pc, size) and does not report an out-of-memory error itself; then it calls invoke_malloc_hook(p, size) (also when p is null) and returns p. p is null only if the allocator returns null for the request, which user_alloc/user_memalign do (setting errno) only when allocator_may_return_null is enabled; otherwise the allocator reports the error and does not return. A non-null result is released with operator delete[].
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for the nothrow forms (OPERATOR_NEW_BODY(..., true) skips ReportOutOfMemory, tsan_new_delete.cpp:31-44); the old prose was already correct for the non-nothrow aligned forms.

name: operator new (aligned)
prose: C++ aligned allocation operator (macro OPERATOR_NEW_BODY_ALIGN with nothrow false). If in_symbolizer() it returns InternalAlloc(size, nullptr, (uptr)align) directly with no hook call. Otherwise, inside a SCOPED_INTERCEPTOR_RAW scope, it sets p = user_memalign(thr, pc, (uptr)align, size) and, if p is null, builds a fatal stack trace and calls ReportOutOfMemory(size, &stack), which does not return; then it calls invoke_malloc_hook(p, size) and returns p. So outside the symbolizer it returns a non-null pointer or does not return. A non-null result is released with operator delete.
note: Round-15 reviewer wrong for the nothrow forms (OPERATOR_NEW_BODY(..., true) skips ReportOutOfMemory, tsan_new_delete.cpp:31-44); the old prose was already correct for the non-nothrow aligned forms.
